- Project page: http://www.simonweckert.com/googlemapshacks.html

#### Fooling Automated Surveillance Cameras: Adversarial Patches to Attack Person Detection — Simen Thys (2019)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: A detector's idea of a 'person' can be switched off by a pattern no human would read as camouflage.
- What it is: A paper and demo in which a printed cardboard patch, held in front of the body, makes a person disappear from the YOLOv2 person detector used in automated surveillance.
- How it works: Simen Thys, Wiebe Van Ranst and Toon Goedemé optimise the patch pixels to minimise YOLOv2's objectness and class scores on the Inria person dataset, with printability and smoothness terms so the printed patch works in front of a real camera.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Failure, glitch & error
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/CVPRW.2019.00012 (CVPR Workshops 2019)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MIbFvK2S9g8
- Project page: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.08653

#### Mask.ID — Peng! Collective (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A biometric passport photo can belong to two people at once.
- What it is: A Peng! member merged her face with that of EU foreign-policy chief Federica Mogherini and obtained a real German passport with the morphed photo; the campaign asked citizens to do the same to help refugees travel.
- How it works: Face-morphing software blends two faces until face recognition matches both; the image was submitted through a standard passport application.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Images: https://pen.gg/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/MaskID_Kabine_1_Melber-1800x1200.jpg
- Project page: https://pen.gg/campaign/mask-id-2/

#### Nonfacial Portrait — Shinseungback Kimyonghun (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Portraiture becomes a search for the narrow visual space only humans can perceive.
- What it is: Painters are asked to paint a portrait that people recognise but in which no face-detection algorithm can find a face. A camera watches the canvas and a screen warns the painter whenever a face is detected.
- How it works: Three face-detection algorithms monitor the canvas through a camera; each painting is shown with a video of its making.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: NTT InterCommunication Center (ICC), Tokyo

#### Perception Engines — Tom White (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Art can be made for the machine's eye: the prints show which few marks are 'enough' for a classifier.
- What it is: A series of abstract prints that ImageNet classifiers confidently recognise as a cello, a cabbage, a hammerhead shark or an iron, though people see only a few coloured strokes.
- How it works: A constrained drawing system is optimised against an ensemble of ImageNet classifiers, and the results are printed as risographs and screen prints.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Opacity & latent space
- Images: http://static1.squarespace.com/static/5c3518f55cfd7963746dd576/t/5cfed9300e5c0200015a2735/1560205650916/tom_white_electric_fan_2019+%281%29.jpg?format=1500w https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5c3518f55cfd7963746dd576/1609721536034-7SU963UJO2QP104FXYBO/cello_16_095_240_thumbnail.jpg
- Project page: https://drib.net/perception-engines

#### Robust Physical-World Attacks on Deep Learning Visual Classification — Kevin Eykholt (2018)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: What looks like graffiti to a driver can rewrite the road for a self-driving car.
- What it is: A few black and white stickers on a real stop sign make a road-sign classifier read it as a 45 mph speed-limit sign from many distances and angles.
- How it works: The Robust Physical Perturbations (RP2) algorithm optimises sticker-like perturbations over varied physical conditions and tests them in lab and drive-by settings (Eykholt et al., CVPR 2018).
- Lens: Machine seeing, Failure, glitch & error
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/CVPR.2018.00175 (CVPR 2018)
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1109/CVPR.2018.00175
- Code: https://github.com/evtimovi/robust_physical_perturbations

#### Adversarial Patch — Tom B. Brown (2017)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Computer vision
- Idea: The machine's attention can be hijacked: one salient patch outweighs the whole scene.
- What it is: Google Brain researchers made a printable, psychedelic sticker that, placed next to a banana, makes image classifiers see only a 'toaster'.
- How it works: A universal, scene-independent patch is optimised over many images, positions and scales against ImageNet classifiers such as Inception (Brown, Mané, Roy, Abadi, Gilmer).
- Lens: Machine seeing, Failure, glitch & error, Opacity & latent space
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.09665 (arXiv 2017 (NIPS 2017 Workshop))
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i1sp4X57TL4
- Project page: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.09665

#### Autonomous Trap 001 — James Bridle (2017)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: A machine that obeys the symbols it sees can be trapped by those symbols, like a spirit in a magic circle.
- What it is: On Mount Parnassus the artist draws a salt circle with road markings around a self-driving car: a dashed line lets it in, a solid line forbids it to leave.
- How it works: A salt circle with dashed and solid lane markings traps a car running the artist's own self-driving software; performed on 14 March 2017.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Failure, glitch & error, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Entangled Realities, HEK Basel 2019; AI: Who's Looking After Me?, Science Gallery London 2023
- Images: https://jamesbridle.com/media/pages/works/autonomous-trap-001/329e6817a6-1680515123/1-autonomous-trap-001-003.jpg https://jamesbridle.com/media/pages/works/autonomous-trap-001/7f4c4c6acb-1680515123/autonomous-trap-001-001.jpg
- Project page: https://jamesbridle.com/works/autonomous-trap-001

#### HyperFace — Adam Harvey (2017)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Instead of hiding a face, flood the machine with faces only it can see.
- What it is: A textile print covered with patterns that face detectors read as many false faces, so the real face nearby gets a lower confidence score.
- How it works: Patterns were generated from what face-detection algorithms score as faces; developed with Hyphen-Labs for NeuroSpeculative AfroFeminism.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: 33C3 Hamburg 2016; Sundance Film Festival 2017 (NeuroSpeculative AfroFeminism)

#### Wearable Face Projector — Jing-cai Liu (2017)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Against face recognition, one answer is to wear someone else's face.
- What it is: A head-mounted mini projector that casts another person's face onto the wearer's own, to confuse face and emotion recognition in public space.
- How it works: Small projector on a head-mounted arm projects face video onto the wearer; design prototype and film.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Embodiment & kinesthesia

#### Accessorize to a Crime — Mahmood Sharif (2016)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: A face-recognition system can be steered by a few centimetres of pattern on the face.
- What it is: Researchers at Carnegie Mellon printed colourful eyeglass frames that let a wearer dodge a face-recognition system or be recognised as someone else, such as a celebrity.
- How it works: Adversarial perturbations are optimised only within an eyeglass-frame region, made smooth and printable, and tested physically against deep-network face recognition and Face++ (ACM CCS 2016; Sharif, Bhagavatula, Bauer, Reiter).
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Failure, glitch & error
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/2976749.2978392 (ACM CCS 2016)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6Xh1vuwnVhU
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1145/2976749.2978392

#### Hidden Voice Commands — Nicholas Carlini (2016)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Voice & listening machine
- Idea: The listening machine does not hear what we hear; the gap between human and machine hearing is a space where commands can hide.
- What it is: Security research showing that speech recognisers such as Google Now can be commanded by audio that sounds like noise to people, including black-box attacks on commercial assistants and a defence study.
- How it works: Iteratively distorts speech features (MFCCs) so that recognisers still decode a command while human listeners in user studies cannot understand it; tested against Google Now and an open-source recogniser.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Failure, glitch & error
- Paper: https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity16/technical-sessions/presentation/carlini (USENIX Security 2016)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x4bqJh4wyjU
- Project page: https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity16/technical-sessions/presentation/carlini

#### Deep Neural Networks are Easily Fooled — Evolving AI Lab (2015)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Computer vision
- Idea: A classifier's certainty is not seeing: it recognises features, not things.
- What it is: Anh Nguyen, Jason Yosinski and Jeff Clune evolved images, from static noise to abstract patterns, that state-of-the-art classifiers label with over 99% confidence as a king penguin, a starfish or a baseball.
- How it works: Evolutionary algorithms and gradient ascent generate images that maximise class scores of ImageNet- and MNIST-trained convolutional networks (CVPR 2015).
- Lens: Machine seeing, Opacity & latent space, Failure, glitch & error
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/CVPR.2015.7298640 (CVPR 2015)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M2IebCN9Ht4
- Project page: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.1897

#### URME Surveillance — Leo Selvaggio (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: If the system can only match faces, many bodies sharing one face make its records meaningless.
- What it is: The artist sells a photo-realistic 3D-printed prosthetic of his own face; anyone wearing it in front of face-recognition cameras is identified as Leo Selvaggio.
- How it works: A resin prosthetic made from a 3D scan of the artist's face, launched via an Indiegogo campaign and shown with a face-tracking mirror installation.

#### How Not to Be Seen: A Fucking Didactic Educational .MOV File — Hito Steyerl (2013)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Being seen is a matter of resolution; invisibility can be a tactic against machine vision, but it is also how the poor and disappeared are erased.
- What it is: A deadpan instructional video in five lessons on how to disappear from a world of high-resolution cameras, satellites and aerial targets: hide in plain sight, become smaller than a pixel, live in a gated community, or be a woman over 50.
- How it works: Filmed partly at a disused aerial photo-calibration target in the California desert, mixing green-screen performances, 3D animation and parodies of training videos.

#### Stealth Wear — Adam Harvey (2013)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: When the machine sees in heat, privacy becomes a question of what your clothes radiate.
- What it is: An anti-drone hoodie, hijab and burqa made of silver-plated fabric that hides the wearer's body heat from overhead thermal cameras.
- How it works: Garments are sewn from silver-plated synthetic fabric that reflects thermal radiation; they were tested with a FLIR thermal camera.

#### Facial Weaponization Suite — Zach Blas (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: Opacity can be collective: a face that belongs to many people is a face the machine cannot identify.
- What it is: Blas runs community workshops where participants' faces are scanned and merged into amorphous, colourful collective masks that face recognition cannot read. The masks are worn in public actions and in the video 'Facial Weaponization Communiqué: Fag Face'.
- How it works: Participants' faces are 3D-scanned, the biometric data are aggregated in modelling software and the combined forms are fabricated as wearable masks; the Fag Face Mask answers studies claiming to detect sexual orientation from faces.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing
- Shown at: Workshops and public actions in Los Angeles, San Diego, New York and Mexico City, 2012–14

#### Privacy Visor — Isao Echizen (2012)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: It works in the gap between human and machine sight: what looks like ordinary glasses to a person is a blinding light to the camera.
- What it is: Glasses that stop cameras from finding a face: the 2012 prototype carried near-infrared LEDs that people cannot see but camera sensors pick up as glare, and later versions used light-absorbing and reflecting patterns to break face detection.
- How it works: Near-infrared LEDs around the eyes and nose bridge (later, patterned light-absorbing and reflecting materials) add noise to the light-dark facial features that face detectors look for; developed at Japan's National Institute of Informatics.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing
- Shown at: IWSEC 2012 (first presentation)
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-40779-6_13 (Communications and Multimedia Security (CMS 2013), LNCS)

#### CV Dazzle — Adam Harvey (2010)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: A face is whatever the detector's template says it is; designing against that template reveals it.
- What it is: A camouflage strategy of bold make-up and asymmetric hairstyles that breaks the features a face detector looks for, so the wearer stays visible to people but disappears for the algorithm.
- How it works: Looks were designed and tested against the Viola-Jones Haar-cascade face detector in OpenCV (later looks, 2020, against CNN face recognition).
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: NYU ITP thesis 2010; The New York Times Op-Art 2013; Designs for a Different Future 2020
- Video: https://vimeo.com/12774628
- Images: https://adam.harvey.studio/cvdazzle/cvd-look1.webp https://adam.harvey.studio/cvdazzle/cvdazzle-06-copyright-adam-harvey-2020.webp https://adam.harvey.studio/cvdazzle/cvdazzle-05-saliency-map.webp
- Project page: https://adam.harvey.studio/cvdazzle/

#### Pixelhead — Martin Backes (2010)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: The pixel mosaic, the screen's own sign of anonymity, can be worn as clothing.
- What it is: A full-face balaclava printed with a pixelated face, so that its wearer cannot be recognised or automatically tagged in photos posted online.
- How it works: Printed textile mask; defeats face detection by hiding facial landmarks.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Images: https://www.martinbackes.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2013/03/martinbackes_web4.jpg
- Project page: https://www.martinbackes.com

## Machine Bodies & Behaviour

Robots and kinetic machines as bodies that move, react, perform, tire and fail in front of us.

### Cybernetic Creatures

Feedback machines from the 1940s–70s that behave as if alive.

#### The Senster — Edward Ihnatowicz (1970)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Shyness is more lifelike than obedience: the machine's withdrawal made visitors change their own behaviour.
- What it is: A 4-metre hydraulic creature shaped like a lobster's claw on a long neck, installed at the Philips Evoluon in Eindhoven, moved its 'head' toward quiet sounds and slow movements and shied away from loud noise and sudden gestures. Visitors shouted at it and waited for it to come closer.
- How it works: A Philips P9201 computer processes input from four microphones and two Doppler radar sensors in the head and drives six electro-hydraulic servo joints modelled on a lobster's claw.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Philips Evoluon, Eindhoven 1970–1974; Nieuwe Instituut, Rotterdam (restored)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1jDt5unArNk
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/14/Edward_Ihnatowicz%2C_The_Senster_%2853386590223%29.jpg https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/45/Edward_Ihnatowicz%2C_The_Senster_%2853386711664%29.jpg
- Project page: http://www.senster.com/

#### Colloquy of Mobiles — Gordon Pask (1968)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Machines can be staged as partners in a conversation of desire, and humans can enter that conversation as just one more participant.
- What it is: Five hanging mobiles, three 'females' and two 'males', court each other with beams of light and sound, learning which approaches 'satisfy' their partners. Visitors given mirrors and torches could join in and redirect the machines' desire.
- How it works: Rotating fibreglass bodies with lights, mirrors and photocells are driven by motor-driven 'drives' that build up and discharge; each mobile adjusts its behaviour to reward signals from the others.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Cybernetic Serendipity, ICA London 1968; Centre Pompidou reconstruction 2020
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RlXDL8Ab0oQ
- Project page: https://cyberneticserendipity.net/

#### Cybernetic Sculpture — Wen-Ying Tsai (1968)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Feedback between sound, light and vibration makes a steel sculpture seem to listen and respond.
- What it is: Clusters of thin stainless-steel rods vibrate on a motorised base under strobe light; when visitors clap or speak, the strobe frequency shifts and the rods appear to freeze, sway or dance.
- How it works: A motor vibrates the rods at a fixed rate while a sound-sensing feedback circuit changes the strobe's frequency, producing stroboscopic motion effects.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Howard Wise Gallery, New York 1968
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/75/Tsai_cyberneticsculpture79.jpg https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f1/Tsai_tuningfork1974.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wen-Ying_Tsai

#### SAM (Sound Activated Mobile) — Edward Ihnatowicz (1968)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Turning to listen is the simplest gesture of attention, and it is enough to make a machine seem to be someone.
- What it is: A flower-like head of fibreglass petals on an articulated aluminium neck turns toward whoever is speaking or making noise nearby, as if listening.
- How it works: Four microphones in the head compare sound levels; small hydraulic pistons move the neck vertebrae toward the loudest direction.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Cybernetic Serendipity, ICA London 1968
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8b52qpyV__g
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ee/Sound_Activated_Mobile.jpg
- Project page: http://www.senster.com/ihnatowicz/

#### Robot K-456 — Nam June Paik, Shuya Abe (1964)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A robot made clumsy, noisy and bodily, closer to a street performer than to a symbol of technical progress.
- What it is: A 20-channel radio-controlled humanoid built in Tokyo that walked the streets, played a recorded speech by John F. Kennedy and dropped beans as excrement. It debuted in Paik's Robot Opera at the 1964 New York Avant Garde Festival.
- How it works: Metal armature with motors and a 20-channel radio remote built by engineer Shuya Abe; restored in 2025 by the Nam June Paik Art Center, which holds it (1964/1996).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: Robot Opera, 2nd Annual New York Avant Garde Festival 1964; Nam June Paik: Becoming Robot, Asia Society 2014; Nam June Paik Art Center (collection)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JciiqCsRhdY
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nam_June_Paik

#### The Hopkins Beast — Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (1962)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A machine whose whole world is organised around one need, finding food, already looks like an animal.
- What it is: A wheeled automaton wanders the white corridors of the laboratory on its own and, when its batteries run low, looks for black wall sockets, plugs itself in and recharges. Later versions used sonar to avoid people and recognise doors and stairs.
- How it works: Transistor logic without a computer links touch switches, sonar and, in Mod II, an optical sensor for dark sockets to tracks, a wall-following arm and extendable plug prongs.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zMpEeag7kkM
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3e/00-01964_APL_66196_001_The_Beast.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_Beast

#### CYSP 1 — Nicolas Schöffer (1956)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: The first sculpture to have sense organs and a nervous system made the artwork an agent that reacts rather than an object that is looked at.
- What it is: A tower of steel and aluminium plates on a wheeled base turns, spins its polychrome blades and moves across the floor in response to light, colour and sound around it. In 1956 it performed with Maurice Béjart's dancers on the roof of the Cité radieuse in Marseille.
- How it works: Photocells and microphones feed an electronic 'brain' built with Philips that drives the motors in the wheeled base and the rotating plates; excitation and calm states depend on the stimuli.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Cité radieuse, Marseille 1956; Artistes & Robots, Grand Palais 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8nxktU1R6E
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Sch%C3%B6ffer

#### Theseus (maze-solving mouse) — Claude Shannon (1950)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Learning becomes visible as a small body in a maze, even though the 'brain' is a bank of telephone relays under the floor.
- What it is: A magnetic toy mouse, moved from below the table by relays, explores a reconfigurable maze by trial and error, remembers the route and then runs straight to the 'cheese'. When the maze is changed, it relearns.
- How it works: About 75 telephone relays store, for each square of a 25-square maze, the last direction that led out; a magnet on a motorised carriage beneath the board pulls the mouse.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_9_AEVQ_p74
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Shannon

#### Machina speculatrix (Elmer and Elsie) — W. Grey Walter (1949)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Two 'neurons' and a body in a room are enough for behaviour that people read as curiosity, hunger and self-recognition.
- What it is: Two small three-wheeled 'tortoises' with a light sensor and a touch switch wander a room, seek moderate light, back off from bright light and obstacles, and return to a lit hutch to recharge. With a light on its shell, one tortoise reacts to its own reflection in a mirror or to the other one, as if recognising itself.
- How it works: Analogue circuits with two vacuum-tube 'neurons' connect a rotating photocell and a shell touch contact to steering and drive motors; behaviour emerges from feedback between the body and its environment.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Festival of Britain, London 1951
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wQE82derooc
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/Cybernetic_Tortoise_by_William_Grey_Walter_c_1950_%28Ank_Kumar%29.jpg https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/77/Replica_of_Grey_Walter%27s_tortoise_%283572415081%29.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turtle_(robot)

#### Homeostat — W. Ross Ashby (1948)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Adaptation can be built without a model of the world: a machine that blindly tries new settings until it is calm again already behaves like something that learns.
- What it is: Four interconnected units, each topped by a pivoting magnet needle, keep themselves stable: when someone disturbs a unit or rewires them, the machine switches its own circuit settings at random until all needles settle back at the centre. In 1949 Time called it 'the closest thing to a synthetic brain so far designed by man'.
- How it works: Four ex-RAF bomb-control units coupled by feedback; each unit's magnet drives a needle dipping into a water-filled trough, and stepping switches (uniselectors) re-set the connections at random whenever a needle leaves its limits, which Ashby called ultrastability.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Ninth Macy Conference on Cybernetics, New York, 1952
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/43/W._Ross_Ashby%27s_1948_Homeostat.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeostat

### Artificial Life & Machine Collectives

Evolving agents, swarms and self-organising machine ecologies.

#### Lasermice — So Kanno (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Making a machine network's communication visible and audible shows collective behaviour as it forms.
- What it is: A swarm of 60 small robots that talk to each other with laser beams and photodetectors and tap the floor, so a firefly-like synchronised rhythm emerges without a central controller.
- How it works: Each robot carries a laser, photodetectors and a solenoid; pulse-coupled oscillator rules, inspired by fireflies, synchronise their firing.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Ars Electronica 2019; 22nd Japan Media Arts Festival, Excellence Award 2019; Biennale Nemo, Paris 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4afSgcWleFo
- Images: https://www.kanno.so/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/lasermice_by_Quentin_Chevrier_2-copy.jpg
- Project page: https://www.kanno.so/project/lasermice

#### Putting the Pieces Back Together Again — Ralf Baecker (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Order emerges and dissolves in a field of simple machines, making self-organisation visible as motion.
- What it is: An array of 1,250 small stepper motors, each turning a white bar, forms a surface across which waves, clusters and swarm-like patterns pass, as the motors align with and disturb their neighbours.
- How it works: Each motor is an element of a coupled-oscillator or spin-like model; local interaction rules computed in real time set each bar's angle (commissioned for the Drehmoment festival in a former newspaper building).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: Drehmoment, KulturRegion Stuttgart, Kirchheim unter Teck 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8GtFttw8z9U
- Project page: https://rlfbckr.io/project/ptpbta/

#### Lichtsuchende — Dave Murray-Rust, Rocio von Jungenfeld (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Give machines one shared resource and one channel of communication and something like social behaviour appears, legible to us as light.
- What it is: A society of small sunflower-like robots that turn their heads towards light to feed on it and flash light to address one another; grouped together they form a flickering photo-kinetic community that visitors walk into and disturb with their own lamps.
- How it works: Each robot has light sensors and a motorised head that tracks light plus LEDs to emit it; simple bio-inspired rules for energy exchange and signalling produce group behaviour.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Lumen Prize 2019, BCS Artificial Intelligence Award
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-16498-4_15 (EvoMUSART 2015, Lecture Notes in Computer Science)
- Video: https://vimeo.com/207512856
- Images: http://static1.squarespace.com/static/65e7176a61627736e02f6c4a/6606a60245e66065f7018332/6606a8f3e120ce2d55829d39/1711713362629/Lichtsuchende-1000x0-c-default.jpeg
- Project page: https://lumenprize.org/2019-winners/dave-murray-rust-rocio-von-jungenfeld

#### Plantoid — Primavera De Filippi (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: A blockchain can give a machine an economic life of its own, with humans as its pollinators.
- What it is: A metal robotic flower that dances and lights up when it receives cryptocurrency donations. When it has collected enough, it commissions artists to build its offspring, choosing among proposals by vote of its donors: a machine that owns and reproduces itself.
- How it works: A sculpture with sensors, lights and motors is linked to a smart contract on a blockchain that holds its funds and runs the voting for new plantoids (with Okhaos).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5gMbhCgHGjY

#### Kilobots: a thousand-robot swarm — Radhika Nagpal (2014)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A swarm of cheap, error-prone machines can still build a collective form, with errors absorbed by the group.
- What it is: 1,024 coin-sized robots on three wiry legs slowly assemble themselves into a star, a letter K and other shapes, using only local signals with their neighbours; traffic jams and stragglers are part of the result.
- How it works: Each Kilobot moves by vibration motors and communicates by infrared reflected off the table; a distributed algorithm uses edge-following, gradient formation and localisation (with Michael Rubenstein and Alejandro Cornejo).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1254295 (Science 2014)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G1t4M2XnIhI
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d9/Kilobot_robot_swarm.JPG

#### Swarm Study (series) — Random International (2010)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Collective motion rules alone can give light the feel of a living group that notices us.
- What it is: Lights in a grid of brass rods move like a flock of birds or a shoal of fish, gathering and scattering in response to the people below. Swarm Study / III (2011) is in the V&A collection.
- How it works: A flocking algorithm drives individually addressable lights on brass rods; sensors register visitors' positions and presence as disturbances to the swarm.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Victoria and Albert Museum, London (Swarm Study / III)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ajV8A5Y2_dE
- Project page: https://www.random-international.com/

#### Delicate Boundaries — Chris Sugrue (2007)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Computer vision
- Idea: Artificial life becomes unsettling when it leaves the frame and treats your body as terrain.
- What it is: Small glowing digital bugs swarm on a screen; when a visitor touches it, they crawl out of the screen onto the visitor's hand and arm and explore the body before returning.
- How it works: A camera tracks hands and arms touching the screen, and an overhead projector continues the flocking simulation on the body's surface.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: VIDA 10.0, Special Mention (2007)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QJ-uUnsFdxg

#### Propagaciones — Leandro Núñez (2007)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Embodying a cellular automaton in robots makes an abstract model of life into something that happens in the room.
- What it is: A grid of small robots turns on and off according to the rules of Conway's Game of Life, so patterns of 'living' and 'dying' cells propagate through a physical machine population.
- How it works: Each robot reads the states of its neighbours and updates its own light and movement following Game of Life rules; the whole grid runs without central control.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5BTa1c3Y6Fo
- Project page: https://www.leonunez.com.ar/

#### ALAVs 2.0 (Autonomous Light Air Vessels) — Jed Berk (2006)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Drones read differently when they behave like a gentle, needy flock than like tools.
- What it is: A flock of small helium blimps drifts through a space, avoiding walls, flocking with one another, approaching visitors and 'eating' when they run low; visitors can call them by mobile phone.
- How it works: Each vessel carries propellers, infrared and sonar sensors and a microcontroller running flocking and obstacle-avoidance behaviours, plus a phone interface for human messages.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: VIDA 10.0, Special Mention (2007); Taipei Digital Art Festival
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8CKrjCUMhdA

#### Parásitos Urbanos (Urban Parasites) — Gilberto Esparza (2006)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Treat the city's cables and waste as a habitat, and robots become a new wild species that lives off it.
- What it is: A family of small robots built from discarded electronics that hang on city power lines and walls, stealing electricity and making sounds like animals living in the urban ecosystem.
- How it works: Recycled motors, circuits and speakers are assembled into 'species' (with Latin names such as Furtum electricus) that tap live power lines and react to light and noise.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: VIDA 9.0, Incentive for Ibero-American Production (2006); Intermediae Madrid 2011; Fundación Telefónica Lima, Cultivos (2014)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X64KRaQpyCY
- Images: http://gilbertoesparza.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/COLGADO-Furtum-electricus-sinuatum-1024x683.jpg http://gilbertoesparza.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/DIABLITO-_-LITTLE-DEVIL-Furtum-electricus-imitor-1024x683.jpg
- Project page: https://gilbertoesparza.net/portfolio/parasitos-urbanos/

#### Resilient Machines Through Continuous Self-Modeling — Josh Bongard, Hod Lipson (2006)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A machine that models its own body can survive injury, a first step toward a kind of machine self-awareness.
- What it is: A four-legged 'starfish' robot does not know its own shape. It moves a little, builds competing models of its body, and uses them to learn to walk; when a leg is shortened, it notices the damage and invents a new gait.
- How it works: The robot uses tilt sensors and joint encoders to test action hypotheses and select among candidate self-models, then optimises locomotion on the best model (with Viktor Zykov).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Failure, glitch & error, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1133687 (Science 2006)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x579QKA6fkY

#### Proxemia (Proxemics) — Mariela Yeregui (2005)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Social distance and fear of touch can be staged as machine behaviour, making the visitor an obstacle in a robot community.
- What it is: Twenty-five glowing acrylic spheres roll freely across the floor; whenever one touches a visitor, another sphere or a wall it changes colour and veers away, as if phobic of contact. One transparent sphere, with its robot visible inside, behaves differently from the rest.
- How it works: Each 25 cm sphere contains a small robot with position and motion sensing, bump detection and its own lights; contact triggers a change of direction and light.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MEYvKy38x1o
- Images: https://marielayeregui.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/esferasx2-1024x683.jpg
- Project page: https://marielayeregui.com/proxemia-proxemics/

#### Self-reproducing machines (Molecubes) — Hod Lipson (2005)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Self-reproduction, long a defining trait of life, can be performed by simple modular machines given a supply of parts.
- What it is: A tower of four magnetically linked robotic cubes bends, picks up fresh cubes from feeding stations and stacks them into a copy of itself, in about two and a half minutes.
- How it works: Each 10 cm cube has a swivel joint, electromagnets on its faces and a microcontroller; a pre-programmed sequence moves cubes from feeders to build the replica (Cornell, with Victor Zykov, Efstathios Mytilinaios and Bryant Adams).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/435163a (Nature 2005)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gZwTcLeelAY

#### ArtSBots — Leonel Moura (2003)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Emergent machine collectives can produce 'non-human art' whose author is the swarm.
- What it is: A swarm of small wheeled robots with coloured pens moves over a large canvas, each reacting to colour left by the others, until a painting emerges that no one planned. In 2006 Moura's RAP (Robotic Action Painter) extended the idea to a single autonomous painter.
- How it works: Each robot has colour sensors, obstacle sensors and a microcontroller running stigmergy-like rules: it paints more where colour already is, as ants follow pheromones (with Henrique Garcia Pereira).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XlUxXQPmKUc
- Project page: https://www.leonelmoura.com/robot-art/

#### Autopoiesis — Ken Rinaldo (2000)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A group of machines that talk to each other develops a collective mood that no single arm contains.
- What it is: Fifteen robotic arms made of grapevine and electronics hang from the ceiling, sense visitors and bend toward them, and signal to each other with tones so that the group's behaviour shifts as a whole.
- How it works: Each arm has infrared sensors and a microcontroller; the arms share information through a central computer and audible tones, and a camera tracks visitors' positions.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Alien Intelligence, Kiasma, Helsinki 2000; VIDA 3.0, first prize; Prix Ars Electronica 2001, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9TfrKQH6OPg
- Images: https://www.kenrinaldo.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/Autopoieis3-440x450.jpg https://archive.aec.at/asset/1318971/preview/
- Project page: https://www.kenrinaldo.com/portfolio/autopoiesis/

#### Eden — Jon McCormack (2000)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Human attention becomes an ecological resource that artificial creatures evolve to capture.
- What it is: An evolving ecosystem of sonic creatures lives on a cellular world projected onto translucent screens. The creatures learn to sing, mate and find food; because visitors' presence makes food grow, creatures that attract people with their songs survive.
- How it works: Agents with learning classifier systems move on a lattice and generate sound; infrared sensors detect visitors and increase food in nearby cells.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Machine listening & voice, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yrww68pnqqM
- Images: https://i0.wp.com/jonmccormack.info/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Eden3.jpg?fit=1920%2C1280&ssl=1
- Project page: https://www.jonmccormack.info/artworks/eden/

#### Golem project — Hod Lipson (2000)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Machines can design and make their own bodies, with humans reduced to plugging in the motors.
- What it is: Computers evolved simple bar-and-actuator robots in simulation, selecting them for their ability to crawl, then 3D-printed them; after motors were added by hand, the physical 'lifeforms' crawled across the floor as in simulation.
- How it works: An evolutionary algorithm co-evolves morphology and neural control in a physics simulation; winning designs are fabricated by rapid prototyping (with Jordan Pollack, Brandeis University).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/35023115 (Nature 2000)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tgJcYx-yewA

#### Galápagos — Karl Sims (1997)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Aesthetic preference becomes a selection pressure, and the artist hands authorship to an evolutionary process.
- What it is: Twelve screens each show an abstract animated organism. Visitors stand on sensors in front of the ones they like; those survive, mate and mutate, while the others die, so the audience acts as natural selection.
- How it works: Twelve computers render organisms from genetic codes; step sensors in front of each screen register selections, and the chosen genotypes are copied, recombined and mutated.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: NTT InterCommunication Center (ICC), Tokyo 1997–2000
- Images: https://www.karlsims.com/galapagos/galapagos-icc.jpg https://www.karlsims.com/galapagos/image39.jpg
- Project page: https://www.karlsims.com/galapagos/index.html

#### Life Spacies — Christa Sommerer & Laurent Mignonneau (1997)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Language becomes DNA: what people write literally shapes the bodies of machine creatures.
- What it is: Visitors send text messages over the internet; each text is read as a genetic code that creates a unique artificial creature, which then lives, feeds on further text and reproduces in a shared online and gallery world.
- How it works: A text-to-form genetic algorithm translates characters and their order into body parameters; typed text also becomes food in the environment.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: NTT InterCommunication Center (ICC), Tokyo 1997
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-OXpk0PmMLc

#### Sympathetic Sentience — Simon Penny (1995)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A machine collective can have a life of its own that humans can only disturb, not control.
- What it is: Twelve small electronic units on the walls and ceiling of a dark room chirp and pass their rhythms to each other by infrared, so that a complex, never-repeating sound pattern builds up. Visitors walking through break the chain and the room slowly falls silent, then rebuilds its song.
- How it works: Each identical unit chirps once a minute and combines its own rhythm with the infrared data stream it receives before passing it on (with Jamieson Schulte).
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZX9Zta2T1do
- Project page: https://simonpenny.net/works/sympathetic.html

#### A-Volve — Christa Sommerer & Laurent Mignonneau (1994)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Artificial life becomes tangible when a drawn form has to survive in a shared environment with other creatures and human hands.
- What it is: Visitors draw a shape on a touch screen and it becomes a 3D creature swimming in a real pool of water. The creatures hunt, mate and die according to their form, and visitors can touch and protect them with their hands in the water.
- How it works: Drawings are converted into genetic code that sets each creature's shape and swimming ability; creatures are projected into a water-filled glass pool where cameras track visitors' hands.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 1994, Golden Nica (Interactive Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0WG45k93pCA
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/1390558/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/142357/

#### Evolved Virtual Creatures — Karl Sims (1994)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Evolution in simulation produces machine bodies no engineer would draw, strange yet obviously purposeful.
- What it is: Block-bodied creatures swim, walk, jump and fight over a cube in a physically simulated world. Both their bodies and their neural 'brains' were evolved by a genetic algorithm, not designed.
- How it works: Directed graphs encode morphology and neural controllers; populations are selected for swimming, walking, jumping, following or competition in a rigid-body physics simulation on a Connection Machine CM-5.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/192161.192167 (SIGGRAPH 1994)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RZtZia4ZkX8
- Images: http://www.karlsims.com/creatures-crab-vs-arm.jpg
- Project page: https://www.karlsims.com/evolved-virtual-creatures.html

#### Interactive Plant Growing — Christa Sommerer & Laurent Mignonneau (1992)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Living plants and virtual growth are coupled so that the garden grows only through human–plant contact.
- What it is: Visitors touch or approach five real plants, and each gesture makes virtual plants grow on a large projection; the living plants act as the interface to an artificial garden.
- How it works: The plants' electrical potential changes when touched are measured and translated into growth parameters for real-time 3D plant models.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: ZKM Karlsruhe collection
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JXX7JNFD2X8

#### Strandbeest — Theo Jansen (1990)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A machine without electronics can still evolve, sense and 'survive' in its own habitat.
- What it is: Large walking skeletons of PVC tubing that are powered by wind on Dutch beaches, store air in bottles, and in later generations sense water and turn back from the sea.
- How it works: Leg linkages with 'holy numbers' found by a computer-evolved algorithm convert wind-driven rotation into walking; plastic bottles act as air 'stomachs' and tubes as logic.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2005, special prize (Interactive Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C97kMKwZ2-g
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/1050599/preview/
- Project page: https://www.strandbeest.com/

#### Boids — Craig Reynolds (1987)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Collective life can emerge without a leader or plan, which changed how we imagine swarms of machines.
- What it is: Simulated 'bird-oid' agents flock, split around obstacles and regroup like real birds, although each follows only three local rules. The model was soon used for bats and penguins in films such as Batman Returns (1992).
- How it works: Each agent steers by separation, alignment and cohesion relative to nearby flockmates, computed in a 3D animation system.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/37401.37406 (SIGGRAPH 1987)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=86iQiV3-3IA
- Project page: https://www.red3d.com/cwr/boids/

### Industrial Arms & Choreography

Factory robots taken out of the factory: arms that dance, draw, labour or plead.

#### Manus — Madeline Gannon (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Computer vision
- Idea: Industrial robots can be designed as a social group with shared attention rather than as isolated tools.
- What it is: Ten industrial robot arms in a row share one perception system and behave as a pack, turning together to follow passers-by and passing attention along the line.
- How it works: Depth sensors at the base feed a single tracking system; each ABB arm chooses targets according to pack-behaviour rules.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: World Economic Forum Annual Meeting of the New Champions, Tianjin 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lyQwqi-Hycw
- Project page: https://atonaton.com/manus

#### The Punishment — Filipe Vilas-Boas (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Robot ethics as a schoolroom punishment asks whether rules can be learned by repetition, and who is really being disciplined.
- What it is: An industrial robot arm sits at a school desk and writes, over and over in neat handwriting, the line 'I must not hurt humans', like a child punished with lines.
- How it works: A small industrial arm holding a pen replays a handwriting trajectory on paper in an endless loop.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wA0zU2wC2dk
- Images: https://payload.cargocollective.com/1/19/638884/12653201/prt_1497962393_2x.jpg
- Project page: https://www.filipevilasboas.com/the-punishment

#### Mimus — Madeline Gannon (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Computer vision
- Idea: A factory robot given curiosity instead of a task is no longer a threat but a creature to meet.
- What it is: A 1,200 kg ABB industrial robot in a glass enclosure at the Design Museum in London notices visitors, follows the most interesting one and gets bored when they stay still, like a curious animal.
- How it works: Depth sensors in the ceiling track visitors; custom software (no pre-programmed movements) decides where the arm looks and moves in real time.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Fear and Love, Design Museum London 2016
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B9jwNWiEd_M
- Images: http://static1.squarespace.com/static/5758289d27d4bdf581e1c031/t/64386d617b6835253f5680cd/1681419617332/charlie-longexposure-2.jpg?format=1500w
- Project page: https://atonaton.com/mimus

#### Box — Bot & Dolly (2013)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Industrial robot arm
- Idea: When industrial arms move the stage, precision itself becomes the illusion, and the machine hides by performing perfectly.
- What it is: A live performance filmed in one take: two industrial robot arms move large screens while a performer interacts with projection-mapped illusions of depth, cubes and collapse. The arms are the invisible stagehands.
- How it works: Robot arms carrying projection surfaces are synchronised with projection mapping and a motion-control camera in Autodesk Maya-based choreography.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Opacity & latent space
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lX6JcybgDFo

#### Double-Taker (Snout) — Golan Levin (2008)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Computer vision
- Idea: Surveillance becomes eye contact: a machine gaze staged as curiosity makes people feel seen in a way a CCTV camera never does.
- What it is: A 2.5-metre industrial robot arm dressed as a giant inchworm or trunk sits on a roof above a museum entrance; it turns an oversized googly eye towards passers-by, tracks them and performs 'double-takes' as if surprised by each person.
- How it works: ABB industrial arm driven by a real-time machine-vision system that tracks bodies below and triggers expressive 'double-take' motions.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2009, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jXqYf4m-HA8
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/327892/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/327893/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/327894/preview/
- Project page: https://www.flong.com/archive/projects/snout/index.html

#### SEEK — Architecture Machine Group (MIT) (1970)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A machine that manages a world for its inhabitants has to guess what they want, and the inhabitants keep proving its model wrong.
- What it is: Inside a glass enclosure, a computer-driven electromagnet on a gantry stacks and straightens small metal cubes while a colony of gerbils keeps knocking them over; the machine tries to keep its 'city' in order and to adjust its model to the changes the animals make. At the Jewish Museum the system kept breaking down and the gerbils fought each other.
- How it works: A small computer drives a gantry robot with an electromagnet end-effector and pressure sensors over a field of metal-plated blocks, compares the scene with a stored 3D plan and restacks or realigns blocks; built by Nicholas Negroponte's Architecture Machine Group at MIT.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: Software — Information Technology: Its New Meaning for Art, Jewish Museum, New York, 1970
- Images: https://cyberneticzoo.com/wp-content/uploads/Seek_p3-x640.jpg https://cyberneticzoo.com/wp-content/uploads/gerbs-x640.jpg
- Project page: https://cyberneticzoo.com/?p=3794

### Androids & the Uncanny

Humanlike machines and the unease of near-likeness.

#### Cutting Open IRON — XPeng (2025)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: The uncanny test runs in reverse: the robot moved so well that it had to be opened up to prove it was not a person in a suit.
- What it is: After XPeng unveiled its 'female' humanoid IRON in November 2025, its human-like gait led many viewers to claim a person was inside; days later, at a car launch in Guangzhou, CEO He Xiaopeng had a technician cut open the robot's leg on stage while it stayed powered on, exposing actuators and wiring.
- How it works: IRON has an internal lattice of artificial muscles and joints under a soft covering; the leg was cut open live for about three minutes, after XPeng had released unedited footage of the internal structure.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m_Ag_SgsHVg
- Images: https://assets.newatlas.com/dims4/default/01e1e63/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1766x927+0+145/resize/1200x630!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewatlas-brightspot.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com%2Ff9%2F9a%2F3dedff18431fad5bc142bebdbd96%2Fscreenshot-2025-11-18-at-3-40-16-pm.png&na.image_optimisation=0
- Project page: https://newatlas.com/ai-humanoids/watch-iron-humanoid/

#### Emo — Yuhang Hu, Hod Lipson (2024)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Humanoid & android, Computer vision
- Idea: Timing makes the feeling: mimicry that lags looks fake, while a face that anticipates your expression reads as genuine.
- What it is: A blue-skinned humanoid robot face from Columbia's Creative Machines Lab that watches a person's face and smiles at the same moment they do, predicting a smile about 0.84 seconds before it appears.
- How it works: Soft silicone face driven by 26 actuators with cameras in the eyes; one model learns the robot's own motor-to-expression mapping through self-modelling, another predicts a person's coming expression from subtle early changes in their face.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1126/scirobotics.adi4724 (Science Robotics, 2024)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pWTTzR_wXuQ
- Images: https://www.creativemachineslab.com/uploads/6/9/3/4/69340277/emo.jpg
- Project page: https://www.creativemachineslab.com/

#### Requiem for an Exit — Frode Oldereid & Thomas Kvam (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: The machine voices the conscience that people hand over to bureaucracies and algorithms, and its tired hydraulic body makes the line 'what we delegate, we do not escape' land as weight rather than argument.
- What it is: A robot head almost four metres high, on a steel and hydraulic exoskeleton, with a hyper-real ageing face projected onto its skin, turns and sinks while an AI-generated baritone delivers a monologue on genocide through history and on who is responsible for it.
- How it works: Industrial hydraulics move a sculpted head mapped with a CGI-animated face; the monologue was developed with large-language-model scripting and spoken by a generative AI voice, with a low, constant site-responsive soundscape.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Meta.Morf Biennale 2024, Trondheim (co-production with TEKS); Prix Ars Electronica 2025, Golden Nica (New Animation Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uNj0bAAmVyA
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6780f6831a26627e750dd6ef/3b3f2394-c81c-4f08-8a20-c0b584566d02/Kvam+robot.jpg https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6780f6831a26627e750dd6ef/7d803604-3fd9-47b1-9cb7-0166daeaf3e0/Halden+2024_DSC6720+small.jpg
- Project page: https://oldereid-kvam.com/

#### Ameca — Engineered Arts (2021)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Humanoid & android, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Its viral clips show how much feeling people read into a machine face, even when they know the expression is programmed.
- What it is: A grey-skinned, deliberately genderless humanoid robot whose first video, waking up and looking at its own hands with surprise, went viral; it is now shown at fairs and museums, often talking through a large language model.
- How it works: A modular humanoid platform with dozens of facial actuators, cameras in the eyes and cloud software for animation and conversation.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IPukuYb9xWw
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5e/Ameca_Generation_1.jpg
- Project page: https://www.engineeredarts.co.uk/robot/ameca/

#### Annelies, Looking for Completion — L.A. Raeven (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Instead of a robot that serves us, a robot that needs us, and the discomfort of comforting a machine.
- What it is: A lifelike android clone of the twin artists, a 'third sister', sits crying in a corner; when visitors try to comfort her she looks up with a tear-streaked face.
- How it works: Silicone android modelled on the artists' faces and bodies, with motorised facial expressions, tear mechanism and sensors reacting to approach.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Robot Love, Eindhoven 2018; Collection Bonnefanten, Maastricht
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jyfq-xq5GyA
- Project page: https://robotlove.nl/en/expo/

#### ORLAN-OÏDE — ORLAN (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: An artist famous for remaking her body builds a machine self and lets it speak in her place.
- What it is: A humanoid robot double of the artist, with her face and voice, that answers questions and speaks about art; ORLAN has interviewed it in public.
- How it works: Robotic bust with a conversational AI trained on the artist's texts and a synthesised copy of her voice; later versions developed with RaspiAudio.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: Artistes & Robots, Grand Palais, Paris 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uSeo1wMvG_g
- Project page: https://www.orlan.eu/

#### SEER: Simulative Emotional Expression Robot — Takayuki Todo (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Computer vision
- Idea: Being looked back at by a machine is enough to feel that something is there.
- What it is: A small, stylised humanoid head that tracks the viewer's gaze and mirrors their facial expression with subtle eye, eyelid and eyebrow movements.
- How it works: A camera with face and gaze tracking drives motors in the eyes and eyelids and wire-driven, flexible eyebrows; the face is deliberately not realistic.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Machine seeing
- Shown at: Ars Electronica 2018; Laval Virtual 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BJZcGJSK1Z0
- Project page: https://www.takayukitodo.com/

#### Alter — Takashi Ikegami, Hiroshi Ishiguro (2016)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Humanoid & android, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Spontaneity, not realism, is what makes a machine feel alive.
- What it is: An android with a human face and an exposed mechanical body that moves on its own: its gestures come from an artificial-life neural network reacting to sensors, not from a script.
- How it works: About 40 pneumatic axes driven by central pattern generators and a spiking neural network fed by proximity, noise and temperature sensors; Alter3 (2019) added cameras and later GPT-4 control.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Miraikan, Tokyo 2016; Prix Ars Electronica 2018, Interactive Art+; AI: More than Human, Barbican 2019 (Alter 3)
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1162/isal_a_00463 (ALIFE 2021)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iYzOZQDsm5w
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takashi_Ikegami

#### Sophia — Hanson Robotics (2016)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Humanoid & android, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A robot staged as a person shows how easily personhood is granted to a performance.
- What it is: A female-presenting humanoid robot with an expressive face that appeared on talk shows and at the UN; in 2017 Saudi Arabia announced it had granted Sophia citizenship. Roboticists criticised the scripted appearances as misleading about AI.
- How it works: Animatronic face in Frubber skin with motors and cameras, combined with scripted and chatbot dialogue.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: SXSW 2016; Future Investment Initiative, Riyadh 2017; AI for Good Global Summit 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sKrV2CVDXjo
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1e/Sophia_at_the_AI_for_Good_Global_Summit_2018_%2827254369347%29_%28cropped%29.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophia_(robot)

#### (Female figure) — Jordan Wolfson (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Computer vision
- Idea: Eye contact from a machine turns looking into being looked at, and makes the viewer complicit in a sexualised display.
- What it is: A life-size animatronic woman in a witch mask, bikini and dirty boots dances seductively against a mirror, then looks the viewer in the eye while speaking in the artist's voice.
- How it works: An animatronic figure built with Spectral Motion runs choreographed routines; facial-recognition cameras let it lock eyes with viewers.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: David Zwirner, New York 2014
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XSFP6JHnn9c
- Project page: https://www.davidzwirner.com/artists/jordan-wolfson

#### Affetto — Hisashi Ishihara, Minoru Asada (2011)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Developmental robotics builds a baby to study care: the robot's task is to be looked after, and its realism tests how far caregiving extends to machines.
- What it is: A realistic android child, first a head (2011) and later a pneumatic upper body, built at Osaka University to study how caregivers respond to an infant's face and movements; its soft skin and moving face made it one of the most discussed uncanny robots.
- How it works: Pneumatic actuators under soft silicone skin move the face and, from 2015, a 22-degree-of-freedom upper body; a 2018 study measured and redesigned its facial surface motions.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: IEEE ICDL 2011, Frankfurt; Miraikan, Tokyo 2026
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/devlrn.2011.6037346 (IEEE ICDL 2011)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nHWimp9uvfo
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1109/devlrn.2011.6037346

#### The Man Machine — Vincent Fournier (2010)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Social & companion robot
- Idea: Portraiture, a genre for persons, applied to machines makes us ask what in them looks back.
- What it is: A photographic series of real humanoid robots, including ASIMO and REEM-B, posed in laboratories, homes and landscapes with the stillness of formal portraits.
- How it works: Staged large-format colour photographs made on location with robotics labs in Japan, Europe and the US.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Hello, Robot., Vitra Design Museum 2017
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JUhIQo6PvQo
- Project page: https://www.vincentfournier.co.uk/

#### Dirk, the homeless robot — Electric Circus (2008)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: People will extend pity or unease to a machine before deciding whether it is alive; the android tests how we treat those at the edge of the street.
- What it is: A lifelike animatronic 'homeless man' that sits and moves on streets and at festivals; passers-by talk to him, give him money or recoil before realising he is a machine.
- How it works: Animatronic figure built by inventor Fred Abels and puppeteer Mirjam Langemeijer, with moving head, eyes and hands, operated in public space.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2010, Honorary Mention (Hybrid Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cwX6CuUyeFw
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/452494/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/452495/preview/
- Project page: http://www.electric-circus.eu

#### Geminoid HI-1 — Hiroshi Ishiguro (2006)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: When a copy stands in for its maker, people start to ask where the 'person' actually is.
- What it is: A teleoperated android copy of Hiroshi Ishiguro, built with silicone skin and pneumatic actuators; Ishiguro sends it to give lectures while he speaks through it from elsewhere.
- How it works: An operator's voice and lip and head movements, captured by camera and microphone, drive about 50 air actuators in the android; small idle motions run automatically.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Ars Electronica 2009
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.5772/4876 (Humanoid Robots: New Developments (I-Tech), 2007)

#### JoAn, l'home de carn — Marcel·lí Antúnez Roca (1992)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A machine clad in flesh shows that the uncanny comes as much from the audience's laughter and barking dogs as from the robot.
- What it is: A life-size seated male robot covered in sewn pig skin sits in a glass case and moves its neck, shoulder, elbow and penis whenever visitors speak, sing, whistle or clap near it.
- How it works: Computer analyses the sound in the room and sends signals to motors at four joints of a mechanically articulated figure.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Machine listening & voice
- Images: https://www.marceliantunez.com/media/cache/07/7c/077c994ce12858786f4a25a749c0ba02.jpg
- Project page: https://www.marceliantunez.com/work/joan-lhome-de-carn/

#### ROSA BOSOM — Bruce Lacey (1965)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: A deliberately crude android shows how much of the robot fantasy is gender, theatre and a remote control.
- What it is: A clanking, junk-built 'female' robot actress on wheels whose name spells Radio Operated Simulated Actress Battery Or Standby Operated Mains. At Cybernetic Serendipity she was shown with her partner MATE, parodying the dream of the machine woman.
- How it works: Radio-controlled motors move a body assembled from scrap, domestic objects and mannequin parts; it runs on batteries or mains power as the name says.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: Cybernetic Serendipity, ICA London 1968
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nTMNiYV5yIE
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Lacey

#### The Writer — Pierre Jaquet-Droz (1774)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: An 18th-century android already raised the question of writing without a mind behind it.
- What it is: A doll-sized boy at a desk dips a goose quill in ink and writes a text of up to 40 characters, following the letters with his eyes. It is still demonstrated at the Musée d'art et d'histoire in Neuchâtel.
- How it works: About 6,000 parts, with a programmable wheel of interchangeable cams that sets each letter; made with Henri-Louis Jaquet-Droz and Jean-Frédéric Leschot.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Musée d'art et d'histoire, Neuchâtel
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ux2KW20nqHU
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaquet-Droz_automata

### Robotic Sculpture & Kinetic Installation

Autonomous robotic sculptures and machine installations that behave in a space with visitors.

#### Guanaquerx — Paula Gaetano Adi (2025)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: Robotics can be rooted in local, Andean knowledge and landscape rather than in Silicon Valley's image of the machine.
- What it is: An autonomous rover built with artisans and amateur mechanics in San Juan, Argentina, crosses the Andes toward Chile, re-enacting José de San Martín's 1817 independence expedition as a multi-day performance.
- How it works: An all-terrain rover inspired by local 'guanaqueras' (home-built off-road vehicles) navigates mountain terrain autonomously, with community workshops as part of the work.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2025, Golden Nica (Artificial Life & Intelligence)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TRGilwpKi-I
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/3849576/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/303077/

#### MirrorBot — Serena Ge Guo (2025)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A robot can be a social instrument rather than a social partner: by bending sightlines it stages the first eye contact between people instead of asking for attention itself.
- What it is: A soft, four-foot mobile robot carrying two actuated mirrors. Placed in front of two strangers in a waiting room, it angles the mirrors so each sees themself in one and the other person in the other, prompting first glances, smiles and conversation.
- How it works: Mobile base with two motorised mirrors, teleoperated (Wizard of Oz) through preset mirror positions; studied with 16 stranger pairs and analysed for icebreaking, synchrony, avoidance and the roles people gave the robot (mediator, observer, magnifier, disrupter).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: CHI 2025 Interactivity, Yokohama; HRI 2026 Best Paper (Design Track), Edinburgh
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3757279.3785647 (HRI 2026)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=97qIaLC5hNM
- Images: https://news.cornell.edu/sites/default/files/styles/full_width/public/2026-04/mirrorbot_teaser_image_with_2_people.jpg?itok=HM4s14xr https://news.cornell.edu/sites/default/files/styles/story_thumbnail_lg/public/2026-04/0402_microbot_tnd.jpg?itok=Jx8Oiu4f
- Project page: https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2026/04/mirrorbot-fostering-human-connection

#### Little Ark — Choe U-Ram (2022)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A machine that rows without going anywhere becomes an image of collective paralysis.
- What it is: A large kinetic ark made of scrap cardboard boxes and steel whose oars open and close in a slow choreographed cycle, surrounded by other machine creatures. Shown in the MMCA Hyundai Motor Series, it stages a society adrift.
- How it works: Motorised steel structure with cardboard skins and programmed motion; built and tested in a temporary workshop before installation.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: MMCA Hyundai Motor Series 2022: Choe U-Ram – Little Ark, MMCA Seoul 2022–23
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zKHfM4PUZ7k
- Project page: https://www.uram.net/

#### πTon — Cod.Act (2017)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: When sound comes from the contortions of a soft machine body, the machine seems to sing its own effort.
- What it is: A huge ring of rubbery tube lies on the floor and writhes, twists and contracts like a living creature; its convulsions produce a vocal, choral sound.
- How it works: Internal motors and cables deform the elastic tube; its movement data are transformed in real time into a vocal soundscape.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine listening & voice
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fB1kI5EGzqY
- Images: https://codact.ch/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/PiTon230518SC-09.jpg
- Project page: https://codact.ch/

#### Mother of Machine: NoodleFeet — Sarah Petkus (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A robot built without a use case invites a different relation: care and curiosity instead of service.
- What it is: NoodleFeet is an 'adolescent' robot with pool-noodle feet that walks, tastes the ground and grabs objects; its maker describes the ongoing build as raising a child who should develop its own ways of reacting to the world.
- How it works: Legged robot of light metals, 3D-printed parts and found objects with sensors on feet and 'tongue' that trigger behaviours; hardware and code are rebuilt iteratively.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2018, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art+)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lbf6xV47L8I
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/2567402/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/2567404/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/2567408/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/236785/

#### Study for Fifteen Points / I — Random International (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Fifteen moving points are enough for us to see a human; the machine exploits our perception of biological motion.
- What it is: Fifteen points of light on mechanical rods move so that, together, they are instantly seen as a person walking, although there is no body, only machinery.
- How it works: Motors move fifteen lights along rods to reproduce a point-light walker, developed after a residency at Harvard's School of Engineering and Applied Sciences.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine seeing, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qnkxo7CWACs
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/663ca532b3e3797d82159fe2/0d90a48e-3f33-4c69-b508-9cbc6a607893/STUDY+FOR+FIFTEEN+POINTS+%3A+I%2C+2016++.jpeg
- Project page: https://www.random-international.com/study-for-fifteen-points

#### Jller — Benjamin Maus, Prokop Bartoníček (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Computer vision can be slow and contemplative: a machine reading deep time.
- What it is: An industrial machine picks up stones collected from the Iller river in southern Germany one by one, photographs them and lays them out in rows by geological age.
- How it works: Gantry robot with vacuum gripper and camera; image features (likely colour, texture and veining) classify each stone by geological origin, trained on stones labelled by the artists.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Machine seeing
- Images: https://media.wired.com/photos/5926f95bcfe0d93c47431f8b/191:100/w_1280,c_limit/RockRobot-1.jpg
- Project page: http://www.prokopbartonicek.com/jller-ignorance-with-benjamin-maus-2015

#### Mirage — Ralf Baecker (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A learning machine can dream of a world it senses but never sees, and we see only its hallucination.
- What it is: A laser line reflected off a thin, trembling mirror sheet projects a slowly shifting landscape on the wall, the 'dream' of a neural network fed by the Earth's magnetic field.
- How it works: A fluxgate magnetometer feeds an unsupervised learning algorithm modelled on the Helmholtz machine; its generated variations drive 48 muscle wires that deform the mirror.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2015, Honorary Mention (Hybrid Art); ACT Festival, Asia Culture Center, Gwangju 2015
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VY1hOjWlVO8
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/1882015/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/212751/

#### Nyloïd — Cod.Act (2013)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
