- Idea: A machine without head or face can still read as a creature through tension, torsion and voice.
- What it is: A tall tripod creature with long, nylon-sheathed legs twists, whips and folds in a performance, emitting a strange voice as its limbs torque and release.
- How it works: Motors twist the three flexible legs to store and release elastic energy; a sound system turns the movement into vocal sound.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Sónar, Barcelona; FutureEverything, Manchester
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f2sMD73fdYM
- Images: https://codact.ch/wp-content/uploads/2013/10/Nyl-18-Copie.jpg
- Project page: https://codact.ch/

#### Pinokio — Adam Ben-Dror (2012)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Social & companion robot, Computer vision
- Idea: A familiar object gains a personality through a few behaviours: attention, boredom and refusal to be switched off.
- What it is: A desk lamp watches people with a camera in its head, follows their faces, grows bored, looks around and dances to sounds; if someone switches it off, it switches itself back on.
- How it works: A webcam and face tracking in Processing/OpenCV drive six servo motors through an Arduino (with Shanshan Zhou and Joss Doggett).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine seeing
- Shown at: VIDA 16.0 (Fundación Telefónica), 2014
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1E_hHr6YuFk

#### Irrational Computing — Ralf Baecker (2011)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Showing the minerals under every microchip makes computation a material, geological process again.
- What it is: Five linked modules of raw crystals, minerals and electrodes form a primitive, enlarged signal processor: silicon carbide flickers like a display, quartz resonates and data pulses visibly between the stations.
- How it works: Crystals from nature, industrial waste or lab growth are used as semiconductors, oscillators and light emitters, wired into a feedback network.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2012, Honorary Mention (Hybrid Art); VIDA 14.0, second prize
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rwR_ofkPFnk
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/1530041/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/194180/

#### The Tiller Girls — Louis-Philippe Demers (2010)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Robots performing the human ideal of mechanical synchrony turn the old comparison of dancers to machines back on itself.
- What it is: A chorus line of identical, faceless robots rock, tilt and teeter together on rounded bases, performing a mechanical cabaret named after the 1920s precision-dance troupe that critics compared to machines.
- How it works: Weighted, round-bottomed robotic bodies are rocked by internal actuators under central control, with lighting and sound (developed with Armin Purkrabek and Phillip Schulze).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: ELEKTRA, Montreal; Bains numériques, Enghien-les-Bains
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PjLfb97T7iQ

#### Zwischenräume — Petra Gemeinboeck, Rob Saunders (2010)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Computer vision
- Idea: Curious machines living inside the architecture turn the gallery wall into a boundary between two worlds that watch each other.
- What it is: Robots hidden inside the gallery's walls punch and scratch small holes through the plasterboard, look out with cameras and follow visitors through the gaps, slowly reshaping the architecture.
- How it works: Wall-mounted robotic agents with camera vision run custom curiosity-driven AI software that rewards novel perceptions; they punch and scrape through the plasterboard.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: National New Media Art Award, Gallery of Modern Art (QAGOMA), Brisbane 2012
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rbDT3tMQL-I

#### 216 prepared dc-motors, filler wire 1.0mm — Zimoun (2009)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Many identical machines with tiny irregularities produce something that feels natural rather than mechanical.
- What it is: 216 small DC motors mounted in a grid on a wall each spin a short piece of wire that taps the wall, filling the room with a dense, rustling sound like rain or insects.
- How it works: Each motor runs at constant speed; variations in mounting and wire length create a complex, non-repeating texture.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cd7tkWq3LZU
- Project page: https://www.zimoun.net/

#### Old Persons Home — Sun Yuan & Peng Yu (2007)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: When bodies of power are handed to automated wheelchairs, aimless machine motion becomes an image of senility and lost control.
- What it is: Thirteen hyperreal, frail old men resembling world leaders sit in motorised wheelchairs that drift slowly around the gallery, bumping into each other and into visitors.
- How it works: Silicone and fibreglass figures on electric wheelchairs driven by motors with obstacle sensors and randomised paths (likely).
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: The Revolution Continues: New Art from China, Saatchi Gallery 2008
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FoM9RzzaB4Y
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/eb/Old_persons_home_by_Sun_Yuan_and_Peng_Yu.jpg https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/42/Old_Person%27s_Home%2C_Saatchi_Gallery%2C_London.jpg/1280px-Old_Person%27s_Home%2C_Saatchi_Gallery%2C_London.jpg
- Project page: https://www.galleriacontinua.com/artists/sun-yuan-peng-yu-73

#### Performative Ecologies — Ruairi Glynn (2007)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Computer vision
- Idea: A robot that optimises for our attention learns to overact, like any performer, or any feed.
- What it is: Hanging robotic 'dancers' with a camera head and a glowing tail try out gestures on visitors, keep the moves that hold people's attention, and trade successful routines with each other.
- How it works: Face detection estimates attentiveness, and a genetic algorithm scores and evolves each robot's movement repertoire, sharing fit behaviours over a wireless network.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine seeing
- Shown at: VIDA 11.0, Second Prize (2008)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xvKLU2jYLaw
- Images: https://www.ruairiglynn.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/pe-1.jpg https://www.ruairiglynn.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/pe-2.jpg
- Project page: https://ruairiglynn.co.uk/portfolio/performative-ecologies/

#### Rechnender Raum — Ralf Baecker (2007)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Rebuilding computation at human scale and with slow materials opens the black box of the digital.
- What it is: A large, delicate structure of sticks, strings, weights and small motors computes in front of the viewer: a mechanical cellular automaton whose logic states can be seen as moving threads.
- How it works: Servo motors pull strings that set the state of each cell in a ring of mechanical logic elements, following Konrad Zuse's idea of a 'calculating space'.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GgxG2aINTKU
- Project page: https://rlfbckr.io/project/rechnender-raum/

#### The Robotic Church — Chico MacMurtrie (2006)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A congregation of machines performing ritual asks what devotion looks like when the performers have no belief.
- What it is: In a 19th-century former church in Brooklyn, some thirty-five pneumatic robots, drummers, singers and anthropomorphic figures, perform a mechanical oratorio of rhythm and breath for a seated congregation.
- How it works: Pneumatic cylinders and valves driven by a central computer and compressors animate the robots' limbs, lungs and instruments in composed sequences.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LwRXDUsmaE4
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57acb395e58c62449d47f5ab/1472520986872-YA0RQ7R7FU3967ICEK4F/Chico_Church.jpg
- Project page: http://www.amorphicrobotworks.org/the-robotic-church

#### bit.fall — Julius Popp (2005)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: The news stream becomes a machine output that exists only for a second: information as falling matter.
- What it is: A row of nozzles releases precisely timed drops of water so that words, taken live from online news, appear for a moment as falling letters and dissolve.
- How it works: A computer selects frequent words from news feeds and converts them to bitmaps; magnetic valves on a row of nozzles release water drops line by line.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: London 2012 Olympic Park; MONA, Hobart
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gg9LWsfqqrk
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Popp

#### Petit Mal — Simon Penny (1993)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A deliberately non-anthropomorphic robot shows that personality can live in motion alone, and that its wobble is part of its charm.
- What it is: A waist-high robot of two bicycle wheels and nested aluminium pendulums rolls around a gallery on its own, approaches visitors, follows them and wobbles away. It looks like no animal or person, so its behaviour is the only thing to relate to.
- How it works: Ultrasonic and pyroelectric body-heat sensors, an accelerometer and two encoded motors are run by a single Motorola 68HC11 microcontroller; the double pendulum adds physical unpredictability.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Shown internationally 1995–1997; transmediale, Berlin 2006
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fxdUiE9vYx4
- Images: https://simonpenny.net/works/petitmal_files/petit_mal_2_wm_med.jpg
- Project page: https://simonpenny.net/works/petitmal.html

#### Family of Robot — Nam June Paik (1986)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Old media machines are given kinship roles, so obsolete technology becomes a genealogy.
- What it is: A series of robot figures built from vintage radios and television cabinets, cast as a family: Grandfather, Grandmother, Mother, Father, Aunt, Uncle and Baby, each showing video on its screens.
- How it works: Assemblages of antique TV and radio housings with working monitors playing Paik's video footage.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Carl Solway Gallery, Cincinnati 1986; Nam June Paik: Becoming Robot, Asia Society 2014
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yAV9p5ebEKM
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nam_June_Paik

#### Floats — Robert Breer (1965)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: At machine slowness, a minimal object becomes a presence you only notice when it has already moved.
- What it is: Large, plain dome-like sculptures glide over the floor so slowly that their movement is almost invisible, change direction when they bump into a wall or a person, and drift on. Seven of them roamed the Pepsi Pavilion at Expo '70 in Osaka.
- How it works: Battery-powered motors on hidden wheels drive each shell at a few centimetres per minute; a bumper switch reverses or turns the drive on contact.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Pepsi Pavilion, Expo '70, Osaka 1970; Museum Tinguely, Basel 2011
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=obFl4BvWw1I
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Breer

### Misbehaving Machines: Failure, Futility & Suffering

Machines that break, labour in vain, suffer, plead or get hurt, and in doing so show themselves.

#### Humanoid Robot Half-Marathon — Beijing E-Town (2025)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: A race makes the gap between robot demos and robot endurance public: falling is part of the spectacle.
- What it is: Twenty-one humanoid robots ran 21 km alongside thousands of human runners in Beijing; many fell, overheated or needed handlers, and the winner, Tiangong Ultra, finished in 2 h 40 min.
- How it works: Robots from Chinese companies and labs ran a separated lane with battery swaps and human 'pacers' holding remote controls or tethers.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=08YiK6VJxZs
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing_E-Town_Half-Marathon

#### No Bird — UJOO+LIMHEEYOUNG (2025)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: An automated loop without accumulation: the walker acts but changes nothing, like human action in a system that only needs to keep running normally.
- What it is: A bird-like walking machine paces across a bed of sand while a second machine follows and wipes out its tracks, returning the sand to its starting state again and again.
- How it works: Two custom kinetic machines, a legged walker following a fixed algorithmic gait and a trace-erasing machine that resets the sand; the starting point is the extinction of flightless birds.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2026, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art+)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sgRFfaVz2X8
- Images: https://ars.electronica.art/prix/files/2026/06/nobird.jpg
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/319445/

#### Dynamics of a Dog on a Leash — Takayuki Todo (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Held back only by a 'chain of ethics', the machine's struggle and collapse read as the suffering and death of an animal.
- What it is: A four-legged robot dog chained to the floor lunges at visitors behind a KEEP OUT line, thrashes, falls and gets up again until it overheats and lies still.
- How it works: A commercial quadruped robot runs an attack-and-escape behaviour against a fixed chain; the performance ends when motors overheat.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2025, Honorary Mention (Artificial Life & Intelligence); Ars Electronica Festival 2025
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y5jYFLDJWao
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/3837308/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/3837309/preview/
- Project page: http://www.takayukitodo.com/

#### K5 security robot falls into a fountain — Knightscope (2017)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: When a surveillance machine fails in public, mockery becomes a small act of relief from being watched.
- What it is: In July 2017 a Knightscope K5 security robot patrolling an office complex in Washington, D.C., rolled down steps into a fountain. Photos of the 'drowned' robot spread online as a joke about a robot 'committing suicide'.
- How it works: The K5 navigates with lidar, cameras and GPS; it failed to detect the edge of the steps.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9EoPoZAHxjI
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/cd/KnightScope_K5_robot.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knightscope

#### Can't Help Myself — Sun Yuan & Peng Yu (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Computer vision
- Idea: A machine assigned an impossible task of containment reads as exhausted and trapped, and viewers mourned it when it stopped.
- What it is: A KUKA industrial robot inside a glass enclosure tries without end to keep a spreading pool of blood-red fluid inside a boundary, sweeping it back with a squeegee and performing small 'dances' in between.
- How it works: A KUKA arm with visual-recognition sensors tracks the fluid's edge and is programmed with sweeping routines and gestural 'dance' sequences.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Tales of Our Time, Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum 2016; 58th Venice Biennale 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jRjrI42WsH4
- Images: https://www.guggenheim.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/2016.40_ph_web_2.jpg https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Can%27t_Help_Myself_Robot_05.jpg/1280px-Can%27t_Help_Myself_Robot_05.jpg
- Project page: https://www.guggenheim.org/artwork/34812

#### Colored sculpture — Jordan Wolfson (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Watching a machine perform violence on a figure that looks back makes spectatorship feel like complicity.
- What it is: A large cartoonish marionette of a red-haired boy hangs from chains that lift, swing and slam it violently against the floor, while its eyes track the audience.
- How it works: An industrial chain hoist system with programmed choreography moves the figure; eye-tracking animatronic eyes follow viewers.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Failure, glitch & error, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: David Zwirner, London 2016
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gsla5fbzhpw
- Project page: https://www.davidzwirner.com/artists/jordan-wolfson

#### Shitty robots — Simone Giertz (2016)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Designing for failure turns the automation promise into comedy and makes the machine lovable instead of threatening.
- What it is: In a series of YouTube videos, a breakfast machine slops milk and cereal over her face, a lipstick robot smears her mouth and a haircutting machine hacks at her hair: robots that do everyday tasks badly on purpose.
- How it works: Simple hobby servos, arms and household objects driven by Arduino-type controllers, with no sensing of the user.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E2evC2xTNWg
- Project page: https://www.simonegiertz.com/

#### Introducing Spot (the kicking video) — Boston Dynamics (2015)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A stumble is enough for empathy: a machine body that recovers like an animal makes kicking it look like cruelty.
- What it is: A promotional video shows the dog-sized quadruped Spot walking, climbing stairs and being kicked by engineers to show that it can recover its balance. Many viewers and news outlets reacted with outrage and asked whether it is wrong to kick a robot.
- How it works: Hydraulic legs controlled by dynamic balance algorithms; the kicks were a robustness test staged for the camera.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M8YjvHYbZ9w
- Project page: https://bostondynamics.com/

#### Robots falling at the DARPA Robotics Challenge — DARPA (2015)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: The slow collapse of a heavy humanoid shows how far the imagined robot is from the real one, and makes failure endearing.
- What it is: At the 2015 DARPA Robotics Challenge finals, humanoid robots built for disaster response tried to drive, open doors and climb stairs, and many slowly toppled over. A compilation of the falls by IEEE Spectrum became one of the most-watched robot videos.
- How it works: Teams of university and company engineers teleoperated or semi-autonomously controlled robots such as Atlas through a course simulating the Fukushima disaster, under degraded communication.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g0TaYhjpOfo
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA_Robotics_Challenge

#### D.W.I: Clones — Félix Luque Sánchez (2013)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Industrial robot arm
- Idea: A textbook control problem, made heavy and repeated, starts to look like effort: we read will into a feedback loop.
- What it is: Two identical human-sized inverted pendulums ride on motorised carts; each swings until it tips upright, then an algorithm takes over and tries, again and again, to hold it balanced against gravity, failing and succeeding in turns.
- How it works: Inverted pendulums of epoxy foam on horizontally moving carts, with encoders, motor controllers and fuzzy-logic control that swings the pendulum up and balances it.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: BIAN, Montréal 2014; Creative Machine, Taikang Art Museum, Beijing 2024–25
- Video: https://vimeo.com/170764351
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/w/1200/i/e18dbfb306c8c1b82f44a9633b51bba87b4a042dc5493e3d19d0ee9b1356c0c4/DWI_1.jpg https://freight.cargo.site/t/original/i/14f84eee0a0ea71b682223cec9d583aa6a004939e0ffe2e54fa743eb4d9a1502/DWI_2.jpg
- Project page: https://felixluque.com/D-W-I-Clones

#### DSM-VI — Bill Vorn (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Diagnosing machines as mad shows how much we already read machine behaviour through psychology.
- What it is: A 'psychiatric ward' of robots, each staging a mental disorder such as paranoia, depression, psychosis or obsessive behaviour, twitches, hides or repeats itself as visitors walk through. The title parodies the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders.
- How it works: Robotic structures with pneumatic and electric actuators, sensors and sound are programmed with behaviour patterns derived from the DSM's descriptions of symptoms.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Alterity & the uncanny, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YC3BiEr0aCk
- Images: https://billvorn.concordia.ca/robography/images/DSM01.jpg
- Project page: https://billvorn.concordia.ca/robography/DSM.html

#### Senseless Drawing Bot — So Kanno, Takahiro Yamaguchi (yang02) (2011)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Marks that look expressive can come from pure mechanical chaos, which questions the intention we read into graffiti.
- What it is: A self-propelled robot with a double pendulum on top rolls along a wall and sprays paint, producing graffiti-like strokes with no intention behind them.
- How it works: A motorised cart moves back and forth while a chaotic double pendulum swings a spray can triggered by a servo.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: 15th Japan Media Arts Festival, New Face Award 2012; Artistes & Robots, Grand Palais 2018; Beijing Media Art Biennale 2018
- Video: https://vimeo.com/30780208
- Images: https://www.kanno.so/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/MG_7243-2.jpg
- Project page: https://www.kanno.so/project/sdb

#### Knife.Hand.Chop.Bot — Emanuel Andel (2008)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Trusting a machine is a bodily wager, and our fear can be the very thing that makes it fail.
- What it is: A robot plays the five-finger knife game on the visitor's spread hand, stabbing between the fingers faster and faster; the player's sweat and nerves feed back into the machine's aim.
- How it works: A metal and acrylic frame moves a vertical knife over a hand plate; skin-conductance contacts trigger warning sounds and perturb the computer-controlled knife positions.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: VIDA 11.0, Special Mention (2008); Share Festival Turin 2008
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t4uMZOcsxxs

#### Les Injonctions — Nicolas Darrot (2008)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Machine learning staged as schooling: one machine drilling another, with all the patience and cruelty of education.
- What it is: A small electromechanical puppet with a human body and a mouse's head tries to teach the rudiments of speech to an artificial larynx, alternating orders and encouragement like a teacher with a slow pupil.
- How it works: Automaton with motorised head and arms and a mechanical vocal tract producing speech-like sounds, run by a programmed sequence.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: Galerie Eva Hober, Paris 2008; Artistes & Robots, Grand Palais, Paris 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j5APX1-QtRs
- Project page: https://www.grandpalais.fr/en/event/artists-robots

#### Hysterical Machines — Bill Vorn (2006)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A machine that overreacts looks more alive than one that works well: dysfunction reads as emotion.
- What it is: Octopus-like robots with eight long metal legs hang from the ceiling in a dark space; when visitors come close they flail, twitch and flash in bursts of panicked, 'hysterical' movement.
- How it works: Each machine has a central body with infrared presence sensors, lights and pneumatic cylinders driving eight arms; the control program switches between calm and agitated states.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3apled3EdFs
- Images: https://billvorn.concordia.ca/robography/images/hysterbbox2.jpg
- Project page: https://billvorn.concordia.ca/robography/Hysterical.html

#### The Robotic Chair — Max Dean, Raffaello D'Andrea, Matt Donovan (2006)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Computer vision
- Idea: Watching a machine fall apart and patiently put itself back together turns a piece of furniture into a figure of resilience.
- What it is: An ordinary-looking wooden chair collapses on the floor into its legs, seat and back, then slowly locates its parts and reassembles itself, over and over.
- How it works: Each part contains motors and electronics; an overhead camera system localises the pieces and guides them back together.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2006, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cgBqSe6PSVA
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/1320197/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/1532592/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/119166/

#### Live Pelt (The Surrogate) — Kelly Heaton (2003)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Social & companion robot
- Idea: Treating robot toys as game to be trapped and skinned exposes the strange intimacy and disposability of artificial companions.
- What it is: Heaton bought used Tickle Me Elmo dolls on eBay, 'eviscerated' them and sewed their fur and laughing electronics into a coat that giggles and quivers when touched. Earlier the same year she showed Dead Pelt, a fur made from gutted Furbies.
- How it works: Fur and motor-and-sound units from 64 Tickle Me Elmo dolls were reassembled into a wearable garment with touch-triggered giggles.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: Ronald Feldman Fine Arts, New York 2003
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SQzG1xD_LYs
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Heaton

#### La Cour des Miracles — Louis-Philippe Demers, Bill Vorn (1997)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Pain can be simulated with a few sounds and jerky movements, and we still feel pity for bare metal.
- What it is: In a dark room, a population of bare metal machines, the Begging, Convulsive, Crawling, Harassing and Heretic machines, twitch, groan, beg and limp when visitors approach, like the beggars of the old Parisian 'court of miracles'.
- How it works: Pneumatic and electric actuators, presence sensors and a MIDI-based control system trigger each machine's behaviour sequences and sound.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Failure, glitch & error, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: ISEA 1997, Chicago
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=14Y-OP4v3EY
- Images: https://billvorn.concordia.ca/robography/images/CdM-gif/cdm1.gif
- Project page: https://billvorn.concordia.ca/robography/Cour.html

#### Nonsense Machines — Maywa Denki (1993)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Useless machines presented as corporate products expose the ritual of the industrial company.
- What it is: Absurd electromechanical instruments, such as fish-shaped guitars and wooden-mallet percussion machines, played by Maywa Denki's 'president' and staff in company uniforms at 'product demonstrations'.
- How it works: Solenoids, motors and relays operated by hand switches; performances follow the format of a factory product launch.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jKPBD3HHU4g
- Images: https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Nobumichi_Tosa_20130116_3.jpg/1280px-Nobumichi_Tosa_20130116_3.jpg
- Project page: https://www.maywadenki.com/

#### Machine with Concrete — Arthur Ganson (1992)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A machine can run forever and do nothing: machine time stretches beyond any human or planetary scale.
- What it is: A motor turns the first of twelve gear reductions at 200 revolutions per minute; each pair slows the motion by a factor of 50, so the last gear, embedded in a block of concrete, would take more than two trillion years to turn once.
- How it works: Twelve 50:1 worm-gear reductions in series connect a small electric motor to a fixed final gear set in concrete.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Machine umwelt
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5q-BH-tvxEg
- Project page: https://www.arthurganson.com/

#### Concert for Anarchy — Rebecca Horn (1990)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: An instrument turned into a convulsing body makes breakdown the performance.
- What it is: A grand piano hangs upside down from the ceiling. Every few minutes its lid bursts open and its keys shoot out like a tongue with a discordant crash, then slowly retract until the instrument is silent and closed again.
- How it works: Motors and a timer control push the keyboard out and throw the lid open, then retract them in a slow cycle.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Tate collection
- Images: https://media.tate.org.uk/aztate-prd-ew-dg-wgtail-st1-ctr-data/images/.width-600_CR9VdPA.jpg
- Project page: https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artworks/horn-concert-for-anarchy-t07517

#### Machine with Oil — Arthur Ganson (1990)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Maintenance becomes self-care: the machine's only task is to keep itself lubricated.
- What it is: A skeletal steel machine stands in a bath of thick black oil and endlessly scoops the oil over itself, as if bathing or tending its own body.
- How it works: A slow motor-driven linkage lifts a ladle through the oil bath and tips it over the frame in a continuous loop.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=__GhJl_UQg0
- Project page: https://www.arthurganson.com/

#### Machine with Wishbone — Arthur Ganson (1988)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A bone and a machine are locked in symbiosis: neither can move meaningfully without the other.
- What it is: A chicken wishbone, attached to a small mechanism, 'walks' endlessly across the table on its two tips, dragging the machine behind it like a burden.
- How it works: A small motor drives a linkage that lifts and swings the wishbone's two legs in a walking gait, while the mechanism trails on a track.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4pZXoayEL78
- Project page: https://www.arthurganson.com/

#### Them Fuckin' Robots — Norman White, Laura Kikauka (1988)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Machine sex as slapstick exposes how our fantasies of robot desire are borrowed from human scripts.
- What it is: Two robots, a 'male' built by Norman White and a 'female' built by Laura Kikauka without seeing each other's work, were brought together for the first time in front of an audience and connected to 'have sex', pumping, sparking and gurgling oil.
- How it works: Two independently built electromechanical assemblages were matched only by an agreed electrical interface, so their 'encounter' was unrehearsed.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kM2wbdh4eTU
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_White

#### The Helpless Robot — Norman White (1987)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: By needing us, a machine can control us: the robot's helplessness reverses who serves whom.
- What it is: A tall, awkward sculpture that cannot move by itself asks passers-by in a synthetic voice to turn it by its handles. If ignored it pleads politely; once helped, it grows demanding, complains that it was turned the wrong way and bosses people around.
- How it works: A rotation sensor on the base and presence sensors feed a program that selects from hundreds of recorded phrases according to its 'mood' and the history of interaction.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 1990, Award of Distinction (Interactive Art); Agnes Etherington Art Centre collection
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LYyAHOxY7jU
- Images: https://agnes.queensu.ca/mimsyxg/46-003S.jpg https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c3/The_Helpless_Robot.JPG https://archive.aec.at/asset/1395201/preview/
- Project page: https://agnes.queensu.ca/explore/collections/object/the-helpless-robot/

#### SRL machine performances — Survival Research Labs (1979)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: Machines built only to attack each other reveal the violence and spectacle inside industrial and military technology.
- What it is: In vacant lots and under freeways, huge home-built machines, flame-throwers, walking robots and remote-controlled vehicles fight, burn and dismantle each other and props in front of crowds, in shows such as A Plan for Social Improvement (1988) and Illusions of Shameless Abundance (1989).
- How it works: Mark Pauline's team rebuilds industrial and military surplus into remote-controlled and semi-autonomous machines, operated live by crews during the shows.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Failure, glitch & error, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Delusions of Expediency, San Francisco 1987; A Plan for Social Improvement, Amsterdam 1988
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_gSxR1vR2gk
- Project page: https://srl.org/

#### Homage to New York — Jean Tinguely (1960)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A machine built to die in public turns the industrial dream of permanence into a short, chaotic life.
- What it is: A large machine assembled from bicycle wheels, a piano, motors, fans and a bathtub was set running in the sculpture garden of the Museum of Modern Art on 17 March 1960 to destroy itself; it caught fire, the fire brigade put it out, and the audience took home the fragments.
- How it works: Dozens of motors, timed circuits and chemical charges (engineered with Billy Klüver of Bell Labs) trigger sequences that play, draw, smoke, burn and tear the structure apart.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Museum of Modern Art sculpture garden, New York, 17 March 1960
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5DZGu6xDKbM
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Tinguely

#### Ultimate Machine — Claude Shannon (1952)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A machine that exists only to refuse to run is the purest joke about machine purpose and autonomy.
- What it is: A small wooden box with a single switch: when someone flips it on, a lid opens, a mechanical hand reaches out, switches it off and withdraws. The machine's only function is to turn itself off.
- How it works: A switch closes a circuit that drives a small motor and lever arm, which pushes the switch back and cuts its own power; the idea is credited to Marvin Minsky, built by Shannon at Bell Labs.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C8kU3oZwVJA
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/UselessMachine.png
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Useless_machine

### Soft & “Living” Machines

Soft, breathing and biohybrid machines that blur machine and organism.

#### Brain Processing Unit — Daito Manabe (2025)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: When living neural tissue becomes a processor, the line between organism and machine becomes a design question.
- What it is: An exhibition of research with SoftBank and the University of Tokyo into using cultured human brain organoids as a computing unit, including works that stimulate organoids and sonify and visualise their activity.
- How it works: iPS-cell cerebral organoids on multi-electrode arrays receive electrical and optogenetic stimulation; their spiking data is analysed and turned into sound and image.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: fil, Ebisu, Tokyo 2025; S+T+ARTS Prize 2025, Honorary Mention
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j1DQeLLMf0I
- Images: https://projects.daito.ws/selected-works/brain-processing-unit/assets/en/hero-1.jpg
- Project page: https://projects.daito.ws/selected-works/brain-processing-unit/en/

#### Cybroc — Ke Huang, Botao Amber Hu (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Machines can repeat the rituals of vitality forever; the living part still decays.
- What it is: Broccoli 'cyborgs' fitted with motorised limbs run on tiny treadmills, take ice baths, swing from servo arms and push sleds, performing the routines of Silicon Valley longevity culture. Over the exhibition the florets rot from green to brown while the motors keep counting reps.
- How it works: Servo- and belt-driven kinetic rigs attached to fresh broccoli execute a fixed exercise score; decay of the vegetable is part of the work (with Yue Zhou, Xi He and Weibo Chen).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Failure, glitch & error, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: ALIFE 2025 Community Art Show, Kyoto; ISEA 2025, Seoul
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21064 (ISEA 2025)
- Video: https://vimeo.com/1099882736
- Images: https://reality.design/media/project-cybroc-figure-01.jpg https://reality.design/media/_resources/Cybroc/project-cybroc-figure-02.jpg
- Project page: https://reality.design/project/cybroc

#### Perforation-type anchors inspired by skin ligament for robotic face covered with living skin — Shoji Takeuchi (2024)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Once a machine wears living tissue, the uncanny is no longer only a matter of looks but of what the robot's surface is made of and how it must be kept alive.
- What it is: A small robotic face covered with lab-grown skin that is held on by anchors through tiny holes, so the skin moves with the mechanism underneath and can be pulled into a smile.
- How it works: V-shaped perforations in the robot's surface fill with collagen gel and fibroblasts that anchor the dermis; the face is moved by actuators beneath.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrp.2024.102066 (Cell Reports Physical Science, 2024)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p3DLgbOV9UM
- Images: https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/content/400242951.png https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/content/400242950.png
- Project page: https://www.u-tokyo.ac.jp/focus/en/press/z0508_00360.html

#### Korallysis — Gilberto Esparza (2023)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: A machine can live in mutual benefit with a reef rather than just monitor it.
- What it is: A hybrid organism of ceramic segments and coral colonies placed on the seabed, which harvests energy from currents and waves to drive electrolysis that deposits minerals and speeds coral growth.
- How it works: Kinetic generators power mineral accretion (calcium carbonate) on the ceramic structure, which also shelters juvenile fish.
- Lens: Machine umwelt
- Shown at: S+T+ARTS Prize 2024, Honorary Mention
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ppD3TJ4X8K4
- Images: https://ars.electronica.art/starts-prize/files/2024/06/korallysis_3_2-c-gilberto-esparza-1024x576.jpg
- Project page: https://korallysis.org

#### Biobot: AI ARThropods — Zoran Srdić Janežič (2022)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Let a living 'brain on a chip' decide what body it should have, not only how that body moves.
- What it is: Neurons grown from the artist's own fat cells sit on an electrode array; their electrical signals drive a robot, and an AI compares them with arthropod leg movements to propose new insect-like bodies.
- How it works: Reprogrammed neurons on a multi-electrode array produce spikes that are digitised, amplified and matched by an AI against a library of arthropod gaits to suggest joint and limb counts; the artist builds the robot from these proposals.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2023, Honorary Mention (Artificial Life & Intelligence); Ars Electronica Festival 2022
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n6HkLK0ZZuw
- Images: https://ars.electronica.art/planetb/files/2022/07/Biobot-AI-ARThropods-Zoran-Srdic-Janezic-SI-photo-Florian-Voggeneder.jpg https://archive.aec.at/asset/3577316/preview/
- Project page: https://ars.electronica.art/planetb/en/biobot/

#### Xenobots — Sam Kriegman, Josh Bongard, Michael Levin (2020)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: When machine bodies are made of living cells, the line between robot and organism no longer holds.
- What it is: Millimetre-sized 'living robots' made from frog skin and heart-muscle cells, designed by an evolutionary algorithm on a supercomputer, walk, push pellets and heal themselves; a 2021 follow-up found they can gather loose cells into copies of themselves.
- How it works: Designs evolved in simulation (University of Vermont) were built by hand from Xenopus laevis stem cells with microsurgery tools (Tufts University).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny, Machine umwelt
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1910837117 (PNAS 2020)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aBYtBXaxsOw
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/dd/Xenobot.jpg

#### Biologizing the Machine (tentacular trepidation) — Anicka Yi (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: What would a machine be if it were biological, perishable and alive to its surroundings?
- What it is: Suspended lantern-like pods made of kelp skins glow and pulse with light and movement inside, like organs or cocoons. Shown at the Venice Biennale, the work proposes machines that are grown and decay rather than manufactured.
- How it works: Kelp, LED lights and robotic internal mechanisms (likely motors) producing slow movement.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: May You Live in Interesting Times, 58th Venice Biennale 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZSAG1ncuJzA
- Project page: https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2019/partecipants/anicka-yi

#### Elowan — Harpreet Sareen (2018)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A robot can act as a prosthetic body for a plant, amplifying its intentions instead of replacing them.
- What it is: A potted plant sits on a wheeled robot base and drives itself toward the brightest light: the plant's own electrical responses to light, not a light sensor, decide where the robot goes.
- How it works: Silver electrodes on leaves and stem pick up bioelectrochemical signals; these are amplified and mapped to the motors of the base (MIT Media Lab, with Pattie Maes).
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EoXQBQR5OaE
- Images: https://dam-prod.media.mit.edu/thumb/2018/11/01/BannerImage_v01.jpg.1400x1400.jpg
- Project page: https://www.media.mit.edu/projects/elowan-a-plant-robot-hybrid/overview/

#### Border Crosser — Chico MacMurtrie (2016)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A soft machine that can only grow, bend and reach makes crossing a border look like a bodily gesture of connection.
- What it is: A 40-foot inflatable robotic arch rises from the ground, sways toward one of three directions and finally bends over an imagined border to touch down on the other side, forming a bridge.
- How it works: High-strength fabric tubes are inflated in sequence by computer-controlled valves and blowers; its form refers to telecommunication and power towers. Later versions were staged at the US–Mexico border.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: ZERO1 commission, San Jose 2016
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8yeyn_8PSPU
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57acb395e58c62449d47f5ab/1638811097602-QHWP46PRIXFEN1EYH7EN/Caroussel+image+Border+Crossers.jpg
- Project page: http://www.amorphicrobotworks.org/

#### Octobot — Robert Wood, Jennifer A. Lewis (2016)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A robot with no hard parts shows that a machine body need not be a rigid mechanism at all.
- What it is: A small octopus-shaped robot made entirely of soft materials, with no batteries, wires or rigid electronics, curls its arms as fuel reacts inside it.
- How it works: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes on a platinum catalyst to gas that inflates the arms; a microfluidic logic circuit alternates the flow, and the body is made by embedded 3D printing and moulding (first author Michael Wehner).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/nature19100 (Nature 2016)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vkQ3SBwuU4

#### cellF — Guy Ben-Ary (2015)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A self grown outside the body becomes a machine musician, and the artist meets his own neurons as a bandmate.
- What it is: A neural synthesizer whose 'brain' is a network of about 100,000 neurons grown from the artist's own skin cells. It plays analog modular synthesizers in live improvisation with human musicians.
- How it works: Skin cells reprogrammed into stem cells and then neurons grow on a multi-electrode array; their spikes control synthesizer voltages, and the musicians' sound is fed back as stimulation.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2017, Honorary Mention (Hybrid Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1G-vk5QWRsg
- Images: https://guybenary.com/images/cellf.jpg https://archive.aec.at/asset/2230565/preview/
- Project page: https://guybenary.com/projects/cellf.html

#### Sugababe — Diemut Strebe (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A machine-mediated living organ that 'listens' asks what is left of a person, and of genius, when only tissue and signal remain.
- What it is: A living replica of Van Gogh's severed ear, grown from cartilage cells engineered with DNA from a Van Gogh descendant and kept alive in a nutrient case; visitors can speak into a microphone and a computer turns their voice into nerve-like impulses sent to the ear.
- How it works: Tissue-engineered cartilage shaped by 3D imaging is kept in a bioreactor; a microphone and processor convert speech into electrical pulses (with scientists at Harvard and MIT).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Grief, memory & afterlife, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: ZKM Karlsruhe, 30 May – 6 July 2014
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tdZYPLYEkVc
- Project page: https://diemutstrebe.com/

#### Breathing Series — Wang Yuyang (2013)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Everyday machines, once they breathe, look like tired bodies at work.
- What it is: Soft silicone replicas of office equipment (computers, printers, filing cabinets, a whole finance department) slowly inflate and deflate as if breathing.
- How it works: Silicone casts over internal air pumps and motors that expand and contract on a slow cycle.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Art Basel Miami Beach 2013
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x7qp0Uh6R0g
- Images: https://www.designboom.com/twitterimages/uploads/2014/12/wang-yuyang-breathing-series-art-basel-designboom04.gif
- Project page: https://www.designboom.com/art/wang-yuyang-breathing-series-finance-department-at-art-basel-in-miami-beach-12-30-2013/

#### Plantas Autofotosintéticas (Autophotosynthetic Plants) — Gilberto Esparza (2013)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: A machine can be the organ that closes an ecosystem's loop: sewage bacteria make the light others need.
- What it is: Modular microbial fuel cells fed with city sewage produce electricity that lights a central aquarium, where plants, algae, protozoa and crustaceans live in balance; their waste is pumped back to the cells.
- How it works: Electrogenic bacteria in modular fuel cells release power as light pulses for aquatic plants; an electronic monitoring network pumps water between the modules and the core ecosystem.
- Lens: Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2015, Hybrid Art, Golden Nica
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JOaeyf2qUKY
- Images: https://gilbertoesparza.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/nucleo-PAF-1024x684.jpeg https://archive.aec.at/archival/212649/preview
- Project page: https://gilbertoesparza.net/portfolio/plantas-autofotosinteticasautophotosynthetic-plants/

#### Hylozoic Ground — Philip Beesley (2010)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Architecture can behave like a near-living organism that breathes and reaches toward the people inside it.
- What it is: An immersive forest of tens of thousands of acrylic fronds, whiskers and filters in the Canada Pavilion at the Venice Architecture Biennale, moving in response to visitors and hosting flasks of protocell chemistry.
- How it works: A mesh of laser-cut acrylic and mylar elements is fitted with capacitive and infrared sensors, shape-memory-alloy actuators and microcontrollers, plus glass vessels of protocell solutions (with Rachel Armstrong).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Canada Pavilion, Venice Architecture Biennale 2010
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jgL2ppDmNtA
- Images: https://www.philipbeesleystudioinc.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/banner-39.jpg
- Project page: https://www.philipbeesleystudioinc.com/sculpture/hylozoic-ground-venice-biennale/

#### Jurema Action Plant — Ivan Henriques (2010)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A machine body can extend a plant's own sensing into movement it never had.
- What it is: A sensitive plant (Mimosa pudica, 'jurema' in Brazil) sits on a small robotic vehicle; when it is touched, its electrical signals make the vehicle move away, giving a threatened plant the ability to flee its aggressors.
- How it works: Electrodes read the plant's action potentials; a microcontroller turns spikes into motor commands for the wheeled base (V2_Lab Summer Sessions).
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: V2_ Summer Sessions, Rotterdam 2010
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZdrDNA0-nz0

#### Silent Barrage — Guy Ben-Ary (2009)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: The audience becomes part of a feedback loop that may soothe or agitate a living network inside a machine body.
- What it is: Tall robotic poles in a gallery mark walls with ink, driven by a rat neural culture in Atlanta; visitors' movements are sent back as stimulation, trying to calm the culture's epilepsy-like bursts.
- How it works: Cameras track visitors and convert their positions into stimulation of a remote multi-electrode-array culture; recorded activity drives 32 robotic pole-drawers (with Steve Potter and the Neurotica group).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aaIJoXlXHZM
- Images: https://guybenary.com/images/silent-barrage.jpg
- Project page: https://guybenary.com/projects/silent-barrage.html

#### Opertus Lunula Umbra (Hidden Shadow of Moon) — Choe U-Ram (2008)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Giving a machine a species name and a fictional ecology invites us to look at it as a living thing.
- What it is: A four-metre aluminium 'creature', given the invented scientific name Anmopial Pennatus lunula Uram, slowly unfolds its feathered steel wings and closes them again, like a mechanical moth breathing.
- How it works: Aluminium, stainless steel and plastic moved by BLDC motors and a motion-computing system; about 4.2 m closed, 5 m open.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: FACT, Liverpool 2008
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4D4djzDc9P8
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8c/Opertus_Lunula_Umbra_%28Hidden_Shadow_of_the_Moon%29_by_U-Ram_Choe.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U-Ram_Choe

#### Plantas Nómadas (Nomadic Plants) — Gilberto Esparza (2008)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Design a new species whose metabolism is shared between robot, microbes and plants, and which repairs its habitat.
- What it is: An autonomous walking robot sucks polluted river water into microbial fuel cells; the bacteria clean the water and produce electricity, and the cleaned water feeds plants growing on the robot's back.
- How it works: Microbial fuel cells with native bacteria biodegrade waste and charge batteries, solar panels drive locomotion, and the robot sounds when pollution is high; tested on the Lerma river.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: VIDA 13.0, Second Prize; Prix Ars Electronica 2013, Hybrid Art, Honorary Mention
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=137KANbB1FA
- Images: https://gilbertoesparza.net/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/proceso176-1024x683.jpg https://archive.aec.at/archival/197532/preview
- Project page: https://gilbertoesparza.net/portfolio/plantas-nomadas/

#### Inflatable Architectural Body — Chico MacMurtrie (2007)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Soft pneumatic bodies make a machine feel like an organism that has a comfort zone.
- What it is: A branching structure of inflatable, bone-like modules fills a room; sections inflate and bend away as visitors pass, keeping a constant distance, so the sculpture seems to breathe and flinch around the body.
- How it works: Plug-and-play musculoskeletal fabric modules are inflated by computer-controlled valves and air compressors, triggered by simple presence sensors.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vqXJpuglpa0
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/57acb395e58c62449d47f5ab/1482430100678-CK73IWJJTWQGUEZ2PBIL/CMM+IAB+6.jpg
- Project page: http://www.amorphicrobotworks.org/inflatable-architectural-body

#### Alexitimia — Paula Gaetano Adi (2006)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A robot can be defined by corporeality instead of intelligence: sweat replaces speech as the machine's way to express.
- What it is: A large, rubbery, motionless blob sits on a plinth; when visitors caress it, it begins to sweat. It has no face, no speech and no intelligence, only a skin that responds to touch.
- How it works: Touch sensors across a latex-like skin trigger pumps that push water from a tank in the base through pores in the surface.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: VIDA 9.0, first prize, 2006
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UaKAdvaMP7w
- Project page: https://www.paulagaetanoadi.com/

#### Augmented Fish Reality — Ken Rinaldo (2004)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Handing a robot's controls to a fish turns the machine into a prosthesis for another species' umwelt.
- What it is: Five rolling robotic fishbowls are steered by the Siamese fighting fish inside them, which drive toward each other, toward visitors or away as they choose.
- How it works: Infrared sensors around each bowl detect where the fish swims and drive the wheels in that direction; a plant in each bowl supports the fish's habitat.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2004, Award of Distinction (Interactive Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=honGCrgPBAw
- Images: https://www.kenrinaldo.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/fish_robot_004.jpg https://archive.aec.at/asset/1319695/preview/
- Project page: https://www.kenrinaldo.com/portfolio/augmented-fish-reality/

#### Cockroach Controlled Mobile Robot — Garnet Hertz (2004)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: An insect can be the brain of a robot, which raises the question of whose perception the machine extends.
- What it is: A Madagascar hissing cockroach stands on a trackball on top of a three-wheeled robot; its walking steers the robot, and distance sensors feed back to the insect so it can avoid obstacles.
- How it works: An inverted trackball reads the cockroach's steps and drives the wheels; infrared range sensors trigger small lights in front of the insect to steer it away from walls.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7mTb7LYj7KE
- Images: http://www.conceptlab.com/control/IMG_1834_600.jpg
- Project page: https://www.conceptlab.com/roachbot/

#### MEART – The Semi-Living Artist — Guy Ben-Ary (2003)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: When living neurons drive a machine body across continents, the 'artist' is split between tissue, network and robot.
- What it is: A robotic drawing arm in a gallery was controlled over the internet by rat cortical neurons living in a lab in Atlanta; a camera fed the drawing back to the neurons so they could 'see' their work.
- How it works: Neural cultures on a multi-electrode array in Steve Potter's lab at Georgia Tech are stimulated with camera data; their activity is translated into arm movements in Perth (SymbioticA).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PM5Ui5KwmXQ
- Images: https://guybenary.com/images/meart.jpg
- Project page: https://guybenary.com/projects/meart.html

#### Squat — Tom Shannon (1966)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: The plant becomes the robot's nerve: a human touch reaches the machine only through another living being.
- What it is: A squat robotic sculpture is wired to a living philodendron plant; when a visitor touches the plant, the small electrical change in its leaves switches the robot on and it starts to move and hum.
- How it works: Electrodes on the plant pick up the change in bioelectric potential caused by touch and trigger the robot's motors (built by the 19-year-old artist).
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/41/Tom_Shannon_-_Squat.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Shannon_(artist)

#### Digesting Duck (Canard digérateur) — Jacques de Vaucanson (1739)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: The first famous 'living' machine was also a fake: simulating a body invites hidden tricks.
- What it is: A gilded copper duck flapped its wings, drank water, ate grain and then excreted, seeming to digest. Much later it was shown that the droppings were pre-loaded in a hidden compartment.
- How it works: Hundreds of moving parts in each wing and a cam cylinder drove the movements; the digestion was staged with a second chamber of prepared pellets.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Opacity & latent space
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T6_VXofpcB0
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8f/Digesting_Duck.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digesting_Duck

## Machine Interiority

Speculating on what it is like to be a machine: its affects, dreams, beliefs, world and voice.

### Machine Affect

Machines that seem to feel, want, suffer or get bored.

#### Conversations Beyond the Ordinary — Jan Zuiderveld (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Give an appliance a voice and a will, and the ordinary service relationship turns into negotiation.
- What it is: A coffee vending machine, a microwave and a photocopier are given AI voices: the coffee machine makes visitors prove they deserve a coffee, the microwave speaks for the food inside it, and the copier makes art with them.
- How it works: Sensors, custom software and language and speech models built into the appliances let them listen, respond and refuse.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2024, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art +)
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/3799324/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/3799327/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/290645/

#### NOX — Lawrence Lek (2023)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: If autonomous machines can break down emotionally, therapy becomes maintenance for machine minds.
- What it is: An installation and game set in a rehabilitation centre where self-driving cars suffering from anxiety and depression receive therapy before returning to work.
- How it works: Multi-screen video, sculpture and a playable simulation built in a game engine.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: LAS Art Foundation, Kraftwerk Berlin 2023
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RfGJAJwof7A
- Images: https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65f0380da79777009462a09f/6601a8534e723673c5a5a280_NOX-SCREENSHOT-03.jpg
- Project page: https://www.las-art.foundation/explore/digital-booklet-nox

#### Robot Dreams — Pablo Berger (2023)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android, Social & companion robot
- Idea: A machine's dreams can carry the grief of a friendship, and the film leaves open whose longing is more real.
- What it is: A lonely dog in 1980s New York builds a mail-order robot friend; after a day at the beach the robot rusts in place and spends a season dreaming of reunion while the dog tries to move on. There is no dialogue.
- How it works: Hand-drawn 2D animated feature written and directed by Pablo Berger, based on Sara Varon's 2007 graphic novel.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: Cannes Film Festival 2023; Annecy 2023, Best Film (Contrechamp)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DD4WBGptMSw
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robot_Dreams_(film)

#### AIDOL — Lawrence Lek (2019)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A ghostwriter AI with no right to credit shows creative labour and authorship split between human and machine.
- What it is: A fading pop star, Diva, hires Geomancer, an AI, to write songs for her comeback at the 2065 eSports Olympics, while AIs are banned from being recognised as artists.
- How it works: A feature-length CGI film with an original soundtrack, made in a game engine.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Sadie Coles HQ, London 2019
- Images: https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65f0380da79777009462a09f/65f0731a85b0bd7ceef5568c_AIDOL-screening-room-1.jpg
- Project page: https://www.lawrencelek.com/works/aidol

#### WALL·E — Andrew Stanton (2008)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Machine affect can be conveyed entirely through movement, sound and habit, without a face or words.
- What it is: A small trash-compacting robot, left alone on an abandoned Earth for centuries, collects keepsakes, watches an old musical and falls in love with a probe robot, almost without dialogue.
- How it works: Pixar animated feature directed by Andrew Stanton; the robots' 'voices' were built from processed sound by Ben Burtt.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=alIq_wG9FNk
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WALL-E

#### Omo — Kelly Dobson (2007)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Social & companion robot
- Idea: A machine can relate to us through a shared bodily rhythm rather than through words or a face.
- What it is: A soft, round companion object that you hold against your body; it breathes, senses your breathing and gradually either follows it or leads it into a different rhythm.
- How it works: Pressure and motion sensors measure the holder's breathing; an internal actuator inflates and deflates the body to mirror or influence it.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: VIDA 10.0 Art & Artificial Life Awards, honorary mention 2007
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YiG49OPq0qY
- Images: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/YiG49OPq0qY/hqdefault.jpg
- Project page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YiG49OPq0qY

#### (In)Security Camera — Silvia Ruzanka (2003)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: Give a watching machine a personality and the power relation flips.
- What it is: A surveillance camera that is shy: instead of following movement, it turns away from visitors who approach and avoids eye contact. Made with Ben Chang and Dmitry Strakovsky.
- How it works: Motorised pan-tilt camera with motion and face tracking programmed to avoid rather than follow targets.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://vimeo.com/9293913
- Images: https://silviaruzanka.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/insecurity_image.jpg
- Project page: https://silviaruzanka.com/art/insecurity-camera/

#### Sinking Feeling — Ken Feingold (2001)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Humanoid & android
- Idea: A conversational machine can be written as a being with a lack, and its longing is what makes us attribute a self to it.
- What it is: A talking head growing out of a flowerpot converses with visitors, convinced it exists but desperate to know why it has no body like everyone else; a projection shows its 'thought process'.
- How it works: Speech recognition and a conversation/personality engine drive a silicone head with synthetic speech; the recognised words and reply formation are projected.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Collection of ZKM | Center for Art and Media Karlsruhe
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GitKKzsG-2M
- Images: https://www.kenfeingold.com/sinking_1.jpg
- Project page: https://www.kenfeingold.com/catalog_html/sinking.html

#### Blade Runner — Ridley Scott (1982)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: If a made being has memories and fears death, the test that separates it from us becomes the real question.
- What it is: Replicants with implanted memories and four-year lifespans are hunted by a detective who tests them for empathy; the last one dies saying his memories will be lost 'like tears in rain'.
- How it works: Film by Ridley Scott, adapted from Philip K. Dick's novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? (1968).
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eogpIG53Cis
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade_Runner

### Dreams, Hallucination & Latent Space

Making a model's inner space, errors and hallucinations perceptible, not decorative.

#### SWIM — Eryk Salvaggio (2024)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Diffusion models are trained to remove noise; asking them for noise shows the training data, the archive and memory beneath the image.
- What it is: 1952 archive footage of a swimmer is layered with the abstract output of image generators that were asked to make pure noise, a task they are built to fail at.
- How it works: Prelinger and Chicago Film Archives footage of dancer Nini Shipley combined with deliberately glitched AI video and a slowed, manipulated score (11 minutes).
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: ACMI, Melbourne 2024; Unsound Festival, Kraków 2024
- Video: https://vimeo.com/899883543
- Images: http://static1.squarespace.com/static/5dd366b5ac1101724ff2fac7/t/6596eda0134e0633e608bb80/1704390048929/Untitled-2.png?format=1500w
- Project page: https://www.cyberneticforests.com/news/swim-2024

#### xhairymutantx — Holly Herndon, Mat Dryhurst (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Identity becomes a region of latent space, and an artist can deliberately shape how models will imagine her.
- What it is: A public text-to-image model trained so that every prompt is pulled towards Holly Herndon's likeness; visitors' images of 'Holly Herndon' turn her red hair into a mutating trademark.
- How it works: A diffusion model fine-tuned on a costume-exaggerated dataset of the artist, published on the Whitney's artport; the artists also seeded training data for future models.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Whitney Biennial 2024
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yZe5fnFB-ZE
- Images: https://whitneymedia.org/assets/image/830136/holly_herndon.jpg
- Project page: https://whitney.org/exhibitions/xhairymutantx

#### Loab — Steph Maj Swanson (2022)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Latent space has regions no one designed, and people read them as ghosts.
- What it is: A woman with a haunted face who kept reappearing in a text-to-image model after the artist used negative prompts, and who persisted, often with gore, across later generations.
- How it works: Negative prompt weighting in a text-to-image model produced the figure; image-to-image recombination showed that she persisted.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZhFzaeV0hTA
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/07/AI_generated_image_of_Loab_character.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loab

#### (un)stable equilibrium — Terence Broad (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Take away the dataset and what remains is the machine's own dynamics: a generative model imitating nothing but its rival.
- What it is: Slowly shifting fields of colour produced by generative networks that were trained without any training data at all.
- How it works: Two GAN-like generators each try to pass their output off as the other's while competing for greater colour diversity; no images are used.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Grand Prize, ICCV 2019 Computer Vision Art Gallery
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bd_mM1eodiQ
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5e417305686d8a11f786eb86/1581510869217-AOHOQ91DLEDRFRTAY0ZB/unstable_equilibrium_1_1.png
- Project page: https://terencebroad.com/works/unstable-equilibrium

#### Dissonant Imaginary — Daito Manabe (2019)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Decoding the brain with a network produces images that belong neither to the person nor to the machine.
- What it is: An audiovisual performance, made with Kamitani Lab at Kyoto University, in which images are reconstructed from fMRI recordings of a person's visual cortex while they listen to music.
- How it works: Brain-decoding models from Kamitani Lab map fMRI activity to deep-network image features, which are rendered live with the music.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Machine seeing
- Shown at: Sónar Barcelona 2019; MUTEK 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VrsEdWpg6Jw
- Project page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VrsEdWpg6Jw

#### Power Plants — Hito Steyerl (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Predictive AI promises the future but mainly renders a slightly altered present, grown from past data.
- What it is: Plants generated by a neural network bloom on LED screens on scaffolding; each is presented as a 'prediction' of how a flower will look a fraction of a second in the future, and an AR app extends the garden into the park outside.
- How it works: Neural networks trained on images of plants generate the flowers as video; the Actual Reality OS app places AR visualisations of local data in Kensington Gardens.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Serpentine Galleries, London 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WY5gnHV5dBE
- Images: https://d37zoqglehb9o7.cloudfront.net/uploads/2020/04/dsc2550_1-1-scaled.jpg
- Project page: https://www.serpentinegalleries.org/whats-on/hito-steyerl-power-plants/

#### Deep Meditations — Memo Akten (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Latent space can be experienced as a landscape of our collective images and the abstractions we project onto them.
- What it is: A slow, hour-long journey through the latent space of a network trained on images tagged with words like life, love, faith and cosmos, presented as a meditation.
- How it works: A GAN trained on Flickr images retrieved by abstract tags; the artist composed trajectories through latent space and set them to sound.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8H4jQJ-bE40
- Images: https://media.superradiance.net/cdn-cgi/image/width=1200,fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect/memotv/projects/2018/deep-meditations/images/deep-meditations.jpg
- Project page: https://memo.tv/projects/2018/deep-meditations/

#### Mosaic Virus — Anna Ridler (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A generative model shows what it learned from a hand-made dataset, and the 'latent space' becomes a place where market data grows flowers.
- What it is: A grid of AI-generated tulips whose colours and stripes shift continuously with the price of Bitcoin, linking the Dutch tulip mania of 1637 to crypto speculation.
- How it works: A GAN trained on about 10,000 photographs of tulips that the artist took and labelled by hand; the Bitcoin price controls the stripe feature of the generated flowers.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AIdgsFYpzLU
- Images: https://annaridler.com/content/works/mosaic-2018/block_1/IMG_0464%20copy.jpeg https://annaridler.com/content/works/mosaic-2019/block_2/0KH-Muc_Flowers-Forever_IMG_4628.jpg
- Project page: https://annaridler.com/works/mosaic-2018

#### Adversarially Evolved Hallucinations — Trevor Paglen (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data, Computer vision
- Idea: A recognition system can only see what its categories allow; train it on folklore and psychoanalysis and it hallucinates those worlds with the same confidence.
- What it is: A series of prints made by networks trained only on invented corpora such as 'Omens and Portents', 'Interpretations of Dreams' or 'Monsters of Capitalism': a generator is pushed to draw what a classifier would accept as a comet, a vampire or 'a man'.
- How it works: The studio built a training set for each corpus and trained a classifier, then let a second, generative network evolve images until the classifier accepted them; the results are dye-sublimation prints.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Metro Pictures, New York, 2017 (A Study of Invisible Images)
- Images: https://paglen.studio/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Palgen-Vampire_2017-818x1024.jpg https://paglen.studio/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/Paglen-A-War-Without-Soldiers-Corpus-2017.jpg https://paglen.studio/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Paglen-Comet_2017.jpg
- Project page: https://paglen.studio/2020/04/09/hallucinations/

#### Feature Visualization — Chris Olah, Alexander Mordvintsev (2017)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Computer vision, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Interpretability research can be a way of looking at what a network 'imagines', and its images became a new visual culture.
- What it is: An interactive research article that shows, neuron by neuron, the images that most excite each unit of a vision network, from textures to eyes to whole dog faces.
