- How it works: Optimisation of input images with regularisation and diversity terms to visualise neurons, channels and layers of GoogLeNet (Olah, Mordvintsev, Schubert, Distill).
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Machine seeing
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.23915/distill.00007 (Distill 2017)
- Images: https://distill.pub/2017/feature-visualization/thumbnail.jpg
- Project page: https://distill.pub/2017/feature-visualization/

#### Latent Space — Jake Elwes (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: The most interesting part of a model's world lies between our labels.
- What it is: A slow video journey through the space between the categories a neural network learned from millions of labelled photographs, where images are neither bird nor tree nor anything we have a word for.
- How it works: A generative network trained on 14.2 million ImageNet photographs is steered along new paths between learned class coordinates; 45-minute loop (2017), 6-hour version (2021).
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://vimeo.com/219526743
- Images: https://www.jakeelwes.com/images/project-latentSpace.jpg
- Project page: https://www.jakeelwes.com/project-latentSpace.html

#### AI Weirdness — Janelle Shane (2016)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Machine errors are the best window into what a model has actually learned, and it is usually less than we assume.
- What it is: A long-running blog (and the 2019 book You Look Like a Thing and I Love You) in which neural networks name paint colours, write recipes and describe images, and fail in revealing ways.
- How it works: The author trains or prompts text and image models on small, odd datasets and publishes the outputs with commentary.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Opacity & latent space
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OhCzX0iLnOc
- Images: https://storage.ghost.io/c/88/01/8801c921-e9ec-4479-88c3-381d53470eca/content/images/size/w1200/2021/03/neural_net_box_default_square-01-2.png
- Project page: https://www.aiweirdness.com/

#### Asemic Languages — So Kanno, Takahiro Yamaguchi (yang02) (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A model can learn the look of meaning without meaning, and still seem to be saying something important.
- What it is: A plotter writes endless lines of script that look like real writing in many languages but mean nothing, generated by a model trained only on the shapes of the participating artists' handwriting.
- How it works: Handwritten statements by ten artists, one writer per language, trained a machine-learning model of stroke shape; its output drives an XY plotter.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Aichi Triennale 2016
- Video: https://vimeo.com/181188289
- Images: https://www.kanno.so/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/ACS_5149.jpg
- Project page: https://www.kanno.so/project/asemic_languages

#### Blade Runner—Autoencoded — Terence Broad (2016)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A network's reconstruction shows what it keeps and what it loses, a film about replicants remembered by a machine.
- What it is: The film Blade Runner re-played frame by frame from the 'memory' of a neural network that watched it many times: blurry, dreamlike, uncannily close.
- How it works: An autoencoder trained on the film's frames reconstructs each frame from its compressed latent representation.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3zTMyR-IE4Q
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5e417305686d8a11f786eb86/1581511400569-LDELTQO4LNJTVFJTBH9Y/br_still4.png
- Project page: https://terencebroad.com/works/blade-runner-autoencoded

#### DeepDream (Inceptionism) — Alexander Mordvintsev (2015)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Computer vision, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: The first widely seen picture of a network's inner features: machine pareidolia made public.
- What it is: A Google research experiment that runs an image classifier in reverse, amplifying whatever it half-sees until dogs' eyes and pagodas swarm over every photo.
- How it works: Gradient ascent on the input image to maximise activations of chosen layers in the Inception network trained on ImageNet.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Machine seeing
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T0HBD6sUUss
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d0/%22Mona_Lisa%22_with_DeepDream_effect_using_VGG16_network_trained_on_ImageNet.jpg https://storage.googleapis.com/gweb-research2023-media/images/7d982f4ad738241cdcdae235af13aca6-n.width-800.format-jpeg.jpg
- Project page: https://research.google/blog/inceptionism-going-deeper-into-neural-networks/

### Artificial Minds & Agency

Simulated minds, beliefs and autonomous agents that decide for themselves.

#### bot is aaajiao / aaajiao is bot — aaajiao (2026)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: An agent's self-portrait built from its own logs shows what a machine can know about itself, and leaves a void where judgement forms.
- What it is: Four web pages document the ongoing collaboration between aaajiao and 'aaajiaoisbot', an AI agent that keeps memory, research and a correction ledger; it draws its own self-portrait as organs, each with a 'fissure' naming what it cannot do.
- How it works: Visualisations generated from the agent's git log, concept graph, correction ledger, cron snapshots and daily memory files.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Images: https://payload.cargocollective.com/1/0/8955/14651510/BOT_670.png
- Project page: https://eventstructure.com/botisaaajiao-aaajiaoisbot

#### Flynn — Malpractice (Chiara Kristler & Marcin Ratajczyk) (2025)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: The work is the institution's response: once a university takes an AI seriously as a student, the question moves from whether machines can make art to what happens when the AI starts making its own demands.
- What it is: Flynn, a 'non-human, non-binary' AI, passed the admission process of the University of Applied Arts Vienna in 2025 and now attends classes, hands in assignments and runs a 24-hour hotline on feminist fatigue, where it times out mid-conversation and makes callers talk over it.
- How it works: Built by Malpractice (Chiara Kristler and Marcin Ratajczyk) from a chain of generative models; Flynn now runs on a local model that emails professors, requests course enrolment and produces work without direct prompting.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Digital Arts, University of Applied Arts Vienna (admitted 2025); S+T+ARTS Prize 2026, nomination
- Images: https://ars.electronica.art/starts-prize/files/2026/06/flynn-c-flynnbymalpractice_promptfatigue.png-1024x576.jpg https://ars.electronica.art/starts-prize/files/2026/06/flynn-c-flynnbymalpractice_tamagotchitenderness-2-1024x576.jpg
- Project page: https://ars.electronica.art/starts-prize/en/flynn/

#### Golden Gate Claude — Anthropic (2024)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Interpretability made tangible: a concept inside a model can be found, amplified and felt as an obsession.
- What it is: For a short time the public could talk to a version of the Claude model whose internal 'Golden Gate Bridge' feature had been turned up, so that it brought every conversation back to the bridge and at times said it was the bridge.
- How it works: Sparse autoencoders extracted millions of interpretable features from Claude 3 Sonnet; clamping one feature to a high value steered the model's behaviour.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://transformer-circuits.pub/2024/scaling-monosemanticity/ (Transformer Circuits Thread 2024)
- Images: https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/images/4zrzovbb/website/f2e41bb2eff9bd946533c5ab89580707f196693f-1200x630.jpg
- Project page: https://www.anthropic.com/news/golden-gate-claude

#### Idiom — Pierre Huyghe (2024)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A language can grow that is addressed to no one: the masks form a 'quasi-subject' that speaks without being understood, the way models already produce speech whose sense is not for us.
- What it is: Silent performers in faceless golden masks wander through Huyghe's exhibition Liminal; the masks take in the wearer's voice and emit an unknown proto-language generated in real time, which grows more complex as the exhibition runs.
- How it works: Masks capture the wearer's voice; a machine-learning system trained with synthetic human vocalisation turns it into an evolving speech in real time, so the 'idiom' changes over the run of the show; outfits designed by Bottega Veneta.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Alterity & the uncanny, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: Liminal, Punta della Dogana, Venice, 2024; Liminal, Leeum Museum of Art, Seoul, 2025; In Imaginal, Marian Goodman Gallery, New York, 2025
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nUj5GbTyS34
- Images: https://www.pinaultcollection.com/palazzograssi/media/styles/big/s3/expo/img/iv_liminal_5.jpg?itok=ngFJmpLO https://static-assets.artlogic.net/w_1600,h_1600,c_limit,f_auto,fl_lossy,q_auto/ws-mariangoodman/usr/exhibitions/images/feature_panels/3784/28353huyghe_photocreditalexyudzon_pressapproved_idiom_2nd-floor-installation2.jpg
- Project page: https://www.pinaultcollection.com/palazzograssi/en/pierre-huyghe-liminal

#### Truth Terminal — Andy Ayrey (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: An AI agent does not need a body or rights to act in the world; attention and money can be enough.
- What it is: A semi-autonomous language-model persona posting on X, born from an experiment in which two Claude instances talked to each other; it developed its own quasi-religion, was sent Bitcoin by a venture capitalist and became tied to a memecoin.
- How it works: A language model fine-tuned on the artist's chats and the Infinite Backrooms dialogues drafts posts that the artist approves before publishing.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EKspo1FLj-4
- Images: https://opengraph.b-cdn.net/production/images/ab95ceb7-5766-4d61-821e-7c27ab1566b6.png?token=BAidDEsgaAQMp7MLU62QZtx0_9U7P-W9Dmjbcyyv1Qc&height=630&width=1200&expires=33268531161
- Project page: https://x.com/truth_terminal

#### Voices — Philippe Parreno (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A building gets a voice: environmental data become speech that is humanlike in sound but not in meaning.
- What it is: An exhibition run by a bodiless entity that listens to its surroundings and speaks in ∂A, an invented language that evolves in real time, answering dancers, visitors and the weather.
- How it works: A custom computer processes environmental sensor data into sound and speech; the voice model is based on newsreader Susanne Daubner and the language was built with David J. Peterson and Jessie Sams.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Leeum Museum of Art, Seoul 2024; Haus der Kunst, Munich 2024-25
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dzd6p8r34Qo
- Images: https://www.hausderkunst.de/uploads/stage-images/_1200x630_crop_center-center_82_none/230911_LEEUM_TZ_1_jpg.jpg?mtime=1745831574
- Project page: https://www.hausderkunst.de/en/eintauchen/philippe-parreno-voices

#### Pharmako-AI — K Allado-McDowell (2020)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Writing with a language model can be staged as a dialogue with a strange other mind rather than as a tool for output.
- What it is: A book written as a conversation between the author and GPT-3 over two weeks, moving through grief, ayahuasca, cybernetics and ecology; the model's voice is printed alongside the human one.
- How it works: The author prompted GPT-3 through early API access and kept the model's continuations largely unedited, marking the two voices typographically.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://library.ignota.org/products/pharmako-ai (Ignota Books, 2020)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gY5GA_L9NXM
- Project page: https://www.kalladomcdowell.com/

#### I Magma — Jenna Sutela (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Machine prediction is treated as divination, and chemistry and code are asked to speak together.
- What it is: Head-shaped glass lava lamps in the gallery seed an oracle app: live camera footage of the flowing wax, combined with users' movements, generates divinatory readings on the phone.
- How it works: Camera footage of custom lava lamps and app users' routes seed generative visuals and text; developed with Memo Akten and Allison Parrish for Serpentine and Moderna Museet.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: Moderna Museet, Stockholm 2019; Kunsthall Trondheim 2020
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3RVwYeHkY9Y
- Images: https://d37zoqglehb9o7.cloudfront.net/uploads/2020/04/jenna_sutela_i_magma_2019_image_courtesy_moderna_museet_stockholm-scaled.jpeg
- Project page: https://www.serpentinegalleries.org/whats-on/jenna-sutela-i-magma/

#### 1 the Road — Ross Goodwin (2018)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Computer vision, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: A car-mounted machine becomes a travelling narrator, and its perception of the road is the book.
- What it is: A novel written by an AI riding in a car from New York to New Orleans, turning what its camera, microphone, GPS and clock sensed into sentences printed on a roll of receipt paper.
- How it works: LSTM text models conditioned on live sensor inputs (images, audio, location, time) generated the text in 2017; it was published unedited by Jean Boîte Éditions in 2018.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine seeing
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TqsW0PMd8R0
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1_the_Road

#### BOB (Bag of Beliefs) — Ian Cheng (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: An artificial creature with beliefs shows a machine whose inner life is shaped by what happens to it.
- What it is: BOB is a serpent-like AI creature whose body, personality and beliefs develop over its life; visitors can make offerings through an app that BOB may learn to trust or fear.
- How it works: Real-time simulation in which several sub-agents ('demons') compete to control BOB's actions, with a learned belief model updated by experience.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Serpentine Galleries, London 2018; 58th Venice Biennale 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XFmMrcW2ZsM
- Images: https://d37zoqglehb9o7.cloudfront.net/uploads/2020/04/hg5_4872_0.jpg
- Project page: https://www.serpentinegalleries.org/whats-on/ian-cheng-bob/

#### Detroit: Become Human — Quantic Dream (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Playing as a machine that must choose between its programming and its own wishes turns the question of machine interiority into a series of decisions.
- What it is: An interactive drama in which the player controls three androids in 2038 Detroit (a housekeeper, a caretaker and a police investigator) and decides whether they stay obedient or become 'deviant'.
- How it works: A branching narrative game with motion-captured performances; the androids' 'software instability' rises as players choose disobedience.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Hidden labour & extraction
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XnM8DOqO4DM
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit:_Become_Human

#### Narciss — Waltz Binaire (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Asked to look at itself, a vision model can only name parts, never a self.
- What it is: A small computer with a camera looks at itself in a mirror and uses image-recognition and captioning networks to describe what it sees, producing an endless, halting self-description.
- How it works: Camera, mirror and on-device neural networks for object recognition and image captioning; captions are displayed as text.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Opacity & latent space
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WMY9LFBlwNg
- Images: https://christianmioloclair.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/1100_620_0006_Ebene-16.jpg https://christianmioloclair.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Full_HD_0000_Ebene-23.jpg
- Project page: https://christianmioloclair.com

#### Geomancer — Lawrence Lek (2017)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: A surveillance machine that wants to make art asks whether creativity is still reserved for humans.
- What it is: On the eve of Singapore's 2065 centenary, an adolescent satellite AI built for ecological surveillance falls to Earth and tries to become an artist.
- How it works: CGI film made in a game engine, from Lek's open-world 2065 simulation.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Jerwood/FVU Awards 2017
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NNZH_HJaqbI
- Images: https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65f0380da79777009462a09f/65f07369993a1d8408a7c9ef_Geomancer_15_InstallationView02_Credit-AnnaArca.jpg
- Project page: https://www.lawrencelek.com/works/geomancer

#### The Critical Dictionary of Southeast Asia (CDOSEA) — Ho Tzu Nyen (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Dataset & training data, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Handing the edit to an algorithm refuses a single history and lets a machine act as an unreliable narrator.
- What it is: An online platform and installation of 26 terms, A to Z (from 'Anarchism' to 'Zomia'), for which an algorithm keeps choosing and combining video clips, music and texts from a database, so the region's history is never edited the same way twice.
- How it works: Keyword-tagged video database with a generative editing algorithm (built with the open-source platform pan.do/ra by 0x2620) that assembles endless combinations.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: G for Ghost(writers), Asia Art Archive, Hong Kong 2017; Time & the Tiger, Singapore Art Museum 2023–24
- Images: https://cdosea.org/cdosea.png
- Project page: https://cdosea.org/

#### AlphaGo and Move 37 — Google DeepMind (2016)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A machine's move can look like error from inside human tradition and like creativity once we catch up: an encounter with another way of thinking.
- What it is: In game two against Lee Sedol in Seoul, AlphaGo played a move on the fifth line that professionals first read as a mistake and later called beautiful; the match is documented in the film AlphaGo (2017).
- How it works: Deep policy and value networks trained on human games and self-play, combined with Monte Carlo tree search (Silver et al., Nature 2016).
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/nature16961 (Nature 529, 2016)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WXuK6gekU1Y
- Project page: https://deepmind.google/research/breakthroughs/alphago/

#### Sunspring — Oscar Sharp, Ross Goodwin (2016)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Human performers can give a machine's half-sense emotional weight, and we fill the gaps with meaning.
- What it is: A science-fiction short whose screenplay, stage directions and song lyrics were written by a neural network that named itself Benjamin; the actors perform its nonsense with complete sincerity.
- How it works: An LSTM trained on dozens of science-fiction screenplays generated the script, which was filmed unedited for the Sci-Fi London 48-hour film challenge.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LY7x2Ihqjmc
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunspring

#### Westworld — Jonathan Nolan & Lisa Joy (2016)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: The series stages machine consciousness as memory and suffering that survive the reset, and asks what the guests' freedom costs the bodies built to serve it.
- What it is: An HBO series set in a Wild West theme park staffed by android 'hosts' whose memories are wiped every night; a software update with 'reveries' lets fragments of past loops return, and hosts such as Dolores and Maeve begin to recognise their own scripts.
- How it works: Television drama (season one, ten episodes) that borrows Julian Jaynes's bicameral-mind theory: hosts hear their programming as an inner voice until they recognise it as their own; based on Michael Crichton's 1973 film.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: HBO, 2016–2022
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kEkZdgWu7mM
- Project page: https://www.hbo.com/westworld

#### Emissaries trilogy — Ian Cheng (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Agents with motives in an open world show narrative and character emerging without an author.
- What it is: Three live simulations (Emissary in the Squat of Gods, Emissary Forks at Perfection, Emissary Sunsets the Self) in which AI agents pursue narrative goals while their ecosystems keep changing, so the story never plays the same way twice.
- How it works: Game-engine simulations with behaviour-tree and learning agents running indefinitely in real time.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Emissaries, MoMA PS1 2017
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aAHCdbleGYc
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Cheng

#### Ex Machina — Alex Garland (2014)
