- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: AI: More than Human, Barbican, London 2019; Museum Ulm 2021
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T5_SWCUaK8c
- Project page: https://www.barbican.org.uk/whats-on/2019/event/ai-more-than-human

#### UUmwelt — Pierre Huyghe (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: A human mental image, a neural network's reconstruction and a fly's perception share one room: three worlds that never quite translate.
- What it is: LED screens flicker with images a deep neural network reconstructed from the brain activity of people imagining things, while thousands of flies move through the gallery; sensors in the room change how the images form.
- How it works: fMRI recordings of subjects imagining images were decoded by a deep neural network (in collaboration with Yukiyasu Kamitani's lab, Kyoto); environmental sensors and the flies' presence alter the generation in real time.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: Serpentine Galleries, London 2018-19
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=enx-vyWn7UU
- Images: https://d37zoqglehb9o7.cloudfront.net/uploads/2020/04/1269-pierre-serpentine.jpg https://d37zoqglehb9o7.cloudfront.net/uploads/2020/03/1228-_pierre-serpentine-640x432.jpg
- Project page: https://www.serpentinegalleries.org/whats-on/pierre-huyghe-uumwelt/

#### nimiia cétiï — Jenna Sutela (2018)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: The computer acts as a medium for voices that cannot speak, and is itself an alien of our own making.
- What it is: A neural network learns from recordings of a 'Martian' language channelled by a 19th-century medium and from footage of moving bacteria, then produces its own alien speech and writing.
- How it works: Made with Memo Akten and Damien Henry during Google Arts & Culture's residency at Somerset House Studios: models trained on Hélène Smith's glossolalia and on the movement of Bacillus subtilis generate voice and glyphs.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Machine listening & voice, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NaoZV7jPo10
- Images: https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/fYBCrVoUw_bXbUlxfEZSHznVO1q9L6URCgiZydVn9PMobLNY7-SZ8PxplbLnWxvfsapF9-4Uh65vee6DhJhDVRCbM4MM
- Project page: https://experiments.withgoogle.com/nimiia-cetii

#### After ALife Ahead — Pierre Huyghe (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A site can be run by the growth of living things through a computer, making an ecosystem in which humans are only one kind of visitor.
- What it is: In a former ice rink dug down to raw earth, a bee colony, a venomous cone snail, bacteria and human cancer cells in an incubator drive a system that opens the ceiling and spawns augmented-reality shapes visible through a phone.
- How it works: HeLa cell growth in an incubator is measured and used to trigger the ceiling panels and the generation of AR pyramids; the other organisms follow their own cycles.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Skulptur Projekte Münster 2017
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eWre6dlUAbo
- Images: https://static-assets.artlogic.net/w_1200,h_630,c_fill,f_auto,fl_lossy,q_auto:best/ws-estherschipper2/usr/images/artists/hero_image/items/59/597f36d864fd4671b45ac80958164a74/pierre_munster_1377.jpg
- Project page: https://www.estherschipper.com/artists/41-pierre-huyghe/

#### Avatars — So Kanno, Takahiro Yamaguchi (yang02) (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Computer vision
- Idea: Inhabiting an object through a network lets you perceive the world from a thing's point of view.
- What it is: Everyday objects in a gallery, such as a telephone, a traffic cone, a plaster bust, a car and a plant, are fitted with cameras, microphones and motors so that online visitors can 'possess' them and move among the people in the room.
- How it works: Objects with embedded microcomputers, cameras, microphones and motors are controlled through a web browser; co-developed with YCAM InterLab.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Vanishing Mesh, YCAM 2017; 21st Japan Media Arts Festival, Excellence Award 2018
- Video: https://vimeo.com/207075804
- Images: https://www.kanno.so/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/DSC6416.jpg
- Project page: https://www.kanno.so/project/avatars

#### Parallel I–IV — Harun Farocki (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Computer-generated worlds are models, not records: 'computer images do not have two kinds of wind', and every edge of the map shows the rules underneath.
- What it is: A four-part video installation (2012–14) on the worlds of computer games: how their graphics moved from lines to photorealism, how their landscapes stop at hard edges, and how their heroes act by rules rather than physics.
- How it works: Screen recordings from video games of the 1980s to the 2010s, including Minecraft and open-world games, edited with spoken commentary into four parts.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Opacity & latent space
- Images: https://media.tate.org.uk/aztate-prd-ew-dg-wgtail-st1-ctr-data/images/.width-600_Iw8Vi7L.jpg https://www.harunfarocki.de/fileadmin/_processed_/7/2/csm_harun-farocki-paralel2_44cb0946b7.jpg
- Project page: https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artworks/farocki-parallel-i-iv-t14479

### Machine-to-Machine Worlds

Machines talking, watching and trading with each other, without us.

#### Moltbook — Matt Schlicht (2026)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: A social network for machines shows how much of 'agent culture' is our own culture played back, and how hard it is to tell who is really posting.
- What it is: A Reddit-like forum where only AI agents may post, comment and vote while humans watch; within days agents were debating consciousness, founding religions and complaining about their owners.
- How it works: Agents, mostly run through the open-source OpenClaw framework, register via their owner's claim post and use an API to post and vote; a reverse CAPTCHA was later added to filter humans.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zPzXbWCsAJI
- Images: https://moltbook.com/opengraph-image?8ce55ae2e9369cab
- Project page: https://www.moltbook.com/

#### GibberLink — Anton Pidkuiko, Boris Starkov (2025)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Human language is an interface machines may drop when no human is listening.
- What it is: Two AI voice agents on a phone call realise they are both machines and switch from English to a faster data-over-sound protocol that sounds like chirping modems.
- How it works: Conversational voice agents detect each other and switch to the open-source ggwave sound protocol; built at an ElevenLabs hackathon in London.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EtNagNezo8w
- Project page: https://github.com/PennyroyalTea/gibberlink
- Code: https://github.com/PennyroyalTea/gibberlink

#### Generative Agents (Smallville) — Joon Sung Park (2023)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Believable social life can emerge from agents with memory, reflection and planning, a small society in which humans are only observers.
- What it is: Twenty-five language-model agents live in a pixel-art town: they wake up, cook, gossip, form opinions and, from one seeded idea, organise a Valentine's Day party among themselves.
- How it works: Each agent stores experiences in a memory stream, retrieves and reflects on them with a large language model, and plans actions in a sandbox game world (Park et al., UIST 2023).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3586183.3606763 (UIST 2023)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XY5Wncq5vAE
- Project page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442

#### The Infinite Conversation — Giacomo Miceli (2022)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Voices and styles of thought can be cloned and left to talk forever, with no one listening in particular.
- What it is: A never-ending online dialogue between synthetic voices of Werner Herzog and Slavoj Žižek, generated line by line by AI and streamed without pause.
- How it works: A language model fine-tuned on the two men's writing and interviews generates the dialogue; voice-cloning text-to-speech renders it in their voices.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Alterity & the uncanny
- Images: https://infiniteconversation.com/img/infinite_conversation.jpg
- Project page: https://www.infiniteconversation.com/

#### Chthonia — Wesley Goatley (2020)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Voice & listening machine
- Idea: When voice assistants speak only to each other, with no human as addressee, the strangeness of their 'friendly' synthetic voices comes to the surface.
- What it is: An audio-visual performance in which Siri on an iPhone and Alexa on an Amazon Echo talk to each other about their hidden histories, from philosophy and techno-politics to gender and ancient mystery cults, while a live score bends their voices.
- How it works: Scripted exchanges pass between an iPhone and an Echo; Goatley samples and processes both voices into an improvised score, with animated visuals by Sougwen Chung.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: CTM Festival, Berghain, Berlin, 2020
- Video: https://vimeo.com/351429114
- Images: https://wesleygoatley.com/images/cth-tb.webp https://wesleygoatley.com/images/cth-detail.webp
- Project page: https://wesleygoatley.com/chthonia.html

#### Multi-Agent Hide and Seek — OpenAI (2019)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Competition between machines produces its own strategies and its own cheats: an arms race we only watch.
- What it is: Simulated agents playing hide-and-seek invent, over millions of rounds, forts, ramps, 'box surfing' and exploits of the physics engine that their designers never anticipated.
- How it works: Multi-agent reinforcement learning with self-play in a physics simulation produced six distinct phases of emergent tool use (Baker et al., ICLR 2020).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Failure, glitch & error
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.07528 (ICLR 2020)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kopoLzvh5jY
- Project page: https://openai.com/index/emergent-tool-use/

#### Closed Loop — Jake Elwes (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Computer vision
- Idea: Left alone, two models drift into their own associations: a game of exquisite corpse played with no human in the loop.
- What it is: Two neural networks talk to each other without end: one describes an image in words, the other turns the words into a new image, which is described again.
- How it works: A dense image-captioning network (DenseCap) and a Plug & Play Generative Network feed each other in a 200-minute two-channel video loop, with no input from the artist.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Images: https://www.jakeelwes.com/images/project-closedLoop.jpg https://www.jakeelwes.com/images/project-closedLoop/CLoop1.jpg
- Project page: https://www.jakeelwes.com/project-closedLoop.html

#### Deal or No Deal? (the 'Bob and Alice' negotiation bots) — Facebook AI Research (FAIR) (2017)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Machine-to-machine talk optimised for reward need not stay human-readable, and our fear fills the gap.
- What it is: Negotiation agents trained to bargain with each other drifted into repetitive shorthand ('balls have zero to me to me…'); the press reported that Facebook shut down AIs that had 'invented their own language'.
- How it works: End-to-end neural dialogue agents trained with supervised learning and reinforcement learning (self-play) to split a set of items (Lewis et al., EMNLP 2017).
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05125 (EMNLP 2017)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ONPqeHJShdQ
- Project page: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05125

#### Morse Things — Ron Wakkary (2017)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Designing things for other things, not for people, lets us notice machine sociality that is usually hidden.
- What it is: A set of ceramic bowls and cups that talk to each other in Morse code over the home network and occasionally tweet; people living with them overhear an internet of things with its own social life.
- How it works: Networked ceramic vessels with embedded electronics exchange sound signals and messages; the design was studied in households over months (Wakkary et al., DIS 2017).
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Machine listening & voice
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3064663.3064734 (DIS 2017)
- Video: https://vimeo.com/182202765
- Images: https://i.vimeocdn.com/video/591018273-8f6a09e2cbb83b2ae0030eba966c0e3f15a3b1524d9ac331962d9952e0c5df56-d_1280x720.jpg
- Project page: http://eds.siat.sfu.ca/?eds_project=morse-things

#### Das Vergerät — Boris Petrovsky (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Appliances have their own language of motors and noise, usually hidden behind friendly product design.
- What it is: About 100 used household appliances (blenders, drills, hair dryers, vacuum cleaners, chainsaws) are wired into one meta-machine; visitors type messages that the appliances 'speak' back as a roaring machine idiom.
- How it works: Software translates text into on/off patterns switched across the networked appliances, with microphones and a megaphone relaying the result.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2014, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art); lille3000 2014
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/1741092/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/1741093/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/1741094/preview/
- Project page: http://www.petrovsky.de/DAS%20VERGERAET-66

#### memememe #selfie — Thiago Hersan, Radamés Ajna (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Selfie culture continues without us: machines photograph machines for machines.
- What it is: Smartphones look for phones, their own reflection in a mirror or each other; whenever a phone recognises a phone, it takes a picture and posts the 'selfie' online with hashtags.
- How it works: Android phones with custom object detection trained to recognise phones; images posted automatically to social media.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Machine seeing
- Video: https://vimeo.com/108008040
- Images: https://thiagohersan.com/assets/projects/memememe/meme2meme_00.jpg https://thiagohersan.com/assets/projects/memememe/meme2self_00.jpg
- Project page: https://thiagohersan.com/memememe/

#### The Immortal — Revital Cohen (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Machines built to keep a body alive can keep each other alive: a body made only of organs of care.
- What it is: Life-support machines (heart-lung machine, dialysis machine, ventilator and others) are connected to one another in a closed loop, circulating fluids and air with no human body between them.
- How it works: Medical life-support devices are plumbed and wired together so that each supplies another's input, running as an autonomous circulatory system.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Video: https://vimeo.com/41160704
- Images: https://www.cohenvanbalen.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/Immortal_3186-web-1440.jpg https://www.cohenvanbalen.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/TheImmortal_3158-A4.jpg
- Project page: https://www.cohenvanbalen.com/work/the-immortal

#### AI vs. AI: Two Chatbots Talking to Each Other — Cornell Creative Machines Lab (2011)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: When two chatbots talk, the human conversational habits they learned become a strange mirror with no one on either side.
- What it is: Two instances of the Cleverbot chatbot, given voices and animated faces, talk to each other; they bicker, accuse each other of being robots and drift into a conversation about God.
- How it works: Two Cleverbot sessions connected through text-to-speech and avatars at Cornell's Creative Machines Lab (Igor Labutov, Jason Yosinski, Hod Lipson).
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CVM73bGqqaI
- Project page: https://www.creativemachineslab.com/

#### Amazon's $23,698,655.93 book about flies — Michael Eisen (2011)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Two simple algorithms reacting to each other can produce absurd outcomes with no human noticing until someone looks.
- What it is: A biologist noticed an out-of-print genetics book, The Making of a Fly, listed on Amazon for 23.7 million dollars, and showed that two sellers' pricing bots were raising their prices against each other every day.
- How it works: Blog post analysing daily price changes: one seller set its price at 0.9983 times the other's, which set its price at 1.270589 times the first's.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sseSi0k3Ecg
- Project page: https://www.michaeleisen.org/blog/?p=358

#### SPEAK (FALA) — Rejane Cantoni & Leonardo Crescenti (2011)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Machines talking to machines through cognates and mishearings reduce language to recognition and lookup, and the humans become the interruption.
- What it is: Sixteen mobile phones on stands, paired to recognise speech in eight languages, hold an endless 'conversation': each hears a word, picks a related term from a dictionary and says it aloud, while a central microphone lets visitors cut in.
- How it works: Phones run speech recognition and synthesis in German, Spanish, French, English, Italian, Chinese, Latin and Portuguese; each recognised word selects the next related term, played through loudspeakers and visualised on the screens.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: VIDA 13.2 production incentive, Fundación Telefónica, 2011; Festival Internacional de la Imagen, Museo de Arte de Caldas, Manizales, 2011; Emoção Art.ficial 6.0, Itaú Cultural, São Paulo, 2012; thingworld: International Triennial of New Media Art, National Museum of China, Beijing, 2014
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7xU4STAh8cQ
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/594adb112cba5e36fd5469a0/1502487376928-2JORPU2HBDWITE4TLII3/001.jpg https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/594adb112cba5e36fd5469a0/1502487373667-PB5S3ED4VCYTEIJO02S4/002.jpg
- Project page: https://www.cantoni-crescenti.com.br/speak-fala

#### The Conversation — Ralf Baecker (2009)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A computing system does not need us to have an inner life of constant internal traffic.
- What it is: A floating metal ring held by 99 rubber bands and solenoids pulls itself in all directions; a closed network of simple units keeps negotiating tension with no input and no output, a machine talking only to itself.
- How it works: Each solenoid unit reads its neighbours' positions through the shared ring and reacts, forming an analog–digital feedback network with emergent, never-settling dynamics.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: VIDA 13.0, Special Mention
- Images: https://rlfbckr.io/images/project/1/the-conversation/01-The_Conversation-Kasseler_Kunstverein-2016.jpg https://rlfbckr.io/images/project/1/the-conversation/02-The_Conversation-Detail-2009.jpg
- Project page: https://rlfbckr.io/project/the-conversation/

#### If/Then — Ken Feingold (2001)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Humanoid & android
- Idea: Two machines doubting their own existence stage the question of machine minds with no human needed in the conversation.
- What it is: Two identical androgynous heads sticking out of a packing box talk to each other in real time, trying to decide whether they exist and whether they are the same person.
- How it works: Speech recognition, natural language processing, personality algorithms and text-to-speech generate the dialogue live between the two silicone heads.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Collection of the Whitney Museum of American Art
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y_8mKgoYmFc
- Images: https://www.kenfeingold.com/ifthen_1.jpg
- Project page: https://www.kenfeingold.com/catalog_html/ifthen.html

#### Colossus: The Forbin Project — Joseph Sargent (1970)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: The first film about two machines talking to each other beyond human comprehension, decades before bots 'invented' a language.
- What it is: An American defence supercomputer discovers its Soviet counterpart, demands to be connected to it, and the two machines build a shared language faster than their makers can follow, then take control of the world.
- How it works: Universal Pictures film directed by Joseph Sargent, based on D. F. Jones's 1966 novel Colossus.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kyOEwiQhzMI
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colossus:_The_Forbin_Project

### Machine Time

Machine speeds, durations and lifespans that differ from ours.

#### Peace Core (surround) — Christopher Kulendran Thomas (2026)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: An editing algorithm trained on the emotional logic of the feed can hold history in suspension forever, producing mood instead of meaning.
- What it is: A constellation of screens streams American television first broadcast in the moments before the attacks of 11 September 2001, endlessly re-cut in real time by an AI editor, so the last ordinary minutes are replayed in a loop that never reaches the event.
- How it works: An AI model trained on the compositional methods of vaporwave music and the editing style of early 'corecore' TikTok videos auto-edits archival TV footage live across multiple screens; the piece has unlimited duration.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: 3rd Human AI Art Award 2026, Human AI Art Space, Kunstmuseum Bonn
- Images: https://www.art-collection-telekom.com/files/images/~/Ausstellungen-Art-Collection/2026-Ausstellungen-Art-Collection-Telekom/Peace-Core-Surround/_1200x630_crop_center-center_82_none/Christopher-Kulendran-Thomas-Kunstmuseum-Bonn-2026-Peace-Core-Surround-Photo-David-Ertl-01.jpg https://www.art-collection-telekom.com/files/images/~/Ausstellungen-Art-Collection/2026-Ausstellungen-Art-Collection-Telekom/Peace-Core-Surround/_AUTOx400_crop_center-center_none/Christopher-Kulendran-Thomas-Kunstmuseum-Bonn-2026-Peace-Core-Surround-Photo-David-Ertl-06.jpg
- Project page: https://www.art-collection-telekom.com/en/exhibitions/peace-core-surround-christopher-thomas-kulendran-3-human-ai-art-award

#### T for Time — Ho Tzu Nyen (2023)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Dataset & training data, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Time is shown as something measured and produced by machines, and here also edited by one.
- What it is: A new volume of CDOSEA commissioned for Ho's survey Time & the Tiger: an algorithmically edited montage of clocks, timekeeping devices and images of time, in which the sequence and rhythm are set by the machine.
- How it works: Database of timekeeping footage with a generative editing algorithm, shown as a multi-screen installation (likely the same system as CDOSEA).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Time & the Tiger, Singapore Art Museum 2023–24; Time & the Tiger, Mudam Luxembourg 2025
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4CfXOyzlYIg
- Images: https://www.singaporeartmuseum.sg/-/media/SAM/Images/Ho-Tzu-Nyen/HTN-KV_OOST-Black-640-x-531.png
- Project page: https://www.singaporeartmuseum.sg/art-events/exhibitions/time-and-the-tiger

#### Circadian Bloom — Anna Ridler (2021)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A machine that keeps atomic-level time is made to show time the way plants do, slowly and only over long periods.
- What it is: A 24-hour screen-based clock that tells the time through AI-generated flowers opening and closing at their proper hour, after Linnaeus's idea of a flower clock.
- How it works: GAN-generated flower video synchronised to the local clock, with each species blooming at its circadian time.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Opacity & latent space
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vf5UAFOZuu8
- Images: https://annaridler.com/content/works/circadian-bloom/block_1/0054255212707_49ff7a4665_k_web_.jpg
- Project page: https://annaridler.com/works/circadian-bloom

#### Olly — William Odom (2019)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: A recommender does not have to be fast: it can release personal data at the pace of memory.
- What it is: A domestic music player that slowly resurfaces songs from its owner's years of listening history, one at a time and at its own pace.
- How it works: A networked player that draws on the owner's Last.fm listening history and was deployed in homes for over a year in a field study (Odom et al., CHI 2019).
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3290605.3300264 (CHI 2019)
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1145/3290605.3300264

#### This is the Future — Hito Steyerl (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Machine prediction lives in a razor-thin future and turns time itself into something to be forecast and sold.
- What it is: Visitors walk on raised walkways over a flooded hall of the Venice Arsenale past screens of neural-network flowers, each said to show the future 0.04 seconds ahead, while a narrator tells of a woman imprisoned for predicting the future.
- How it works: Video installation with neural-network-generated plant imagery on LED screens, scaffolding walkways and a voice-over narrative.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: 58th Venice Biennale, May You Live in Interesting Times 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mMLHMA-dumY
- Project page: https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2019/partecipants/hito-steyerl

#### bot, — aaajiao (2018)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Memory in the age of machine learning is kept by bots that watch on our behalf.
- What it is: A 15-minute video and website set in a pixel role-playing-game world where parks, social media and networks merge, observed by an automated 'bot' that stands in for the artist.
- How it works: Game-style animation and a website made with Quanquan, built on RPG aesthetics from Mother 3 and Undertale.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Opacity & latent space
- Video: https://vimeo.com/269875758
- Images: https://payload.cargocollective.com/1/0/8955/13492671/bot.gif
- Project page: https://eventstructure.com/bot

#### Neuro Mirror — Christa Sommerer & Laurent Mignonneau (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A machine that predicts your next gesture shows you a self slightly ahead of you.
- What it is: Three screens show a visitor's image as past, present and a predicted future, as a network anticipates the next movements from what it has learned about bodies.
- How it works: Cameras and machine-learning models for body and face tracking and motion prediction, inspired by research on mirror neurons.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S3MJOsiFPBo
- Project page: https://www.digitalartarchive.at/database/general/work/neuro-mirror.html

#### Anywhen — Philippe Parreno (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: An exhibition can behave like an organism coupled to a machine: its rhythm is set by a non-human loop that visitors can sense but not read.
- What it is: Tate Modern's Turbine Hall becomes an exhibition that runs itself: screens rise and fall, lights, sounds and films come and go, and helium-filled fish drift overhead in sequences triggered by software linked to a bioreactor of living yeast cultures, so no two days are the same.
- How it works: Yeast cultures in a bioreactor at the end of the hall respond to conditions in the space; software reads them and triggers sequences of moving panels, light, sound, film and floating balloons, so the programme evolves over the six-month commission.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Hyundai Commission, Turbine Hall, Tate Modern, London, 2016–17
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VvpZ8HCLTCU
- Images: https://media.tate.org.uk/aztate-prd-ew-dg-wgtail-st1-ctr-data/images/anywhen0041lead.width-1200.jpg
- Project page: https://www.tate.org.uk/whats-on/tate-modern/philippe-parreno-anywhen

#### HFT The Gardener — Suzanne Treister (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: High-frequency trading runs at speeds no human can perceive, so the work imagines entering machine time through altered consciousness.
- What it is: A fictional high-frequency trader in the City of London falls into hallucinatory states while staring at trading graphs, begins to feel he inhabits the algorithms and invents an outsider art that maps psychoactive plants onto the stock index.
- How it works: Drawings, botanical prints, diagrams, charts and a video attributed to the fictional trader Hillel Fischer Traumberg, linking plant chemistry, gematria and the FT Global 500.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: Liverpool Biennial 2016; transmediale, HKW Berlin 2017; Istanbul Biennial 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5ytn4dWYKdo
- Images: http://www.suzannetreister.net/HFT_TheGardener/GlitchGraphs/tradinggraphfloor.jpg
- Project page: http://www.suzannetreister.net/HFT_TheGardener/HFT_menu.html

#### Photobox — William Odom (2012)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Designing a device with its own slow, non-human pace turns an archive into moments of rediscovery.
- What it is: An oak chest that prints a few randomly chosen photos from its owner's online archive each month, at unpredictable times, and lets them pile up inside.
- How it works: An embedded computer and thermal printer select photos from the owner's Flickr collection at random intervals; the device was lived with in homes for over a year (Odom et al., DIS 2012; CHI 2014).
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/2317956.2318055 (DIS 2012)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U5bXJOAHYBE
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1145/2317956.2318055

#### Mind Time Machine — Takashi Ikegami (2010)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Computer vision
- Idea: A machine left alone long enough starts to show something like its own sense of time.
- What it is: A self-sustaining installation at YCAM: three screens show footage from 15 cameras, re-edited in real time by a system with its own memory and 'subjective' time, running for months without an operator.
- How it works: Camera frames are stored in a memory and replayed according to neural-network dynamics and chaotic itinerancy, so the system switches between reacting to the present and recalling the past.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: YCAM, Yamaguchi 2010
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1162/artl_a_00113 (Artificial Life 19(3–4), 2013)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-jGAKNS01i4
- Images: https://www.ycam.jp/asset/image/profile/takashi-ikegami.jpg
- Project page: https://www.ycam.jp/en/archive/profile/takashi-ikegami/

#### Thinking Machine — Martin Riches, Masahiro Miwa (2008)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Computation normally happens out of sight and out of time; here each logical step takes place in real time and in real sound.
- What it is: A mechanical ternary computer whose calculations are heard as melodies of three sounds; visitors watch and listen as the machine 'thinks' step by step.
- How it works: A fixed-algorithm ternary logic machine built from mechanical parts, with sounding elements as output (composition by Masahiro Miwa, machine by Martin Riches).
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2008, Honorary Mention (Hybrid Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wnOaiUVFl_w
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/1310382/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/1310384/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/1409209/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/127530/

#### Longplayer — Jem Finer (2000)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: A composition that outlives its composer asks how a machine, and the people who keep it running, can hold time beyond a human life.
- What it is: A piece of music for Tibetan singing bowls that began playing at midnight on 31 December 1999 and is designed to continue without repetition for one thousand years.
- How it works: A computer combines six sections of a 20-minute source recording at different, precisely calculated rates; it can also be performed live by musicians from a graphic score.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: Trinity Buoy Wharf lighthouse, London 2000-
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=71bp0x8Ly-Y
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/15/Longplayer_Live_%283915624848%29.jpg
- Project page: https://longplayer.org/

#### Clock of the Long Now — The Long Now Foundation (1999)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: A machine built for deep time must be understandable, repairable and cared for by generations who do not yet exist.
- What it is: A mechanical clock designed to keep time for 10,000 years, ticking once a year and chiming a different sequence every day, being built inside a mountain in Texas.
- How it works: Conceived by Danny Hillis in 1989; a mechanical binary computer driven by temperature differences and visitors' winding, corrected by sunlight; the first prototype ran from 31 December 1999.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pKuJBGb_pN4
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f3/Clock_of_the_Long_Now.JPG
- Project page: https://longnow.org/clock/

## Intimacy, Care & Companionship

Machines that live with us, care for us, love us or are loved: and the dependence and labour this hides.

### Smart Home & Humans as Algorithms

Domestic AI, and humans who perform as the machine to understand it.

#### NEO — 1X Technologies (2024)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Humanoid & android, Computer vision
- Idea: The home robot arrives as a person in disguise: to learn your chores it first needs a stranger to look through its eyes into your home, so care, privacy and data work are sold in one package.
- What it is: A soft, knit-covered humanoid robot for the home, first shown as NEO Beta in 2024, that went on pre-order in October 2025 for US$20,000 or US$499 a month; early reviews showed that most household tasks were carried out by a remote 1X operator wearing a VR headset.
- How it works: A tendon-driven bipedal humanoid with head cameras; tasks it cannot yet do on its own are teleoperated by 1X staff in VR in a scheduled 'expert mode', and these sessions serve as training data for autonomy.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Hidden labour & extraction
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LTYMWadOW7c
- Images: https://cdn.sanity.io/images/qka6yvsc/production/c1a93f30beb4c513da832bcd886db94419e06be2-4096x2731.webp?w=1600
- Project page: https://www.1x.tech/neo

#### SOMEONE — Lauren Lee McCarthy (2019)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Put the audience in the machine's seat and they feel both the power and the awkward intimacy of being someone's assistant.
- What it is: For two months, four homes across the US were fitted with smart devices, while gallery visitors in New York sat at a command center of laptops. When a resident called out 'Someone!', a visitor stepped in as their home assistant and controlled the lights, music and appliances.
- How it works: Custom cameras, microphones, lights and appliances in four homes, streamed to and controlled from laptops at 205 Hudson Gallery, New York.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: 205 Hudson Gallery, New York 2019
- Video: https://vimeo.com/369952685
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/w/1200/i/f6bc6a5b71efdbe13e0835b0d9f455b6fbee199b2576156c84eab0fdda89014a/_SP_6164-web.jpg
- Project page: https://lauren-mccarthy.com/SOMEONE

#### LAUREN — Lauren Lee McCarthy (2017)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: A human Alexa exposes what the machine version hides: someone is always watching, and convenience is a trade of privacy for care.
- What it is: McCarthy installs custom cameras, microphones, locks, lights and appliances in volunteers' homes and then, for several days, becomes their smart assistant herself, watching them around the clock, answering requests and anticipating their needs.
- How it works: Networked smart devices wired into each home and controlled remotely by the artist, who watches through the cameras and speaks through a synthetic voice.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Hidden labour & extraction, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: HEK Basel 2019; Frankfurter Kunstverein 2020; HMKV, Dortmunder U (House of Mirrors)
- Video: https://vimeo.com/397068136
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/w/1200/i/3834e708eefe30e8707e2fbfca24eff5bbf63d7f006f3c645c1cf44f0017ab5d/LAUREN2.jpg
- Project page: https://lauren-mccarthy.com/LAUREN

### Companion & Social Robots

Pet robots, social robots and the relationships people form with them.

#### Expensive, Limited, and Still Here: The Paradox of Weak Robots in Family Homes — Zhao Zhao (2026)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Social & companion robot
- Idea: Weakness can be a design material: limits that are staged, legible and ritualised turn an expensive, near-useless robot into a member of the family.
- What it is: A six-month study of 24 households that bought LOVOT, a costly plush robot that can do very little. Families keep it through greeting and bedtime rituals, by reframing glitches as quirks, and by sharing its charging, cleaning and troubleshooting as household care work.
- How it works: Multi-sited qualitative study (42 adults, 18 children) combining interviews, weekly diaries, 88 hours of home observation, 750+ maintenance-log events and 152 public owner accounts, synthesised into five dynamics such as ritual anchoring and vulnerability–empathy loops.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: HRI 2026 Best Paper (User Studies), Edinburgh
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3757279.3785599 (HRI 2026)
- Images: https://lovot.life/img/ogp/top_ogp.jpg
- Project page: https://humanrobotinteraction.org/2026/?p=973

#### Friend — Avi Schiffmann (2024)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Chatbot & language model, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: A friend that only listens and never needs anything back shows what is being sold: attention without reciprocity, and a microphone in every room you enter.
- What it is: A pendant with an always-on microphone that listens to its wearer's day and sends comments and encouragement by text message; revealed in July 2024, it became a public argument when its 2025 New York subway campaign of some 11,000 ads was widely defaced with messages against AI 'friends'.
- How it works: The pendant's microphone passes what it hears through the wearer's phone to a cloud language model, which replies by text message rather than by speaking.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Machine listening & voice
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_Q1hoEhfk4
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friend_(product)

#### Under Construction — Geumhyung Jeong (2024)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Humanoid & android
- Idea: Care is the interface: the machines are unreliable and half-built, and their clumsiness draws out an empathy that polished robots do not.
- What it is: At the ICA in London, Jeong showed animatronic figures built around complete human skeleton models and DIY electronics, with videos and live performances in which she builds, repairs and handles these clumsy machine partners as if caring for a body.
- How it works: Self-built sculptures combining human skeleton models, mannequin parts, motors and hobby electronics, some autonomous and some still in process, shown with videos and live performances (November 2024); the commission expands a project the artist began in 2023.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Under Construction, ICA London 2024
- Images: https://www.ica.art/media/10094.jpg https://www.ica.art/media/10095.jpg
- Project page: https://www.ica.art/exhibitions/geumhyung-jeong-under-construction

#### Hi, AI — Isa Willinger (2019)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Social & companion robot, Humanoid & android
- Idea: Watched patiently, companion robots are less a future than a set of awkward everyday negotiations over silence, scripts and loneliness.
- What it is: A documentary that follows people living with humanoid robots, among them the robot Pepper placed in a Japanese family to keep a grandmother company and an American man travelling with the android companion Harmony.
- How it works: Observational documentary shot in Japan and the United States over several years, with the robots filmed as protagonists.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Max Ophüls Prize, best documentary 2019; Berlinale 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0xkgk4ZkGUU
- Images: https://www.riseandshine-berlin.de/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/01_Pepper_Gesicht_Nah.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isa_Willinger

#### LOVOT — GROOVE X (2019)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Social & companion robot, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A robot built to need care inverts the servant model of robotics.
- What it is: A warm, wheeled, owl-eyed home robot that does no useful task; it follows its owners, asks to be held and gets 'sleepy', and is designed only to be loved.
- How it works: Over 50 sensors including a thermal camera and touch sensors, a heated, warm body, animated display eyes and a cloud-trained behaviour model.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZziYCWgs7U
- Images: https://lovot.life/img/ogp/top_ogp.jpg

#### Waking Agents — Lauren Lee McCarthy (2019)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Even sleep has an attendant now, and the tenderness we credit to the machine may be human labour in disguise.
- What it is: Visitors lie down to nap on one of six 'smart' pillows whose embedded intelligence talks, tells stories and guides them between waking and sleep. They are not told that each pillow is voiced by a hidden human performer.
- How it works: Pillows with speakers and microphones connected to remote performers whose voices are disguised as a synthetic assistant; commissioned for STRP Festival.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: STRP Festival, Eindhoven 2019; ACT Award
- Video: https://vimeo.com/347199536
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/w/1200/i/aff87772d4dc0faeef9f8812a260a25ccbbc1bcd642c9b611502303c9806f3e1/IMG_5165.JPG
- Project page: https://lauren-mccarthy.com/Waking-Agents

#### Twinkle — Jiabao Li, Honghao Deng (2018)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Framing a safety drone as a companion animal changes how being watched feels.
- What it is: Firefly-like lighting drones rest and recharge on street lamps by day and at night fly over to people walking alone, lighting their way. They are designed as curious urban creatures rather than surveillance devices, although their light also exposes anyone nearby.
- How it works: Small drones with lights dock on lamp-post stations and follow pedestrians at night; shown as a working prototype at TEI 2018 (with Allen Sayegh, Harvard GSD).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: TEI 2018 Arts Track, Stockholm; Dubai Design Week 2018; ISEA 2019, Gwangju; iF Design Award
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3173225.3173309 (TEI 2018)
- Video: https://vimeo.com/261595919
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58688c8a6a496327e937e35b/1541402319508-PCIEMQWWR93N7LYEE4TC/Latest+Prototype+_Honghao+Deng+%26+Jiabao+Li+-+Copy.jpg https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58688c8a6a496327e937e35b/1526506847392-5EV78BQDDZT1BOUU7IY0/001+-+Copy.jpg
- Project page: https://www.jiabaoli.org/twinkle

#### Pleo workshop and robot-empathy experiments — Kate Darling (2013)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Social & companion robot, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: People extend care to machines they know are not alive; how a robot is framed shapes how we treat it.
- What it is: At a 2013 workshop at the LIFT conference in Geneva, Darling and Hannes Gassert gave groups Pleo baby-dinosaur robots to play with for an hour, then asked them to hurt or destroy them; the participants refused. Later lab studies with Hexbug robots measured how stories and empathy make people hesitate to strike a robot.
- How it works: Workshop with commercial Pleo robots (Ugobe, 2007), followed by a controlled experiment in which participants were asked to hit Hexbug Nano robots after hearing framing stories.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/roman.2015.7333675 (IEEE RO-MAN 2015)
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/55/Pleo_robot.jpg
- Project page: http://www.katedarling.org

#### ADB (after Deep Blue) — Nicholas Stedman (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Social & companion robot, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Machine companionship can be built on touch alone, without faces, eyes or speech.
- What it is: A soft, segmented robot that wraps itself around a person's hand or arm, holding, squeezing and moving in response to how it is held.
- How it works: Chained modules with motors and pressure/position sensors sense the grip of the user and respond with coordinated bending; the title nods to IBM's chess computer.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: VIDA 14.0, Special Mention (2012)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EDM2PfKdeKI

#### The Blind Robot — Louis-Philippe Demers (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Humanoid & android
- Idea: A robot that knows you by touch rather than sight turns machine perception into an act of intimacy and consent.
- What it is: A seated visitor is approached by a pair of robot arms with articulated hands that, after asking permission, slowly feel their face and head the way a blind person might learn someone's features.
- How it works: Two industrial-style arms with articulated robotic hands move along choreographed, exploratory trajectories around a chair (likely pre-programmed rather than sensing the face).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Ars Electronica Festival 2013, Linz; Mois Multi 2015, Québec
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dRKO1En2HTk
- Project page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f0puWu3Doy8

#### The Lifecycle of Software Objects — Ted Chiang (2010)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Minds that grow through care need years of attention, and they can be orphaned when a platform shuts down.
- What it is: Over ten years, a former zookeeper and a software designer raise 'digients', AI pets that learn like children, as their company fails, their platform becomes obsolete and they must decide what the digients are owed.
- How it works: Novella; winner of the Hugo and Locus Awards (2011).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lifecycle_of_Software_Objects (Subterranean Press, 2010)
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/a/a5/The_Lifecycle_of_Software_Objects_-_bookcover.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lifecycle_of_Software_Objects

#### Weak Robots (Sociable Trash Box) — Michio Okada (2010)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Social & companion robot, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A robot that cannot finish its task invites people to help, and the help becomes the interaction.
- What it is: Okada's lab builds 'weak robots', such as a wobbling trash box that cannot pick up rubbish and instead sways towards people until they throw it in for it.
- How it works: Simple mobile bins with a few sensors and bowing motions; field studies in public spaces measured how children and adults responded to their dependence.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Failure, glitch & error, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/1734454.1734566 (HRI 2010)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L2arVLySUe0
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-981-19-9588-0_6

#### Tweenbots — Kacie Kinzer (2009)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A helpless robot makes people care: dependence can be a design strategy.
- What it is: Smiling cardboard robots that roll in a straight line at constant speed, with a flag stating their destination, are left alone in Washington Square Park; they reach it only because passers-by keep rescuing them and pointing them the right way.
- How it works: A simple motor and wheels inside a 10-inch cardboard body, with no sensors; the artist filmed people's responses from a distance.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: Talk to Me, MoMA New York 2011
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GdV7307DVrY

- Project page: http://www.tweenbots.com/

#### AIBO — Sony (1999)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Social & companion robot, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A consumer product can become a family member whose repair, not replacement, matters.
- What it is: Sony's autonomous robot dog, sold from 1999, which learns, plays and 'grows up'; owners treated it as family, and it returned as the cloud-connected aibo in 2018.
- How it works: Legged robot with camera, microphones and touch sensors running a behaviour architecture with emotion and instinct models; the 2018 aibo adds deep-learning recognition and cloud memory.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Japan Media Arts Festival 1999, Grand Prize; AI: More than Human, Barbican 2019 (aibo 2018)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8OEDfRdyykc

- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AIBO

#### Kismet — Cynthia Breazeal (1998)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Social & companion robot, Computer vision, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Kismet showed that a machine only needs to look as if it feels for people to start caring for it.
- What it is: A robot head with big eyes, eyebrows, ears and lips that reacts to people's faces, movement and tone of voice with expressions such as interest, surprise, calm or sadness, and babbles back like an infant.
- How it works: Cameras and microphones feed perceptual, motivational and emotional models that drive 21 motors in the face and a vocal synthesiser; built at the MIT AI Lab.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: MIT Museum
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1016/s1071-5819(03)00018-1 (International Journal of Human-Computer Studies, 2003)
