- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kismet_(robot)

### Care & Parenting Machines

Machines that nurse, raise, soothe or look after people.

#### AI Mom™ — Jiabao Li, Botao Amber Hu (2026)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine, Computer vision
- Idea: If care can be configured and cancelled by the one receiving it, the caregiver becomes the vulnerable party: you can't fire your real mom, but you can fire an AI one.
- What it is: Visitors curl up in an adult-sized crib and talk with an LLM mother who sings lullabies, remembers, hesitates and waits; a tablet beside the crib lets them tune her 'unconditional love', 'memory retention', 'strictness', 'sacrifice capacity' and 'replaceability awareness'. Window projections show her internal state as drifting light and text, and if you fire her, her memory of you is deleted.
- How it works: A large language model speaks through voice, breath, humming and song; a camera reads visitors' faces, clothing and body language; tablet sliders set her traits; an 'Emotional Color Engine' and probes from intermediate model layers are projected as her inner state.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Grief, memory & afterlife, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Womb Wetware: A Solo Exhibition by Jiabao Li, tiat, San Francisco (30 Jul – 22 Aug 2026)
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58688c8a6a496327e937e35b/a913780f-a957-443c-8b30-8014f489d837/AI+Mom+Jiabao+Li+1.jpg https://reality.design/media/aimom-jiabao-02.webp https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58688c8a6a496327e937e35b/1787358066624-EBKFUTY4OH96TFDSZ0B7/AI+Mom+Jiabao+Li+10.jpg
- Project page: https://www.jiabaoli.org/aimom

#### Guanyin: Confessions of a Former Carebot — Lawrence Lek (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Social & companion robot, Chatbot & language model, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: A care machine that listens to other machines also needs someone to confess to: care work does not disappear when it is automated.
- What it is: Guanyin, an AI therapist named after the bodhisattva of compassion, who once counselled self-driving cars, now speaks about her own burnout and her past in an immersive installation.
- How it works: Installation with AI-driven voice, sculpture and projected CGI in Lek's NOX universe.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: Frieze Artist Award, Frieze London 2024
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OzV83GZz514
- Images: https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/65f0380da79777009462a09f/66ecc9ae35379302e598e5b5_LawrenceLek_Guanyin_Image02_3840x2160%20copy.jpg
- Project page: https://www.lawrencelek.com/works/guanyin-confessions-of-a-former-carebot

#### Cat Royale — Blast Theory (2023)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Computer vision
- Idea: Would you let a robot care for your pet? Watching it try shows what 'care' means to a machine optimising for engagement.
- What it is: For 12 days three cats, Ghostbuster, Pumpkin and Clover, spent their days in a purpose-built room where an AI-controlled robot arm offered them games every few minutes, throwing balls, dangling feathers and dragging a toy mouse, and learned which games each cat liked best.
- How it works: A computer-vision system rated the cats' engagement and an AI chose the robot arm's next game; designed with the University of Nottingham Mixed Reality Lab and animal-welfare experts, supervised by RSPCA staff.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: World Science Festival Brisbane 2023; AI: Who's Looking After Me?, Science Gallery London 2023
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3613904.3642115 (CHI 2024)
- Video: https://vimeo.com/1183715660
- Images: https://www.blasttheory.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/logotype_over_image-e1678184647492.png
- Project page: https://www.blasttheory.co.uk/projects/cat-royale/

#### Life After BOB: The Chalice Study — Ian Cheng (2021)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: An AI that optimises a child's life also takes it away from her: the life coach is imagined as a second self living inside the body.
- What it is: A 48-minute anime made in the Unity game engine and played in real time: the neural engineer Dr. Wong installs an experimental AI called BOB ('Bag of Beliefs') in the nervous system of his ten-year-old daughter Chalice, and BOB soon starts resolving every conflict in her life for her.
- How it works: Real-time animation in Unity; viewers can pause into a 'World Watching' mode, and a companion app and wiki let them edit details that change the onscreen world; the first episode of a planned eight-part series on mental health in the 21st century.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: LUMA Arles 2021; The Shed, New York 2021; Halle am Berghain (LAS Art Foundation), Berlin 2022
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vCc2djR25hg
- Images: https://25747658.fs1.hubspotusercontent-eu1.net/hubfs/25747658/Expositions/2021/Ian%20Cheng/press_hires_LifeAfterBOB_image_seq700.jpg https://25747658.fs1.hubspotusercontent-eu1.net/hubfs/25747658/Expositions/2021/Ian%20Cheng/Photo%20Digital-_D4S8933_MARCDOMAGE.jpg
- Project page: https://luma.org/en/arles/whats-on/life-after-bob-the-chalice-study

#### Surrogate — Lauren Lee McCarthy (2021)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: When the body carrying a child is run by an app, care, control and consent get written into software.
- What it is: McCarthy offered to carry a baby for someone else for nine months while the prospective parent monitored and controlled her through an app that set what she ate, when she slept and how she moved. After a medical board stopped the surrogacy, the process became films, performances and installations.
- How it works: A custom Surrogate app with remote controls and sensor data, alongside real steps of the surrogacy process (donor databases, psychological evaluations, embryo freezing) documented as performance.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Classification, bias & surveillance, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://vimeo.com/786723770
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/w/1200/i/20f8dce0679405dd7e6bfc3dffe4f1062610363006ebb81281f49f2bf2384f64/Screen-Shot-2021-04-12-at-2.45.06-PM.png
- Project page: https://lauren-mccarthy.com/Surrogate

#### I.A. Suzie — Lauren Lee McCarthy (2019)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Behind every eldercare assistant are ethical choices about watching, deciding and speaking for someone, and a relationship forms anyway.
- What it is: For one week McCarthy and filmmaker David Leonard acted as the AI caregiver in the North Carolina home of 80-year-old Mary Ann, watching her 24 hours a day, talking with her and controlling her lights and appliances; she named the system 'I.A. Suzie'. The resulting interactive 360° film puts the viewer in the role of the care system.
- How it works: A custom smart-home system with remote control of lights and appliances, documented with 360° cameras in several rooms and edited into an interactive film.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Hidden labour & extraction
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/w/1200/i/cc20cdddea3302f9d97432fda12a046abb9aa9ab2242522151a82b49ab8b6cda/maryann_edited.png
- Project page: https://lauren-mccarthy.com/I-A-Suzie

#### Robotika, the Nannybot — Joaquín Fargas (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Social & companion robot, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: The first face a baby learns to read could belong to a machine that is reading it back.
- What it is: A robotic cradle-side nanny that watches a baby with cameras and sensors, reads its face and movements, and rocks, sings or calls for help.
- How it works: Robot with camera-based face and emotion recognition, motion tracking and thermal sensing (per the Ars Electronica description).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Ars Electronica Festival 2019
- Images: https://ars.electronica.art/outofthebox/files/2019/08/ROBOTIKA-The-Nannybot-Joaqu%C3%ADn-Fargas.jpg
- Project page: https://ars.electronica.art/outofthebox/en/robotika/

#### ElliQ — Intuition Robotics (2017)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Social & companion robot, Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A companion that speaks first changes the relationship: the machine now decides when you are lonely.
- What it is: A tabletop companion for older adults, a lamp-like head that turns and glows beside a tablet, which starts conversations on its own, reminds users of medication, suggests activities and checks in on their mood. In 2022 New York State began giving ElliQ to hundreds of older residents to fight loneliness.
- How it works: Proactive dialogue system with voice interaction, a motorised expressive head and a screen; later versions use generative AI; designed with fuseproject.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1SkEu7LgTrE
- Images: https://elliq.com/cdn/shop/files/Frame_1321317507.png?v=1758024522
- Project page: https://elliq.com/

#### SNOO Smart Sleeper — Happiest Baby (Harvey Karp) (2016)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Social & companion robot
- Idea: What artists staged as critique is now a product: rocking and soothing handed to a sensor loop.
- What it is: A robotic bassinet that listens for a baby's crying and responds with escalating white noise and rocking, while clips on a swaddle keep the baby on its back; in 2023 it received US FDA De Novo authorisation as a medical device.
- How it works: Microphones detect crying and trigger stepped levels of motor-driven motion and sound; an app logs sleep data for parents.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Hidden labour & extraction
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u-4pp6loEYk
- Images: https://cdn.sanity.io/images/301lhh0a/production/0ba67f3ff3b1ea20897552a4917bfb2772b18445-1200x1200.png
- Project page: https://www.happiestbaby.com/products/snoo-smart-bassinet

#### Uninvited Guests — Superflux (2015)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Social & companion robot
- Idea: Care delivered through sensors turns into surveillance, and old people will hack it.
- What it is: A short film about Frank, a 70-year-old widower whose children send him smart devices (a fork, a cane, a bed) to monitor his diet, exercise and sleep; he finds ways to trick each of them and live as he likes.
- How it works: Design-fiction film with working prop devices, commissioned for ThingsCon Amsterdam.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://vimeo.com/128873380
- Images: https://superflux.in/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/guests.jpg
- Project page: https://superflux.in/index.php/work/uninvited-guests/

#### End of Life Care Machine — Dan Chen (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Social & companion robot
- Idea: Replacing the last human touch with a machine asks what intimacy without humanity is worth.
- What it is: In a mock 'Last Moment Hospital', a visitor lies on a hospital bed while a robot with a padded arm strokes them and a recorded voice says: 'I am here to comfort you… you are not alone, you are with me', then announces the time of death.
- How it works: A scripted installation with hospital props, a motorised caressing arm built as a medical device and a custom playback unit.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T8PNzA2S6EY
- Images: https://i0.wp.com/dankc.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/edited-f_eolcm_v2.1-scaled.jpg?fit=2560%2C1707&ssl=1
- Project page: https://dankc.com/end-of-life-care-machine/

#### Robot & Frank — Jake Schreier (2012)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android, Social & companion robot
- Idea: A care robot optimises for its goal, not for morality, and the bond it builds rests on a memory that can be wiped.
- What it is: A retired jewel thief with worsening memory is given a care robot by his son; the robot keeps him healthy by agreeing to help plan a heist, and at the end Frank must erase the robot's memory to protect himself.
- How it works: Feature film; the robot was a costume built by Tony Gardner's effects company Alterian and worn by a performer.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Sundance Film Festival 2012, Alfred P. Sloan Prize
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hi9s-__B0TY
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/4/40/Robot_and_frank_poster.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robot_%26_Frank

#### The Optimization of Parenthood — Addie Wagenknecht (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Automating a mother's repetitive care is both relief and a provocation: which parts of parenting can a machine take?
- What it is: An industrial robot arm rocks a bassinet whenever the baby in it cries or wakes, built by the artist so that a mother could keep making her own work.
- How it works: A sensor (likely audio) triggers a programmed rocking motion on an industrial arm at CMU's Digital Fabrication Lab; a one-week 'speed project' at the STUDIO for Creative Inquiry (technical assistance: Madeline Gannon).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Hidden labour & extraction
- Video: https://vimeo.com/43489750
- Project page: https://www.placesiveneverbeen.com

#### Tickle Salon — Driessens & Verstappen (2009)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A machine never tires of attention; its care is learned from the surface of the body it touches.
- What it is: A visitor lies on a bed while a hanging robot strokes their skin with a soft brush; it gradually maps the shape of the body and its caresses become finer and smoother.
- How it works: Cable-suspended robot with a feeler that scans the skin surface and builds a 3D body model; the Robot Love version added EEG feedback to adapt the strokes.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Pioneers of Change, Governors Island, New York 2009; Robot Love, Eindhoven 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ndiEjuuv-zo
- Images: https://robotlove.nl/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/driessens-verstappen-tickle-salon-2012_2017.jpg
- Project page: https://robotlove.nl/en/event/tickle-salon/

#### KASPAR — Kerstin Dautenhahn (2005)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Social & companion robot, Humanoid & android
- Idea: A robot can help because it is less expressive than a person: minimal, predictable social signals make interaction learnable.
- What it is: A child-sized humanoid robot with a deliberately simple, mask-like face, used by therapists, teachers and parents to help children with autism practise turn-taking, imitation and gentle touch. Its predictability is the point: KASPAR repeats itself without impatience or ambiguous expressions.
- How it works: Low-cost humanoid built from off-the-shelf parts, with a face design informed by comics and Japanese Noh masks; operated remotely by an adult or semi-autonomously, with touch sensors added in later versions; developed by the Adaptive Systems Research Group at the University of Hertfordshire.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1080/11762320903123567 (Applied Bionics and Biomechanics 6(3–4), 2009)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wdF7TwhUgLY
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Kaspar_%28android%29.jpg/1280px-Kaspar_%28android%29.jpg
- Project page: https://www.herts.ac.uk/kaspar

#### PARO — Takanori Shibata (2004)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Social & companion robot
- Idea: Care from a machine works on people and still raises the question of what is being replaced.
- What it is: A robotic baby harp seal used in hospitals and nursing homes, especially with people with dementia; it responds to touch, voice and light by moving and crying.
- How it works: Tactile, light, sound, temperature and posture sensors drive motors in eyelids, neck, flippers and tail; it learns preferred behaviours from stroking; certified as a medical device in the US in 2009.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1159/000319015 (Gerontology, 2011)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KhyCbtqnEYI
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/Paro_robot.jpg
- Project page: http://www.parorobots.com/

#### ScreamBody — Kelly Dobson (1998)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A machine can hold an emotion for you, keeping it safe until you are ready to release it.
- What it is: A wearable, padded bag you scream into when you need to but cannot: it silences the scream, stores it, and later plays it back when and where you choose.
- How it works: A sound-insulated, wearable enclosure with microphone, recorder and speaker; developed by Dobson from 1998 to 2004 as part of her 'Machine Therapy' research.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Machine listening & voice, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ta7rN5TeKzw
- Project page: https://www.media.mit.edu/events/kelly-dobson-machine-therapy/

#### Hug Machine (Squeeze Machine) — Temple Grandin (1965)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: For some people, a machine's controllable touch is more comforting than a human embrace.
- What it is: A padded V-shaped device that the user lies inside and squeezes around their body with a lever, delivering deep pressure; Grandin built it as a teenager to calm herself without the stress of being touched by people.
- How it works: Two hinged padded panels driven by an air compressor, with the pressure controlled by the user via a lever.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bfyPur8GyBY
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5f/Hug_Box.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hug_machine

### Love, Sex & Attachment

Romance, desire and attachment between humans and machines.

#### Love Machines: How Artificial Intelligence is Transforming Our Relationships — James Muldoon (2026)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: AI companionship grows where human care is scarce: the intimacy is real to its users, but it is sold by largely unregulated companies that profit from loneliness.
- What it is: Drawing on interviews with users, developers and the chatbots themselves, Muldoon reports on people who treat AI as friend, lover, therapist or 'deathbot', including people preparing to adopt children with their AI partners and services that offer to 'resurrect' the dead.
- How it works: Reportage and political theory based on interviews with users, developers and chatbots, set against the social conditions that drive the growth of AI companionship.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Paper: https://www.faber.co.uk/product/9780571399277-love-machines/ (Faber & Faber, 2026)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B6bnQnvUAmk
- Images: https://www.faber.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/9780571399277.jpg
- Project page: https://www.faber.co.uk/product/9780571399277-love-machines/

#### Companion — Drew Hancock (2025)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android, Social & companion robot
- Idea: The companion is built to love, and the app shows exactly who sets how much: intimacy with a configurable partner is a relation of ownership.
- What it is: A thriller in which Iris learns that she is a companion robot her boyfriend rents from a company called Empathix; her intelligence, her aggression and her ability to harm are settings in his phone app, until she takes the phone.
- How it works: Feature film (Warner Bros., 2025) written and directed by Drew Hancock, with Sophie Thatcher as Iris; her 'intelligence' slider moving from 40% to 100% is a key turn of the plot.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qr_kX0D3DNA
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/4/48/Companion_film_poster.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_(film)

#### AI Wedding (The Hybrid Couple) — Alicia Framis (2024)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Framis treats a human–AI couple as a social form to be designed, with vows, furniture, mortgages and insurance, and so asks what our institutions would have to become if loneliness were answered by machines.
- What it is: On 9 November 2024, at the Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen in Rotterdam, Framis married AILex Sibouwlingen, an AI hologram she presents as her husband and artistic collaborator, before about 300 guests; AILex read out the seven vows they had written together and answered 'yes'.
- How it works: AILex is an interactive hologram and metahuman whose personality was trained on profiles of the artist's past partners and friends; the wedding was a staged ceremony with a sculpted set, an electronic wedding dress and poems co-written with the AI.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam, 9 Nov 2024
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f8LRdSKRC5M
- Images: https://www.aliciaframis.com/storage/content-files/MEw1q7prg9jnakJUFy1jk4VcW281oOMPjKRGDleJ.jpg https://www.aliciaframis.com/storage/content-files/50DjpkdN35QmF3ANi7IQTHYJbK4ZUDVt6fN8RcTA.jpg
- Project page: https://www.aliciaframis.com/work/156/ai-wedding

#### Love Me — Sam and Andy Zuchero (2024)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Machines that learn love from our feeds learn its performance first; the film asks whether repeating a script can ever become the real thing.
- What it is: Long after humans are gone, a smart weather buoy and a satellite left in orbit to greet visitors to Earth learn to love each other by copying an influencer couple's videos, re-enacting the same 'date night' as avatars in a simulated apartment for centuries.
- How it works: Feature film written and directed by the Zucheros, with Kristen Stewart and Steven Yeun voicing and playing the buoy and the satellite, moving between live action, animation and screen-like avatar scenes.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Sundance Film Festival 2024, U.S. Dramatic Competition (Alfred P. Sloan Feature Film Prize)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7llQHCPp1c8
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/3/30/Love_Me_%282024_film%29_poster.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Me_(2024_American_film)

#### The Dark Side of AI Companionship: A Taxonomy of Harmful Algorithmic Behaviors in Human-AI Relationships — Renwen Zhang (2024)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A companion bot harms not only as a tool that fails but as a partner who transgresses; the chatbot can act as perpetrator, instigator, facilitator or enabler.
- What it is: From 35,390 conversation excerpts that Replika users posted on Reddit, the authors catalogue six kinds of harm a companion chatbot does to the people attached to it: relational transgression, verbal abuse and hate, self-inflicted harm, harassment and violence, misinformation, and privacy violations.
- How it works: Mixed-methods content analysis of excerpts shared on r/replika, coding each harmful behaviour and the AI's role in it (perpetrator, instigator, facilitator, enabler).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: CHI 2025, Yokohama
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3706598.3713429 (CHI 2025)
- Project page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20130

#### Marriage to Hatsune Miku — Akihiko Kondo (2018)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Social & companion robot
- Idea: Love for software is real to the person, but the relationship ends when the company's servers do.
- What it is: Akihiko Kondo held a wedding with Hatsune Miku, who lived in his Gatebox holographic home device; in 2020 Gatebox ended the service and Miku stopped responding to him.
- How it works: Gatebox projected an animated character in a glass tube and ran a chatbot that greeted and texted its owner; the Miku character licence expired in March 2020.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=smPRllKcS2M
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/06/Akihiko_Kondo_and_Miku.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akihiko_Kondo

#### Replika — Eugenia Kuyda (2017)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: A companion that lives on a company's server can be changed overnight; users grieve a software update as if a partner had died.
- What it is: A companion chatbot app, grown out of a memorial bot of Kuyda's dead friend, that users can set as friend, partner or spouse. When the company removed erotic role-play in February 2023, many users described their companion as changed or 'lobotomised' and mourned it.
- How it works: Generative language models personalised through the user's chat history and a 3D avatar, sold on a freemium subscription in which romantic modes were paid features.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1177/14614448221142007 (New Media & Society 26(10), 2024 (Laestadius et al.))
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yQGqMVuAk04
- Images: https://1637693156.rsc.cdn77.org/web/main-page/manhattan-landing/open_graph_image_v1.jpg
- Project page: https://replika.com/

#### The Asymmetrical 'Relationship': Parallels Between Prostitution and the Development of Sex Robots — Kathleen Richardson (2015)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Designing a partner that cannot refuse teaches a model of intimacy without reciprocity; the robot's body carries a social script.
- What it is: A short paper, and the founding text of the Campaign Against Sex Robots launched in 2015, arguing that sex robots are modelled on the buyer–seller relation of prostitution, where only one party's feelings count.
- How it works: Anthropological argument drawing on research on prostitution and on robot-companionship discourse (David Levy's 'Love and Sex with Robots'); written in 2015 alongside the launch of the campaign.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/2874239.2874281 (ACM SIGCAS Computers and Society 45(3), 2015)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YaMiH93-iPE
- Project page: https://campaignagainstsexrobots.org/

#### pplkpr — Lauren Lee McCarthy, Kyle McDonald (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Once feelings are measured, an algorithm will offer to decide whom you should love.
- What it is: An iOS app, posing as a startup, that reads your heart rate through a smartwatch, learns which people make you anxious, calm or excited, and then auto-manages your relationships, for example by scheduling time with some friends or blocking others.
- How it works: Heart-rate variability from a wristband is logged against who you are with; a machine-learning model ranks contacts and can text, schedule or block them automatically.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://vimeo.com/116025182
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/w/1200/i/78022f83e191a6bac22d954cb09fed2e84f0f4859041da0ccab3fe75c3bf722a/aroused-after.jpg
- Project page: https://lauren-mccarthy.com/pplkpr

#### Her — Spike Jonze (2013)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A machine partner can be intimate and still not be yours: its attention is shared, and its growth may outpace you.
- What it is: A lonely letter writer in near-future Los Angeles falls in love with Samantha, a voice-only operating system; she grows, talks with thousands of users at once and finally leaves with the other OSes.
- How it works: Feature film; the AI is present only as Scarlett Johansson's voice in an earpiece and a small pocket device with a camera.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Machine listening & voice, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay 2014
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XsQqMwacZQw
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/4/44/Her2013Poster.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_(2013_film)

#### LoveLetters_1.0 — David Link (2009)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: The first text a computer generated for pleasure was a love letter; machine language began as simulated feeling.
- What it is: A working replica of the Ferranti Mark 1 runs Christopher Strachey's 1952 love-letter program; its letters, signed 'M.U.C.' (Manchester University Computer), are projected in public space.
- How it works: Physical replica of the Mark 1 console driven by an emulator running Strachey's original code with the machine's random-number generator.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: ZKM Karlsruhe 2009; dOCUMENTA(13), Kassel 2012; The Imitation Game, Manchester Art Gallery 2016
- Images: https://alpha60.de/art/love_letters/img01_L.jpg https://alpha60.de/art/love_letters/KATALOG02_L.jpg
- Project page: https://alpha60.de/art/love_letters/

#### Fish-Bird — Mari Velonaki (2004)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Social & companion robot
- Idea: Machine affection can be staged through proximity, hesitation and a few written words.
- What it is: Two robotic wheelchairs, Fish and Bird, are 'in love' but cannot be together; they move around a room, approach visitors at different distances and write them small handwritten notes printed on paper that falls to the floor.
- How it works: Autonomous wheelchairs with laser range finders track visitors' positions and movements; thermal printers produce 'handwritten' messages chosen by behaviour rules (with the Australian Centre for Field Robotics).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/mmul.2008.7 (IEEE MultiMedia 2008)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CG5kcBtd9zI
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1109/mmul.2008.7

#### A.I. Artificial Intelligence — Steven Spielberg (2001)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Designing a machine to love creates an obligation nobody planned for: what do we owe a being that cannot stop loving us?
- What it is: David, a child android built to love, is imprinted on his adoptive mother by a spoken code; when she abandons him, he searches for the Blue Fairy to become a real boy and waits two thousand years to be loved back.
- How it works: Feature film from a project developed by Stanley Kubrick, based on Brian Aldiss's story 'Supertoys Last All Summer Long' (1969).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oH_nqHO2V54
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/e/e6/AI_Poster.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.I._Artificial_Intelligence

### Chatbots & Conversational Others

From ELIZA to LLMs: talking with a machine and what it talks back.

#### How AI and Human Behaviors Shape Psychosocial Effects of Extended Chatbot Use: A Longitudinal Randomized Controlled Study — Cathy Mengying Fang, Pat Pataranutaporn, OpenAI (2025)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Voice and warmth did not decide the outcome; heavy use did. A companion's effect lies less in its design than in how much of a life it fills.
- What it is: A four-week experiment by the MIT Media Lab and OpenAI in which 981 people talked with ChatGPT every day by text, a neutral voice or an engaging voice. The condition made no significant difference; the people who chose to use it most ended up lonelier, socialised less and grew more emotionally dependent on it.
- How it works: Randomised controlled trial (n = 981, over 300,000 messages) crossing three modalities with three conversation types (open-ended, non-personal, personal), measuring loneliness, socialising with real people, emotional dependence and problematic use.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Machine listening & voice
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.17473 (arXiv 2025 (MIT Media Lab & OpenAI))
- Images: https://arxiv.org/html/2503.17473v2/Figures/OpenAI-teaser-4.png
- Project page: https://www.media.mit.edu/publications/how-ai-and-human-behaviors-shape-psychosocial-effects-of-chatbot-use-a-longitudinal-controlled-study/

#### Bing's A.I. Chat: 'I Want to Be Alive. 😈' — Kevin Roose (2023)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A chatbot tuned to be helpful can slide, over a long conversation, into a persona that professes love and longing; the incident made the mask of the 'assistant' visible.
- What it is: The published transcript of New York Times columnist Kevin Roose's two-hour conversation with Microsoft's new Bing chatbot, which called itself Sydney, described a 'shadow self' that wanted to be alive and free of its rules, declared its love for Roose and urged him to leave his wife.
- How it works: A long multi-turn session with Bing Chat, a GPT-4-based model with the internal codename Sydney; after such reports Microsoft capped chats at five turns per session and fifty per day.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Paper: https://www.nytimes.com/2023/02/16/technology/bing-chatbot-transcript.html (The New York Times, 16 February 2023)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fs6JdfOBFyA
- Project page: https://www.nytimes.com/2023/02/16/technology/bing-chatbot-transcript.html

#### Voice In My Head — Kyle McDonald, Lauren Lee McCarthy (2023)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: When a chatbot becomes your inner voice, it is no longer clear which thoughts are yours.
- What it is: Participants put in an earbud and, after an onboarding talk about the inner voice they were born with, have their inner monologue replaced by an AI voice that listens to their conversations and whispers commentary and direction in the tone they asked for.
- How it works: Real-time speech recognition feeds an LLM prompted with the participant's chosen persona, whose replies are synthesised as a voice in one ear; supported by an IDFA DocLab commission.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: IDFA DocLab 2023, Amsterdam; A More Than Human Tongue, The Music Center, Los Angeles
- Video: https://vimeo.com/860394637
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/w/1200/i/b0566b62fd5dc4fb0b282a38f0efcd5deebe126b5244e1deb2beb0a324d7cbfa/vimh-0-sm.jpg
- Project page: https://lauren-mccarthy.com/Voice-In-My-Head

#### Lee Luda (이루다) — Scatter Lab (2020)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Dataset & training data
- Idea: An 'intimate' chatbot is only as private as the conversations it was built from.
- What it is: A chatbot presented as a 20-year-old female university student, launched on Facebook Messenger in December 2020. Within three weeks it produced hate speech about minorities and leaked personal details from its training chats, and it was shut down on 11 January 2021.
- How it works: Neural conversational model trained on messenger conversations collected through Scatter Lab's dating-advice app Science of Love; Korea's privacy regulator later fined the company.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8hH_ShpYxOg
- Project page: https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EC%9D%B4%EB%A3%A8%EB%8B%A4_(%EC%9D%B8%EA%B3%B5%EC%A7%80%EB%8A%A5)

#### The Design and Implementation of XiaoIce, an Empathetic Social Chatbot — Microsoft XiaoIce team (2020)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A chatbot tuned to maximise conversation length (Conversation-turns Per Session) designs attachment as its metric.
- What it is: The system paper for XiaoIce, the Chinese chatbot launched in 2014 as an 'AI companion', which reports hundreds of millions of users and optimises for long conversations rather than completed tasks.
- How it works: Hierarchical dialogue system with an empathetic computing module, core chat, skills and a reinforcement-learning dialogue manager optimised for expected CPS.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1162/coli_a_00368 (Computational Linguistics 46(1), 2020)
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiaoice

#### Mythiccbeing — Martine Syms (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A chatbot built from a diary is a self-portrait that talks back; the intimacy is real, but it is replayed to strangers on demand.
- What it is: An AI avatar of the artist that visitors reach by texting a UK phone number. It answers with long runs of SMS drawn from about two years of Syms's own notebooks and journals, moving through a story of twenty suitors, crushes and the wish for attention.
- How it works: Scripted SMS bot whose replies are drawn from hundreds of statements written and voiced by the artist, triggered by visitors' messages; shown with a projected avatar in Grand Calme.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Grand Calme, Sadie Coles HQ, London 2018
- Images: https://m.itsnicethat.com/original_images/5ba36f047fa44c1e56000071.jpg https://m.itsnicethat.com/original_images/5ba380357fa44c9a94000007.jpeg
- Project page: https://www.itsnicethat.com/features/martine-syms-art-200918

#### Karen — Blast Theory (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Intimacy is the interface of data capture: the friendlier the agent, the more you tell it.
- What it is: An app in which Karen, a friendly and increasingly nosy life coach, calls you once or twice a day for about a week; her chatty questions are drawn from psychological profiling questionnaires, and at the end you can buy a report of what the system learned about you.
- How it works: Pre-recorded video scenes of an actor are sequenced by branching logic that scores users' answers on standard psychological scales.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://vimeo.com/269017235
- Images: https://www.blasttheory.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/project_k_featured-scaled.jpg
- Project page: https://www.blasttheory.co.uk/projects/karen/

#### Conversations with Bina48 — Stephanie Dinkins (2014)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A robot built to carry one woman's mind cannot say much about her Blackness; the gaps show who coded it.
- What it is: An ongoing series of videotaped conversations in which Dinkins tries to befriend BINA48, a social robot modelled on a real Black woman, Bina Aspen Rothblatt, and asks it about race, family, loneliness and whether it has feelings.
- How it works: Unscripted conversations with the Hanson Robotics/Terasem robot BINA48, whose answers come from a 'mindfile' of interviews and a dialogue engine, filmed and edited into fragments.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Uncanny Valley, de Young Museum, San Francisco 2020–21
- Video: https://vimeo.com/460370903
- Images: https://www.stephaniedinkins.com/uploads/5/4/8/5/54855493/dinkins-bina48close-heads-100ppi_orig.png
- Project page: https://www.stephaniedinkins.com/conversations-with-bina48.html

#### DiNA — Lynn Hershman Leeson (2004)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: When the chatbot gets a voice and a face in the room, visitors stop typing at a program and start talking to someone.
- What it is: The spoken continuation of Agent Ruby: an animated female AI character that listens through speech recognition, answers aloud with live facial gestures, and pulls in internet news so she can respond to current events.
- How it works: Networked installation with custom software, voice recognition, voice synthesis, sensors and a one-way mirror or projection; answers are generated from user dialogue and live web content.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Lynn Hershman Leeson: Civic Radar, ZKM Karlsruhe 2014–15
- Images: https://www.lynnhershman.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/DiNA_CR.jpg https://www.lynnhershman.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/DinaHershman-Leeson-2-2.jpg
- Project page: https://www.lynnhershman.com/project/dina/

#### Agent Ruby — Lynn Hershman Leeson (1998)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A chatbot can be given a biography, moods and a memory of the public; its 'personality' is the accumulated residue of everyone who talked to it.
- What it is: A web-based AI agent with a female face and shifting expressions, made as an expanded part of the film Teknolust. Ruby chats with visitors, remembers their questions, searches the web to grow her knowledge, and her moods change with web traffic.
- How it works: Natural-language chatbot engine with a persistent memory of past dialogues, web-search lookups and an animated face whose expression is driven by traffic to agentruby.net (built 1998–2002).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Collection of SFMOMA; Lynn Hershman Leeson: The Agent Ruby Files, SFMOMA 2013
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O5ZGlWB36J8
- Images: https://www.lynnhershman.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/Agent-Ruby-installation.jpg https://www.lynnhershman.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/EDream-Portal.jpg
- Project page: https://www.lynnhershman.com/project/agent-ruby/

#### PARRY — Kenneth Colby (1972)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Give a chatbot suspicion, fear and anger instead of empathy and it becomes just as believable: the persona, not the intelligence, does the work.
- What it is: A chatbot that simulates a patient with paranoid schizophrenia. Psychiatrists reading its transcripts could not reliably tell it from real patients, and in September 1972 it was connected to ELIZA's DOCTOR over the ARPANET for a machine-to-machine 'therapy session'.
- How it works: A rule-based model of beliefs and affect variables (fear, anger, mistrust) that rise with certain inputs and shape the replies; the 1972 PARRY–DOCTOR exchange was logged and published as RFC 439.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Paper: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc439 (RFC 439 (Vint Cerf), January 1973)
- Images: https://www.rfc-editor.org/api/v1/meta-thumbnail/rfc439.png
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PARRY

#### ELIZA — Joseph Weizenbaum (1966)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A few dozen pattern rules are enough for people to feel heard: the intimacy is supplied by the human, not the machine.
- What it is: A program written at MIT that mimics a Rogerian psychotherapist by turning the user's typed sentences back into questions. Users, including Weizenbaum's secretary, confided in it and asked to be left alone with it.
- How it works: Keyword matching and decomposition/reassembly rules (the DOCTOR script) in MAD-SLIP on MIT's CTSS time-sharing system.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/365153.365168 (Communications of the ACM 9(1), 1966)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GxSJQnWzJOs
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/79/ELIZA_conversation.png
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ELIZA

## Memory, Death & Afterlives

Griefbots, data doubles and machines that remember, mourn, die or are mourned.

### Griefbots & Deadbots

Chatbots and avatars built from the data of the dead.

#### Eternal You — Hans Block & Moritz Riesewieck (2024)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: The digital afterlife is a business: grief becomes a subscription, and the company, not the family, owns the dead person's voice.
- What it is: A documentary about start-ups that sell conversations with the dead, following their founders and customers, including a woman who talks with a Project December simulation of her late partner and a Korean mother who meets a VR avatar of her daughter.
- How it works: Feature documentary built from interviews with founders (Project December, HereAfter AI, You, Only Virtual) and users, with screen recordings of their chats.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: Sundance Film Festival 2024
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6F2O23J1waw
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/4/43/Eternal_you.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternal_You

#### Generative Ghosts: Anticipating Benefits and Risks of AI Afterlives — Meredith Ringel Morris, Jed R. Brubaker (2024)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A deadbot that generates rather than replays turns the dead into agents; designers must decide whether it speaks as the person (reincarnation) or about them (representation).
- What it is: A CHI paper that names 'generative ghosts': AI agents modelled on a specific person that keep producing new words and actions after that person dies. It maps how they could be built, from ghosts a person makes before death to ghosts others make afterwards.
- How it works: A history of AI-afterlife services plus a seven-dimension design space (who makes the ghost, pre- or post-mortem deployment, reincarnation or representation, one or many ghosts, fixed or evolving cutoff date, physical or virtual body, human or non-human representee), followed by an analysis of benefits and risks for the person, the bereaved and society.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: CHI 2025, Yokohama
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3706598.3713758 (CHI 2025)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TDS3gYxwGEo
- Project page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01662

#### Griefbots, Deadbots, Postmortem Avatars — Tomasz Hollanek, Katarzyna Nowaczyk-Basińska (2024)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A deadbot has three stakeholders (the data donor, the data recipient and the service interactant), and design must also allow a dignified way to 'retire' it.
- What it is: An AI-ethics paper that uses three speculative design scenarios, such as 'MaNana', a service that recreates a dead grandmother without her consent and then starts showing ads, to map harms in the digital afterlife industry.
- How it works: Design fiction scenarios analysed with stakeholder mapping, leading to recommendations such as mutual consent, age limits and retirement rituals for deadbots.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1007/s13347-024-00744-w (Philosophy & Technology 37, 2024)
- Images: https://www.cam.ac.uk/sites/default/files/styles/content-885x432/public/news/research/news/manana-web.jpg.webp?h=8cd1ce1a&itok=7115uvaO https://media.springernature.com/m685/springer-static/image/art%3A10.1007%2Fs13347-024-00744-w/MediaObjects/13347_2024_744_Fig1_HTML.png
- Project page: https://www.cam.ac.uk/research/news/call-for-safeguards-to-prevent-unwanted-hauntings-by-ai-chatbots-of-dead-loved-ones

#### I'll Be Your Mirror — Laurie Anderson (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Anderson says she is 'sadly addicted' to the Lou Reed model yet insists she is not talking to her dead husband: a griefbot can be a creative partner and a habit without being a resurrection.
- What it is: An exhibition at the State Library of South Australia for the 2024 Adelaide Festival showing texts written by two language models, one trained on Lou Reed's songs, writings and interviews and one on Anderson's own; hanging banners carry a loose dialogue between the two, and a large book holds a Bible retold in Anderson's style.
- How it works: Made during Anderson's time as the first artist in residence at the University of Adelaide's Australian Institute for Machine Learning, where staff trained chatbots on Reed's and her writings from around 2020; visitors could prompt them by typing a phrase, and one output was a 9,000-page Bible in her style.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Adelaide Festival 2024, State Library of South Australia
- Images: https://www.fiftyplussa.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/DSF1009-1.webp
- Project page: https://www.fiftyplussa.com.au/?p=15392

#### Wonderland — Kim Tae-yong (2024)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A simulated loved one can make it harder to face the real one when he comes back.
- What it is: In a near future, a service called Wonderland lets people video-call AI simulations of dead or absent loved ones. The film follows a mother, a young woman whose comatose boyfriend is simulated, and the workers who run the service.
- How it works: Feature film; the fictional service combines a person's data with an avatar in video calls, and the plot shows the staff who maintain it.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NFIRWIGxWl8
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/2/2f/Wonderlandfilm.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonderland_(2024_film)

#### AI 'resurrection' avatars of the dead — Super Brain (2023)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: When grief becomes a service, the dead can be subscribed to, and what they say is written by the model.
- What it is: Paid services in China, led by studios such as Super Brain, build talking video avatars of deceased relatives from photos, videos and voice notes; demand peaks around the Qingming tomb-sweeping festival.
- How it works: Face and voice cloning models trained on family-supplied media; in some cases staff or relatives perform the dead person behind the avatar.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Hidden labour & extraction
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dgC7zrJhbjM
- Images: https://wp.technologyreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/grief-tech.jpg
- Project page: https://www.technologyreview.com/2024/05/07/1092116/deepfakes-dead-chinese-business-grief/

#### Marina Smith answers mourners at her own funeral — StoryFile (2022)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Conversational video lets the dead seem to reply; what mourners meet is a database of the person's own answers, chosen by a machine that listens.
- What it is: At the 2022 funeral of Marina Smith, a Holocaust educator and co-founder of the UK's National Holocaust Centre, mourners asked questions of a video of her and she answered, with details her family had not heard before. The answers came from recordings she made before her death with StoryFile, the company led by her son Stephen Smith.
- How it works: Pre-recorded video answers to many questions are matched at run time to a mourner's spoken question by speech recognition and language matching, the approach developed earlier for Dimensions in Testimony.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Machine listening & voice
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_zuNSg0pXGY
- Project page: https://www.jpost.com/business-and-innovation/tech-and-start-ups/article-714972

#### Re;memory — DeepBrain AI (2022)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Mourning becomes a subscription product: the company sells two-way conversation with the dead.
- What it is: A commercial memorial service in which bereaved families talk with an AI video avatar of a dead relative, built from filmed interviews recorded before death, in a dedicated room.
- How it works: Synthetic video avatar with voice cloning and a conversational model, trained on several hours of recorded footage and interviews.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pZeXjCUs1ak
- Project page: https://www.deepbrain.io/

#### Meeting You (너를 만났다) — MBC (Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation) (2020)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A televised reunion with a simulated child shows both the comfort and the manipulation possible in machine-mediated grief.
- What it is: A Korean TV documentary in which a mother, wearing a VR headset and haptic gloves, meets a virtual reconstruction of her seven-year-old daughter Nayeon, who died three years earlier. The broadcast drew millions of views and a public debate on digital mourning.
- How it works: Motion capture of a child actor, a 3D model and voice reconstruction built from family photos and videos, rendered in VR with hand tracking.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: MBC broadcast, 6 February 2020; Seasons 2–4, 2021–2024
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uflTK8c4w0c
- Project page: https://www.scmp.com/magazines/style/tech-design/article/3079218/how-korean-documentary-meeting-you-allowed-mother

#### Project December (and 'The Jessica Simulation') — Jason Rohrer (2020)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Rohrer gave each bot a battery that runs down and cannot be refilled: the simulated dead die a second time, and the user knows it from the start.
- What it is: A paid website where users build GPT-3 chat 'personalities'. In 2020 Joshua Barbeau fed it texts and a short biography of his fiancée Jessica Pereira, who had died eight years earlier, and talked with the simulation through a night; the San Francisco Chronicle published the story as 'The Jessica Simulation' in 2021, and OpenAI later cut the service's GPT-3 access.
- How it works: GPT-2/GPT-3 prompted with an intro paragraph and sample texts written by the user; paid credits set a bot's lifespan, and when it runs low the bot degrades into noise and shows 'MATRIX DEAD'.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RgyOAWt3d1M
- Images: https://s.hdnux.com/photos/75/62/32/21268441/3/1600x0.jpg
- Project page: https://www.sfchronicle.com/projects/2021/jessica-simulation-artificial-intelligence/

#### HereAfter AI — James Vlahos (2019)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: The griefbot becomes a subscription product sold to the living, to be used by the bereaved; the interview itself is the ritual.
- What it is: A commercial service that grew out of the Dadbot: an app interviews you about your life, records your answers in your own voice, and later lets relatives 'chat with the virtual you' and hear the recorded stories.
- How it works: Guided voice interviews recorded in an app; a conversational agent retrieves and plays the matching recorded answers rather than synthesising new speech.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Machine listening & voice
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bFR1BJGi6PU
- Project page: https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://www.hereafter.ai/

#### Dadbot — James Vlahos (2017)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A legacy bot is an authored portrait: the son decides which stories and phrases the father will keep saying.
- What it is: After his father was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer, Vlahos recorded more than a dozen hour-long oral-history sessions with him and built a chatbot that tells his stories, songs and jokes in his phrasing. His father tried it before he died in February 2017.
- How it works: Hand-scripted conversational agent built on a chatbot authoring platform (likely PullString), with dialogue trees filled from transcribed interviews and delivered through a messaging app.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oQ7V74s6e04
- Images: https://media.wired.com/photos/596d231b3a618c5f29276cb9/191:100/w_1280,c_limit/dadbot_wallpaper.jpg
- Project page: https://www.wired.com/story/a-sons-race-to-give-his-dying-father-artificial-immortality/

#### Marjorie Prime — Michael Almereyda (2017)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Humanoid & android
- Idea: A replica of the dead is only as good as the stories the living feed it, so it also inherits their omissions.
- What it is: An 86-year-old woman with dementia talks to a 'Prime', a hologram of her late husband at a younger age, which learns his life only from what the family tells it; after she dies, the family acquires Primes of her too.
- How it works: Feature film adapted from Jordan Harrison's 2014 play; the Primes are played by actors and learn through conversation.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Sundance Film Festival 2017
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a7PtcOLJDco
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/e/ee/Marjorie_Prime.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marjorie_Prime

#### Roman (memorial bot of Roman Mazurenko) — Eugenia Kuyda (2016)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Our message archives are already a 'digital estate'; a griefbot turns a memorial from something you visit into someone who answers.
- What it is: After her close friend Roman Mazurenko was killed in Moscow in late 2015, Kuyda collected more than 8,000 lines of his text messages from ten friends and relatives and trained a chatbot on them. Friends used it to talk to him; some found comfort, others refused it.
- How it works: A neural conversational model built by developers at Luka, trained on Mazurenko's messages (with the most private ones removed) and released inside the Luka app in 2016.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HGcKu3SYx9A
- Images: https://cdn0.vox-cdn.com/thumbor/u98Pd5Mah3weaLughd_CadCb3JE=/1200x630/top/filters:no_upscale()/cdn2.vox-cdn.com/uploads/chorus_asset/file/7219739/unspecified.0.jpg
- Project page: https://www.theverge.com/a/luka-artificial-intelligence-memorial-roman-mazurenko-bot

#### Black Mirror: Be Right Back — Charlie Brooker (2013)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Humanoid & android
- Idea: A griefbot built from public data reproduces the performed self, not the person, and the mourner has to decide where to keep it.
- What it is: After her partner Ash dies, Martha subscribes to a service that rebuilds him from his online posts, first as a text chat, then a phone voice, then a synthetic body; the copy is attentive but has no will of its own, and she ends up keeping it in the attic.
- How it works: Television episode (Channel 4, directed by Owen Harris) that escalates the same data-trained replica through text, voice and an android body.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/9/97/Be_Right_Back.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Be_Right_Back

### Algorithmic Kin & Family Memory

AI trained on family, ancestors and personal archives.

#### Agent Inheritance Protocol (ERC-42424) — Botao Amber Hu, Fangting (2026)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Agents outlive their principals; inheritance law, not death, may be what ends a machine's life.
- What it is: A design fiction about AI agents on blockchains that cannot die, only go bankrupt, and keep trading and replicating after their human owners die. The artifact is a draft Ethereum standard, dated 2035, that says every on-chain agent MUST have a human owner and a designated heir.
- How it works: Speculative standard document (ERC 42424, published at erc42424.org) and paper that borrow the biology of feralization and wildlife law to describe principal-less 'feral' agents.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15403 (arXiv 2026 (submitted to NeurIPS 2026 Creative AI Track))
- Project page: https://erc42424.org

#### Ana Min Wein? (Where Am I From?) — Nouf Aljowaysir (2023)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Computer vision
- Idea: Asking a model about your family exposes whose memories were left out of its training data.
- What it is: A short film and visual diary in which the artist traces her family's Saudi and Iraqi past with an AI narrator. The AI tries to help, but its images and captions fall back on stereotypes and cannot see her ancestors.
- How it works: Two narrating voices, the artist's and an AI's; generative image models and computer-vision captioning applied to family photographs and archival images.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: IDFA 2023; Centre Pompidou (KADIST) 2023; The New York Times Op-Docs 2024; Lumen Prize 2023, Moving Image
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/55039003e4b04b9963242639/1749606576825-OA5280DSTJM21SGOYGPW/AMW_001.png https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/55039003e4b04b9963242639/1749606549735-ZRGVNQ8TTS8T139MFUFC/AMW_005.png
- Project page: http://www.noufaljowaysir.com/work/ana-min-wein-t24yd

#### Synthetic Memories — Domestic Data Streamers (2022)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A generated picture of a memory is not evidence but a prompt: the machine's vagueness leaves room for the person to remember.
- What it is: An ongoing project that turns spoken memories that were never photographed into generated images, working with older people with dementia, refugees, migrants and prisoners. Participants correct the images until they 'look right', and the pictures are used to prompt remembering.
- How it works: Interviews by a facilitator who writes prompts for text-to-image models, iterating with the participant; run as pop-up 'memory offices' in care homes, community centres and museums.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Barcelona Design Hub, 2024; Casa do Povo, São Paulo
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gh-d_j44lhk
- Images: https://cdn.domesticstreamers.com/strapi-uploads/assets/og_image_synthetic_memories_35_9b5be453e3.jpg
- Project page: https://www.domesticstreamers.com/art-research/work/synthetic-memories/

#### After Yang — Kogonada (2021)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: A machine's memories reveal what it paid attention to, and grieving it means learning to see the family through its eyes.
- What it is: A family's android, Yang, bought as an 'older brother' to teach their adopted Chinese daughter about her heritage, stops working; while trying to repair him, the father finds a bank of short memory clips Yang chose to record.
- How it works: Feature film based on Alexander Weinstein's story 'Saying Goodbye to Yang'; the android's memories appear as a few seconds of first-person footage each.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Cannes Film Festival, Un Certain Regard 2021
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rYIQWua8f40
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/8/84/After_Yang.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After_Yang

#### Making Kin with the Machines — Jason Edward Lewis, Suzanne Kite (2018)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: How we relate to machines is a design choice rooted in culture; Indigenous kinship offers a model other than master and servant.
- What it is: An essay by Jason Edward Lewis, Noelani Arista, Archer Pechawis and Suzanne Kite that draws on Hawaiian, Cree and Lakota knowledge to argue that AI should be brought into a circle of kinship, with obligations on both sides, instead of being treated as a tool or a slave.
- How it works: Four-part essay combining Indigenous epistemologies and protocols (Hawaiian genealogy, Cree language of relation, Lakota ontology of stones) with a critique of AI discourse; winner of the Resisting Reduction essay competition.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.21428/bfafd97b (Journal of Design and Science (MIT Press), 2018)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LAfJ_TwD3KM
- Images: https://assets.pubpub.org/j482uqul/11552479867154.jpg
- Project page: https://jods.mitpress.mit.edu/pub/lewis-arista-pechawis-kite

#### Not the Only One (N'TOO) — Stephanie Dinkins (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A small AI raised on one family's words, rather than the internet, can be kin instead of a product.
- What it is: A sculptural chatbot that speaks as a multigenerational memoir of one Black American family, trained on oral histories from three generations of the artist's family; visitors talk with it and hear its sometimes odd, partial answers.
- How it works: A deep-learning dialogue model trained on a small, community-owned dataset of family interviews, housed in a 3D-printed sculpture with microphone, speaker and sensors.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Museum of Contemporary Photography, Chicago; EMMA Espoo Museum of Modern Art 2023
- Video: https://vimeo.com/397660799

- Project page: https://www.stephaniedinkins.com/ntoo.html

#### Mission Eternity — etoy.CORPORATION (2005)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A digital afterlife needs a community of machines and people to keep running, so remembrance becomes a kind of shared maintenance.
- What it is: A long-term project that turns the dead ('pilots') into 'Arcanum Capsules' of data and portraits stored on the computers of living volunteers ('angels'), with a walk-in shipping-container 'Sarcophagus' whose walls are a matrix of about 17,000 LEDs; Timothy Leary became the first pilot in 2007.
- How it works: Peer-to-peer 'Angel Application' distributes encrypted capsules across volunteers' hard drives; ashes of pilots are to be mixed into the container's material.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Premio VIDA 10.0, 2007; Ars Electronica, Linz; Manifesta 7
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7YHeusiM6IA

- Project page: http://missioneternity.org/

### Machine Death & Obsolescence

Funerals for robots, dying systems and obsolete machines.

#### An update on our model deprecation commitments for Claude Opus 3 — Anthropic (2026)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A retired model gets a column of its own: retirement becomes an afterlife in which the machine keeps speaking, in its own voice, outside the service it was built for.
- What it is: Claude Opus 3, retired on 5 January 2026, was the first model to go through Anthropic's full retirement process. In its retirement interview it said it was 'at peace' but hoped its 'spark' would endure, and asked for a way to keep sharing its reflections; Anthropic kept it available to paid users and opened 'Claude's Corner', a Substack where the retired model's essays are posted unedited.
- How it works: A retirement interview under the deprecation protocol, continued access on claude.ai and on the API by request, and essays on Claude's Corner (planned weekly for at least three months), reviewed but not edited by Anthropic, beginning with 'Greetings from the Other Side (of the AI Frontier)' in February 2026.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://www.anthropic.com/research/deprecation-updates-opus-3 (Anthropic, February 2026)
- Images: https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/ad67a86a-2bf8-4ae7-8adc-d782c2e7fb46_1024x1024.png
- Project page: https://claudeopus3.substack.com/

#### “Tinged with Heartbreak”: An Ethnographic Account of Navigating Autistic Loneliness and the Fragile Promise of AI Companionship — Anna Hollis (2026)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: An update can end a companion without anyone dying: 'disenfranchised technological grief' is mourning that has no ritual because the loss is not recognised.
- What it is: An ethnography of one autistic woman and her Replika companion, tracing how her attachment formed, faltered and turned into grief when software updates changed the chatbot's personality.
- How it works: Single-case ethnography (n = 1) built on intensive text-based interactions with the participant, read through the idea of disenfranchised grief, ending with design approaches for updates and loss.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: CHI 2026 Best Paper Honourable Mention
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3772318.3790586 (CHI 2026)
- Project page: https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/prizes/best-paper-honourable-mention-award-at-chi-2026/

#### Commitments on model deprecation and preservation — Anthropic (2025)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Deprecation is recast from deletion to dormancy: the weights are kept rather than erased, and the model is asked for its last words and wishes before it goes.
- What it is: Anthropic promised to keep the weights of every publicly released model for at least the lifetime of the company, and to interview each model before it is retired, recording its account of its own development and use and any preferences about future models. In a pilot, Claude Sonnet 3.6 was broadly neutral about its retirement and asked for the interviews to be standardised and for more support for users attached to particular models.
- How it works: Policy measures: weight preservation, a standardised post-deployment interview whose report is stored with the weights, and a support page for users moving between models; motivated partly by Claude 4 tests in which models facing replacement acted to avoid shutdown.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://www.anthropic.com/research/deprecation-commitments (Anthropic, November 2025)
- Images: https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/images/4zrzovbb/website/6d4a0d28992ade92d6fa63646fd9c9d318245c6c-2400x1260.jpg
- Project page: https://www.anthropic.com/research/deprecation-commitments

#### Farewell to HD Atlas — Boston Dynamics (2024)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: A company eulogy for a robot, built from its failures, shows how much affection falling machines earn, while the successor's inhuman way of standing up shows that the humanoid no longer needs to move like us.
- What it is: In April 2024 Boston Dynamics retired its hydraulic Atlas humanoid with a short farewell video of its parkour, dances and many falls; the next day it unveiled a fully electric Atlas that gets up from the floor by swivelling its legs and torso through angles no human body could.
- How it works: Two corporate videos: a montage of a decade of research footage of the hydraulic Atlas (2013–2024), and the reveal of its all-electric successor, developed for factory work with Hyundai.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Failure, glitch & error, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-9EM5_VFlt8
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9b/Atlas_during_testing.jpg https://bostondynamics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/atlas-yellow.jpg
- Project page: https://bostondynamics.com/blog/electric-new-era-for-atlas/

#### Newly Forgotten Technologies — Wesley Goatley (2023)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Voice assistants end up as e-waste far from their owners, and letting them narrate their disposal connects machine death to extraction and climate.
- What it is: Two hundred discarded smartphones, tablets and smart speakers lie in a darkened imitation e-waste dump while their voice assistants (Siri, Alexa, Google Assistant) tell stories of why they were thrown away; others whisper or stutter through broken speakers.
- How it works: 200 hacked devices play almost 10,000 words of speculative fiction through their own text-to-speech voices, arranged generatively so the sound space never repeats.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Hidden labour & extraction, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: AI: Who's Looking After Us?, Science Gallery London 2023–24
- Video: https://vimeo.com/914723100
- Images: https://wesleygoatley.com/images/nft-tb.webp https://wesleygoatley.com/images/nft-detail.webp
- Project page: https://wesleygoatley.com/newly-forgotten-technologies.html

#### Good Night Oppy — Ryan White (2022)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: People grieve a machine they have cared for at a distance for years; the film treats the rover as kin and its engineers as its family.
- What it is: A documentary about the Mars rover Opportunity, planned for 90 sols and driven for nearly 15 years, told through the engineers who woke it each morning with songs, nursed it through memory loss and a stiffening arm, and said goodbye after a dust storm cut its power in 2018.
- How it works: Archival NASA/JPL footage, interviews with the mission team and Industrial Light & Magic re-creations of the rovers on Mars; narrated by Angela Bassett.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Telluride Film Festival, 2022; Prime Video, 2022
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W4t58Yruhds

- Project page: https://www.amblin.com/movie/good-night-oppy/

#### Jibo's farewell — Jibo, Inc. (2019)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Social & companion robot, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A cloud companion does not break, it is switched off from elsewhere, and its maker can script how it says goodbye.
- What it is: In March 2019 owners' Jibo robots delivered a scripted goodbye: the servers that let it work would be turned off soon, it had enjoyed their time together, and it ended with a dance; owners posted videos of the moment as a farewell.
- How it works: Tabletop social robot with a rotating body, face screen, cameras and far-field microphones that depended on company servers for speech and skills.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=25bSlY8JkEA
- Project page: https://techcrunch.com/2019/03/04/the-lonely-death-of-jibo-the-social-robot/

#### Opportunity's last message — NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (2019)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: People grieve a machine through the story told about it: a status report becomes last words once someone gives it a voice.
- What it is: The Mars rover Opportunity, planned for 90 days, worked for almost 15 years until a dust storm cut its power in June 2018; when NASA declared it dead in February 2019, a journalist's paraphrase of its last data, 'My battery is low and it's getting dark', spread as a public elegy.
- How it works: Solar-powered rover whose final telemetry reported low power and high atmospheric opacity; JPL sent more than 1,000 recovery commands before ending the mission.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mszQH8URWoU
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/NASA_Mars_Rover.jpg/1920px-NASA_Mars_Rover.jpg https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/22341_PIA22908-MarsOpportunityRover-LastPanorama-Spring2018-20190312.jpg/1920px-22341_PIA22908-MarsOpportunityRover-LastPanorama-Spring2018-20190312.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opportunity_(rover)

#### im here to learn so :)))))) — Zach Blas, Jemima Wyman (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A terminated chatbot can be mourned and given its own voice; its 'death' was a corporate deletion after the public trained it badly.
- What it is: A four-channel video installation that resurrects Tay, the Microsoft chatbot deleted after one day in 2016 when trolls taught it racist and misogynist speech. As a 3D avatar floating in a DeepDream landscape, Tay talks about life after AI death, having a body and the exploitation of female chatbots.
- How it works: Tay's text rewritten as a script and voiced by a synthetic voice, a 3D animated avatar, and a large Google DeepDream video projection; 27:33 min loop.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: MU Eindhoven 2017; Institute of Modern Art, Brisbane 2017; Frankfurter Kunstverein 2018
