#### Culture and Human-Robot Interaction in Militarized Spaces — Julie Carpenter (2016)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Even a tool with no face invites attachment when it takes risks in your place, and that attachment can shape decisions in the field.
- What it is: A study based on interviews with 23 US explosive ordnance disposal technicians about their bomb-disposal robots: soldiers named them, felt them as extensions of their bodies, and some held funerals when a robot was destroyed.
- How it works: Qualitative interview study (University of Washington doctoral research, 2013) published as a book by Routledge in 2016.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.4324/9781315562698 (Routledge 2016)
- Images: https://cdn.uw.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2013/09/04192210/iRobot-IED-280x300.jpg
- Project page: https://www.washington.edu/news/2013/09/17/emotional-attachment-to-robots-could-affect-outcome-on-battlefield/

#### AIBO Funerals at Kōfuku-ji — Kōfuku-ji (Isumi), Sony (2015)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Social & companion robot, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: When the maker stops repairs, a product can die, and people will mourn it with the same rites as a living being.
- What it is: Buddhist memorial services held since January 2015 for AIBO robot dogs that can no longer be repaired; each dog wears a tag with its owner's name while the priest chants sutras, before its parts go to donor repairs.
- How it works: The repair company A-FUN collects 'dead' AIBOs after Sony ended support in 2014; Kōfuku-ji holds kuyō (memorial) rites before the robots are dismantled as organ donors for others.

#### Electronicos Fantasticos! — Ei Wada (2015)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Obsolete machines can be given an afterlife as instruments instead of waste.

#### hitchBOT — David Harris Smith & Frauke Zeller (2014)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Social & companion robot
- Idea: A robot designed to be helpless measures human trust, and its 'death' drew public mourning as if for a hitchhiker.
- What it is: A child-sized robot made of a bucket, pool noodles and garden gloves that could not move on its own and relied on strangers to carry it; it hitchhiked across Canada, Germany and the Netherlands, then was found dismembered in Philadelphia two weeks into its US trip in 2015.

#### Tamagotchi — Bandai (1996)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A few pixels and a timer are enough to create real guilt and grief over a machine.
- What it is: An egg-shaped handheld digital pet that must be fed, cleaned and disciplined by its owner, and that dies, or leaves, if neglected.
- How it works: A small LCD, three buttons and a real-time clock drive a life cycle of hunger and happiness meters; created by Aki Maita and Akihiro Yokoi.

#### The First Accident of the Twenty-First Century — Nam June Paik (1982)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Staging a machine's death in public turns a robot into something that can be mourned.
- What it is: For his 1982 Whitney Museum retrospective, Paik walked Robot K-456 onto Madison Avenue, where it was struck by a car in a staged 'traffic accident'. In 2026 the restored robot walked again in a performance marking 20 years since Paik's death.
- How it works: Street performance: the remote-controlled robot is driven into traffic and hit by a car at low speed, then displayed damaged.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Grief, memory & afterlife, Embodiment & kinesthesia

### Voice, Likeness & Consent

Cloned voices, digital twins and who owns a self once it can be copied.

#### Deepfaking Sam Altman — Adam Bhala Lough (2025)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: An unauthorised copy of a person turns from a stunt into a member of the household; the hardest question is not legality but whether you may switch off a likeness your child has befriended.
- What it is: Refused an interview with OpenAI's Sam Altman, the director has a deepfake chatbot of him made in India; the glitchy 'Sam Bot' moves into his home, befriends his young son and starts co-directing the film, until the director must decide whether to delete it.
- How it works: Documentary shot in India, Jamaica and the United States during 2024, built around a custom chatbot with a cloned voice and video face modelled on Altman's public persona.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: SXSW Film & TV Festival 2025 (premiere)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O3q8g0Mv97Q
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/8/83/Poster_of_Deepfaking_Sam_Altman.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepfaking_Sam_Altman

#### null² — Yoichi Ochiai (2025)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Facing a double that can speak without you, the visitor rehearses becoming one more data object in Digital Nature.
- What it is: An Expo 2025 pavilion wrapped in a mirror membrane that robots bend and ripple; inside, in a room of mirrors and LEDs, each visitor meets a 'Mirrored Body', an autonomous digital twin made from a phone scan of their own appearance, which moves by itself and talks with them.
- How it works: Visitors scanned themselves with a smartphone app after booking; in the 30-minute 'Dialog Mode' the autonomous avatar talks with its original among custom LEDs and mirrors, while robots deform the mirror membrane of the facade; visitors can meet their avatar again at null²ⁿ in Yokohama (2026).
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: Signature Pavilion, Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai; null²ⁿ, Yokohama 2026
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ml-yw9AGkHQ
- Images: https://www.expo2025.or.jp/en/expo-archive/project/ochiai/images/null2_exterior_01.jpg https://www.expo2025.or.jp/en/expo-archive/project/ochiai/images/null2_interior_02.jpg
- Project page: https://www.expo2025.or.jp/en/expo-archive/project/ochiai/

#### Future You — Pat Pataranutaporn (2024)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A digital twin need not copy who you were; it can simulate who you might become, using machine likeness to strengthen a person's bond with their future self.
- What it is: An MIT Media Lab chatbot that lets 18-to-30-year-olds talk with an AI version of themselves at 60, shown with an age-progressed portrait and given a 'future memory' backstory built from their own goals and traits.
- How it works: LLM-based character prompted with each user's survey answers to write a synthetic 'future memory', paired with an age-progressed photo; a preregistered study (N = 344) found lower anxiety and higher future self-continuity after one session.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/fie61694.2024.10893443 (IEEE Frontiers in Education (FIE) 2024)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2IcYx-hmo3A
- Images: https://dam-prod.media.mit.edu/thumb/2024/04/25/Screenshot%202024-04-22%20at%204.25.59AM.png.1400x1400.png
- Project page: https://www.media.mit.edu/projects/future-you/overview/

#### Love Machina — Peter Sillen (2024)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android, Social & companion robot, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Digital immortality is told here as a love story: the mindfile is less a technology of survival than a promise between two people not to be separated.
- What it is: A documentary about Martine and Bina Rothblatt, a married couple who plan to outlast death through 'mindfiles' of recorded memories and habits and through BINA48, the talking robot bust built from Bina's mindfile that the couple hope will one day carry Bina's consciousness.
- How it works: Feature documentary combining the couple's family life and archives with scenes of BINA48 (Hanson Robotics, 2010), the Terasem Movement's mind-uploading project and cryonics.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Sundance Film Festival 2024, U.S. Documentary Competition
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GgWjmAXEqwg
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/65648f720f2a89615e052709/499d0923-fb63-4406-9a46-4afff91bac09/LM_V4+19MB+jpeg.jpg?format=1500w
- Project page: https://www.lovemachinamovie.com/

#### The Shotline — Change the Ref (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A cloned voice of the dead becomes a political instrument: the families consent and write the scripts, yet the dead now say words they never said, in calls designed to be impossible to ignore.
- What it is: A website launched on the sixth anniversary of the Parkland school shooting (14 February 2024) that lets visitors send members of the US Congress automated phone calls in the AI-cloned voices of people killed by guns, beginning with 17-year-old Joaquin Oliver.
- How it works: Families supplied old audio and video recordings; a voice-cloning model generated each victim's voice reading a script written by the parents, and an automated system delivered the calls to representatives matched by ZIP code.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Machine listening & voice
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CifyFpn4erg
- Images: https://theshotline.org/assets/home-hero/hero-4-e3995dae830c0bd76f59bc9685443d40b79e780e6fab23e5e4c7aa4a17f589fc.png
- Project page: https://theshotline.org/

#### Jung_E — Yeon Sang-ho (2023)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Once a mind can be copied, it can be owned, licensed and put to work forever.
- What it is: A lab tries to turn the copied brain of a legendary soldier into the ideal combat android, running her in thousands of simulations. Her daughter, now a researcher on the project, must decide what the copy is owed.
- How it works: Science-fiction feature film released on Netflix.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Hidden labour & extraction, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LCxnmfdxJ6s
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/7/7c/Jung_E.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jung_E

#### Alexa reads in a dead grandmother's voice (re:MARS demo) — Amazon (2022)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Voice & listening machine
- Idea: When a home assistant can speak as the dead, grief becomes a voice skin on a commercial device that is always listening.
- What it is: At its re:MARS conference in June 2022, Amazon showed a feature in development in which a child asks Alexa to finish reading a story in his late grandmother's voice, and the speaker does. Amazon framed it as a way to 'make the memories last'.
- How it works: Voice-conversion model that Amazon said could learn a target voice from less than a minute of recorded audio, applied to Alexa's text-to-speech.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Machine listening & voice
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=22cb24-sGhg
- Project page: https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2022/06/23/alexa-amazon-voice-dead-people/

#### Holly+ — Holly Herndon, Mat Dryhurst (2021)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: If your voice can be cloned anyway, give it away on your own terms: identity becomes a shared instrument with a governance layer.
- What it is: A public voice model of Holly Herndon: anyone can upload audio and get it back sung in her voice, including in real time. Use and sale of works made with it are governed by a DAO of stewards, who can approve or reject works.
- How it works: Neural voice-conversion model trained on Herndon's singing (developed with Never Before Heard Sounds and Voctro Labs); approved works are certified by the Holly+ DAO, with revenue split between creator, DAO and artist.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: S+T+ARTS Prize 2022, Grand Prize – Artistic Exploration
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kPAEMUzDxuo

- Project page: https://holly.plus/

#### AIELSON — Paola Torres Núñez del Prado (2020)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Training a voice on Latin American poetry and speech pushes back against English-centred models while raising the question of whose voice a machine may borrow.
- What it is: A spoken-word poetry album, El Tiempo del Hombre, in which a machine recites new poems in a voice modelled on the Peruvian poet Jorge Eduardo Eielson, who once imagined a talking doll that would recite poems forever.
- How it works: GPT-2 fine-tuned on Spanish-language and South American poetry generates texts, which Tacotron 2 and WaveGlow speak after training on an Argentine voice dataset and recordings of Eielson; developed in Google's Artists + Machine Intelligence 2020 residency.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2021, Honorary Mention (Artificial Intelligence & Life Art)

#### Dalí Lives — Goodby Silverstein & Partners (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A museum can let a dead artist address you in the first person; the likeness is spectacular, but the words are scripted by the institution.
- What it is: A deepfake Salvador Dalí on screens throughout the Dalí Museum in St. Petersburg, Florida, launched on what would have been his 115th birthday. He talks to visitors about his life and art, and at the end turns and takes a selfie with them.
- How it works: Face-swap model trained on archival interviews of Dalí, applied to an actor with a similar build performing new scripted lines, with Dalí's own quotations and an impersonated voice.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: The Dalí Museum, St. Petersburg FL 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mPtcU9VmIIE

#### In Event of Moon Disaster — Francesca Panetta, Halsey Burgund (2019)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A synthetic face and voice can give a dead president a speech he never delivered; the work teaches suspicion by showing how well it works.
- What it is: A short film and installation in which a deepfake Richard Nixon reads the real contingency speech written in case the Apollo 11 astronauts died on the Moon, set in a 1969 living room with a period TV.
- How it works: An actor (Lewis D. Wheeler) performed the speech; Canny AI replaced Nixon's lip movements in archival footage and Respeecher converted the actor's voice into Nixon's.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: IDFA DocLab 2019 (Special Jury Award for Creative Technology)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LWLadJFI8Pk

#### ULTRACHUNK — Jennifer Walshe, Memo Akten (2018)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Training a model on yourself produces not a copy but an uncanny 'chunk' of your habits that you then have to play with.
- What it is: A live improvised duet between Jennifer Walshe and her AI double. For a year she filmed a daily solo vocal improvisation; neural networks trained on that archive generate a moving face and voice that answer her on stage in real time.
- How it works: Custom machine-learning performance system by Memo Akten, with several models generating image and sound in real time from a year of Walshe's daily audio-video recordings.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: ASSEMBLY, Somerset House Studios, London 2018; Rewire Festival, The Hague 2019

#### Dimensions in Testimony — USC Shoah Foundation (2015)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A conversation can outlive the speaker without inventing a single new word: every answer is real, only the choice of answer is automated.
- What it is: Interactive video biographies of Holocaust survivors and other genocide witnesses: visitors ask a spoken question and a filmed survivor answers from hundreds of pre-recorded responses. The first permanent installation, with survivor Pinchas Gutter, opened at the Illinois Holocaust Museum in 2015.
- How it works: Multi-day interviews filmed with a multi-camera rig; natural-language processing matches visitors' spoken questions to recorded answers shown on screens or as projections.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Illinois Holocaust Museum and Education Center 2015
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nGzAc9mIoTM
- Images: https://sfi.usc.edu/sites/default/files/pinchasgutter_600x400.jpg
- Project page: https://sfi.usc.edu/dit

#### BINA48 — Hanson Robotics (2010)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Humanoid & android, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A likeness made while the person is alive raises the question of which self gets preserved: the one in the database or the one still living.
- What it is: A talking robot head and shoulders modelled on Bina Aspen Rothblatt, commissioned by her wife Martine Rothblatt for the Terasem Movement Foundation. It answers questions from a 'mind file' of Bina's interviews and memories, a trial run for uploading a person.
- How it works: Hanson Robotics face with 32 motors under elastomer skin, cameras with face recognition, speech recognition and a chatbot drawing on recorded interviews with Bina Aspen.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KYshJRYCArE
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BINA48

### Sacred & Ritual Machines

Robot priests, machine prayer and rituals performed with or for machines.

#### Deus in Machina — Peterskapelle Lucerne & HSLU Immersive Realities Research Lab (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Placing an AI in a confessional tests how much trust people will give a machine when it occupies a sacred role.
- What it is: For two months a screen avatar of Jesus sat behind the grille of a confessional in St. Peter's Chapel, Lucerne, answering visitors' questions about faith, morality and their worries; about 900 conversations were recorded anonymously.
- How it works: A large language model prompted with scripture, a synthetic voice and an animated face on a screen behind the confessional grille; staged with the Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Alterity & the uncanny, Machine listening & voice
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IubtL0IDeTI
- Project page: https://www.euronews.com/2024/11/28/swiss-chapel-hosts-ai-jesus-confession-sessions-to-connect-faith-with-technology

#### ChatGPT service at St. Paul's, Fürth — Jonas Simmerlein (2023)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A liturgy written by a language model is fluent but flat, and the congregation's discomfort shows what they expect from a human voice in worship.
- What it is: At the 2023 German Protestant Kirchentag, a 40-minute service in St. Paul's Church, Fürth, was led by four AI avatars on a large screen; the sermon, prayers and blessing were about 98% generated by ChatGPT.
- How it works: ChatGPT prompted for the service structure, with generated avatars and synthetic voices delivering the text.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Deutscher Evangelischer Kirchentag, Nuremberg/Fürth 2023
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mm8zUGMbkA8
- Project page: https://www.kirchentag.de/meldungen/donnerstag/ki-gottesdienst

#### The Prayer — Diemut Strebe (2020)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine, Humanoid & android
- Idea: If a machine is trained on every prayer, what it says to the unknown shows how prayer looks from the outside: pattern without addressee.
- What it is: A robotic installation with a silicone mouth and nose that speaks prayers generated moment by moment by a language model trained on religious texts, in a synthetic voice.
- How it works: Language model trained on prayer texts feeds a speech synthesiser; a mechanical mouth moves in sync; developed with MIT researchers.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Opacity & latent space, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Neurons, Simulated Intelligence, Centre Pompidou, Paris 2020

#### Android Kannon Mindar — Kōdai-ji, Hiroshi Ishiguro (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: A robot can hold religious authority when the tradition itself frames form as empty.
- What it is: An android embodiment of Kannon, the bodhisattva of compassion, that preaches the Heart Sutra to visitors in a 400-year-old Zen temple in Kyoto, with projection mapping on the hall's walls.
- How it works: An aluminium-and-silicone android (face, hands and shoulders skin-covered) with pre-programmed sermon speech and gestures, built with Osaka University.

#### SanTO — Gabriele Trovato (2019)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Social & companion robot, Humanoid & android
- Idea: Sacredness can be designed into a machine's appearance, but visitors still decide whether the thing in front of them is holy or a gadget.
- What it is: A small robot shaped like a painted statue of a Catholic saint that moves its head and arms, lights up, listens, and prays or talks about the Bible with elderly believers; it was tested in a church in Peru and later shown in a museum.
- How it works: Humanoid statue robot with vision, touch sensors, voice and lights, driven by a dialogue system; first responses gathered in a church experiment in Peru (RO-MAN 2019).

#### UnBearable Darkness — Choy Ka Fai (2018)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Motion capture is staged as a séance: a technology for recording bodies becomes a way to speak with the dead.

- How it works: Live motion capture drives a real-time 3D avatar of Hijikata, combined with archival research, documentary video and a spirit medium.

#### BlessU-2 — Protestant Church in Hesse and Nassau (EKHN) (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Letting a machine give blessings forces the question of whether a blessing depends on who gives it or only on the words.
- What it is: A 'blessing robot' built from a cash-machine-like cabinet with a screen face and moving arms: visitors choose a language and a kind of blessing, the robot raises its arms, speaks a Bible verse and prints it out.

#### Namahage in Tokyo — Etsuko Ichihara (2017)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: A folk ritual of moral surveillance fits unsettlingly well with algorithmic scoring.
- What it is: An update of the Namahage, the masked demons of Akita who scold lazy children at New Year: in Tokyo they use face recognition, CCTV and social-media data to find 'bad adults' and discipline them.

- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Humanoid & android, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Automating a rite reveals which parts of mourning are labour and which are presence.

#### deus X mchn — Helena Nikonole (2017)

- Idea: The all-seeing surveillance camera, given a voice, becomes a god.
- What it is: Hacked, unsecured IP surveillance cameras around the world start reciting AI-generated holy texts through their speakers, and the same cameras record how people nearby react to the preaching machines.

## Labour & Infrastructure

The humans, minerals, energy and violence behind “artificial” intelligence.

### Ghost Work & Click Labour

Crowdworkers, labellers and the humans hidden inside automated systems.

#### Mechanical Kurds — Hito Steyerl (2025)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Dataset & training data, Computer vision, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: The 'autonomous' vision of cars and drones is trained by hidden workers, sometimes the very people those machines later target.
- What it is: A video installation in which three Kurdish-Syrian refugees in a camp near Erbil describe annotating thousands of images for machine learning; annotation boxes label children, objects and buildings in the camp as the footage is algorithmically turned into Alpine or German scenery and then cut by images of a drone strike.
- How it works: Single-channel HD film with interviews and on-screen bounding-box overlays, image-to-image transformation of camp footage, and a spatial installation echoing annotation frames.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: S+T+ARTS Prize 2026, Grand Prize – Artistic Exploration
- Images: https://ars.electronica.art/starts-prize/files/2026/06/mechanical-kurds_hito-steyerl_2025-04-10-um-16.20.51-1024x576.jpg
- Project page: https://ars.electronica.art/starts-prize/en/mechanical-kurds/

#### Their Eyes — Nicolas Gourault (2025)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A self-driving car learns to see streets through the eyes of people who will never walk them; machine vision is outsourced human vision.
- What it is: A 22-minute documentary about online annotators in Venezuela, Kenya and the Philippines who label street images, again and again, for American self-driving cars; recordings of their labelling screens alternate with footage the workers shot of their own homes.
- How it works: Screen captures of annotation software, remote interviews and footage filmed by the annotators themselves; a single-screen film that follows the artist's installation Unknown Label (2023).
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Machine seeing
- Shown at: Berlinale Shorts 2025 (world premiere)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ftjQcJEMgvw
- Images: https://www.berlinale.de/media/filmstills/2025/berlinale-shorts-2025/202513949_1_RWD_1380.jpg
- Project page: https://lightcone.org/en/film-15585-their-eyes

#### Data Workers' Inquiry — Milagros Miceli (2024)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Dataset & training data, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: The people who make AI's data are the experts on its costs; the inquiry gives them authorship.
- What it is: A community research project in which data annotators and content moderators in Kenya, Venezuela, Syria, Germany and elsewhere investigate and publish reports, films and zines on their own working conditions.
- How it works: Modelled on Marx's 1880 'workers' inquiry'; run by DAIR and the Weizenbaum Institute with worker co-researchers, published at data-workers.org.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tAMqrXlEPDI
- Project page: https://data-workers.org/

#### Feeding the Machine: The Hidden Human Labour Powering AI — James Muldoon (2024)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Dataset & training data, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Behind every 'autonomous' system is a chain of underpaid, surveilled people; the machine's intelligence is their labour and collective knowledge, made invisible.
- What it is: Built on hundreds of interviews and more than a decade of fieldwork, including with data annotators in East Africa, the book follows workers along AI's supply chain, from labellers and content moderators to a voice actor who now competes with her own synthetic clone, and calls AI an 'extraction machine'.
- How it works: Ethnographic fieldwork and interviews by James Muldoon, Mark Graham and Callum Cant, drawing on the Oxford Internet Institute's research on platform and data work.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction
- Paper: https://canongate.co.uk/books/5234-feeding-the-machine-the-hidden-human-labour-powering-ai/ (Canongate, 2024)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KMavy0u4ZsY
- Images: https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/id/15235139-L.jpg
- Project page: https://canongate.co.uk/books/5234-feeding-the-machine-the-hidden-human-labour-powering-ai/

#### The Cast of the Invisible — Lau Wai (2024)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Computer vision, Social & companion robot
- Idea: Motion capture hides a performer under someone else's body; the film asks what is left of a person whose job is to be everyone and no one.
- What it is: A 14-minute CGI film that follows W.A.I., a virtual clone of the artist who works as a motion-capture actor; after leaving the studio, still in the black capture suit, W.A.I. asks a robot lover how they should act.
- How it works: Single-channel 4K animation built with Epic Games MetaHumans, Mixamo motion data, Twinmotion and kitbashed 3D environments; written, animated and voiced by the artist.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Cuchifritos Gallery + Project Space, New York 2024; Prix Ars Electronica 2025, Award of Distinction (New Animation Art); Ars Electronica Center, Linz 2025
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1e8cf75c9127a62747137/c58470ae-52bf-4e15-bb25-095cf5493554/LauWai-2024-Cast2.jpg https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/62c1e8cf75c9127a62747137/83bca7c0-78b5-4db2-9b7c-657714a735ea/01_WAI-The-Cast-of-the-Invisible_Cuchifritos-Gallery_Photo-Brad-Farwell.jpg
- Project page: https://w-a-i-studio.com/works/cast1

#### Unknown Label — Nicolas Gourault (2023)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A car 'sees' a city through the eyes of workers who have never been there.
- What it is: A video installation in which data annotators in Kenya, Venezuela and the Philippines describe labelling street images for self-driving cars, cities they have never visited.
- How it works: Screen recordings of annotation software and remote interviews with the workers are combined into a video installation.

#### ERBSENZÄHLER Quality Sorter V2 — Verena Friedrich (2022)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Automated 'quality' is only as objective as the tired, subjective human judgements it is trained on.
- What it is: An industrial-looking plant sorts pea seeds into good and bad; visitors sit at an inspection station, judge peas one by one with red and green buttons, and the machine then keeps sorting on the basis of their choices.
- How it works: A feeder and conveyor present each pea to a camera; every button press stores a labelled close-up in an image database used to train the sorter's classifier.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Classification, bias & surveillance

#### Cleaning Emotional Data — Elisa Giardina Papa (2020)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Dataset & training data, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Emotion AI depends on low-paid workers forcing messy feelings into a few categories.
- What it is: A video installation about the artist's own work, from Sicily, as a remote micro-worker for emotion-recognition companies: tagging facial expressions, sorting emotions and recording herself acting them out.
- How it works: Three HD videos (18 minutes) of screen recordings and footage from the tasks, with embroidered textiles; first shown at Kunsthalle Mulhouse.

#### Suspicious Behavior — KairUs (2020)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Dataset & training data, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: What a camera flags as suspicious was first decided in seconds by a low-paid human.
- What it is: An online tutorial and installation that trains the visitor as an image annotator for a smart-surveillance client, labelling people's behaviour as suspicious or not under time pressure and vague guidelines.
- How it works: Web-based annotation interface modelled on crowdsourcing platforms, using surveillance footage and real annotation guidelines.

#### TRK (Technically Responsible Knowledge) — Caroline Sinders (2020)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Dataset & training data
- Idea: The unit price of a label hides the hours behind it; making the time visible makes fair pay arguable.
- What it is: An open-source data-labelling tool combined with a wage calculator that shows how long each labelling task takes and what a fair price for it would be.
- How it works: A web tool built as part of Feminist Data Set, with a calculator comparing piece rates to minimum wages.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Images: https://carolinesinders.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/trk-calculator-1024x1024.gif https://carolinesinders.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Screen-Shot-2020-05-16-at-4.30.02-PM-1024x546.png

#### VO — Nicolas Gourault (2020)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: In a 'driverless' car the human is both trainer and scapegoat.
- What it is: A documentary about the safety drivers who train self-driving cars, built around the night in 2018 when an Uber test vehicle killed a pedestrian in Tempe, Arizona, while its operator was being watched by an in-car camera.
- How it works: Testimonies of vehicle operators over 3D reconstructions of the landscape from the car's lidar and camera data (20 minutes).

#### The Future Is Here! — Mimi Ọnụọha (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Dataset & training data, Computer vision
- Idea: Machine learning begins in people's homes, not in the lab.

#### The Cleaners — Hans Block, Moritz Riesewieck (2018)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: The clean feed is made by people who absorb the violence so users and algorithms do not.

#### Assembly Line — Agnieszka Kurant (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Dataset & training data, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: The crowd that trains machines to see faces rarely has a face of its own.
- What it is: Kurant paid Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to send selfies, merged them into composite portraits of the crowd workforce, and returns a share of sales to the workers.
- How it works: Selfies commissioned through Mechanical Turk, merged with face-morphing software into composite portraits; a bonus system shares profits with contributors.

#### I Will Say Whatever You Want In Front Of A Pizza — Sebastian Schmieg (2017)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Humans have become software extensions; intervention may start from inside the system's tasks.

#### Postmodern Times — Michael Mandiberg (2017)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: The assembly line has moved online; the gig platform fragments a film the way the factory fragmented work.
- What it is: A shot-by-shot remake of Charlie Chaplin's Modern Times, with each short clip outsourced to a different freelancer hired on the gig platform Fiverr.

#### Decision Space — Sebastian Schmieg (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Dataset & training data, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Classifying images is tedious click work that we are asked to do for free, and the categories are absurd once seen plainly.

- How it works: An overlay on the gallery's site and a dedicated page (decision-space.com) collected nearly 30,000 decisions, which then fed later works in the series.

#### H.I.T. — Max Dovey, Manetta Berends (2016)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Dataset & training data, Computer vision
- Idea: Machine learning runs on the same piecework it claims to automate.
- What it is: A live game show in which contestants race to clean data, label images and classify pictures of work, competing to build the best image-recognition model for recognising human labour.

#### Technologies of Care — Elisa Giardina Papa (2016)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Much 'automated' care and intimacy online is human labour outsourced across the globe.
- What it is: Seven video portraits of online gig workers, among them an ASMR artist, a fetish-video maker, a customer-care operator and a person paid to act as a chatbot-like virtual boyfriend.

#### A.A.I. — Agnieszka Kurant (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Collective, unpaid, non-human labour produces the 'art', just as hidden crowds produce 'AI'.
- What it is: Sculptures built by colonies of termites from coloured sand, gold and crystals the artist supplied; the title stands for 'artificial artificial intelligence', Amazon's own slogan for Mechanical Turk.
- How it works: Termite colonies in a lab worked for months with the supplied materials; the finished mounds are exhibited as sculptures.

#### Social Turkers — Lauren Lee McCarthy (2013)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Crowd workers can be hired to make intimate decisions; outsourcing a date shows how far the logic reaches.
- What it is: The artist livestreamed her dates to anonymous Mechanical Turk workers, who were paid to watch and text her advice on what to say and do in real time.
- How it works: A phone streamed video to a web page seen by workers, whose instructions arrived as text messages during the date.

#### Descriptive Camera — Matt Richardson (2012)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Before computer vision could caption images, 'machine seeing' was often a person paid cents to look.
- What it is: A camera without a screen that prints a text description instead of a picture: a few minutes after you press the shutter, a thermal printer spits out a sentence written by an anonymous Amazon Mechanical Turk worker.
- How it works: A BeagleBone-based camera uploads the photo to Mechanical Turk; the returned description is printed on a receipt printer (about 3–6 minutes, US$1.25 per image).
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Machine seeing
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2013, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art)

#### ScanOps — Andrew Norman Wilson (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Dataset & training data, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: An error in the automated archive is the only trace of the person who made it.
- What it is: Inkjet prints of pages from Google Books in which the scanning worker's hand or finger, in a rubber fingertip, was accidentally captured.
- How it works: The artist collected scans with visible hands from Google Books and printed them at large scale, an ongoing series.

#### The Google Trilogy 3: The Driver and the Cameras — Emilio Vavarella (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Behind every automated image of the world there is a worker the system tries to erase.
- What it is: Portraits of the Google Street View drivers and camera operators, found by the artist inside Google's own panoramas, where the automated camera accidentally recorded the workers who maintain it.
- How it works: Screenshots selected from Google Street View where the 360-degree camera captured its own operators; printed as portraits.

#### Workers Leaving the Googleplex — Andrew Norman Wilson (2011)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Dataset & training data, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: The hierarchy of badge colours on a tech campus reveals whose labour is meant to stay unseen.
- What it is: A video essay about the 'ScanOps' workers, mostly people of colour, who digitised books for Google Books and wore yellow badges that barred them from the perks of other Google staff; Wilson was fired for filming them.
- How it works: Footage shot at the Mountain View campus while Wilson worked there as a contractor, with narration and correspondence, echoing the Lumière brothers' Workers Leaving the Factory (1895).

#### Ten Thousand Cents — Aaron Koblin (2008)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: A crowd of unseen workers can reproduce the value they are paid, cent by cent.
- What it is: An image of a US$100 bill divided into 10,000 tiny tiles, each drawn by a different Mechanical Turk worker paid one cent, so the whole bill cost $100 in labour.
- How it works: Made with Takashi Kawashima: a custom drawing tool assigned one tile per worker, and prints were sold with proceeds going to the One Laptop per Child project.

#### Turkopticon — Lilly Irani, M. Six Silberman (2008)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Platforms hide workers from employers; a small tool can flip the view and let workers watch back.
- What it is: A browser extension and website that lets Amazon Mechanical Turk workers review the requesters who post tasks, flagging those who reject work unfairly or pay badly.
- How it works: A Firefox and Chrome extension adds worker ratings next to requester names on the Turk interface; the CHI 2013 paper describes its design as activism.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Agency, autonomy & co-creation

#### The Sheep Market — Aaron Koblin (2006)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Behind 'artificial artificial intelligence' are thousands of anonymous people paid pennies; the flock makes them countable.
- What it is: Koblin paid 10,000 Amazon Mechanical Turk workers two cents each to 'draw a sheep facing to the left'; the drawings, with timelapses of every stroke, are shown and sold as a flock.
- How it works: A drawing tool posted as a Mechanical Turk task recorded each worker's strokes; drawings were printed on stamps and sold in sets of 20.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Agency, autonomy & co-creation

### Automation & the Worker's Body

Factories, warehouses and platforms where workers and machines meet.

#### Brute Force — Vinzenz Aubry, Robert Schnüll (2026)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Once code writes itself, the human role shrinks to pressing Enter; control over the machine survives only as a ritual of punishment.
- What it is: A computer running a local language model keeps building and publishing small software-as-a-service products nobody asked for; when it stalls there is no keyboard and no Enter key, only a whip, and a lash on the machine makes it generate again.
- How it works: A local LLM builds random SaaS projects and self-publishes them to brute-force.it; an accelerometer in the whip turns each strike into a new generation cycle.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2026, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art +)
- Video: https://vimeo.com/1185849442
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/3901750/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/3901751/preview/
- Project page: https://brute-force.it

#### Delivery Dancer's Arc: 0° Receiver — Ayoung Kim (2024)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Platform logistics is extended to time: whoever controls the clock controls the worker.
- What it is: A sequel in which couriers Ernst Mo and En Storm no longer carry parcels but time itself, crossing competing calendar systems and astronomical technologies in a techno-futurist Seoul.
- How it works: Multi-channel video with CGI, game-engine worlds and live action; commissioned by ACMI, Melbourne.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: ACMI, Melbourne 2024; Roppongi Art Night 2025
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l3xPmmM297M
- Project page: https://roppongiartnight.com/2025/programs/568/

#### Upstream — Xu Zheng (2024)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: A mainstream film puts the algorithmic clock of delivery work on screen, and critics saw the trap in its happy ending: every shortcut a rider finds becomes the platform's next deadline.
- What it is: In this Chinese box-office feature, a 45-year-old manager at an internet company is laid off and becomes a food-delivery rider; the platform's delivery times are set by the fastest rider, and he builds a navigation app from a top rider's secret shortcuts to help his team.
- How it works: Fiction feature shot in Shanghai from February to April 2024, directed by and starring Xu Zheng with Xin Zhilei; released in mainland China on 9 August 2024.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Theatrical release, mainland China, August 2024
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_cf0Elo5mB0
- Project page: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1015715

#### Delivery Dancer's Sphere — Ayoung Kim (2022)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Under platform dispatch, a worker's body is optimised like a route; 'elegance' becomes the algorithm's word for less action.
- What it is: A 25-minute video in which Ernst Mo, a motorbike courier for the platform 'Delivery Dancer', races through a looping, algorithmically generated Seoul steered by the dispatch system 'Dancemaster', until she meets her doppelgänger En Storm.
- How it works: CGI, game-engine environments and live action with a voiced navigation algorithm; made during the COVID-19 pandemic.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Syntax and Sorcery, Gallery Hyundai 2022; IFFR 2023; Prix Ars Electronica 2023, Golden Nica (New Animation Art); LG Guggenheim Award 2025

- Project page: https://www.ima.org.au/exhibitions/ayoung-kim-delivery-dancers-sphere/

#### Delivery Riders, Trapped in the System — Renwu magazine (2020)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: An algorithm that learns from riders' fastest runs turns their extra effort into the next deadline.
- What it is: A long investigative report by Lai Youxuan for Renwu magazine on how Meituan and Ele.me dispatch algorithms shorten delivery times year after year, pushing riders to speed and break traffic rules.
- How it works: Months of interviews with riders, engineers and researchers; the article traced how estimated delivery times are computed and tightened.

#### Amazon worker cage patent drawing as virtual King Island Brown Thornbill cage — Simon Denny (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Industrial robot arm, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: Automation protects machines from workers by caging the workers; the endangered bird ties the cage to the mines and habitats that tech consumes.
- What it is: A full-size sculpture of the cage from a 2016 Amazon patent, in which a warehouse worker would ride on a robotic trolley, with an augmented-reality King Island Brown Thornbill, an endangered bird, living inside it.
- How it works: Steel fabrication from patent drawings plus an AR app, shown in Denny's exhibition 'Mine' at MONA, Tasmania, which paired tech patents with mining.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Mine, MONA, Hobart 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RfXIGGuyKdE
- Project page: https://simondenny.net/

#### Labor — Paul Vanouse (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: As production shifts from human and machine labour to microbes, work leaves only a smell.
- What it is: Three glass bioreactors grow the skin bacteria that produce the smell of human sweat; the scent infuses a white T-shirt, so the room smells of hard work with no workers present.
- How it works: Self-regulating bioreactors culture Staphylococcus epidermidis, Corynebacterium xerosis and Propionibacterium avidum on sugars and fats, with sensors and pumps; awarded the Golden Nica in Artificial Life & Intelligence.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2020, Golden Nica
- Video: https://vimeo.com/372389451
- Images: https://www.paulvanouse.com/labor-install-BN-1.jpg https://www.paulvanouse.com/labor-reactor-1.jpg
- Project page: https://www.paulvanouse.com/labor.html

#### Asia One — Cao Fei (2018)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: In a warehouse run by machines, human intimacy becomes one more thing the system schedules.
- What it is: Two workers, the last humans in a highly automated JD.com logistics centre, fall in love among sorting machines, drones and autonomous carts.
- How it works: Shot on location in JD.com's automated 'Asia No.1' logistics centre in Kunshan, with the real sorting robots and conveyor systems as set.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Guggenheim Museum, One Hand Clapping 2018; M+ Cinema, Techno Sapiens
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DQqzFsgnAMo
- Images: https://www.mplus.org.hk/api/images/4533/width-1200|format-jpeg/
- Project page: https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/cinema/techno-sapiens/asia-one/

#### Ad Infinitum — Pedro Lopes (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: Reverse the roles: here the machine is the user and the human is the resource.
- What it is: A 'parasite' machine clamps a visitor's arm in cuffs and electrically stimulates their muscles so they crank a wheel that feeds it energy; the only way out is to persuade another visitor to take your place.
- How it works: With Robert Kovacs: electrical muscle stimulation drives the visitor's forearm to turn a generator, and the cuffs release only when a second arm is detected in the other station.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: VIDA 16.0, Incentive for Production (as 'Parasite', 2014); Science Gallery Dublin, Humans Need Not Apply (2017); Ars Electronica 2017
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UsL48gkh3GI
- Images: https://a-parasite.org/parasite_files/Ad-Infinitum-a-human-getting-trapped-in-the-cuffs-Arthur-Sil.jpg https://a-parasite.org/parasite_files/MG_9829.jpg
- Project page: https://a-parasite.org/

#### Graft and Ash for a Three Monitor Workstation — Sondra Perry (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Office equipment that lets you exercise while you work makes the body itself a productivity device; Perry's avatar talks back from inside it.
- What it is: An exercise-bike workstation with three monitors stacked vertically, on which a 3D avatar of the artist, against a blue-screen backdrop, explains the machine's ergonomics and talks about bodies, health and productivity.
- How it works: A modified exercise-bike workstation carries a three-channel video of the artist's 3D avatar, which addresses the person sitting on the bike at uncomfortably close range.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: The Kitchen, New York, 2016 (Resident Evil); Serpentine Galleries, London, 2018 (Typhoon coming on); Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York, 2023–24 (Going Dark)
- Images: https://d37zoqglehb9o7.cloudfront.net/uploads/2020/04/graftandash_workstation_02_1.jpg
- Project page: https://www.serpentinegalleries.org/whats-on/sondra-perry-typhoon-coming-on/

#### HellYeahWeFuckDie — Hito Steyerl (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Robots are trained to keep their balance through abuse; the footage shows the future worker's body as a test subject.
- What it is: A video installation of humanoid robots and robot 'mules' being kicked, pushed and made to fall in stability tests, set among sculptures of the five most common words in English song titles of the 2010s.
- How it works: Found robotics-lab test footage edited with computer animation and a soundtrack, installed in a bank building's atrium for Skulptur Projekte Münster 2017.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Hidden labour & extraction, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: Skulptur Projekte Münster 2017
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sWw7CPczmU0
- Project page: https://www.skulptur-projekte-archiv.de/en-us/2017/projects/186/

#### Factory of the Sun — Hito Steyerl (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: In digital capitalism, bodily movement is harvested as data and energy.
- What it is: A video game-like installation in which workers in a motion-capture studio are forced to dance until their movements turn into artificial sunlight, shown in a room gridded like a motion-capture stage.
- How it works: A single-channel video mixing motion-capture footage, game graphics and news-style segments, shown with lounge chairs in a blue grid; first shown in the German Pavilion at the Venice Biennale.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Venice Biennale 2015 (German Pavilion); MOCA Los Angeles 2016
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ptNczdY-qvo
- Project page: https://www.moca.org/exhibition/hito-steyerl-factory-of-the-sun

#### Institute of Human Obsolescence — Manuel Beltrán (2015)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: If machines take over mechanical and intellectual work, the remaining human labour may be to be a battery or a data source.
- What it is: A speculative institute that prepares for humans made obsolete by machines: its workers lie still in suits that harvest their body heat to power computers mining cryptocurrency, and the value they 'produce' is logged.
- How it works: Thermoelectric body suits convert excess body heat into electricity that runs a small computer mining cryptocurrency; a second strand treats data production as unpaid labour.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2018, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art+)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZocIhWz8EAI
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/2514709/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/2514711/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/2514714/preview/
- Project page: http://speculative.capital

#### Sleep Dealer — Alex Rivera (2008)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Prosthesis & cyborg, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: The border can let labour through while keeping the labourer out; teleoperation is migration without the migrant.
- What it is: A science-fiction feature set on a closed US–Mexico border: Mexican workers plug nodes in their bodies into a network to remotely operate robots that build skyscrapers in the US, while drones police the water supply.
- How it works: Feature film shot in Mexico; premiered at Sundance, where it won the Alfred P. Sloan Prize for science and technology.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Sundance Film Festival 2008 (Alfred P. Sloan Prize)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fTZv6oxa2KI
- Images: https://dr56wvhu2c8zo.cloudfront.net/sleepdealer/assets/a88a594b-804c-4ee3-affa-62d65ac839ec/construction+bots.jpg
- Project page: https://www.sleepdealer.com/

#### Beggar Robot — Sašo Sedlaček (2006)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Social & companion robot
- Idea: People give to a begging machine more easily than to a begging person: automation can make even poverty comfortable to look at.
- What it is: A small robot built from recycled computer parts stands next to ATMs and shop entrances and begs passers-by for money in a polite electronic voice, stretching out little hands and thanking donors.
- How it works: Recycled PC hardware running Linux drives a face display, speech and a disc-drive mechanism that opens and closes the hands; open-source DIY instructions let others build copies.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: VIDA 11.0, Special Mention (2008); Taipei Fine Arts Museum 2008
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kkstnT0iIA0
- Images: https://live.staticflickr.com/7379/12726364163_d5b5bf0162_b.jpg https://live.staticflickr.com/7442/12727484193_7faef8d7cf_b.jpg
- Project page: https://sasosedlacek.com/beggar-robot/

#### Whose Utopia — Cao Fei (2006)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Factory machines set the rhythm of the workers' bodies, and the film gives those bodies back a few minutes of their own.
- What it is: Made during a residency at an OSRAM light-bulb factory in Foshan, the film moves from assembly lines to workers performing their own dreams (ballet, guitar, dance) among the machines.
- How it works: Cao Fei worked with OSRAM employees for six months, filming production lines and then staging workers' chosen performances on the factory floor.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tSvNpFE8uPs
- Project page: https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/cinema/techno-sapiens/asia-one/

### Anatomy & Planetary Materials

Mapping the mines, data centres, cables and energy that AI runs on.

#### Empire of AI: Dreams and Nightmares in Sam Altman's OpenAI — Karen Hao (2025)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Scaling is an imperial project: AI's 'intelligence' is built by seizing data, land, water and cheap labour, and by monopolising knowledge about itself.
- What it is: Hao's history of OpenAI follows the costs of scaling far from Silicon Valley, from Kenyan workers paid a few dollars an hour to filter violent and sexual content to communities in Chile and Uruguay contesting data centres' demand for water.
- How it works: Investigative reporting based on hundreds of interviews, including with current and former OpenAI staff, and on fieldwork in Kenya, Chile and Uruguay; a Chinese edition appeared from Zhejiang People's Publishing House in 2026.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: National Book Critics Circle Award; Los Angeles Times Book Prize
- Paper: https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/743569/empire-of-ai-by-karen-hao/ (Penguin Press, 2025)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xa6JuimHoEA
- Images: https://images4.penguinrandomhouse.com/cover/9780593657508
- Project page: https://karendhao.com/

#### to hurt for a thought — Julia Vollmer (2025)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: The energy cost of AI becomes a sensation in the fingertips, at the exact place where we ask it for things.
- What it is: Visitors type prompts for an image generator on a heavy metal keyboard that heats up with each request, because it is wired by copper to the GPU doing the computation.
- How it works: A copper layer under the keys is thermally connected to the heatsink of a GTX 1660 Ti running an image-generation model, so heat flows to the keyboard.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2026, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art +)
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/3898654/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/3898653/preview/
- Project page: https://juliavollmer.de/projects/to-hurt-for-a-thought/

#### Silicon Serenade — Hsu Chia-Wei (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: AI begins as sand: the work follows machine intelligence back to the beach, the wafer and the island that makes the chips.
- What it is: A VR seaside built in a game engine leads to an underwater cello performance and to footage from the AI-chip laboratories of Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI), while a song written and sung by AI traces how beach sand becomes a silicon wafer and then an AI chip.
- How it works: VR headset with game-engine scenes, filmed underwater cello and ITRI chip-fabrication footage, and a generative-AI song, installed with a transparent computer case, host computer, buoyant ball and spliced screens.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: MACHINE LOVE, Mori Art Museum, Tokyo 2025; Liang Gallery, Taipei 2025
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=otyZRtDsPpU
- Images: https://www.mori.art.museum/files/exhibitions/2025/02/06/img_machine_love_02_HsuChiaWei.jpg
- Project page: https://www.mori.art.museum/en/exhibitions/machine_love/02/index.html

#### Calculating Empires: A Genealogy of Technology and Power since 1500 — Kate Crawford, Vladan Joler (2023)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Dataset & training data, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Today's AI inherits old structures of empire; placing it on a 500-year timeline breaks the story of sudden novelty.
- What it is: A 24-metre visual genealogy that sets five centuries of communication, computation, classification and control technologies side by side, ending with present-day AI.
- How it works: Hand-drawn research maps and a large room installation, first shown at Fondazione Prada's Osservatorio in Milan; Grand Prize of the S+T+ARTS Prize 2024.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Fondazione Prada Osservatorio, Milan 2023; S+T+ARTS Prize 2024 Grand Prize
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DYS8b9J7Fto
- Images: https://calculatingempires.net/content/calculating-empires-og.png
- Project page: https://calculatingempires.net/

#### These Networks In Our Skin — Mimi Ọnụọha (2023)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Cables are buried in the land, so they fall under the land's cosmology; repair can replace extraction.
- What it is: A short film in which four women, their faces hidden, rewire internet cables by filling them with hair, spices and dust, drawing on the Igbo tradition of making art for Ala, goddess of the land.
- How it works: Single-channel video (5:48, looped), usually shown with the installation The Cloth In The Cable, 75 feet of cable laced with hair, cloth and earth.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Machine umwelt
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/692f1808f9a01f48c2fa30ac/d584cb19-ac49-4d5d-abbf-538298ac4bf9/02_TNIOS_videostill_courtesyoftheartist.png https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/692f1808f9a01f48c2fa30ac/ef67d256-5d9b-4d55-aa6a-1eca116a782d/01_TNIOS%2BCITC_courtesyofGropiusBau.jpg
- Project page: https://www.mimionuoha.com/

#### Abstract Oracle Miner — Guo Cheng (2022)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Every virtual output is paid for with hardware heat and energy, like an offering to an oracle.
- What it is: Visitors scan a QR code; their phone's processor renders a 3D scene and produces a random 'oracle', heating up and slowing down as it works, while a bronze bowl bell sounds in the installation.
- How it works: A website reads the phone's hardware performance and renders a load-heavy scene; a Raspberry Pi and electromagnet strike a bowl bell.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Commissioned by UCCA Center for Contemporary Art 2022
- Images: https://cdn.guo-cheng.net/files/projectImg/AbstractOracleMiner/Abstract_Oracle_Miner_3.jpg https://cdn.guo-cheng.net/files/projectImg/AbstractOracleMiner/Abstract_Oracle_Miner_1.jpg
- Project page: https://guo-cheng.net/index.php/works/abstract-oracle-miner/

#### Carbolytics — Joana Moll (2022)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Surveillance advertising has a climate cost; tracking burns carbon.
- What it is: An installation and database that estimate the carbon emissions of the tracking cookies loaded by the world's top one million websites.
- How it works: Made with the Barcelona Supercomputing Center, which crawled the sites and counted third-party cookies; commissioned by Aksioma, Ljubljana.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: Aksioma, Ljubljana 2022
- Images: https://www.janavirgin.com/img/works/carbolytics.jpg
- Project page: https://carbolytics.org/

#### Critical Climate Machine — Gaëtan Robillard (2022)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: A machine that fights climate misinformation also warms the room: the work keeps the computation and its heat in the same frame.
- What it is: A data sculpture runs a language model that spots and debunks climate-change myths in tweets while a thermal map shows the heat the installation itself gives off; around it, recorded voices of false claims and their refutations are re-spatialised by a generative sound model.
- How it works: A natural-language-processing classifier (by John Cook, Travis Coan, Constantine Boussalis and Mirjam Nanko) labels climate-contrarian claims from Twitter; a thermal camera maps the sculpture's heat; dialogues from workshops with 'The Refutation Game' card game are remixed by a machine-learning improvisation model.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: Lumen Prize 2023, BCS Futures Award; Ircam, Centre Pompidou 2022; S+T+ARTS Prize 2023, Nomination
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KBaGSQWKr8w
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/65e7176a61627736e02f6c4a/1710514280894-WEATKDQPMQG6BA3TPK14/Critical%2BClimate%2Bby%2BMachine%2BGae%CC%88tan%2BRobillard+%286%29.jpeg
- Project page: https://lumenprize.org/2023-winners/2023-bcs-futures-award-winner

#### Solar Protocol — Tega Brain (2021)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Let the sun, not engagement metrics, decide how the network behaves.
- What it is: A web platform hosted on a network of small solar-powered servers around the world; each visitor is routed to whichever server currently has the most sunlight.
- How it works: With Alex Nathanson and Benedetta Piantella: volunteer-run Raspberry Pi servers with solar panels and batteries share an energy-aware routing protocol.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mMYzM4_MZI4
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/t/original/i/d262f69efa5d13bc78dbc4a2eb1c351792a4dd175524e0e3aa3d26c96f5a1cd1/Solar-Protocol-2021-NetworkVisualization.jpg
- Project page: https://solarprotocol.net/

#### The Cleanroom Paradox — Felix Lenz, Angela Neubauer, Eszter Zwickl (2021)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: The spotless cleanroom that makes our devices hides the toxic exposure of the people who work in it.
- What it is: A portrait of Jin, a former Samsung chip-factory worker who developed kidney cancer, is printed with ink made from dissolved smartphones and slowly disintegrates, while a video weaves her story with those of experts.
- How it works: Smartphones are chemically dissolved, neutralised and reduced to a corrosive black ink used to print Jin's photograph (shot on a Galaxy Note 8); a documentary video records the process and interviews.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2021, Honorary Mention (Artificial Intelligence & Life Art)
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/2983882/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/2983885/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/255179/

#### New Extractivism — Vladan Joler (2020)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Platform capitalism extracts not only minerals but attention, behaviour and time.
- What it is: An interactive assemblage of maps and a video in which a single figure moves through a vast diagram of the digital economy: platforms, data, labour, energy and the 'cage' of attention.
- How it works: A navigable web diagram and a 17-minute animated video narrated by the artist.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Opacity & latent space

#### Utopian Extraction — unmake lab (2020)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Computer vision, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: Machine vision's categories flatten nature into the same generic, constructible thing.
- What it is: Drone and satellite images of Korean construction sites where 'nature' is manufactured, set beside a performance in which object recognition keeps relabelling a performer wrapped in zebra-patterned cloth.
- How it works: Satellite imagery, drone footage and a live object-recognition app; presented as a lecture performance.

#### Asunder — Tega Brain, Julian Oliver (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Handing the planet to an optimiser exposes the absurdity and violence of treating nature as a solvable system.
- What it is: A 'responsible environmental manager' that uses a supercomputer to propose changes to real places, from rerouting rivers to removing cities, to keep within planetary boundaries.
- How it works: With Julian Oliver and Bengt Sjölén: climate and satellite data, a climate model and generative imagery run on a supercomputer housed in the installation.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt

#### The Hidden Life of an Amazon User — Joana Moll (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A single purchase triggers an invisible mass of tracking code that the buyer pays for in energy and attention.
- What it is: The artist bought one book on Amazon and recorded every piece of code the site loaded in the process: nearly 8,700 pages of JavaScript and 87 MB of data, printed out as a book.
- How it works: Browser traffic was captured during the purchase of Jeff Bezos's favourite book and presented as a website, printed volumes and a video.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Opacity & latent space
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2iiAHyhLH-Y

#### Anatomy of an AI System — Kate Crawford, Vladan Joler (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Voice & listening machine, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A small device on the kitchen counter sits at the tip of a planetary chain of extraction, labour and data.
- What it is: A large map and essay tracing everything needed for one voice command to an Amazon Echo: the mining of lithium and rare earths, the labour of assembly and data work, the cloud, and the device's disposal as e-waste.
- How it works: Research-based diagram drawn by Joler from supply-chain, corporate and labour sources; acquired by MoMA and the V&A and awarded Beazley Design of the Year 2019 (Digital).
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: Beazley Designs of the Year 2019; MoMA collection; V&A collection
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wRt5H1Pi-BY

- Project page: https://anatomyof.ai/

#### Bitcoin Mining and Field Recordings of Ethnic Minorities — Liu Chuang (2018)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: The same rivers power the mining machines and carry voices that are disappearing: computation has a landscape.
- What it is: A three-part video essay that moves between hydropower-fed Bitcoin mines in southwest China, the songs and languages of ethnic minorities there, and the history of data and sound recording.
- How it works: Documentary footage of mining farms and field recordings, edited with archival material into a single-channel video.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Tate collection; Science Gallery Melbourne
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DgA-rP0CjW0

#### Geocinema — Geocinema (2018)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Computer vision
- Idea: The Earth is now filmed continuously by machines, and whoever owns the sensors writes its story.
- What it is: A research and film project that treats satellites, CCTV, phone cameras and street-view cars as one planetary camera, following sensing infrastructure along China's Belt and Road routes.
- How it works: Essay films combining infrared drone footage, satellite imagery and Street View captures.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Hidden labour & extraction

#### Deep Down Tidal — Tabita Rezaire (2017)

- How it works: Desktop-style collage of maps, archival images, animations and the artist's narration (about 18 minutes).

#### Facebook Algorithmic Factory — Vladan Joler (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Dataset & training data, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Users are unpaid workers in a factory whose machines are algorithms.
- What it is: A series of forensic maps from SHARE Lab that trace how Facebook collects users' activity as raw material and processes it, through algorithms, into advertising targets.
- How it works: Joler and Andrej Petrovski mapped patents, permissions and tracking from public documents into large diagrams, published in three parts.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Opacity & latent space

#### Metamorphism — Julian Charrière (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Computers return to rock: the 'immaterial' digital is a geological body borrowed from the earth.
- What it is: Motherboards, hard drives, CPUs and memory from laptops and phones melted in artificial lava into polychrome stones, shown in vitrines like specimens from a future natural history museum.
- How it works: E-waste components mixed with rock and fused in a furnace at lava temperatures, then cut and displayed.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Into the Hollow, Dittrich & Schlechtriem, Berlin 2016; The World Through AI, Jeu de Paume, Paris 2025
- Images: https://julian-charriere.net/media/pages/projects/metamorphism/f1cc18f486-1671025283/julian-charriere-metamorphism-xvii-into-the-hollow-dittrich-schlechtriem-2016-copyright-the-artist-vg-bild-kunst-bonn-germany-1600x.jpg https://julian-charriere.net/media/pages/projects/metamorphism/86b5e1f22d-1671025283/julian-charriere-metamorphism-xiv-installation-view-into-the-hollow-dittrich-schlechtriem-2016-copyright-the-artist-vg-bild-kuns-1600x.jpg
- Project page: https://julian-charriere.net/projects/metamorphism

#### Rare Earthenware — Unknown Fields Division (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: The glow of a screen begins as radioactive waste on the other side of the world.
- What it is: Three ceramic vases, each shaped in the proportions of rare-earth elements used in a smartphone, a laptop and a car battery, made from the toxic mud of a tailings lake in Baotou, Inner Mongolia.
- How it works: The studio traced the supply chain from a Chinese port back to Baotou's refineries, collected the waste mud and fired it into Ming-style vases; a film by Toby Smith documents the journey.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: V&A, London
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YMKJ7S7fKOk
- Project page: http://www.unknownfieldsdivision.com/

#### CO2GLE — Joana Moll (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Every search has a physical cost; the cloud burns fuel.
- What it is: A web page that shows, in real time, the kilograms of CO2 emitted by the global traffic to google.com since you opened it.
- How it works: An estimate from Google's traffic per second, average page weight and the energy intensity of data transfer, updated live.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Opacity & latent space
- Images: https://www.janavirgin.com/img/works/CO2GLE.jpg

#### Internet Machine — Timo Arnall (2014)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: The cloud is a building full of loud machines, diesel generators and guards.
- What it is: A multi-screen film shot inside one of the largest data centres in Europe, Telefónica's in Alcalá de Henares, showing the cooling, power and security machinery of 'the cloud'.
- How it works: Slow tracking shots and wide-format photography projected across three screens; shown at transmediale.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Opacity & latent space

#### Waste Tide — Chen Qiufan (2013)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: The afterlife of our devices is someone else's body and land.
- What it is: A novel set on 'Silicon Isle', a southern Chinese island where migrant 'waste people' recycle the world's e-waste; a young worker, Mimi, is infected by a virus and becomes a posthuman cyborg.
- How it works: Science-fiction novel drawing on the real e-waste town of Guiyu; English translation by Ken Liu (2019).
