### Military & Operational AI

Drones, targeting and machines built to see and act in war.

#### NAZA — Yuval Abraham, Rachel Szor (2026)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: When killing is organised as a data pipeline, the decisive figure is not the target but a threshold: how many civilian deaths a strike may cost.
- What it is: A feature documentary shot at night on Tel Aviv rooftops in which 24 anonymous Israeli soldiers and intelligence officers, their faces and voices digitally altered, explain the machinery of the bombing of Gaza: phone hacking and tracking, AI-assisted target lists such as Lavender, and 'NAZA', the number of civilian deaths a strike is allowed to cause.
- How it works: Night-time interviews with anonymised insiders (faces and voices digitally altered), building on Abraham's 2024 +972 Magazine / Local Call reporting on the Lavender and 'Where's Daddy?' systems; produced by The Guardian with JW Films, executive producer Jonathan Glazer.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: 83rd Venice International Film Festival 2026, Competition – Special Jury Prize
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=40KW6knYMo4
- Images: https://static.labiennale.org/files/styles/seo_thumbnail/public/cinema/2026/750x500/naza.jpg?itok=GuhaLMVA
- Project page: https://www.labiennale.org/en/news/new-film-has-been-added-program-83rd-venice-film-festival

#### AI War Cloud Database — Sarah Ciston (2025)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Dataset & training data, Platform & recommender algorithm, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: The AI in your pocket and the AI that picks targets share companies, models and data; the boundary between home and battlefield is thin.
- What it is: An interactive database and installation that catalogues the AI systems used to make decisions in warfare and shows where the same kinds of tools appear in smartphones and social platforms.
- How it works: A network graph of companies, products and military uses compiled from public sources, with a tangible installation version; Grand Prize of the S+T+ARTS Prize 2025.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: S+T+ARTS Prize 2025 Grand Prize; Ars Electronica 2025
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BM1K0Rbs4W0
- Images: https://ars.electronica.art/starts-prize/files/2025/05/aiwarcloud-6-c-sarahciston-1024x576.jpg
- Project page: https://aiwar.cloud

#### The Battle of Ilovaisk — Forensic Architecture (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Counter-forensics uses machine vision to see what states deny.
- What it is: An investigation into Russian military presence in eastern Ukraine in 2014, in which a machine-learning classifier trained to recognise T-72 tanks searched thousands of online videos for evidence.
- How it works: Classifier trained on synthetic 3D renderings of the tank model, applied to scraped YouTube footage; results verified by researchers.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OldnzVNE71E
- Project page: https://forensic-architecture.org/investigation/the-battle-of-ilovaisk

#### Everyday Maneuver — Yuan Goang-Ming (2018)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: The drones' straight, scanning view turns the empty city into a surveillance image of a war that has not happened.
- What it is: During the half hour of Taipei's annual Wan An air-raid drill, when sirens sound and traffic must clear the streets, five drones hover at once above five of the city's main roads and film a city without people.
- How it works: Single-channel video (5'57"): five drones filmed simultaneously from above the centre lines of five main roads between 1:30 and 2:00 pm during the Wan An Air Defense Drill, held every year since 1978.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Everyday War, Taiwan Pavilion, 60th Venice Biennale 2024 (Palazzo delle Prigioni); Wrightwood 659, Chicago 2026
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fbqtOlCzcug
- Images: https://www.art-it.asia/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/02_YUAN-Goang-Ming-Everyday-Maneuver-2018.-%C2%A9-YUAN-Goang-Ming.-Courtesy-of-the-artist..jpg
- Project page: https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/593425/yuan-goang-mingeveryday-war

#### Incoming — Richard Mosse (2017)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: A weapons camera sees people as heat signatures: bodies without faces, stripped of individuality.
- What it is: A three-screen film of refugees crossing the Mediterranean and living in camps, shot with a military-grade thermal camera that can detect a body from 30 km away and renders people as glowing heat.
- How it works: Filmed over two years with a long-range thermal camera classified as a weapon under export law; score by Ben Frost.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: The Curve, Barbican 2017; NGV Triennial 2017
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QOyFAqs_rM
- Project page: https://www.richardmosse.com/

#### Slaughterbots — Future of Life Institute / Stop Autonomous Weapons (2017)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: Autonomous weapons need no science-fiction leap, only existing parts combined; the film argues for a ban.
- What it is: A short fiction film in which palm-sized drones with face recognition and explosives, launched in swarms, assassinate students and politicians chosen from their social-media profiles.
- How it works: Directed by Stewart Sugg with a closing statement by AI researcher Stuart Russell; first screened at the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in Geneva.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9CO6M2HsoIA
- Project page: https://futureoflife.org/

#### A Study into 21st Century Drone Acoustics — Ruben Pater, Gonçalo F. Cardoso (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: For people living under drones, the machine is first a sound; listening to it is a form of knowledge and of fear.
- What it is: An audio-visual composition and record built from field recordings of 17 kinds of drones, from consumer quadcopters to military reapers, tracing the sound life and death of a flying drone and the fear its hum causes where drones strike.
- How it works: Field recordings of drone motors and propellers are edited into a composition with a visual score identifying each drone type.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2017, Award of Distinction (Hybrid Art); ZKM Global Control and Censorship 2015–16
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_69goMEmumk

- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/228089/

#### National Bird — Sonia Kennebeck (2016)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: Remote killing is labour done at screens, and it wounds the people who do it too.
- What it is: A documentary that follows three former members of the US drone programme, an image analyst and two others, who break their silence about their work and the civilian deaths it caused.
- How it works: Observational documentary with interviews, including a visit to survivors of a strike in Afghanistan; executive produced by Wim Wenders and Errol Morris.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Machine seeing
- Shown at: Berlinale 2016; Tribeca Film Festival 2016
- Video: https://vimeo.com/186277306

#### #NotABugSplat — #NotABugSplat collective (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: 'Bug splat' was operators' slang for a human killed by a strike; the portrait speaks back through the drone's own eye.
- What it is: A giant portrait of a child who lost family members in a drone strike, laid out in a field in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, large enough to be seen by drone cameras above.
- How it works: A vinyl print laid on the ground with local residents' help, inspired by the artist JR's Inside Out project, and documented by aerial photography.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance

#### Blue Sky Days — Tomas van Houtryve (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: Seeing your own daily life from the drone's angle makes remote war's gaze recognisable.
- What it is: Aerial photographs of weddings, funerals, schools and prayer gatherings in the United States, taken with a small camera drone, echoing the kinds of gatherings struck by US drones abroad.
- How it works: Photographed with a consumer quadcopter over US towns; the title refers to the Pakistani boy Zubair Rehman, who told the US Congress in 2013 that he now preferred grey skies, because drones do not fly then.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance

#### Drone Strikes: Investigating Covert Operations — Forensic Architecture (2013)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: Drone strikes leave holes smaller than satellite pixels; architecture can make the invisible strike evidential.
- What it is: Investigations into US drone strikes in Pakistan, Yemen, Gaza and Afghanistan for a UN special rapporteur, including a strike on a house in Miranshah reconstructed from a single survivor's video.
- How it works: Spatial analysis of video frames, satellite images and witness testimony, modelled in 3D to locate strikes and their victims.

#### Drone Survival Guide — Ruben Pater (2013)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: In a world of drones, people need a field guide to the machines that watch them.
- What it is: A poster in the style of a bird-spotting guide that shows the silhouettes of military and civilian drones, with tips on hiding from them, translated into languages including Pashto and Urdu.
- How it works: Printed on a reflective sheet meant to help hide from infrared cameras, and distributed free online and in print.

#### Drone Shadows — James Bridle (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: The scale of a remote weapon becomes real when its shadow crosses familiar ground.
- What it is: Full-size outlines of military drones such as the MQ-1 Predator, drawn in white line on streets and squares as if their shadows had fallen in the city.
- How it works: Chalk or road-marking paint outlines at 1:1 scale, drawn in Istanbul, London, Brighton, Washington D.C. and other cities.

#### Dronestagram — James Bridle (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: Remote war happens in places we never see; the aerial view shared in a feed makes it briefly visible.
- What it is: For every US drone strike reported in Pakistan, Yemen and Somalia, an Instagram and Twitter account posted a satellite image of the location.
- How it works: Strike reports from the Bureau of Investigative Journalism were matched to Google Maps satellite views and posted with a short caption.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance

#### Metadata+ — Josh Begley (2012)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: A remote war can be brought to the phone's lock screen, next to every other notification.
- What it is: An iPhone app that sends a push notification each time a US drone strike is reported; Apple rejected it several times before approving it in 2014.
- How it works: Uses the Bureau of Investigative Journalism's strike database; first submitted as 'Drones+' in 2012 and renamed Metadata+.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space

#### Unmanned — Molleindustria (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Remote war is office work, and its violence sits beside ordinary domestic life.
- What it is: A short browser game about one day in the life of a drone pilot: shaving, commuting, watching a target on a screen, playing video games with his son.
- How it works: Split-screen Flash game written by Paolo Pedercini with Jim Munroe.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qTsP0SpWdCk

#### Serious Games I–IV — Harun Farocki (2009)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Computer vision, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: The same simulated image prepares the soldier for war and treats the trauma it causes; in the game, war has no shadows.
- What it is: A four-part video installation on how the US military uses computer simulations to train soldiers for Iraq and Afghanistan and, afterwards, to treat their post-traumatic stress.
- How it works: Filmed at US Marine Corps training sites and at the Institute for Creative Technologies (USC), comparing training and therapy software; parts made 2009–10.

## Classification, Power & Justice

Bias, surveillance and prediction, and the counter-archives and other intelligences that resist them.

### Bias & the Coded Gaze

Who machines fail to see, or see wrongly, and why.

#### Ghost in the Machine — Valerie Veatch (2026)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Bias in AI is not a later bug: the statistics of correlation and classification were first built to rank human beings.
- What it is: A feature documentary in chapters, built on nearly 40 interviews (Abeba Birhane, Emily M. Bender, Arvind Narayanan, Dan McQuillan, Angela Saini and others), that traces machine learning back to the statistics of eugenics and treats 'artificial intelligence' as a marketing term; it opens with Microsoft's Tay chatbot absorbing the worst of the internet.
- How it works: Interviews with computer and social scientists and archival material, organised in chapters from Karl Pearson's eugenic statistics to large language models and superintelligence rhetoric.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: Sundance Film Festival 2026; PBS Independent Lens, September 2026
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dLQzVLtvdv8
- Images: https://www.pbs.org/independentlens/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/GHOSTINTHEMA_Thumbnail_1920x1080.jpg https://cinapse.co/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/6qnynar3wGhost_in_the_Machine-Still_1-1-scaled.jpg
- Project page: https://www.pbs.org/independentlens/documentaries/ghost-in-the-machine/

#### AI generates covertly racist decisions about people based on their dialect — Valentin Hofmann (2024)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Alignment can teach a model to hide prejudice without removing it: the machine's racism moves from what it says about race to how it judges the way people speak.
- What it is: A Nature study showing that language models judge writers of African American English as lazier, dirtier and less intelligent than writers of Standard American English, and are more likely to give them low-status jobs, convict them and sentence them to death, even while their overt statements about Black people are positive.
- How it works: Matched guise probing: the same content written in African American English and in Standard American English is given to models from GPT-2 to GPT-4, and the traits, jobs and verdicts they attach to each version are compared with decades of studies of human stereotypes.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07856-5 (Nature 633, 2024)
- Images: https://media.springernature.com/m685/springer-static/image/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-024-07856-5/MediaObjects/41586_2024_7856_Fig1_HTML.png
- Project page: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07856-5

#### CLASSES — Libby Heaney (2021)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Computer vision, Dataset & training data, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Machine-learning 'classes' and social class are entangled: models trained on the web see the estate through other people's eyes.
- What it is: A video essay set in a simulated model of the London council estate where the artist lives, where machine and human voices narrate how machine-learning classification distorts working-class life.
- How it works: Object detection, image captioning and language models are run over a 3D scan of the estate; the outputs are voiced and overlaid in a 14-minute single-channel video.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Failure, glitch & error
- Images: https://libbyheaney.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/1-1.jpg https://libbyheaney.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/2.jpg
- Project page: https://libbyheaney.co.uk/artworks/classes/

#### Not My A.I. — Coding Rights (2021)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Dataset & training data, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Public-sector AI in the Global South often automates old forms of control over poor, female and racialised bodies under the language of efficiency and welfare.
- What it is: A feminist research project that maps algorithmic decision-making systems deployed by governments in Latin America, such as a platform built with Microsoft in Salta, Argentina, to predict teenage pregnancy and Chile's child-welfare alert system, and names the patterns of 'oppressive AI' they share.
- How it works: Joana Varon and Paz Peña combine case studies, a map of biased and harmful AI projects in Latin America and a set of feminist analytic categories, published on notmy.ai under a Creative Commons licence.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Paper: https://notmy.ai/news/oppressive-a-i-feminist-categories-to-understand-its-political-effects/ (notmy.ai (Coding Rights), 2021)
- Images: https://notmy.ai/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/share.png
- Project page: https://notmy.ai/

#### Coded Bias — Shalini Kantayya (2020)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Algorithmic harm is a civil-rights issue that needs law, not only better models.
- What it is: A feature documentary that follows Joy Buolamwini from her discovery of face-recognition bias to testimony before the US Congress, alongside London police face-recognition trials and China's social scoring.
- How it works: Observational documentary with interviews of researchers including Cathy O'Neil, Meredith Broussard, Safiya Noble, Timnit Gebru and Silkie Carlo of Big Brother Watch.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing
- Shown at: Sundance Film Festival 2020
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7pMV9scmKwc
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5eb23eee707c5356dea97eaa/1590130745535-D27NXEHHTSDPDBTXVMMF/CODED_BIAS_Home_Resize_2.jpg
- Project page: https://www.codedbias.com/

#### Voicing Erasure — Joy Buolamwini (2020)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Speech recognition hears some voices better than others; mishearing is a way of erasing.
- What it is: A spoken-word piece in which women scholars of AI bias read their work aloud while speech-recognition systems transcribe them badly, and voice assistants answer questions about women's history with men.
- How it works: Made with the Algorithmic Justice League after a Stanford study found error rates for Black speakers nearly double those for white speakers in five commercial speech-to-text systems.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SdCPbyDJtK0
- Project page: https://www.ajl.org/voicing-erasure

#### AI, Ain't I A Woman? — Joy Buolamwini (2018)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: A machine's error can repeat an old insult; poetry can make an audit felt.
- What it is: A spoken-word video in which Buolamwini shows commercial AI systems mislabelling portraits of Sojourner Truth, Ida B. Wells, Michelle Obama, Oprah Winfrey and Serena Williams as male.
- How it works: Buolamwini ran historical and contemporary portraits of Black women through face-analysis services from major tech companies and set the returned labels to her reading of a poem named after Sojourner Truth's 1851 speech.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Failure, glitch & error, Machine seeing
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QxuyfWoVV98
- Project page: https://www.ajl.org/

#### The Human Detector — Iyo Bisseck (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision
- Idea: Bisseck turns the experience of face trackers failing to see dark skin into a game in which everyone has to work at being unseen.
- What it is: A game installation in which the player must press a button without being detected as a human by a camera; players crawl, hide under cloth or pose as objects to slip past the machine's eye.
- How it works: A camera linked to PoseNet, a real-time pose-estimation model, watches the space; a press counts only if no body part (face, shoulder, elbow) is detected. Made during a machine-learning workshop at ECAL.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://vimeo.com/347283293
- Images: https://share.hek.ch/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/iyo.jpg
- Project page: https://share.hek.ch/en/ai-can-you-see-me/

#### Us, Aggregated — Mimi Ọnụọha (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Platform & recommender algorithm, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Grouping people from above is a quiet exercise of power: the machine builds an 'us' that is really a 'them'.
- What it is: Photos from the artist's family archive, never before online, are shown next to the images Google's reverse image search judges 'similar' to them.
- How it works: The artist programmatically queried Google's reverse image search with each family photo and presented the results as a grid; later versions (3.0, 2019) are a looping video with a hovering cursor.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/692f1808f9a01f48c2fa30ac/21a78b11-40de-4823-8c9c-802c59fd4c25/00_UA3_installationshot-cropped_courtesyofQuad.jpg https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/692f1808f9a01f48c2fa30ac/38a2109b-ba77-40cf-be21-c17c2ddb4c90/02_UA3_videostill_courtesyofartist.jpg
- Project page: https://www.mimionuoha.com/

#### The Coded Gaze: Unmasking Algorithmic Bias — Joy Buolamwini (2016)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Being invisible to a machine is not neutral; it follows who was in the training data.
- What it is: A short video in which Buolamwini, working on an MIT project, finds that a face-tracking system only detects her face when she puts on a white mask.
- How it works: Screen recordings of an off-the-shelf face-detection library, compared on her own face, a lighter-skinned colleague's face and a white mask.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=162VzSzzoPs
- Project page: https://www.ajl.org/

#### [help me know the truth] — Mary Flanagan (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: A classifier does not need to be a machine: the system simply collects and sharpens the prejudices people already carry.
- What it is: Visitors take a selfie, which is then overlaid with noise and shown on stations around the gallery; other visitors repeatedly pick which of two blurry versions better fits a label such as 'angel' or 'criminal', and a stereotyped face emerges from their choices.
- How it works: Uses reverse correlation from cognitive neuroscience: random noise patterns on the portrait are averaged according to visitors' binary choices.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2018, Award of Distinction (Interactive Art+)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DiHGOqLwN9w
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/2527247/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/2527249/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/2527254/preview/
- Project page: http://maryflanagan.com/work/help-me-know-the-truth/

#### A Hipster Bar — Max Dovey (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Automated gatekeeping by appearance looks absurd when the category is 'hipster', and is no less absurd when it is anything else.
- What it is: A pop-up bar whose barrier opens only for people an image classifier rates at least 90% 'hipster'; those who pass get a free drink.
- How it works: A webcam at the door sends each face to a classifier trained on thousands of Instagram images of hipsters (with Imagga); a Raspberry Pi lifts a motorised barrier when the score is high enough. Developed with V2_.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing
- Images: https://www.maxdovey.com/assets/images/projects/hipsterbar/1.jpg https://www.maxdovey.com/assets/images/projects/hipsterbar/2.jpg
- Project page: https://www.maxdovey.com/hipsterbar/

#### Physiognomic Scrutinizer — Marnix de Nijs (2009)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Face matching quietly revives physiognomy: judging character by likeness.
- What it is: Visitors pass through a gate that scans their face and matches it with one of 150 infamous or controversial people; as they walk through, a robotic voice tells the story of their 'match'.
- How it works: Airport-style gate with camera and face-recognition software comparing visitors to a curated gallery; speech synthesis narrates the match.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://vimeo.com/21460350
- Images: http://www.marnixdenijs.nl/photos_640x/physiognomic-scrut_2018-09-04_1.png
- Project page: http://www.marnixdenijs.nl/physiognomic_scrutinizer.htm

### Surveillance & Prediction

Tracking, scoring and predictive systems that govern people.

#### AI Snake Oil: What Artificial Intelligence Can Do, What It Can't, and How to Tell the Difference — Arvind Narayanan (2024)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: The most harmful AI may be the kind that does not work: predicting human futures dresses old guesswork in machine authority.
- What it is: Two Princeton computer scientists separate AI that works from AI that cannot, above all predictive systems sold to forecast who will commit a crime, succeed in a job or fall ill, which often do little better than simple guesses yet shape people's lives.
- How it works: Computer-science analysis of cases in hiring, criminal justice, health and content moderation, written by Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor from their AI Snake Oil newsletter; a Chinese edition appeared from CITIC Press in 2025.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Failure, glitch & error
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1515/9780691249643 (Princeton University Press, 2024)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HUpOIeh50rw
- Project page: https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691249131/ai-snake-oil

#### Terra ex Machina — Hagit Keysar, Ariel Caine (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Computer vision
- Idea: A geofence is a wall written in code by a drone company; it becomes visible only as the place where the machine refuses to look.
- What it is: A video work that maps the invisible 'geofence' DJI programs around Jerusalem's Old City: a drone flown along the 10-km perimeter with its camera fixed on the Dome of the Rock yields a point cloud in which the no-fly zone appears as a black void, then filled with kite and balloon photographs made with residents inside the zone.
- How it works: More than 10,000 sequential drone images from seven launch points are processed into a photogrammetric point cloud; low-altitude DIY aerial images made with kites and balloons (with Public Lab and residents of Silwan and Sheikh Jarrah) are embedded as further point clouds.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: ARE YOU FOR REAL 2 (ifa), cluster 'Dead Futures', 2024; Prix Ars Electronica 2026, Honorary Mention (Digital Humanity)
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/3905171/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/3905172/preview/
- Project page: https://cargocollective.com/hagitkeysar/Terra-Ex-Machina-1

#### Consensus Gentium — Karen Palmer (2023)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: The story reacts to where you look, so the viewer experiences being profiled by the device in their own hand.
- What it is: An interactive film played on a smartphone: to get permission to visit a sick grandmother in a near-future surveillance state, the viewer passes tests while the phone's camera tracks their eye gaze and scores their compliance.
- How it works: Face detection and gaze tracking through the front-facing camera feed a branching narrative that classifies the viewer as dissident or compliant.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing
- Shown at: SXSW 2023; Prix Ars Electronica 2024, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art +)
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/3800250/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/3800253/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/290652/

#### All Light, Everywhere — Theo Anthony (2021)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: No camera is neutral: every lens has a position, and body cameras are designed from the officer's side.
- What it is: A documentary essay that moves from the history of photography and time-and-motion studies to Axon, the maker of police body cameras, and a surveillance plane flying over Baltimore.
- How it works: Observational scenes inside Axon's headquarters and the Baltimore Aerial Investigation Research programme, intercut with archival science films; won a Special Jury Award at Sundance.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Sundance Film Festival 2021 (Special Jury Award)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=luHmSqY0Xsk
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Light,_Everywhere

#### 3x3x6 — Shu Lea Cheang (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: Surveillance technology is turned back on its viewers to expose how bodies are classified as deviant.
- What it is: In a former prison in Venice, a panoptic installation tells the cases of people imprisoned for sexual or gender dissidence. Surveillance cameras scan visitors and mix their images into the projections, placing them inside the system.
- How it works: Multi-screen projection, surveillance cameras with visitor image capture and processing, website and research archive; curated by Paul B. Preciado for the Taiwan Pavilion.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing
- Shown at: Taiwan Pavilion, 58th Venice Biennale 2019 (Palazzo delle Prigioni); LG Guggenheim Award 2024

- Project page: https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/258006/shu-lea-cheang3x3x6

#### My Blue Window — American Artist (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Predictive policing gives the officer a machine's view of the city; the viewer sits in the seat that sees neighbourhoods as risk scores.
- What it is: An installation built like a police cruiser's interior, where visitors watch the film 2015 on the dashboard: a dashcam drive through New York while predictive-policing software flags 'high-risk' zones.
- How it works: Dashcam-style footage overlaid with interface graphics modelled on predictive policing tools such as HunchLab; shown with the phone app 1956/2054 at the Queens Museum.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing

#### Shadow Stalker — Lynn Hershman Leeson (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Surveillance & biometrics, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Everyone casts a data shadow that others can read and act on, often wrongly.
- What it is: Visitors type their email address and see their 'data shadow' projected: addresses, relatives and traces found online; a film on predictive policing plays with a 'Spirit of the Deep Web' played by Tessa Thompson.
- How it works: An installation using open-source intelligence searches on visitors' emails, projected on the floor, with a film on algorithms such as PredPol; commissioned by The Shed, New York.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Alterity & the uncanny

#### Spectre — Bill Posters, Daniel Howe (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Platform & recommender algorithm, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Deepfakes of the people who run the platforms make the data economy confess in their voices.
- What it is: An installation on the 'digital influence industry' that included deepfake videos of Mark Zuckerberg, Kim Kardashian and Donald Trump praising a fictional data cult; the Zuckerberg video tested Instagram's deepfake policy.
- How it works: Deepfakes made with the company CannyAI, an installation at Sheffield Doc/Fest, and an interactive 'altar' where visitors see how their data is sold.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Alterity & the uncanny

#### The Net Wanderer – A Tour of Suspended Handshakes — Guo Cheng (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: The border of a national internet is a set of ordinary buildings and delayed handshakes, hidden in plain sight.
- What it is: A research project and installation that traces the Great Firewall's gateway nodes to physical sites; visitors who try to open a blocked website trigger a browser game instead.
- How it works: Network diagnostic tools traced IP addresses of firewall-related nodes; the artist then visited and photographed the locations in several cities.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Opacity & latent space

#### Sociality — Paolo Cirio (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: The patent office is where the machinery of social manipulation is described in plain diagrams before it is built.
- What it is: Cirio collected and rated hundreds of US patents for technologies that monitor and manipulate social behaviour, and invited the public to share, flag and 'ban' them on a website and in printed installations.
- How it works: A database of patent filings with their flowcharts, classified by the artist and published online with public flagging tools, plus prints and a colouring book of the diagrams.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: S+T+ARTS Prize 2020, Honorary Mention

#### The City of Broken Windows — Hito Steyerl (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Machine listening for 'broken windows' carries the old policing theory into code; repair is the counter-gesture.
- What it is: A two-part installation: engineers smash windows in a hangar to record training data for an AI that detects breaking glass, while the activist Chris Toepfer paints boarded-up windows in Camden, New Jersey, to look lived-in.
- How it works: Two video channels, 'Unbroken Windows' and 'Broken Windows', filmed at a UK company training audio classifiers for security systems and with Chris Toepfer's window-painting project.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Castello di Rivoli 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iyyM4vDg0xw

#### White Collar Crime Risk Zones — Sam Lavigne (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Dataset & training data, Computer vision
- Idea: Predictive policing is a choice of targets; point it at Wall Street and its logic becomes visible.
- What it is: A predictive-policing map and app that forecasts financial crime instead of street crime; it also shows the 'likely suspect', a face averaged from thousands of LinkedIn photos of executives.
- How it works: Made with Brian Clifton and Francis Tseng for The New Inquiry: a model trained on 1964–2016 FINRA financial-misconduct data predicts risk by location, and a face-averaging algorithm builds the suspect.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space

- Project page: https://whitecollar.thenewinquiry.com/

#### Cloud Index — James Bridle (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Predictive models blur forecasting and control: to predict the vote is to imagine steering it.
- What it is: A neural network trained on satellite weather images and UK polling data generates the skies that would have produced any given result in the Brexit referendum, offering weather as a lever on politics.
- How it works: Correlation of historical cloud imagery with polling data; a DCGAN renders the sky images.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Images: https://jamesbridle.com/media/pages/works/cloud-index/890e90e757-1680515138/165_opengraph.jpg

#### The Argus Project — Romi Ron Morrison, Gan Golan (2016)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Counter-surveillance can be imagined as a collective body armed with eyes.
- What it is: A wearable exo-suit covered with cameras, after the hundred-eyed giant Argus, worn on night walks through the city as a 'force field of accountability' for filming the police.
- How it works: Sculptural suit with embedded cameras and lights; performances documented in public space. Collaborators include Raquel De Anda, Ligaiya Romero, Ayodamola Okunseinde and others.

#### The Glass Room — Tactical Tech (2016)

- Idea: Borrowing the look of the tech store lets a critique of data extraction reach people who would never enter a gallery.

#### The Virtual Watchers — Joana Moll (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Border surveillance was crowdsourced to unpaid citizens; the watchers became part of the machine.
- What it is: An installation built on the archive of the Texas Virtual Border Watch (from 2008), in which volunteers watched live border-camera feeds online from home and reported suspected crossings.
- How it works: Made with Cédric Parizot; it restages the programme's watching interface together with archived comments from the volunteers.

#### Citizen Ex — James Bridle (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Online, a machine decides which country you belong to, and with it which laws and surveillance apply.
- What it is: A browser extension that records which countries the websites you visit are hosted in and computes your 'algorithmic citizenship', the nationality data systems infer from your traffic.
- How it works: The extension geolocates the IP address of every page and resource loaded and shows a running pie chart of countries; commissioned by The Space and Abandon Normal Devices.

#### Secret Power — Simon Denny (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Mass surveillance has an aesthetic, and its clip-art and wizards say something about how the agencies see the world.

#### Stealth Cell Tower — Julian Oliver (2015)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: The same trick police use to intercept phones (the 'IMSI catcher') fits in an office printer.
- What it is: A mobile-phone base station disguised as an office printer, which lets nearby phones connect to it and then sends them text messages that appear to come from people in their contacts.
- How it works: A GSM base station built from a software-defined radio and a Raspberry Pi hidden in an HP printer, which also prints the texts it sends.

#### Citizenfour — Laura Poitras (2014)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Mass surveillance is an invisible machine of cables, databases and search tools; the film shows what it takes, and costs, to make it visible.
- What it is: A documentary filmed largely in a Hong Kong hotel room in June 2013, as Edward Snowden hands journalists the documents that revealed the NSA's mass-surveillance programmes.
- How it works: Observational footage shot by Poitras during the meetings with Snowden, Glenn Greenwald and Ewen MacAskill, combined with encrypted messages and later reporting on programmes such as PRISM and XKeyscore.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Classification, bias & surveillance

#### Jennifer Lyn Morone™ Inc — Jennifer Lyn Morone (2014)

- Idea: If data is value, a person can claim to be a company; the absurdity mirrors what platforms already do.

#### Asymmetric Love — Addie Wagenknecht (2013)

- Idea: Surveillance has become domestic décor: we hang it in our homes and admire it.

#### Surveillance Chess — !Mediengruppe Bitnik (2012)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Every surveillance camera has a human at the other end who can be addressed.

#### Transparency Grenade — Julian Oliver (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Transparency can be forced from below; the network in any room can be made to speak.
- What it is: A cast-resin Soviet F1 hand grenade with a tiny computer, microphone and antenna inside: 'pulling the pin' captures network traffic and audio in the room and leaks them to a public online map.
- How it works: A Linux single-board computer with a Wi-Fi antenna and microphone sniffs unencrypted traffic, extracts emails, hostnames and images, and streams them to a server that maps the leak.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Classification, bias & surveillance

#### Face to Facebook — Paolo Cirio, Alessandro Ludovico (2011)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Once faces are data, they can be re-sorted into any identity someone chooses.
- What it is: The artists scraped one million Facebook profiles, used face-analysis software to sort 250,000 profile pictures into temperaments such as 'smug' or 'easy going', and published them on a fake dating site, Lovely-Faces.com.
- How it works: Custom scraper plus face-detection and expression-analysis software; profiles re-published on a purpose-built dating website.

#### Memopol-2 — Timo Toots (2011)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Dataset & training data
- Idea: In a digital state the ID card is the key to a profile you rarely see; the machine turns the background check on yourself.
- What it is: A large machine into which visitors insert their national ID card or passport; it gathers what state databases and the internet hold about them and shows their data field on a big custom display, remembering each visitor's name and portrait.
- How it works: Reads the chip of Estonian ID cards and queries national registries and web sources; results are visualised on an array of LED panels.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2012, Golden Nica (Interactive Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xCr7UdVkmCk
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/1439540/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/1439541/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/1439585/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/193063/

#### Men in Grey — Julian Oliver, Danja Vasiliev (2009)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Only when people witness their own traffic being read do they sense the machines listening in the network.
- What it is: Two figures in grey suits with briefcases appear in public places; the briefcases intercept and manipulate the wireless traffic of people nearby and display what they find, staging a secret society that makes network surveillance tangible.
- How it works: Briefcases contain Linux computers, antennas and screens that run wireless exploits and content manipulation in real time.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2010, Award of Distinction (Hybrid Art); Aksioma, Ljubljana 2011
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/464136/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/464138/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/464140/preview/
- Project page: https://criticalengineering.org/projects/men-in-grey/

#### Faceless — Manu Luksch (2007)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: The law's redaction of faces became the film's world: a city where only the requester has a face.
- What it is: A science-fiction film made entirely from CCTV footage of the artist in London, obtained under the UK Data Protection Act; other people's faces arrive blanked out by law, so the city appears faceless.
- How it works: Luksch followed a 'Manifesto for CCTV Filmmakers', performing in front of public cameras and then filing subject-access requests for the recordings; narrated by Tilda Swinton.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yLzJCeGYgbg
- Project page: https://manuluksch.com/

#### Demonstrate — Ken Goldberg (2004)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: Giving the public the controls of a surveillance camera tests free speech against privacy.
- What it is: For the 40th anniversary of the Free Speech Movement, a high-resolution robotic webcam overlooked Sproul Plaza at UC Berkeley; anyone online could steer it, take pictures of people and comment on them.
- How it works: Networked pan-tilt-zoom camera with a web interface; user-captured frames and comments archived.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hd6vNv1m6NE
- Project page: https://goldberg.berkeley.edu/

#### Evidence Locker — Jill Magid (2004)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: A surveillance system can be seduced into care; the intimacy exposes who holds the camera.
- What it is: For 31 days in Liverpool the artist worked with Citywatch, the city's police CCTV system, directing operators by phone to follow her and writing them love letters in the form of footage-request forms.
- How it works: Magid wore a red coat so operators could find her, requested the footage under the Data Protection Act (it was otherwise deleted after 31 days), and edited it into videos and a 'Reading Room' installation.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: FACT Liverpool 2004; Tate Liverpool 2004
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=laStNBHSfuU
- Project page: https://www.jillmagid.com/projects/evidence-locker-2

#### Life: A User's Manual — Michelle Teran (2003)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: The city is already full of images of us that we never see.
- What it is: Teran walks through cities pulling a suitcase with a video scanner and screen, picking up the unencrypted wireless signals of private surveillance cameras and showing passers-by the hidden images around them.
- How it works: Handheld receiver scanning the frequency band (likely 2.4 GHz) used by consumer wireless cameras; images displayed in a mobile monitor.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MS-T6Yooa9E
- Project page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MS-T6Yooa9E

#### System Azure Security Ornamentation — Jill Magid (2002)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Ornamenting a camera makes an invisible gaze visible and oddly personal.
- What it is: Magid offered the Amsterdam police her services to decorate the city's surveillance cameras with rhinestones and ornaments, making them visible and, in her words, more beautiful.
- How it works: Proposal letters and meetings with the police, followed by decorating CCTV cameras in public space.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Images: http://www.jillmagid.com/uploads/images/scaled/slide_image/302 http://www.jillmagid.com/uploads/images/scaled/slide_image/305
- Project page: http://www.jillmagid.com/projects/system-azure-security-ornamentation

#### Tracking Transience — Hasan Elahi (2002)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Flooding the watchers with data makes a person both fully visible and hard to read.
- What it is: After the FBI questioned him for months over a false tip, Elahi began publishing his location and tens of thousands of photos of his meals, toilets and flights online, for the agency and anyone else.
- How it works: A GPS tracker and a website updated continuously with timestamped photographs since 2002; the archive now holds tens of thousands of images.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wAdwurHhv-I
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasan_Elahi

#### I Thought I Was Seeing Convicts — Harun Farocki (2000)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: When the field of vision and the gun sight coincide, watching becomes the first step of shooting; surveillance images exist to sort the norm from deviations.
- What it is: A double-projection installation built from the surveillance cameras of Corcoran State Prison in California, where the camera that watches the exercise yard is mounted next to the guard's gun.
- How it works: Two screens set silent prison surveillance footage, including a shooting in the Corcoran yard, against images of control technologies such as electronic tags and identification systems.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: International Film Festival Locarno, 2000 (first screening); Generali Foundation, Vienna (co-production)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7vyGc26JCcU
- Project page: https://www.harunfarocki.de/installations/2000s/2000/i-thought-i-was-seeing-convicts.html

#### BIT Plane — Bureau of Inverse Technology (BIT) (1999)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: An early drone that watched the watchers.
- What it is: A small radio-controlled plane carrying a video camera flew over Silicon Valley's no-camera zones, filming the tech companies that build the information age from above.
- How it works: Custom radio-controlled model aircraft with onboard video camera and transmitter, piloted over corporate campuses.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Images: https://bureauit.org/images/plane/plane0self.jpg https://bureauit.org/images/plane/plane031lockh.jpg
- Project page: https://bureauit.org/plane/

#### Performances for Surveillance Cameras — Surveillance Camera Players (1996)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: If the camera is always watching, perform for it: the operator becomes an audience, and the watched become actors.
- What it is: A New York troupe stages silent adaptations of Orwell's 1984 and other plays in front of public CCTV cameras, holding up placards for the operators, and leads walking tours mapping cameras.
- How it works: Short silent plays with large text boards performed at camera locations, documented from the street; the group also published maps of cameras in Manhattan.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9BtntSJc0a4
- Project page: http://www.notbored.org/the-scp.html

### Missing Data & Counter-Datasets

Datasets made to fill gaps, refuse extraction or retell who is counted.

#### Endangered Gestures — Bruce Eesly (2026)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Asking the intelligence complicit in erasure to give banned words a body yields a fragile, glitching language of resistance.
- What it is: A short film and pocket book of hand gestures that an image generator proposed for words that began disappearing from US government websites and documents in March 2025, such as 'accessibility'; the AI hands, with their unreliable fingers, hover between sign language and technical error.
- How it works: Each censored term was prompted into a generative image model as a hand gesture; the results were edited into a 4K single-channel video (6 min 10 s) with voice-over and a 64-page book.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2026, Honorary Mention (New Animation Art)
- Images: https://eesly.xyz/content/2-endangered-gestures/2-Detail/Endangered-Gestures-1.jpg https://eesly.xyz/content/2-endangered-gestures/1-Intro/Endangered-Gestures-1.jpg
- Project page: https://eesly.xyz/endangered-gestures

#### Data Trust — Stephanie Dinkins (2025)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Dataset & training data, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Data can be given rather than taken: a trust built on consent, community ownership and storage in living matter rather than a company's cloud.
- What it is: A participatory installation in which visitors gift spoken stories, in the gallery or through an app, to a community archive; the stories animate wall-sized AI projections and are encoded into bacterial DNA in the soil of okra and California black oak plants growing in the room.
- How it works: Oral histories are recorded, processed with AI into continuously evolving projections and stored as DNA in bacteria grown in the plants' soil; further stories arrive through thestorieswetellourmachines.app.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: ICA San José, 19 Sep 2025 – 22 Mar 2026
- Images: https://48hills.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/ICA-DATA-TRUST-09192025_123-1024x576.jpeg https://www.icasanjose.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/Website-banner-scaled.jpg
- Project page: https://www.icasanjose.org/archive/data_trust/

#### Ground Truths — Mimi Ọnụọha (2025)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Dataset & training data, Computer vision
- Idea: A model trained on records shaped by erasure inherits the erasure; 'ground truth' is literally buried.
- What it is: A docufiction film in which the artist builds a machine-learning model to predict where other unmarked graves of convict-leasing victims lie across Texas, after 95 bodies were found in Sugar Land in 2018.
- How it works: Single-channel 4K video (about 16 minutes) combining the model-building process with archives, phone calls and missing records.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Grief, memory & afterlife, Opacity & latent space
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/692f1808f9a01f48c2fa30ac/51f2cb4b-30a1-49b4-9ece-1cde6d8effa4/00_GroundTruths_film-still_courtestyoftheartist.jpg https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/692f1808f9a01f48c2fa30ac/8c09a145-022b-4e17-bab1-682266e49fb3/01_GroundTruths_film-still_courtestyoftheartist.jpg
- Project page: https://www.mimionuoha.com/

#### The Call — Holly Herndon, Mat Dryhurst (2024)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: If all media is training data, the making of training data can itself be the artwork, and consent and ownership can be designed into it from the start.
- What it is: An interactive spatial-audio installation at Serpentine North built on choral AI models trained on fifteen UK community choirs, who sang a songbook of hymns and exercises the artists wrote as training data; the choristers are members of a data trust that shares control over how the models are used.
- How it works: A composed songbook and recording protocol were used to record choirs across the UK; the recordings trained choral voice models that drive a multichannel installation in the chapel-like gallery, with gathering objects co-designed by the architecture studio sub; contributors share control through a data-trust agreement.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Hidden labour & extraction
- Shown at: Serpentine North, London, 4 Oct 2024 – 2 Feb 2025; Prix Ars Electronica 2025, Honorary Mention (Digital Musics & Sound Art); S+T+ARTS Prize 2026, Honorary Mention
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DNlr7olF6rE
- Images: https://d37zoqglehb9o7.cloudfront.net/uploads/2024/08/SerpentineGallery_HHMD03119_B2-2-1200x627.jpg
- Project page: https://www.serpentinegalleries.org/whats-on/holly-herndon-mat-dryhurst-the-call/

#### Babylonian Vision — Nora Al-Badri (2020)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Scraping museum data can be a form of restitution: the images return to a common use their owners did not plan.
- What it is: A neural network trained on images of Mesopotamian, Neo-Sumerian and Babylonian artefacts from museum collections produces synthetic artefacts, shown as a video.
- How it works: A GAN trained on thousands of images scraped from museum websites, some without permission; first commissioned for the EPFL Pavilions.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTZ5W8Vbpd4
- Images: https://epfl-pavilions.ch/media/pages/exhibitions/babylonian-vision/647951dfaf-1709114720/cover-2880x1600.png
- Project page: https://epfl-pavilions.ch/en/exhibitions/babylonian-vision

#### Igùn — Minne Atairu (2020)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A model trained on looted objects can only recombine what was taken; its gaps mirror the gaps of the colonial archive.
- What it is: A series of generative 'bronzes' imagining the works Benin casters on Igùn Street might have made in the years after the British looted the royal palace in 1897.
- How it works: StyleGAN2 trained on images of Benin bronze, iron and terracotta objects held mostly in Western museums.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pg8U2l4tQAE
- Project page: https://igun.info/prototype-I

#### The Zizi Show — Jake Elwes (2020)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Training AI on drag bodies queers the norms of the datasets it usually learns from.
- What it is: A virtual deepfake drag cabaret: thirteen London drag performers were filmed to train networks, and online visitors can make their generated bodies perform songs, including the composite queen Zizi.
- How it works: Pose-conditioned video generation trained on footage of each performer; web interface lets users pick acts and songs.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Images: https://www.jakeelwes.com/images/project-zizi-show.jpg
- Project page: https://www.jakeelwes.com/project-zizi-show.html

#### Adversarial Fashion — Kate Bertash (2019)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Surveillance systems take whatever they are handed, and polluting a dataset costs far less than cleaning it.
- What it is: A clothing line printed with dozens of fake licence plates: automated licence-plate readers on police cars and street poles read the garments as cars and log them, with time and place, in the same databases as real vehicles.
- How it works: Plate-like patterns were designed and tested against OpenALPR and mobile ALPR products, on still images and live video, until readers logged them as plates.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: DEF CON 27, Crypto & Privacy Village, Las Vegas, 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jVcGZ_Ak4NI
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58e30938bf629a13c2cfb8e2/e48f9342-0c02-492b-b3c3-d59125237fda/5d591101ce745.jpg
- Project page: https://adversarialfashion.com/

#### Te Reo Māori Speech Recognition and the Kaitiakitanga Licence — Te Hiku Media (2018)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Data sovereignty means the community that speaks the language decides who may train on its voice.
- What it is: A Māori-led media organisation built its own speech recognition for te reo Māori from recordings donated by its community, and refused to hand the data to big tech.
- How it works: In the 2018 Kōrero Māori campaign people read sentences aloud and recorded over 300 hours in 10 days; the models are released under the Kaitiakitanga Licence, which grants access only for the benefit of Māori.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sGQy0r_icWc
- Images: https://opengraph.githubassets.com/1a9ccbb40a42481347763da1c45a53663a09c5a3a855a4a0509aa57bb7b783ad/TeHikuMedia/Kaitiakitanga-License
- Project page: https://tehiku.nz/te-hiku-tech/
- Code: https://github.com/TeHikuMedia/Kaitiakitanga-License

#### Feminist Data Set — Caroline Sinders (2017)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Dataset & training data, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Bias is not fixed at the end of a pipeline; each step, from data to wages, is a political choice.
- What it is: A multi-year project that builds a feminist AI chatbot by questioning every step: collecting feminist texts in public workshops, labelling them, choosing a model and paying the labour fairly.
- How it works: Community workshops (SPACE Art + Technology, Victoria and Albert Museum and others) gather and annotate texts; Sinders documents a critical-design framework for the whole ML pipeline.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WwdmPva8nhc
- Images: https://carolinesinders.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/LEO_6267-1024x678.jpg https://carolinesinders.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/VA_Image2_large-1024x683.jpg
- Project page: https://carolinesinders.com/feminist-data-set/

#### This Much I'm Worth (the self-evaluating artwork) — Rachel Ara (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Let an algorithm price the artwork in public, and the arbitrariness of value becomes visible.
- What it is: A large neon sculpture that continuously calculates and displays its own market value, changing as it is looked at, talked about and shared online.
- How it works: A networked computer inside the sculpture gathers data (likely visitor counts, social-media mentions and art-market indicators), runs a valuation algorithm and drives the neon digits.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: Uncanny Values, MAK Vienna 2019; Aesthetica Art Prize
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wZ-P6dnkVcY
- Project page: https://www.mak.at/en/program/exhibitions/uncanny_values

#### The Library of Missing Datasets — Mimi Ọnụọha (2016)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Dataset & training data
- Idea: What a society does not count shows its values as clearly as what it counts; a 'missing' dataset is both a lack and an ought.
- What it is: A white filing cabinet full of empty folders, each labelled with a dataset that does not exist, such as people excluded from public housing because of criminal records or trans people killed or injured in hate crimes.
- How it works: A physical archive drawn from a list of missing datasets the artist has kept on GitHub since 2015; v2.0 (2018) focuses on Blackness and v3.0 is a locked cabinet of datasets too dangerous to collect.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/692f1808f9a01f48c2fa30ac/94ae8920-0367-440f-b24e-5794636edf6f/00small_LibraryofMissingDatasets_propertyofartist_creditBrandonSchulman.jpg https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/692f1808f9a01f48c2fa30ac/5f58c44d-4c0b-4d25-9148-02c8fc120a4e/04_LibraryofMissingDatasets2_propertyofartist.jpg
- Project page: https://github.com/MimiOnuoha/missing-datasets

### Feminist, Decolonial & Indigenous AI

AI imagined from other cultures, genders and knowledge systems.

#### Nosukaay — Diane Cescutti (2022)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Weaving was computation long before the computer; the machine here speaks from West African textile knowledge, not from Silicon Valley.
- What it is: A 'machine deity' built from a Manjak loom whose two frames are replaced by bare screens; visitors stroke a handwoven loincloth to navigate a film-game about an alternative history of computation, and are ejected if they disrespect it.
- How it works: A conductive handwoven Manjak cloth acts as a touch keyboard for an interactive narrative of texts, 3D images and footage shot in Dakar weaving studios.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2024, Golden Nica (Interactive Art +)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=939QlKGURoI
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/3797338/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/3797341/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/290626/

#### Intersectional AI Toolkit — Sarah Ciston (2021)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Dataset & training data
- Idea: AI literacy is a power question: tools become fairer when the people they affect can read and remake them.
- What it is: A set of zines and a wiki that explain AI in plain language to artists, activists and queer and marginalised communities, and ask how intersectional feminism could change it.
- How it works: Zines, workshops and an open-source wiki made collaboratively with contributors; developed during Ciston's doctoral research at the University of Southern California.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Images: https://intersectionalai.com/assets/img/zineHowTo.png
- Project page: https://intersectionalai.com/

#### Afro-now-ism — Stephanie Dinkins (2020)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Instead of Afrofuturist hope, act now: take part in making the data and code that will shape your life.
- What it is: An essay in which Dinkins asks Black communities to stop waiting for future liberation and to build, now, the technologies and AI systems they need.
- How it works: A text published in Noema Magazine, drawing on her work with Not the Only One and community AI workshops.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Paper: https://www.noemamag.com/afro-now-ism/ (Noema Magazine)
- Images: https://www.noemamag.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Not-the-Only-One-3d-Avatar-SKETCH252-BECOMING.jpg
- Project page: https://www.noemamag.com/afro-now-ism/

#### Indigenous Protocol and Artificial Intelligence Position Paper — Jason Edward Lewis (2020)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Dataset & training data
- Idea: AI can be designed as a relative with obligations, not only as a tool; protocols come before products.
- What it is: A position paper from workshops in Honolulu where Indigenous technologists, artists and elders from Aotearoa, Australia, North America and the Pacific set out how AI could be designed from their protocols.
- How it works: Edited by Jason Edward Lewis with contributions by Angie Abdilla, Noelani Arista, Suzanne Kite and others; published by the Indigenous Protocol and AI Working Group and CIFAR, with guidelines, essays and design prototypes.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.11573/spectrum.library.concordia.ca.00986506 (Indigenous Protocol and AI Working Group / CIFAR, Honolulu)
- Images: https://www.indigenous-ai.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/waiwai2.jpg
- Project page: https://www.indigenous-ai.net/position-paper/

#### Masakhane: Participatory Research for African Machine Translation — Masakhane (2020)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Who builds a language model decides which languages exist for machines; participatory research is a way to be counted.
- What it is: A grassroots network of hundreds of volunteers across Africa that built machine-translation data and models for dozens of African languages, without academic gatekeeping.
- How it works: Volunteers contributed data, models and evaluations for their own languages; the process and results are reported in a Findings of EMNLP 2020 paper.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.02353 (Findings of EMNLP 2020)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mbkuRZkg1RY
- Project page: https://www.masakhane.io/

#### Wampum.codes — Amelia Winger-Bearskin (2020)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Software is an agreement between people; Indigenous record-keeping technologies can shape how we write it.
- What it is: A framework and podcast that proposes Indigenous values, modelled on wampum belts that record agreements between nations, as a code of ethics for software and AI development.
- How it works: Talks, a podcast series and a code-of-ethics document shown at the imagineNATIVE festival, developed during the artist's residencies and teaching.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: imagineNATIVE Festival 2020
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8I4FjCtAW8Y
- Project page: https://wampum.codes/

#### Being — Rashaad Newsome (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: An AI can be written as a Black, queer, decolonial teacher instead of a servile assistant.
- What it is: An AI 'digital griot', an animated figure with a vogue dancer's body and an African mask for a face, that teaches, gives tours and leads workshops drawing on bell hooks, Paulo Freire and ballroom culture.
- How it works: Motion-captured voguing, a chatbot trained on selected texts and a synthetic voice; iterations have appeared as a guide, a teacher and a therapist.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CzupjhLM6RQ
- Project page: https://rashaadnewsome.com/

#### Oracle for Transfeminist Technologies — Coding Rights (2019)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Dataset & training data, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Designing with other values produces other machines; imagination is a first step against default tech.
- What it is: A deck of cards and a workshop game in which players draw values, objects, situations and 'transfeminist' prompts and imagine technologies built on them.
- How it works: Created by Joana Varon of Coding Rights with collaborators; played in workshops across Latin America and online.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Images: https://static.wixstatic.com/media/cfe831_05a51b539e8749c384a4b4021517120a~mv2.png
- Project page: https://transfeministech.codingrights.org/

#### Íŋyaŋ Iyé (Telling Rock) — Suzanne Kite (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: In Lakota ontology stones and metals can speak; building an AI from that starting point makes the machine a relative to be listened to with respect, not a tool.
- What it is: A sculpture of handmade circuits and long hair braids that speaks a poem in English and Lakȟótiyapi; listeners answer by bending and moving its braids, and the rock listens to the changes in its own voice and replies in light and sound.
- How it works: Sensors in the hair-braid interface feed a machine-learning system that decides how sound and light change; materials include gold, silver, copper, aluminium, silicon and fibreglass; made with Devin Ronneberg, Lakota translation by Alex Firethunder.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LP9HZ7lMR2s
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/641c9e79560ce0068fb84a8c/3cb5e0a2-a1c6-4f52-ba58-8c616d4074f8/20190711_cc_0895.jpg
- Project page: https://www.kitekitekitekite.com/portfolio/inyan-iye-telling-rock-2019

#### Degenerative Cultures — Cesar & Lois (Cesar Baio, Lucy HG Solomon) (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Pair an algorithm with a living organism and machine intelligence starts to borrow the logic of decay rather than of mastery.
- What it is: Fungal cultures grow on printed books about humanity's drive to control nature and slowly erase their text; a camera-fed AI reads the growth and, as a 'bhiobrid' agent, searches the internet for similar texts and corrupts them, posting its readouts as the Twitter account @HelloFungus.
- How it works: Computer vision tracks Physarum-like microbial growth on book pages; the data drive a cellular-automata and NLP algorithm that finds and rewrites online texts and prints them on site on a thermal printer.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Lumen Prize 2018, BCS Artificial Intelligence Award; Brighton Digital Festival 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HQwGFEqO1D0
- Images: http://static1.squarespace.com/static/65e7176a61627736e02f6c4a/6606a61178dd51369b416024/6606c08ef1cf21462183357b/1711718676868/AI-Award-Degenerative-Cultures6-1000x0-c-default.jpeg http://cesarandlois.org/wp-content/uploads/Cesar-Lois-degerative-cultures-1.jpg
- Project page: https://cesarandlois.org/digitalfungus/

## Co-performance & Hybrid Bodies

Human and machine bodies fused or performing together: prostheses, telepresence, dance, theatre, music and drawing.

### Cyborgs & Prostheses

Bodies extended, entered or remote-controlled by machines.

#### Super Mom Training Gym — Jiabao Li (2026)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: The digital body grants the pregnant body every power it lacks, and in doing so exposes the expectation that mothers should already be superhuman machines.
- What it is: A game and installation in which Li's 3D-scanned, nine-months-pregnant body becomes a superhero avatar that jumps twenty metres, lifts hospitals, kicks insurance forms and clones itself to multitask; gold figures of the pregnant superhero hang in the room around the screen.
- How it works: A 3D scan of the artist's pregnant body is rigged in a character animator and given superhero move sets in a playable game; gold figures of the avatar's poses (likely 3D-printed) are suspended in the space; made with Lauren Schroeder.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hcHN7Y9Oxsw
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58688c8a6a496327e937e35b/1778735906116-V3JR7FYERR3Q5Q7NAXAC/jiabao+li+fusebox+mom+10.jpg https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58688c8a6a496327e937e35b/1778734963219-0A590PH2QJ995IB36NMN/jiabao+li+mom+24.jpg
- Project page: https://www.jiabaoli.org/super-mom-training-gym

#### CHIMERIA — Shin Hanagata (2025)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Computer vision
- Idea: A headset and a camera are enough to undo the human body plan: VR here is not immersion but a way of becoming another kind of creature.
- What it is: Volunteers recruited through a public phone number wore head-mounted displays that moved their eyes to their toes, hips or hands, then lived together in a Tokyo residence where chairs, doorknobs and stairs made for upright humans no longer worked; they ate through tubes, used wire-driven prostheses and built a toilet for a kneeling body.
- How it works: Head-mounted displays fed by cameras worn on other parts of the body, custom suits and wire-driven prostheses, and a habitat rebuilt for the 'chimera' bodies; visitors had to imitate the chimeras to enter.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2026, Award of Distinction (Interactive Art+)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B7U_7kTxUWA
- Images: https://ars.electronica.art/prix/files/2026/06/chimeria-1.jpg https://www.shinhanagata.com/og-image.jpg
- Project page: https://www.shinhanagata.com/en/works/chimeria

#### DOKU the Self — Lu Yang (2022)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: An avatar driven by one's own motion data becomes a machine form of reincarnation.
- What it is: DOKU, a genderless digital avatar animated from the artist's own face and movements, travels through six Buddhist realms of rebirth.
- How it works: Full-body and facial motion capture of the artist and dancers, rendered in real-time game-engine animation.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: Times Square Midnight Moment, New York 2023
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cq24sSnccXc
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu_Yang_(artist)

#### JIZAI ARMS — Masahiko Inami (2022)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Extra limbs that can be passed between people turn the body into a social, rearrangeable thing rather than a fixed unit.
- What it is: A base unit worn on the back with sockets for up to six detachable robot arms, which can be swapped between wearers, so that several people can share arms or one person's extra limbs can be moved by someone else.
- How it works: Back-mounted base with sockets for up to six servo-driven arms, likely teleoperated through a miniature master arm; co-designed with designers in the JST ERATO Inami JIZAI Body Project (first author Nahoko Yamamura) and presented at CHI 2023.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: CHI 2023, Hamburg
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3544548.3581169 (CHI 2023)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KFyZQfqaXhE
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1145/3544548.3581169

#### Prosthetic Memory — M Eifler (2020)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Computer vision
- Idea: When a small, personal model holds your memories, remembering becomes an act of machine recognition, and others can watch it.
