- What it is: An ongoing self-augmentation system made to replace the artist's long-term memory, damaged by a childhood brain injury: when a page of their handwritten journal lies on the desk, a camera recognises it and projects the video memory recorded that day beside it.
- How it works: A camera over the journal feeds a custom-trained image classifier that identifies the page and triggers the matching daily video projection; later versions add a deepfake of the artist reading the pages.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: S+T+ARTS Prize 2020, Honorary Mention
- Images: https://ars.electronica.art/starts-prize/files/2020/06/prostheticmemory-1024x512.jpg
- Project page: https://ars.electronica.art/starts-prize/en/prosthetic-memory/

#### Amygdala — Marco Donnarumma (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: An AI prosthesis without a human wearer learns its own gestures: a limb searching for a body and a ritual.
- What it is: A robotic arm with a knife, built like a human limb and driven by an AI that learns by trial and error, repeatedly cuts a skin-like material in a purification ritual.
- How it works: Humanlike robotic arm with sensors and an adaptive neural network that develops cutting movements through reinforcement learning.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h4ykqTG1ZjY
- Images: https://marcodonnarumma.com/live/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/Marco-Donnarumma_Amygdala-MK3_13_ed_web.jpg
- Project page: https://marcodonnarumma.com/works/amygdala/

#### Electromagnetic Brainology — Lu Yang (2017)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Religious states and emotions are staged as circuits that can be switched on from outside.
- What it is: Four deity-like performers, each tied to one of the Buddhist elements (earth, water, fire, wind), fight and dance under the control of electromagnetic brain stimulation.
- How it works: Motion-captured dancers and game-engine avatars are combined with imagery of transcranial magnetic stimulation (likely).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X7A8S2Q79HI
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu_Yang_(artist)

#### Third Thumb — Dani Clode (2017)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Extending the body is not just mechanical: the brain rewrites its picture of the hand to include the machine.
- What it is: A 3D-printed robotic extra thumb worn beside the little finger and controlled with pressure sensors under the big toes; in a later UCL study, people who wore it for days learned new grasps and their brain's map of the hand changed.
- How it works: Two motors pull cables in a 3D-printed thumb; wireless foot sensors map toe pressure to flexion and adduction.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1126/scirobotics.abd7935 (Science Robotics 2021)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UD_LwZD2Kls
- Images: https://dvqlxo2m2q99q.cloudfront.net/000_clients/107233/page/g22141jqBFNhnz6t.jpg
- Project page: https://www.daniclodedesign.com/thethirdthumb

#### Corpus Nil — Marco Donnarumma (2016)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: The machine does not follow the body; it learns from and pushes it, making a new, unfamiliar body together.
- What it is: A near-motionless, painted body slowly contorts on the floor while an AI system listens to its muscle sounds and blood flow and answers with loud sound and light that push the performer into strange configurations.
- How it works: Biosensors (mechanomyography microphones and blood-flow sensors) feed machine-learning software that generates sound and light in real time.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CAIh8FxLMtk
- Images: https://marcodonnarumma.com/live/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/marco-donnarumma_corpus-nil_zkm_onuk.jpg
- Project page: https://marcodonnarumma.com/works/corpus-nil/

#### Inferno — Louis-Philippe Demers, Bill Vorn (2015)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Being moved by a machine is felt from the inside: the participant is both performer and victim of the choreography.
- What it is: Audience members are strapped into robotic exoskeletons that move their arms and torsos to loud industrial music, so the crowd becomes a chorus of bodies puppeteered by machines, a hell after Dante.
- How it works: Wearable exoskeletons with pneumatic or electric actuators on the arms and back, controlled centrally in sync with sound and light.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sGIbZ5DD4fY
- Images: http://billvorn.concordia.ca/robography/images/Inferno01.jpg
- Project page: http://billvorn.concordia.ca/robography/Inferno.html

#### Propel — Stelarc (2015)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Here the machine is the choreographer and the human the payload; the body is one interchangeable end-effector among others.
- What it is: Stelarc's body is strapped to the end of an industrial robot arm that choreographs its trajectory, speed and orientation for 35 minutes; afterwards the robot repeats the same choreography holding a giant carved ear.
- How it works: Industrial robot arm with a 3 m reach programmed with a fixed choreography; the same robot also milled the ear sculpture it later moved.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: DeMonstrable, Lawrence Wilson Art Gallery, Perth (2015)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2bRpTn0KKd8
- Project page: https://stelarc.org/

#### Seismic Sense / Waiting for Earthquakes — Moon Ribas (2013)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: A networked implant can tie a body to planetary time: the dancer cannot choose when she moves.
- What it is: An implanted sensor linked to online seismographs vibrates whenever an earthquake happens anywhere on Earth; in the performance Waiting for Earthquakes, Ribas stands still and turns each tremor she feels into movement.
- How it works: Vibration implant (first in the arm, later in the feet) driven by real-time seismic data; stronger quakes produce stronger vibrations.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Un4MFR-vNI
- Images: https://images.hoobaweb.com/8930/imgf-1200-630/moon-ribas.png
- Project page: https://www.moonribas.com/

#### Prospectus for a Future Body — Choy Ka Fai (2011)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: If a machine can move your muscles, dance history could be stored and replayed in someone else's body.
- What it is: A series of experiments and performances in which electrical muscle stimulation makes dancers' muscles contract, trying to 'transfer' the movements of other dancers, including Tatsumi Hijikata's butoh, into a new body as digital muscle memory.
- How it works: Electrical nerve and muscle stimulation driven by recorded movement data, in four proposals: Eternal Summer Storm, Bionic Movement Research, SynchroMetrics and Notion: Dance Fiction.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Festival Tokyo 2011 (Notion: Dance Fiction); 15th Japan Media Arts Festival, Jury Selection
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5JlYSgxECxs
- Images: https://www.ka5.info/1_PROSPECTUS/3-NOT01.jpg https://www.ka5.info/1_PROSPECTUS/1-ESS02.jpg
- Project page: https://www.ka5.info/prospectus.html

#### 3rdi — Wafaa Bilal (2010)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: A body can carry an automatic eye it cannot look through; the machine sees for others, not for its wearer.
- What it is: For about a year Bilal wore a camera surgically attached to the back of his head; it took a picture every minute and streamed it to a website and to Mathaf in Doha, recording what he left behind.
- How it works: Small camera mounted on a titanium plate implanted in the back of the head, capturing one frame per minute and uploading via a laptop.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art, Doha (2010–11)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h2nNKbO9-Eg
- Project page: https://wafaabilal.com/3rdi/

#### Menstruation Machine – Takashi's Take — Sputniko! (Hiromi Ozaki) (2010)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: A machine on the body can make a gendered experience transferable, and so open to discussion.
- What it is: A metal belt-like device that simulates menstruation, with blood release and lower-abdomen pain, shown in a pop music video about a boy who wears it to experience what his friend goes through.
- How it works: A blood-dispensing mechanism and electrodes that stimulate the lower abdomen, operated on a 28-day cycle; presented with a music video and costume.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: ZKM Karlsruhe
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gnb-rdGbm6s
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/ad/Sputniko.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sputniko!

#### Electric Stimulus to Face — Daito Manabe (2008)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: When a computer drives the face, expression is separated from feeling.
- What it is: Electrodes on faces receive electrical pulses synchronised to music, so the performers' facial muscles twitch into expressions they are not making.
- How it works: A computer sends sequenced electrical muscle stimulation (EMS) through surface electrodes, timed to a soundtrack; later versions read one face's myoelectric signal to drive another.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tJ4_-2_oWuM
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daito_Manabe

#### Ear on Arm — Stelarc (2006)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: An organ can be relocated and repurposed as a public, networked sense for others rather than for oneself.
- What it is: An ear built from cell-cultured tissue and a biocompatible scaffold, surgically constructed on Stelarc's left forearm; the plan is to add a microphone that streams what the ear 'hears' to the internet.
- How it works: Porous polyethylene scaffold inserted under the skin in surgeries from 2006, allowed to grow tissue; an embedded microphone was tested and later removed after infection.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine listening & voice
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s80ZjumSA08
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/23/Stelarc_3rd_ear_2011f.jpg
- Project page: https://stelarc.org/

#### Eyeborg (Cyborg Antenna) — Neil Harbisson (2004)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Computer vision
- Idea: A machine sense can become part of a person's body and identity, not just a tool they use.
- What it is: An antenna osseointegrated in Harbisson's skull converts light frequencies, including infrared and ultraviolet, into vibrations he hears through bone; he paints and composes with this sense.
- How it works: Camera sensor at the tip of the antenna feeds a chip that maps hue to pitch, heard through bone conduction; Bluetooth allows remote colour input.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ygRNoieAnzI
- Project page: https://www.cyborgarts.com/

#### Project Cyborg 2.0 (neural implant) — Kevin Warwick (2002)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Industrial robot arm
- Idea: A nervous system can be networked: touch and movement travel as data between bodies and machines.
- What it is: Warwick had a 100-electrode array implanted into the median nerve of his arm; he used it to move a robot hand over the internet from New York, and to exchange simple nerve signals with his wife, who had a simpler implant.
- How it works: Utah microelectrode array in the median nerve, connected to a computer that recorded and stimulated nerve signals and relayed them over the internet.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1001/archneur.60.10.1369 (Archives of Neurology 2003)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GLq7edATaFo
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Warwick

#### Prosthetic Head — Stelarc (2002)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Humanoid & android
- Idea: A 'prosthesis' can be a mind rather than a limb: the artist extends himself through a talking agent that answers for him.
- What it is: A large projected 3D head with Stelarc's face that talks with visitors who type questions; it has its own opinions, moods and can make up verse, more a conversational double than a portrait.
- How it works: Embodied conversational agent: chatbot engine with a customised knowledge base, text-to-speech and a real-time animated 3D model of the artist's head.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Machine listening & voice
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dprvwAWfy9Q
- Project page: https://stelarc.org/

#### Cyborg series — Lee Bul (1998)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Humanoid & android
- Idea: Techno-perfection is shown as a gendered fantasy, and the cyborg body as incomplete.
- What it is: White silicone figures of female cyborgs, often missing a head or limbs, hung from the ceiling like armour or anime heroines. First shown at Artsonje Center, Seoul, in 1998, the series recasts the machine-enhanced body as fragmentary and eroticised.
- How it works: Cast silicone, polyurethane and paint, drawing on manga, anime and classical sculpture; works such as Cyborg W1–W4 (1998).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Artsonje Center, Seoul 1998; Korean Pavilion, 48th Venice Biennale 1999; Lee Bul: Crashing, Hayward Gallery 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aS5di0wCD1I
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/5a/Untitled_%28Cyborg%27s_pelvis%29_by_Lee_Bul%2C_British_Museum_01.jpg
- Project page: https://www.guggenheim.org/artwork/artist/lee-bul

#### Exoskeleton — Stelarc (1998)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: The body becomes the pilot and the passenger of a larger, non-human body at the same time.
- What it is: Stelarc stands on a six-legged pneumatic walking machine and steers its walk and turns with arm gestures, while the hiss and clank of the machine are amplified into a soundtrack.
- How it works: Pneumatic hexapod robot built with engineers in Hamburg; arm movements read by sensors on an arm-mounted exoskeleton select gaits and directions.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R2MntBUwUxY
- Project page: https://stelarc.org/

#### Time Capsule — Eduardo Kac (1997)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Being readable by machines is a way of being classified; the implant makes the body a database entry.
- What it is: Live on Brazilian television and the web, Kac implanted an identification microchip in his ankle and then registered himself online in a pet-recovery database as both animal and owner.
- How it works: RFID microchip injected with a syringe, scanned live, and the chip number registered in an animal ID database over the internet.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Casa das Rosas, São Paulo (1997)
- Images: https://www.ekac.org/needle.gif
- Project page: https://www.ekac.org/timec.html

#### Ping Body — Stelarc (1996)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: The network can become the body's nervous system: here the body is moved by data it cannot feel.
- What it is: Stelarc sends ping signals to dozens of internet domains; the round-trip times drive a muscle-stimulation system, so the flow of internet traffic, not his will, makes his arms and legs twitch and move.
- How it works: Ping values from global internet hosts mapped to a computer-controlled muscle stimulation system with electrodes on the limbs; the Third Hand is driven by his own EMG.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: DEAF96, V2_ Rotterdam (1996)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=45MOlsFGSHI
- Project page: https://stelarc.org/

#### Epizoo — Marcel·lí Antúnez Roca (1994)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Interfaces make cruelty feel like a game: one click at a distance is felt as pain in another body.
- What it is: Antúnez stands on a turntable wearing a pneumatic exoskeleton; audience members use a computer mouse to make it pull at his nose, ears, mouth, buttocks and chest, while cartoon animations of his body play on screens.
- How it works: Body-worn pneumatic mechanisms driven by a computer and controlled by spectators through a graphical mouse interface.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5utDR8VWxms
- Images: https://www.marceliantunez.com/media/cache/3b/1f/3b1f492a17b1654525596a9cc5d9af01.jpg
- Project page: https://www.marceliantunez.com/work/epizoo/

#### Inter Dis-Communication Machine — Kazuhiko Hachiya (1993)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Computer vision
- Idea: Swapping senses through a machine shows how much the self depends on its own point of view.
- What it is: Two people wear head-mounted displays and winged costumes; each sees and hears only what the other's camera and microphone pick up, so they must move while inside each other's perception.
- How it works: Wireless video cameras and microphones on each wearer transmit to the other's head-mounted display and headphones.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine seeing
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JOzVzcmK0VU
- Images: https://www.ntticc.or.jp/uploads/assets/000/63850.936.large.jpg
- Project page: https://www.ntticc.or.jp/en/archive/works/inter-dis-communication-machine/

#### Third Hand — Stelarc (1980)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: An extra limb is learned, not given: the body slowly makes room for a machine that it controls indirectly.
- What it is: A mechanical right hand attached to Stelarc's arm and driven by the electrical signals of his abdominal and leg muscles, which he wrote and performed with alongside his own two hands for many years.
- How it works: Robotic hand with pinch, grasp and wrist rotation, controlled by EMG electrodes on abdomen and legs, with tactile feedback to the arm.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Or1CVc6A9YA
- Project page: https://stelarc.org/

#### WearComp and EyeTap — Steve Mann (1978)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Living inside a machine's view changes both what you see and how others see you; Mann named the reverse gaze 'sousveillance'.
- What it is: Over decades Mann built and wore ever smaller computers and head-mounted camera-displays in daily life, seeing the world through a computer that could record, alter and share his view.
- How it works: Backpack and later eyeglass-based wearable computers with cameras and displays aligned to the eye (EyeTap) to mediate vision in real time.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/2.566147 (IEEE Computer 1997)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fCco6FMCRmk
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3e/SteveMann_with_Generation-4_Glass_1999.jpg
- Project page: http://wearcam.org/

### Telepresence & Remote Bodies

Acting, touching and being present through a machine at a distance.

#### Avatar Robot Café DAWN ver.β — Ory Laboratory (2018)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Social & companion robot
- Idea: A robot body can give work and social presence back to people whose own bodies keep them home.
- What it is: A café in Tokyo where the waiters are OriHime robots operated from home by people with ALS and other conditions that keep them from going out.
- How it works: Tablet and eye-gaze interfaces control the 1.2 m OriHime-D and desktop OriHime robots over the internet; pilots began in 2018 and a permanent café opened in Nihonbashi in 2021.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tKzCZ_yP4-Y
- Images: https://dawn2021.orylab.com/assets/images/common/ogp2.jpg
- Project page: https://dawn2021.orylab.com/en/

#### Habeas Corpus — Laurie Anderson (2015)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Computer vision
- Idea: Telepresence can give a body a presence that borders and law deny it.
- What it is: Mohammed el Gharani, detained at Guantánamo from age 14 and barred from entering the US, appeared live from West Africa as a giant projection on a white seated statue in New York's Park Avenue Armory, telling his story.
- How it works: Live video stream from Africa projected onto a large 3D sculpture modelled on the Lincoln Memorial statue.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Park Avenue Armory, New York (2015)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kUKLA-W0nDM
- Project page: https://laurieanderson.com/

#### The Machine to Be Another — BeAnotherLab (2012)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Body ownership is fragile: synchronised seeing and touching are enough to let a machine swap bodies.
- What it is: Two participants wear headsets that show the live view from each other's head-mounted camera and mirror each other's movements, so each feels, for a few minutes, that they are in the other's body.
- How it works: Head-mounted cameras and VR displays with synchronised movement and touch, based on body-ownership illusion research.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hjIOUa10YpI
- Images: https://beanotherlab.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/bal_tmtba01.jpg
- Project page: https://beanotherlab.org/home/work/tmtba/

#### Telenoid R1 — Hiroshi Ishiguro (2010)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Humanoid & android, Social & companion robot
- Idea: A deliberately genderless, ageless body lets the listener imagine whoever is speaking, which makes presence feel stronger, not weaker.
- What it is: A small, pale, limb-stub robot with a minimal face that carries a remote person's voice and head movements; people hold it in their arms while talking to someone far away.
- How it works: About 80 cm long and 5 kg, silicone-skinned, with a few actuators in the head and arms driven by the operator's face tracking; tested in elder care in Japan and Denmark.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: RMIT Gallery, Melbourne
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/2048259.2048274 (ACM SIGGRAPH 2011 Emerging Technologies)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hKvsHU1hrxg
- Images: http://www.geminoid.jp/img/robot/telenoid.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telenoid_R1

#### Domestic Tension — Wafaa Bilal (2007)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: Remote-controlled violence feels like a game to the shooter and like war to the target, as with drone warfare.
- What it is: For 30 days Bilal lived in a Chicago gallery watched by a webcam; online visitors could aim and fire a paintball gun at him at any time, which they did tens of thousands of times.
- How it works: Webcam feed plus a robotic paintball gun controlled through a website and chat room.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine seeing
- Shown at: FlatFile Galleries, Chicago (2007)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F_L6BC9O0rY
- Images: http://wafaabilal.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/04/Domestic_Tension_Wafaabilal_1.jpg
- Project page: https://wafaabilal.com/domestic-tension/

#### PRoP (Personal Roving Presence) — Eric Paulos (1998)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Computer vision
- Idea: Remote presence needs more than video: gaze, gesture and the ability to wander make a body socially present.
- What it is: Made with John Canny, a tall mobile robot with a screen showing the remote user's face, a camera, microphone and a pointer arm lets a person roam, look around, gesture and chat in a distant building.
- How it works: Wheeled base with a video screen, pan-tilt camera, audio and a pointing arm, teleoperated over the internet.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/274644.274686 (CHI 1998)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ypKd1pbDbds
- Project page: https://www.paulos.net/

#### Rara Avis — Eduardo Kac (1996)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Computer vision
- Idea: Telepresence places you inside another body among other species, as the odd one out.
- What it is: In an aviary with some 30 zebra finches perches a telerobotic macaw; visitors wearing a VR headset see through its eyes and move its head, and internet users could also look through it and speak through its voice.
- How it works: Robotic macaw with stereo cameras in its eyes, coupled to a VR headset's head tracking, with video and audio also streamed to the internet.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Nexus Contemporary Art Center, Atlanta (1996)
- Images: https://www.ekac.org/rara.avis.jpg
- Project page: https://www.ekac.org/raraavis.html

#### Fractal Flesh — Stelarc (1995)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: A body can be distributed across a network and moved by many remote agents at once.
- What it is: During the Telepolis event, people at terminals in Paris, Helsinki and Amsterdam touched a screen model of Stelarc's body and remotely stimulated his muscles in Luxembourg, making him move without his consent.
- How it works: Touch-screen interface at remote sites sends commands over the internet to a muscle-stimulation system attached to the artist's body.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Telepolis, Luxembourg (1995)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N2VkOE_AgNI
- Project page: https://stelarc.org/

#### The Telegarden — Ken Goldberg (1995)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Care at a distance depends on trusting a machine and an image: did I really water that plant?
- What it is: Made with Joseph Santarromana, a small garden of living plants was tended for nine years by thousands of internet users who planted and watered seeds through an industrial robot arm they could see only on a webpage.
- How it works: Adept-1 industrial robot arm with a camera over a planter, controlled through a web interface; members' actions were logged.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Ars Electronica Center, Linz (1996–2004)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vQE-qJ_aYPw
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/31/Telegarden.jpg https://goldberg.berkeley.edu/garden/telegarden-8x6-72dpi.jpg
- Project page: https://goldberg.berkeley.edu/garden/Ars/

#### Tillie, the Telerobotic Doll — Lynn Hershman Leeson (1995)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Computer vision, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: An object that looks back turns the viewer into the watched, and lends a remote gaze a body.
- What it is: A doll with video cameras for eyes sits in a gallery; web visitors look through her eyes and turn her head, seeing the room from the doll's point of view.
- How it works: Doll fitted with cameras in the eyes and a motorised head, streaming images to a website where users control the viewing direction.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ZOIdUZueHc
- Project page: https://www.lynnhershman.com/

#### The Mercury Project — Ken Goldberg (1994)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Computer vision
- Idea: The web turned a lab robot into a public, shared body, and raised the question of whether what we see remotely is real.
- What it is: One of the first robots anyone could control through the web: visitors directed an arm to blow bursts of air into a sandbox and excavate buried objects, seeing the results in camera images.
- How it works: Industrial robot arm with camera and air nozzle controlled through a Mosaic browser interface via CGI scripts.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/robot.1995.525358 (IEEE ICRA 1995)
- Project page: https://goldberg.berkeley.edu/

#### cyberSM — Stahl Stenslie (1993)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Remote touch through a machine is an early question for networked intimacy: what counts as contact?
- What it is: Made with Kirk Woolford, two participants in different cities wear suits fitted with stimulators and touch each other's 3D body models on screen; the touches arrive as vibration and electrical stimuli on the other's skin.
- How it works: Body suits with stimulators, 3D-scanned body avatars and a telecommunication link (ISDN) between remote sites.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E5TFZJzKbYI
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stahl_Stenslie

#### Telematic Dreaming — Paul Sermon (1992)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Telepresence is felt through the body: people react to a projected hand as if it could touch them.
- What it is: Two double beds in separate places are linked by video: the image of the person on one bed is projected onto the other bed, so strangers lie together, touch and play with each other's projected bodies.
- How it works: Overhead camera and projector at each bed, linked over ISDN lines, with monitors showing the combined image.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Kajaani, Finland (1992)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S4Wt16PnqeY
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sermon

#### Ornitorrinco — Eduardo Kac (1989)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Computer vision
- Idea: Presence can be displaced into a small, slow machine; the remote body is shared rather than owned.
- What it is: A small telerobot named after the platypus is driven by remote participants over ordinary phone lines; they see its surroundings through its camera eye, sharing a machine body across cities.
- How it works: Mobile robot with a camera, controlled via telephone keypad tones, sending back still video images over phone lines (with Ed Bennett).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine seeing
- Images: https://www.ekac.org/ornitorrinco.color.jpg
- Project page: https://www.ekac.org/ornitorrinco.html

#### Hole in Space — Kit Galloway & Sherrie Rabinowitz (1980)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Computer vision
- Idea: A telecom link becomes a public place: people invent how to behave with remote bodies as soon as they meet them.
- What it is: For three evenings, life-size live video screens linked passers-by at Lincoln Center in New York and a shopping centre in Century City, Los Angeles, via satellite, with no signs or explanation; strangers, then families, met across the continent.
- How it works: Two-way satellite video link with cameras and rear-projection screens in shop windows on each coast.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QSMVtE1QjaU
- Project page: http://www.ecafe.com/getty/HIS/

#### Telexistence (TELESAR) — Susumu Tachi (1980)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Humanoid & android, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: A robot can be designed not as another agent but as a second body the human inhabits.
- What it is: Tachi's concept and robot series in which an operator wearing a head-mounted display and haptic suit sees, hears and feels through a remote humanoid robot as if present in its body; TELESAR V (2011) adds fine touch.
- How it works: Stereo cameras on the robot head follow the operator's head motion; master-slave arms and hands transmit force, vibration and temperature back to the operator.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine umwelt
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/MCG.2016.6 (IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications, 2016)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5j_hdDzgGvc
- Images: https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/Telesar%E2%85%A4%2C_telexistence_robot_by_Susumu_Tachi_Laboratory%2C_exhibited_at_Miraikan_%282015-06-15_03.58.07_by_Franklin_Heijnen%29.jpg/1280px-Telesar%E2%85%A4%2C_telexistence_robot_by_Susumu_Tachi_Laboratory%2C_exhibited_at_Miraikan_%282015-06-15_03.58.07_by_Franklin_Heijnen%29.jpg
- Project page: https://tachilab.org/en/about/telexistence.html

### Dancing with Machines

Choreographies for human and machine bodies.

#### Yang BOT — Unitree Robotics, Zhang Yimou (2025)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Folk dance performed by humanoids turns robot bodies into a national image watched by hundreds of millions.
- What it is: Sixteen Unitree H1 humanoid robots in padded jackets dance yangge and twirl handkerchiefs beside human dancers on the CCTV Spring Festival Gala, directed by Zhang Yimou.
- How it works: Choreography learned through motion capture and reinforcement learning, with robots synchronised to dancers and handkerchief-spinning end effectors.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: CCTV Spring Festival Gala 2025
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ykiuz1ZdGBc
- Project page: https://technode.com/2025/01/29/unitree-robotics-humanoid-robots-steal-the-show-at-2025-cctv-spring-festival-gala-with-ai-powered-yangge-dance/

#### Alloyed Bodies [BNE-3-3-1] — Petra Gemeinboeck, Rob Saunders (2024)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Instead of robots that mimic or serve us, the piece builds a shared playground where dancers become a little box-like and a box becomes a little alive, so the relation, not likeness to humans, carries the meaning.
- What it is: An improvised performance installation, premiered at ISEA 2024 in Brisbane, in which four dancers, three cube-shaped costumes and one cube robot mingle in a 'strange and whimsical cube world'; in the last part the audience is invited onto the floor to move among the human and non-human performers.
- How it works: A non-humanoid cube robot, whose movement qualities come from the Machine Movement Lab's dancer-led movement studies, improvises with four dancers and three cube costumes inside an evolving soundscape treated as a further performer.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: ISEA 2024, Brisbane
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-981-96-3525-2_10 (ICSR + AI 2024, Social Robotics (LNCS))
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sEJRIsLQvXw
- Project page: https://isea2024.isea-international.org/machine-movement-lab-alloyed-bodies-bne-3-3-1/

#### Nondance Dance — Shinseungback Kimyonghun (2022)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Computer vision
- Idea: To dance outside a machine's categories, dancers first have to learn how the machine sees dance.
- What it is: Dancers perform while a video-recognition AI watches and signals by voice or light whenever it recognises 'dance'. They try to find movements that are still dance to humans but invisible as dance to the machine.
- How it works: Google Video AI action recognition (20,000+ labels, including many dance categories) gives live feedback to the dancers.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Video: https://vimeo.com/776909143
- Images: https://djhznh41oxwef.cloudfront.net/works/nondance_dance/ssbkyh_Nondance_dance_01.png
- Project page: https://ssbkyh.com/works/nondance_dance/

#### Do You Love Me? — Boston Dynamics (2020)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Choreography is a strong way to make machines likeable, and it hides the engineering, control and purpose behind them.
- What it is: Atlas humanoids, Spot robot dogs and a Handle robot dance to The Contours' 1962 song in a video released at the end of 2020; it drew tens of millions of views and debate about how dance makes robots seem joyful.
- How it works: Motion sequences authored with choreographer Monica Thomas in Boston Dynamics' choreography software and executed by the robots' own balance control, filmed in edited takes.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fn3KWM1kuAw
- Project page: https://bostondynamics.com/

#### Merritt + Robot — Merritt Moore (2020)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Industrial robot arm
- Idea: In isolation, a programmable arm becomes a partner; the duet is also a rehearsal between a dancer and her own code.
- What it is: During the 2020 lockdown, dancer and physicist Merritt Moore programmed a Universal Robots arm as her only partner and filmed a pas de deux in which the robot both leads and follows.
- How it works: Collaborative robot arm (Universal Robots) programmed by the dancer herself.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uSOHc3ODLzU
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/66c15199c6b23b75923ac311/b4ae89c2-ea53-41f0-82e8-2d95034920ed/Merritt_Moore_robots_Mexico.png
- Project page: https://www.merrittmoore.com/

#### Living Archive — Wayne McGregor (2019)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data, Computer vision
- Idea: A choreographer's style, turned into a model, becomes a partner that proposes 'his' next move.
- What it is: Google Arts & Culture trained a model on thousands of hours of video from 25 years of McGregor's choreography; given a dancer's pose, it proposes what could come next, and these phrases were staged in Living Archive: An AI Performance Experiment.
- How it works: Pose estimation on archive video plus a neural network predicting sequences of body poses; dancers learn and adapt the proposals.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: The Music Center, Los Angeles (2019)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hd3BDvfmg4k
- Images: https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/UAE2Fk3CoTgjTWKg9PiFGU6XjasBWnRO5g2xP_LHAHZZVVgfPCx3K3BKv58VuXW9hErbCpVgYhBUk1iAzprsgTkX_eTl
- Project page: https://experiments.withgoogle.com/living-archive-wayne-mcgregor

#### OUTPUT — Catie Cuan (2019)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Choreography can be a design method for robots: the dance studies what it takes for a machine's motion to read as expressive.
- What it is: Cuan dances with an ABB IRB 6700 industrial robot, then both bodies are recorded and replayed as motion capture, video and a web app, so each body's movement is translated into the other's medium.
- How it works: Robot motion programmed from Cuan's movement, captured with motion capture and recombined in video and interactive software.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.3389/frobt.2020.576790 (Frontiers in Robotics and AI 2021)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ng0ioS7oNXY
- Project page: https://www.catiecuan.com/

#### Where Is My (Deep) Mind? — Julien Prévieux (2019)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Dataset & training data, Computer vision
- Idea: Re-enacting with human bodies how machines learn shows how literal, clumsy and socially blind learning from examples can be.
- What it is: A film in which four dancer-actors act out machine-learning experiments, from recognising sports movements to learning to haggle, playing both the experimenters and the subjects with mechanical, childlike bodies.
- How it works: Choreography restages key machine-learning experiments for camera, as a sequel to the stage piece of balls, books and hats (Friche La Belle de Mai, Marseille, 2018); 14'59" HD video.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: Geste, Magasins généraux, Pantin, 2019 (Lab'Bel and cneai)
- Images: https://www.lab-bel.com/wp-content/uploads/julien-previeux.jpg
- Project page: https://www.lab-bel.com/en/collection/julien-previeux/

#### discrete figures — Rhizomatiks, ELEVENPLAY, Daito Manabe (2018)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Computer vision, Generative model & latent space, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: A dancer meeting a model of their own movement sees how a machine abstracts a body.
- What it is: A stage work in which dancers perform with machine-generated 'dancers': a model trained on their motion creates new movement, shown as projected figures and on drones carrying screens.
- How it works: Motion-capture data from ELEVENPLAY dancers trained generative models; real-time tracking aligns projections and drones with the performers; made with Kyle McDonald.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Spiral Hall, Tokyo 2018; Gray Area, San Francisco
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hauXQQhwbgM
- Images: https://research.rhizomatiks.com/s/works/discrete_figures/images/video_image.jpg
- Project page: https://research.rhizomatiks.com/s/works/discrete_figures/en/

#### Co(AI)xistence — Justine Emard (2017)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Treat a learning android as a different kind of intelligence and look for a language both sides can share.
- What it is: A 12-minute video installation in which the performer Mirai Moriyama and the android Alter try to communicate through gesture, signals and speech; Alter learns from the exchange as it goes.
- How it works: Filmed improvisation between a dancer and Alter (Ishiguro Lab, Osaka University, and Ikegami Lab, University of Tokyo), whose motion is driven by a neural network and sensor input.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: AI: More than Human, Barbican, London 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vcdUTEpSV1s
- Project page: https://justineemard.com/coaixistence/

#### 24 drones — Rhizomatiks, ELEVENPLAY, Daito Manabe (2016)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: Choreography can include machine bodies whose precision exposes the dancers' own timing.
- What it is: Five dancers perform with a swarm of 24 small drones that move in formation around and between them, turning the drones into a corps de ballet.
- How it works: Indoor motion capture tracks drones and dancers; flight paths are pre-simulated in software and synchronised to music and light.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SPcZmDTW8KU
- Images: https://research.rhizomatiks.com/s/works/24drones/img/drone_00.png
- Project page: https://research.rhizomatiks.com/s/works/24drones/en/

#### chor-rnn — Louise Crnkovic-Friis, Luka Crnkovic-Friis (2016)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Watching a model learn to dance makes visible what 'style' means to a machine: statistics of joints.
- What it is: A recurrent neural network trained on hours of motion capture of a contemporary dancer learns to generate new choreography in her style; published videos show it moving from twitching noise to dance-like phrases as training goes on.
- How it works: Mixture-density LSTM network trained on Kinect motion-capture joint positions of the choreographer's improvisations.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Opacity & latent space
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.06921 (arXiv 2016)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q4_XSMqN8w0

#### Bionic dance at TED2014 (with Adrianne Haslet-Davis) — Hugh Herr (2014)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: A prosthesis can be designed for expression, tuned to how a dancer moves, not only to walking.
- What it is: Ballroom dancer Adrianne Haslet-Davis, who lost her lower left leg in the 2013 Boston Marathon bombing, danced a rumba on stage at TED2014 on a bionic leg made by Hugh Herr's lab.
- How it works: Powered ankle-foot prosthesis with motors and sensors, tuned using motion data recorded from dancers.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CDsNZJTWw0w
- Images: https://pi.tedcdn.com/r/pe.tedcdn.com/images/ted/ca0520623aeb359f6d5f371d516371fadcae2454_1600x1200.jpg?u%5Br%5D=2&u%5Bs%5D=0.5&u%5Ba%5D=0.8&u%5Bt%5D=0.03&quality=82&w=1200
- Project page: https://www.ted.com/talks/hugh_herr_the_new_bionics_that_let_us_run_climb_and_dance

#### ROBOT — Blanca Li (2013)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android, Social & companion robot
- Idea: Putting humans and robots in the same choreography shows how much of our movement is already mechanical.
- What it is: Eight dancers share the stage with seven small NAO humanoid robots and the musical machines of Maywa Denki; humans move like robots and robots attempt human dances.
- How it works: Programmed NAO robots (Aldebaran) with pre-set choreography, alongside Maywa Denki instruments and live dancers.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Montpellier Danse (2013)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vrH0Ydj3HN4
- Project page: https://www.blancali.com/en/spectacle/robot-2/

#### Huang Yi & KUKA — Huang Yi (2012)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Programming a robot minute by minute becomes a way of looking at one's own loneliness in a machine mirror.
- What it is: A duet, later an evening-length piece, between Huang Yi and a KUKA industrial robot arm that he programmed himself; the arm carries a light, mirrors his moves and partners him in slow, close choreography.
- How it works: KUKA industrial arm programmed by hand (10–20 hours of programming per minute of choreography), with a light or camera on the end-effector.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Ars Electronica Festival 2013; TED2017, Vancouver; Toured 20 countries
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xy6tPmFlN34
- Images: https://huangyistudio.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/huangyiandkuka_TED2017_01.jpg https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/51/Prix_Ars_Electronical_2013_11_Huang_Yi_KUKA.jpg
- Project page: https://huangyistudio.com/archives/project/huang-yi-and-kuka

#### Human Interface — Thomas Freundlich (2012)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Once the safety cage comes down, a factory robot can be read as a personality, not a tool.
- What it is: A dance work for two dancers and two industrial robots in the old boiler hall of the Cable Factory in Helsinki; the robots' programmed movement is exact yet surprisingly human, and they act as equal dance partners.
- How it works: ABB industrial robots programmed by the choreographer, with a safety system that allowed humans inside the robots' working area; follows his 2008 duet Actuator.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Zodiak Center for New Dance, Helsinki (2012)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MCSUVI--0Sw
- Project page: http://www.freundlich.org/

#### Grace State Machines — Bill Vorn (2007)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: When a robot moves from a human's inner signals, the line between the two bodies becomes the choreography.
- What it is: A 27-minute stage duet between performer Emma Howes and a robot: her movements and internal body states are captured and transposed onto the machine's body, so the two move in a shifting, symbiotic dialogue.
- How it works: Motion capture and biofeedback sensors on the performer drive the robot's actuators in real time (with Jonathan Villeneuve).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b6TiJdGRMTw
- Images: https://billvorn.concordia.ca/robography/images/GSMBB.jpg
- Project page: https://billvorn.concordia.ca/robography/GraceState.html

#### Glow — Gideon Obarzanek, Frieder Weiss (2006)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Computer vision
- Idea: Machine vision can be a stage partner: the dancer performs for the camera's reading of her as much as for the audience.
- What it is: A solo dancer moves on a white floor while an infrared camera tracks her body and a computer projects graphics that respond in real time, wrapping, stretching and chasing her shape with light.
- How it works: Infrared video tracking of the dancer (Frieder Weiss's Kalypso software) generating projected graphics on the floor.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C4He543_a80
- Project page: https://chunkymove.com.au/

#### DANCER #1 — Kris Verdonck (2003)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A machine's struggle to function is enough to read it as a dancer and to feel for it.
- What it is: A grinding wheel with a large steel 'L' hangs from the ceiling; when the motor starts, the L spins out of control while the machine keeps trying to find its balance, until it looks like a tragic hero in distress.
- How it works: Industrial grinding motor with an eccentric steel shape, run as a timed performance in a theatre space.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Kunstenfestivaldesarts, Brussels (2003); Festival d'Avignon (2008)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xKbBImj3mWM
- Images: https://www.atwodogscompany.org/media/og/17-dancer_krisverdonckhigh.jpg
- Project page: https://www.atwodogscompany.org/en/projects/dancer-1/

#### Zone — Pablo Ventura, robotlab (2001)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Industrial robot arm
- Idea: A factory arm on stage is a dancer with a different anatomy, not a prop.
- What it is: A KUKA industrial robot, programmed with robotlab, performs as a member of Ventura Dance Company alongside human dancers in a contemporary dance work.
- How it works: KUKA industrial robot with choreography programmed offline and synchronised with the dancers and music.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PD1i6rItAfA
- Project page: https://www.ventura-dance.com/

#### BIPED — Merce Cunningham, Paul Kaiser, Shelley Eshkar (1999)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Computer vision, Humanoid & android
- Idea: Captured movement becomes a second, weightless company that dances with and apart from the dancers.
- What it is: Dancers perform behind a transparent scrim onto which large hand-drawn-looking figures are projected, made from motion-captured Cunningham dancers, so live bodies and their digital traces share the stage.
- How it works: Optical motion capture of dancers rendered as abstract line figures by Kaiser and Eshkar, projected on a scrim; music by Gavin Bryars.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Zellerbach Hall, Berkeley (1999)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b_XItg0Vn1c
- Project page: https://www.mercecunningham.org/the-work/choreography/biped/

#### Ghostcatching — Bill T. Jones, Paul Kaiser, Shelley Eshkar (1999)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision
- Idea: Motion capture separates movement from the mover; what remains is a ghost the dancer can watch.
- What it is: A virtual dance made from motion capture of Bill T. Jones improvising: his movement becomes drawn lines that multiply, collide and are caught inside a box, a dancer without his body.
- How it works: Optical motion capture of Jones's improvisations, rendered as hand-drawn-style strokes in 3D animation.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x-7Mo3cg9jw
- Project page: https://openendedgroup.com/

#### Trackers (with LifeForms) — Merce Cunningham (1991)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: A virtual body with no weight or habits proposes movement that the human body must then learn to inhabit.
- What it is: The first dance Cunningham made with the software LifeForms: he composed sequences on animated 3D figures on a computer and then asked dancers to perform movements that no body had tried before.
- How it works: LifeForms, choreography software from Simon Fraser University (Tom Calvert, Thecla Schiphorst and others), for keyframing human figures in 3D.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/169059.169113 (CHI 1993)
- Project page: https://www.mercecunningham.org/

#### Very Nervous System — David Rokeby (1986)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Computer vision, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: An invisible, room-sized interface makes the whole body the input, so the loop between movement and machine response is felt rather than operated.
- What it is: An interactive sound installation in which video cameras watch a visitor moving through an empty room, and a computer turns every gesture into sound and music in real time.
- How it works: Video cameras feed image processors and a computer that measure changes of movement across the space and drive synthesizers and a sound system; Rokeby later released the system as the softVNS software.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine seeing, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: PetroCanada Media Arts Award, 1988; Prix Ars Electronica 1991, Award of Distinction (Interactive Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qdvyuvfKVU0
- Images: http://www.davidrokeby.com/VNS_Potsdam_web.jpg http://www.davidrokeby.com/venicecameraweb.jpg
- Project page: http://www.davidrokeby.com/vns.html

### Machine Theatre

Robots and AI as actors, characters and directors on stage.

#### Three Approaches to Synthetic Entities #1: El Turco – Living Theater — Diemut Strebe (2024)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Behind 'AI' there is often a hidden human, and beside it a model that can play anyone: the work stages the Turing test as theatre and asks what is left of intelligence when both sides are performances.
- What it is: On a 13-metre screen two hand-drawn avatars hold live conversations with visitors: one is driven by a large language model, the other is played in real time by a person hidden inside the system, as in the 18th-century 'Mechanical Turk' chess automaton.
- How it works: A real-time game-engine installation in which the left avatar is a character shell run by Claude 3.7 Sonnet chained to other AI tools and the right avatar is operated live by a hidden performer; developed with Northeastern University, the University of Utah and Georgia Tech, with support from Anthropic.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Hidden labour & extraction, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: MACHINE LOVE: Video Game, AI and Contemporary Art, Mori Art Museum, Tokyo, 2025
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3vCziUl-f_Y
- Images: https://diemut.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/s-img_1390-1.jpg https://diemut.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/img_1691.jpg
- Project page: https://diemut.net/three-approaches-to-synthetic-entities-1-el-turco-living-theater-live-event-at-the-mori-art-museum-with-anthropic/

#### Prometheus Firebringer — Annie Dorsen (2023)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Generative AI 'restores' the past by averaging it; the piece stages that loss alongside the machine's fluency.
- What it is: A language model generates a 'restoration' of Aeschylus's lost play, performed by AI-generated masks and voices, while Dorsen herself delivers a lecture on what such systems take from human culture.
- How it works: Large language model (GPT-3.5) generating the play, with generated mask images and synthetic voices, alongside a live human lecture.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Theatre for a New Audience, New York (2023)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CKDwPyJaESk
- Images: https://anniedorsen.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Copy-of-Prometheus_Firebringer_Baranova-2869-1900x1267.jpg
- Project page: https://anniedorsen.com/projects/prometheus-firebringer/

#### AI: When a Robot Writes a Play — THEaiTRE (2021)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Humanoid & android
- Idea: A machine-written 'autobiography' of a robot shows both what a model borrows from human drama and where it loses the thread.
- What it is: For the centenary of R.U.R., a team from Charles University and Prague theatres used GPT-2 to generate most of the script of a play about a robot facing birth, death, love and loneliness; it premiered online at Švandovo divadlo in February 2021.
- How it works: GPT-2 generating dialogue from human-written prompts, with human curation and editing in a custom tool, staged by professional actors.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.14668 (arXiv 2020)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8ho5sXiDX_A
- Images: https://www.theaitre.com/wp-content/uploads/THEaiTRE_PLAKAT_FINAL_web-e1614159078389.jpg
- Project page: https://www.theaitre.com/

#### Super Angels — Keiichiro Shibuya, Takashi Ikegami, Hiroshi Ishiguro (2021)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: An android with an artificial-life 'mind' shares a national opera stage with children, so living with machines becomes a story the next generation performs.
- What it is: An opera for singers, children, ballet dancers and the android Alter 3, premiered at the New National Theatre Tokyo: in a future where every child sits an aptitude test at fifteen and lives under 'Mother', an all-powerful AI, Alter 3 sings and moves among a children's choir.
- How it works: Music by Keiichiro Shibuya and libretto by Masahiko Shimada, produced under the theatre's opera director Kazushi Ono; Alter 3 (body by the Ishiguro Lab, artificial-life control by the Ikegami Lab, cameras in its eyes) performed live with orchestra, choir, dancers and video by WEiRDCORE.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: New National Theatre, Tokyo, 21–22 Aug 2021
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=94oJZQdopHo
- Images: https://image.tokion.jp/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/2021SuperAngels_shikama_No_0516-1024x682.jpg https://image.tokion.jp/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/2021SuperAngels_shikama_No_0263-1024x682.jpg
- Project page: https://tokion.jp/en/2021/09/22/super-angels-keiichiro-shibuya/

#### Human Study #4, La Classe — Patrick Tresset (2019)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Clumsy robots staging school discipline make visible how both machines and children are trained to conform.
- What it is: Twenty-one drawing robots sit at desks as a teacher and pupils; in a fifteen-minute play they chatter in distorted Morse code, are called one by one, practise lines and tally marks, briefly revolt and fall back in line.
- How it works: RNP-type robots, each a pen arm with a small camera head, run a scripted, partly generative choreography of sounds and plotted drawings in a classroom set.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Merge Festival, London 2019 (with Tate Modern); Prix Ars Electronica 2019, Honorary Mention (Artificial Life & Intelligence)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=znI6reVdN_M
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/2689289/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/2689291/preview/
- Project page: https://archive.aec.at/prix/244883/

#### Eingeweide — Marco Donnarumma, Margherita Pevere (2018)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Humanoid & android
- Idea: A hybrid body can be machinic, microbial and human at once, and none of them fully in control.
- What it is: A dance-theatre piece in which two performers, one fitted with an AI-driven robotic face prosthesis, struggle and fuse with each other and with membranes of living bacterial cellulose.
- How it works: Robotic face prosthesis controlled by a neural network responding to the performer's muscle signals; stage membranes grown from bacteria.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Romaeuropa Festival, Rome (2018)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6P0Vsg81Om0
- Project page: https://7c.marcodonnarumma.com/

#### Improbotics — Piotr Mirowski, Kory Mathewson (2018)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Improvisation exposes what a language model lacks as a partner: listening, memory of the scene and timing.
- What it is: An improv theatre company in which one performer, the 'cyborg', speaks lines generated live by a language model through an earpiece, while other players and the audience try to guess who is fed by the machine: a staged Turing test.
- How it works: Speech recognition feeds a dialogue model whose replies are read to the human cyborg via earpiece or shown on screen.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.01807 (arXiv 2018)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ICUoJBRNkkU
- Images: https://i0.wp.com/improbotics.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/improbotics_rosettacode_voilaeurope_2019nov8_markhambelton_dsc0219-2-e1573434690902.jpg?fit=1200%2C762&ssl=1
- Project page: https://improbotics.org/

#### Uncanny Valley (Unheimliches Tal) — Rimini Protokoll, Thomas Melle (2018)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: A robotic double can speak about the self more frankly than the self, and makes the audience ask whom they are feeling for.
- What it is: An animatronic replica of writer Thomas Melle sits alone on stage and delivers a lecture about his bipolar disorder, Alan Turing and doubles, while the real Melle is absent.
- How it works: Silicone animatronic made from casts and scans of Melle, with pre-recorded voice and programmed facial and hand movements.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Münchner Kammerspiele (2018)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7dOnjW5sQPk
- Project page: https://www.rimini-protokoll.de/website/en/project/unheimliches-tal-uncanny-valley

#### Cuckoo — Jaha Koo (2017)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Social & companion robot
- Idea: When a rice cooker is the voice that tells you dinner is ready, household machines become companions of loneliness.
- What it is: A performance in which Jaha Koo shares the stage with three talking Cuckoo-brand electric rice cookers. Through their chatter he tells 20 years of Korean history since the 1997 financial crisis and the isolation of his generation.
- How it works: Hacked talking rice cookers with programmed voices and light, combined with documentary video and live music.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: steirischer herbst, Graz 2017 (premiere); Festival d'Automne à Paris; SIFA 2023
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JmC02twjeDU
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaha_Koo

#### I Am Echoborg — Rik Lander, Phil D. Hall (2016)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Putting a machine's words in a human mouth reveals how much we judge a mind by its body.
- What it is: A human performer speaks only the words a chatbot sends through an earpiece; audience volunteers talk with this 'echoborg' and try to work out with it how humans and machines should live together.
- How it works: Custom conversational agent whose output is converted to speech and relayed to a human speaker (the echoborg method from social psychology).
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Machine listening & voice, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2015.00634 (Frontiers in Psychology 2015)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wh5QASc7PFY
- Images: https://echoborg.com/img/E7b_1920x1008_3_og.jpg
- Project page: https://echoborg.com/

#### Spillikin: A Love Story — Pipeline Theatre (2015)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android, Social & companion robot
- Idea: A care robot can also be a vessel of memory and love left by the dead.
- What it is: A play about Sue, who lives with Alzheimer's; her late husband, a roboticist, built a humanoid robot to keep her company and remember their life together, and the robot performs on stage alongside four actors.
- How it works: RoboThespian humanoid by Engineered Arts, programmed with cues and dialogue for each performance.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: Edinburgh Festival Fringe, Pleasance (2015)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CeoxJ2ZWRd0

- Project page: https://www.pipelinetheatre.com/spillikin

#### A Piece of Work — Annie Dorsen (2013)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: When a machine performs the canon, 'what a piece of work is a man' becomes a question about pattern, not character.
- What it is: An algorithmic Hamlet: each night computer programs cut, reorder and remix Shakespeare's text, which is spoken by synthetic voices and, in some scenes, by an actor, with lights and sound also run by code.
- How it works: Markov chains and other text algorithms applied to Hamlet in real time, with speech synthesis and generative lighting cues.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine listening & voice
- Images: https://anniedorsen.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Annie-Dorsen_A-Piece-of-Work_revengepic_photo-by-Bruno-Pocheron-1900x1069.jpg

#### Three Sisters, Android Version — Oriza Hirata, Hiroshi Ishiguro (2012)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: A family can live with an android double of someone who is still there but absent.
- What it is: Hirata's adaptation of Chekhov set in a declining Japanese industrial town, where a withdrawn younger sister is replaced in the family by an android copy of herself.
- How it works: An android (Geminoid F) and a Robovie robot perform with human actors; the android's speech and movement are operated and timed from offstage.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: Théâtre Varia, Brussels
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-8dhuoT8BkA

#### ACTOR #1 — Kris Verdonck (2010)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Humanoid & android
- Idea: An actor can be anything that holds attention on stage; a machine's fall can carry pathos.
- What it is: A three-part piece that tests what an actor is: a figure made of mist, a doll-like performer, and a robot that keeps falling, each asked to 'act' on stage without a human actor.
- How it works: Stage machines, fog effects and a robotic figure programmed for repeated falls, performed without human actors.

#### Data, the robot stand-up comedian — Heather Knight (2010)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Social & companion robot, Humanoid & android
- Idea: Comedy is a test of machine social sense: timing and reading the room are harder than the jokes.
- What it is: A small NAO robot named Data performs stand-up comedy and chooses its next joke from the audience's laughter and applause; it premiered at TEDWomen 2010.
- How it works: NAO humanoid with a joke database; audio and audience-feedback input update which joke is told next.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Alterity & the uncanny

#### Death and the Powers — Tod Machover (2010)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: If a person can live on in a building's machinery, the question becomes whether the family can still reach him.
- What it is: A robot opera: a dying billionaire uploads himself into 'the System', his house, and the stage itself, with a chorus of robotic 'Operabots', moving book-walls and a musical chandelier, becomes his new body.
- How it works: MIT Media Lab stage robotics (Operabots, robotic walls) driven by 'disembodied performance' sensing of the singer's voice and body.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Opéra de Monte-Carlo (2010); Pulitzer Prize finalist (2012)

#### Hello Hi There — Annie Dorsen (2010)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Watching machines debate human nature shows how language can be produced without anyone meaning it.

- How it works: Custom chatbot programs with text corpora (the debate plus other sources), text-to-speech and projected text.

#### Sayonara — Oriza Hirata, Hiroshi Ishiguro (2010)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: An android can keep someone company at death precisely because it will not die with them.

#### END — Kris Verdonck (2008)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: When the human is no longer the centre of the stage, machines and objects can carry the drama of an ending.

#### I, Worker (Hataraku Watashi) — Oriza Hirata, Hiroshi Ishiguro (2008)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android, Social & companion robot
- Idea: A robot that refuses work turns the machine into a mirror for human depression and labour.
- What it is: A 30-minute play in which a couple lives with two household robots, one of which has lost the will to work; the robots act alongside human actors on stage.
- How it works: Commercial humanoid robots perform pre-programmed lines and movements timed precisely to the human cast; the first Robot-Human Theater production of Seinendan and Osaka University.
