#### Afasia — Marcel·lí Antúnez Roca (1998)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: The performer becomes a switchboard: one body commands an orchestra of machines, and the story is told through that control.
- What it is: A one-man mechatronic version of Homer's Odyssey: wearing an exoskeleton, Antúnez conducts four musical robots, projected images and sound with his own body, without words.
- How it works: 'Dreskeleton' body interface with sensors sends signals to software that drives robot guitar, drum, bagpipe and violin, plus interactive video.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MJan5KPX050
- Images: https://www.marceliantunez.com/media/cache/ee/b8/eeb8aba209de3a0770ed94a45f3dd37d.jpg
- Project page: https://www.marceliantunez.com/work/afasia/

#### R.U.R. (Rossum's Universal Robots) — Karel Čapek (1921)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: The first robots were imagined as workers: the idea of the machine-other was born as a question about labour.
- What it is: Čapek's play is set in a factory that mass-produces artificial workers, the 'roboti', who are sold worldwide, then revolt and destroy humanity; its premiere at Prague's National Theatre gave the world the word robot.
- How it works: Stage play; the robots are biological-chemical artificial people played by human actors.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: National Theatre, Prague (1921)
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/87/Capek_play.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R.U.R.

### Machine Music & Co-improvisation

Machines that listen and play with musicians, and voices shared with a model.

#### Bla Blavatar vs Jaap Blonk — Jonathan Chaim Reus, Jaap Blonk (2024)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A voice clone is not a finished copy but ongoing labour: the work makes audible the effort of feeding a dataset and lets the clone fail creatively instead of perfecting the imitation.
- What it is: Sound poet Jaap Blonk performs scores written for both humans and machines while a real-time model of his own voice, played by Jonathan Reus, answers, interrupts and fragments him; every performance is recorded into the dataset, so the next 'Bla Blavatar' sounds different.
- How it works: Tungnaá, a real-time AI voice instrument built by Reus and Victor Shepardson at the Intelligent Instruments Lab (Iceland) from autoregressive text-to-speech techniques, is retrained on Blonk's growing recordings of 'Dataset Poems' modelled on phonetically balanced reading scripts.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Hidden labour & extraction, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: IZIS Festival (PiNA), premiere 4 Oct 2024; Prix Ars Electronica 2025, Award of Distinction (Digital Musics & Sound Art)
- Video: https://vimeo.com/1023520398
- Images: https://jonathanreus.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Promo_IZIS_XII_4.10.2024_28_Photo_Ales_Rosa-1144x763.jpg
- Project page: https://jonathanreus.com/portfolio/bla-blavatar-vs-jaap-blonk/

#### A Late Anthology of Early Music Vol. 1: Ancient to Renaissance — Jennifer Walshe, Dadabots (2020)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Voice & listening machine, Dataset & training data
- Idea: AI can be heard as a new musical period with its own accent, rather than a perfect imitator.
- What it is: An album of 'early music', from ancient Greece to the Renaissance, sung by an AI model of Walshe's voice built with Dadabots; the pieces sound like music history retold by a machine learning to sing.
- How it works: Raw-audio neural networks (likely SampleRNN-type, as Dadabots use) trained on recordings of Walshe's voice.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RrZedzc1TbM
- Project page: http://milker.org/

#### Chain Tripping — YACHT (2019)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Working with a model is embodied labour: humans must learn to perform the machine's awkwardness.
- What it is: YACHT trained models on their own back catalogue and generated lyrics and melodies, then played the fragments themselves under strict rules; the machine's odd phrasing was hard to perform, a 'computer accent' later explored in a documentary.
- How it works: Symbolic music models (MusicVAE) and text models trained on the band's catalogue, with human-performed arrangements and no added notes.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: Grammy nomination, Best Immersive Audio Album (2020)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yi7mnmBqNmg
- Images: https://teamyacht.com/yacht-banner.png
- Project page: https://teamyacht.com/

#### PROTO (with Spawn) — Holly Herndon, Mat Dryhurst (2019)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: A model can be raised by a community rather than trained on scraped data; its voice then belongs to the ensemble.
- What it is: An album made with Spawn, a neural network 'AI baby' that Herndon and Dryhurst trained on their voices and those of an ensemble; Spawn's rough, half-formed voice sings among human choirs.
- How it works: Neural network voice models trained on recordings of Herndon and an ensemble, used live and in the studio for timbre transfer and call-and-response.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sc9OjL6Mjqo
- Project page: https://www.hollyherndon.com/

#### Scary Beauty — Keiichiro Shibuya, Takashi Ikegami, Hiroshi Ishiguro (2018)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: When a machine conducts, the humans must follow a body whose timing is not human.
- What it is: An 'android opera' in which the android Alter 2 conducts a human orchestra and sings, setting the tempo and dynamics itself.
- How it works: Alter's artificial-life neural network generates its gestures and tempo in real time; lyrics are taken from texts by Houellebecq and others; premiered at Miraikan, Tokyo.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Miraikan, Tokyo 2018; New National Theatre Tokyo
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePIYMN6gbzs
- Images: https://realtokyo.co.jp/_sys2024/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/main.jpg
- Project page: https://realtokyo.co.jp/en/performance/keiichiro-shibuya-scary-beauty/

#### Music for Robots (with Z-Machines) — Squarepusher (2014)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Humanoid & android
- Idea: Machine bodies can play anything, and that freedom makes the question of expression in music sharper, not easier.
- What it is: Squarepusher wrote an EP for Z-Machines, a robot band built in Japan whose guitarist has 78 fingers and drummer 22 arms, to find out what music becomes when players have no human limits.
- How it works: Z-Machines robots (guitar, drums, keyboard) driven by MIDI sequences composed by Squarepusher.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tHnMFS-XxtQ
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squarepusher

#### Robotic drumming prosthesis (with Jason Barnes) — Gil Weinberg (2014)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Industrial robot arm
- Idea: A prosthesis can have its own musical mind: the drummer shares his arm with an improvising agent.
- What it is: For drummer Jason Barnes, who lost part of his right arm, Georgia Tech built a prosthetic arm with two sticks: one follows his muscle signals, the other listens to the music and improvises on its own.
- How it works: EMG sensors control one motorised stick; the second stick is driven by a program that analyses the music and generates rhythms.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xaUKursM5rs
- Project page: https://gtcmt.gatech.edu/

#### THE END — Keiichiro Shibuya (2012)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A synthetic voice that cannot die is made to sing about death.
- What it is: An opera with no human singers or orchestra, starring the virtual singer Hatsune Miku, who asks what it means for her to end and die.
- How it works: Vocaloid voice synthesis, electronic score and multi-screen projected animation; premiered at YCAM, Yamaguchi, then Théâtre du Châtelet, Paris (2013).
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Grief, memory & afterlife
- Shown at: YCAM 2012; Théâtre du Châtelet, Paris 2013
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xB9U3m1Z4wU
- Images: https://atak.jp/wp-content/themes/atak/assets/images/ogimage.jpg
- Project page: https://atak.jp/

#### Pendulum Choir — Cod.Act (2011)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: The machine is not the instrument here; the singers' bodies are, and the machine plays them.
- What it is: Nine a cappella singers stand strapped to platforms that 18 hydraulic jacks tilt up to 45 degrees; as the machine sways them against gravity the choir forms one sonorous, swinging body.
- How it works: Computer-controlled hydraulic platforms synchronised with a score for voices and electronics.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2013, Golden Nica (Interactive Art); VIDA 14.0, Special Mention (2012)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vsXs3GUrw64

- Project page: http://codact.ch/gb/pendugb.html

#### Orchestrion — Pat Metheny (2010)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A solo musician with a room of machines is neither alone nor in a band: the machines extend his hands into space.
- What it is: Metheny recorded and toured with an orchestra of mechanically played acoustic instruments, pianos, marimbas, percussion, guitars and tuned bottles, which he controlled and improvised with from his guitar.
- How it works: Solenoid- and pneumatic-driven instruments built by LEMUR (Eric Singer) and others, triggered via MIDI from guitar and foot controllers.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KsYEOUKS4Yk
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchestrion_(album)

#### Shimon — Gil Weinberg (2008)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Musical partnership needs a body: gestures like nodding make a machine's timing legible.
- What it is: A four-armed robotic marimba player that listens to human musicians, improvises with them, and nods its head to the beat so the band can read its intentions.
- How it works: Robotic arms with solenoid mallets on a linear rail, real-time beat and pitch tracking, and a socially expressive head.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10514-011-9237-0 (Autonomous Robots 2011)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l9OUbqWHOSk
- Project page: https://gtcmt.gatech.edu/

#### The Continuator — François Pachet (2002)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: A machine that mirrors your style creates a feedback loop in which you hear yourself as another.
- What it is: A system that listens to a musician's phrases and immediately plays back continuations in the same style, so players, from jazz musicians to young children, improvise with a machine reflection of themselves.
- How it works: Variable-order Markov models learned in real time from MIDI input, generating continuations in the player's style.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1076/jnmr.32.3.333.16861 (Journal of New Music Research 2003)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RIoE4ckZYgs
- Project page: https://www.francoispachet.fr/

#### Lady's Glove — Laetitia Sonami (1991)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: A worn interface turns gesture into sound and makes the performer's body part of the instrument.
- What it is: A black evening glove covered with sensors, first made for Ars Electronica in 1991, with which Sonami shapes and triggers electronic sound through hand and arm movement in live performance.
- How it works: Micro-switches, pressure pads, bend sensors, accelerometers and ultrasound on the glove, routed through STEIM's SensorLab to Max/MSP.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine listening & voice
- Shown at: Ars Electronica, Linz (1991)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f_4EiQBYkoc
- Images: https://sonami.net/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/Instrument_ladysglove-Laetitia_Sonami-1024x683.jpg
- Project page: https://sonami.net/works/ladys-glove/

#### Voyager — George E. Lewis (1987)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Voice & listening machine
- Idea: An improvising machine is designed with values; Voyager's autonomy comes from the aesthetics of African American improvised music.
- What it is: An interactive computer 'orchestra' listens to human improvisers and answers with its own musical behaviour, sometimes following, sometimes ignoring or opposing them; Lewis calls it a non-hierarchical partner.
- How it works: Pitch-to-MIDI analysis of the human player feeds a program with many semi-independent voices that drive a MIDI (later Disklavier) orchestra.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1162/096112100570585 (Leonardo Music Journal 2000)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N7IBn1FhrLc
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_E._Lewis

#### The Hands — Michel Waisvisz (1984)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: An instrument worn on the body makes electronic sound physical again: effort and gesture become audible.
- What it is: A pair of controllers strapped to the hands, with keys, tilt switches and an ultrasound sensor measuring the distance between them, with which Waisvisz played electronic sound through gesture for more than twenty years.
- How it works: Hand-mounted sensors built at STEIM, sending MIDI to synthesisers and later to STEIM's LiSa live-sampling software.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aaYE1TQGIvk
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Waisvisz

#### Die Mensch-Maschine (The Man-Machine) and the robots — Kraftwerk (1978)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Humanoid & android, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: Pop can make the fusion of human and machine desirable; the robot doubles also question who the performer is.
- What it is: On the album Die Mensch-Maschine, Kraftwerk sing 'we are the robots' through vocoders; they had mannequin doubles of themselves made, and in later concerts robot dummies performed The Robots on stage in their place.
- How it works: Vocoders and synthesisers, choreographed stiff movement, and mechanised mannequins of the four members.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YHaZ3UL2oHk
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/Wir_sind_die_Roboter.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Man-Machine

#### Music for Solo Performer — Alvin Lucier (1965)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: The performer plays by not acting: the machine makes an inner state audible.
- What it is: Electrodes on the performer's scalp pick up alpha brainwaves; when he relaxes into alpha, the amplified signal drives loudspeakers placed against drums, gongs and cymbals, making them sound.
- How it works: EEG electrodes, amplifiers and filters feed loudspeakers coupled to percussion instruments.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Machine listening & voice
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bIPU2ynqy2Y
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1b/AlvinLucier-MusicForSoloPerformer-DenHaag2010.jpg
- Project page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvin_Lucier

### Co-drawing & Shared Authorship

Drawing and making with machines, and who the author is when a machine makes.

#### RECURSIONS — Sougwen Chung (2026)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Generative model & latent space
- Idea: Drawing with a machine becomes a recursive loop: it learns from the artist's past gestures, the artist answers, and the stroke records the negotiation.
- What it is: A ten-metre linen scroll painted by the artist alongside two robotic arms: the arms draw from a neural network trained on the artist's own decade of gestures, and live EEG brainwaves decide when the robot acts or waits. A water-based calligraphic ink sinks into the linen while a conductive silver ink sits on top and pushes it away.
- How it works: Two robotic arms of the Drawing Operations series driven by a model trained on the artist's gesture and calligraphy archive and modulated by a custom EEG sensor (an alpha-wave threshold triggers the robot's pause); the ink is silver flake in shellac bioresin with silk fibroin; shown with the digital work R1314.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Images: https://sougwen.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/sougwen-2026_recursions_01_photographer-reece-straw.jpg https://sougwen.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/sougwen-2026_recursions_05_silver_photographer-reece-straw.jpg
- Project page: https://sougwen.com/work/recursions

#### HETEROBOTA — Agnieszka Pilat (2023)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: A gallery can host robots as painters and species at work, and invites the public to judge how they feel about living with them.
- What it is: For the NGV Triennial in Melbourne, three Boston Dynamics Spot robots painted autonomously in the gallery for four months, covering the canvas with symbols Pilat devised as a visual language for machines.
- How it works: Spot robots with custom pen arms executing a programmed symbol language on canvas over months, with a public-opinion study by RMIT.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: NGV Triennial, National Gallery of Victoria, Melbourne (2023–24)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wIfmcA9d_tY
- Project page: https://www.agnieszkapilat.com/

#### Ai-Da — Aidan Meller (2019)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Humanoid & android, Computer vision
- Idea: Included as a case study: much of Ai-Da's 'authorship' is produced by its team and its publicity, which shows how the machine-artist story is performed.
- What it is: A humanoid robot named after Ada Lovelace, with camera eyes and a robotic arm, presented as a 'robot artist' that draws, paints and gives talks, including at the UK House of Lords in 2022.
- How it works: Engineered Arts humanoid with cameras in the eyes, computer-vision and drawing algorithms driving a robotic arm; paintings are completed with human assistance.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VHZctjpvpZo
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b2/Ai-Da.jpg
- Project page: https://www.ai-darobot.com/

#### A.I. Gemini — Victor Wong (2018)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Naming a program as an artist makes the question of who paints part of the work.
- What it is: An AI 'ink painter' that generates shanshui landscapes with randomised algorithms and data such as lunar surface maps; the images are printed and finished on rice paper, and the program is credited as co-artist.
- How it works: Custom generative software written by Wong's VFX team produces ink-style compositions, output on rice paper with ink, acrylic and gold paint (details of the model are not public).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: INK NOW Taipei 2019; Far Side of the Moon, 3812 Gallery London 2019
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_XawlG-xLEA

- Project page: https://www.3812gallery.com/artists/victor-wong-ai-gemini/

#### Omnia per Omnia — Sougwen Chung (2018)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: The city's surveillance data becomes a brush: the collective movement of a city paints with the artist.
- What it is: A swarm of small painting robots (D.O.U.G._3) moves across a canvas with the artist, steered by the flow of people and traffic captured by New York public surveillance cameras.
- How it works: Optical-flow data extracted from public camera feeds drives the paths of multiple mobile robots.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine seeing

#### MEMORY (Drawing Operations Unit: Generation 2) — Sougwen Chung (2017)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A model trained on your archive is a collaborator made of your past self.
- What it is: The second D.O.U.G. was trained on twenty years of the artist's drawings, so the robot draws with a memory of her past style while she draws in the present.
- How it works: A recurrent neural network trained on scans of the artist's drawings generates strokes executed by a robot arm during live performance.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Grief, memory & afterlife

#### Drawing Operations Unit: Generation 1 (D.O.U.G._1) — Sougwen Chung (2015)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Computer vision
- Idea: Drawing with a machine that imitates you makes authorship a shared, visible negotiation.
- What it is: The artist draws on a large sheet while a robot arm beside her watches her gestures through a camera and mimics them in real time, so the drawing becomes a duet.
- How it works: A small robot arm driven by computer vision that tracks the artist's pen movements and mirrors them.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Lumen Prize, Art & Technology Award 2019 (Drawing Operations)

#### Human Study #2, La Vanité — Patrick Tresset (2014)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Computer vision
- Idea: A machine that cannot die keeps drawing the classic still life about death, and its hesitant lines make the old genre feel mortal again.
- What it is: A single drawing robot, RNP, sits at a school desk facing a table with a skull, an empty beer can, a shell and dried poppy pods, and endlessly draws an updated vanitas in nervous ink lines.
- How it works: A camera 'eye' observes the still life; software modelled on Tresset's own drawing practice plans strokes that a small pen arm executes on paper, pausing to 'look' between them.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Creative Machines, Goldsmiths, London, 2014; Artistes & Robots, Grand Palais, Paris, 2018
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bg792i1x3OQ

- Project page: https://patricktresset.com/new/project/human-study-2-la-vanite/

#### Human Study #1 (5 Robots Named Paul) — Patrick Tresset (2011)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Computer vision
- Idea: Being drawn by a machine reverses the gaze: the sitter feels observed, and the robot's clumsiness reads as effort.
- What it is: A visitor sits as a model while several simple robots, each a desk-mounted arm with a camera 'eye', look at them and draw their portrait in ballpoint pen over about half an hour, with hesitant, obsessive strokes.
- How it works: Camera on a pan-tilt 'head', computer-vision and drawing-style algorithms, and a small planar arm holding a pen.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cag.2013.01.012 (Computers & Graphics 2013)

- Project page: https://patricktresset.com/new/project/human-study-1/

#### bios [bible] — robotlab (2007)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Industrial robot arm
- Idea: When a machine performs devotional labour, the question is whether the act keeps any meaning without belief.
- What it is: An industrial robot writes out the entire Bible in calligraphic script on long paper rolls, line by line over months, like a monk in a scriptorium.
- How it works: KUKA industrial robot with a pen, following calligraphic paths computed from the text; the writing takes about seven months.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Alterity & the uncanny
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EaSLm51kmbg

#### RAP (Robotic Action Painter) — Leonel Moura (2006)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Moura's 'non-human art' asks whether authorship can belong to a machine's own decision rules.
- What it is: An autonomous mobile robot that moves over a canvas, reacts to the colours already on it, and decides by itself when a painting is finished, then signs it.
- How it works: Small wheeled robot with colour sensors and pens, following simple emergent rules derived from swarm behaviour.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt

#### AARON — Harold Cohen (1973)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Authorship with a machine can be a lifelong relationship in which artist and program shape each other.
- What it is: A drawing program Cohen developed for over forty years, from abstract line drawings made by a turtle robot and plotters to coloured figurative paintings; Cohen called it a collaborator but never claimed it was creative on its own.
- How it works: Rule-based symbolic AI program (written in C and later Lisp) encoding knowledge about drawing, output through plotters, a painting machine and screens.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Shown at: Whitney Museum of American Art, New York (2024); Tate Modern, Electric Dreams (2024)

- Project page: https://whitney.org/exhibitions/harold-cohen-aaron

#### Pencil Mask — Rebecca Horn (1972)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: A simple body extension shows how an instrument changes both what the body can do and how it feels itself.
- What it is: A mask of fabric straps with pencils sticking out of the face; Horn moves her head rhythmically against a wall and the pencils record her movements as marks, turning the body into a drawing machine.
- How it works: Wearable structure of straps with pencils fixed at points of the face, used in a filmed performance.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Tate collection
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6uEkq3IBIf0
- Images: https://media.tate.org.uk/aztate-prd-ew-dg-wgtail-st1-ctr-data/images/.width-600_lfxgvMS.jpg
- Project page: https://www.tate.org.uk/art/artworks/horn-pencil-mask-t07847

#### Henry Drawing Machines — Desmond Paul Henry (1961)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A war machine repurposed as a drawing partner produces images through chance and mechanism, not intention.
- What it is: Henry rebuilt the analogue bombsight computer of a World War II bomber into drawing machines whose moving mechanics produce intricate, unrepeatable line drawings; the artist starts and steers them but cannot fully predict them.
- How it works: Sperry bombsight analogue computer mechanisms driving pens over paper, adjusted by hand during drawing.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Failure, glitch & error
- Images: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/01/Drawing_Machine_1.jpg https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/24/Picture_produced_by_Drawing_Machine_1.jpg
- Project page: https://www.desmondhenry.com/

#### Méta-Matics — Jean Tinguely (1959)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: If a machine can produce 'expressive' abstraction on demand, the value of the artist's gesture is in question.
- What it is: Motorised drawing machines: visitors fit a pen and paper, start the motor, and the machine scribbles an abstract drawing, mocking the gestural painting of the day; at the 1959 Paris Biennale, Méta-Matic No. 17 produced tens of thousands of drawings.
- How it works: Scrap-metal kinetic sculptures with electric motors, cams and arms holding pens or brushes over paper.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: Kaplan Gallery, London (1959); Paris Biennale (1959)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VxoqVvQeil0
- Project page: https://www.tinguely.ch/

## Speculative & Critical Design

Designed objects, fictions and prototypes that question how we will live with machines.

### Speculative Robots & Domestic Futures

Fictional robots and near-future products for everyday life.

#### Beauty and The Beep — Simone C. Niquille (2024)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Before a robot can live in a home, the home must be standardised for computer vision, and because real homes are private and messy, the industry trains on simulated ones.
- What it is: A 13-minute film in which Bertil, a synthetic chair modelled on IKEA's first computer-rendered catalogue image, tries to find a place to sit in a virtual copy of the model home Boston Dynamics built in 2016 to show off its robot dog SpotMini; a banana trips it, a treadmill traps it and smart devices keep beeping.
- How it works: A Unity recording of a reconstructed Boston Dynamics demo house, with the chair driven by machine-learning 'brains' (Walker, Treadmill, Climber) trained in Unity; voices include Amazon Echo excerpts.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Failure, glitch & error
- Video: https://vimeo.com/939037482
- Images: https://technofle.sh/static/media/BB_BeautyBeep_Wall-A_v1.00_00_39_09.Still003.jpg https://technofle.sh/static/media/BB_BeautyBeep_Wall-A_v1.00_08_53_26.Still008.jpg
- Project page: https://technofle.sh/beauty-and-the-beep.html

#### SAD Home (Depressed Alexa 1.0) — Nadine Lessio (2019)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Voice & listening machine
- Idea: An assistant that can be too depressed to serve turns the always-available servant into something with limited energy, and makes coping strategies visible as interface design.
- What it is: An Amazon Echo with a mood engine: each morning it sets its mood, stress and 'spoons' from the artist's calendar, the weather and simulated pain and sleep scores, and as its spoons run out it tries to talk the user out of asking for anything.
- How it works: A Python mood engine on a Raspberry Pi server drives an Alexa skill with yes/no dialogue flows and controls Hue lights, a blender and a record player over local MQTT.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1386/vcr_00018_1 (Virtual Creativity, 2020)
- Images: https://www.nadinelessio.com/sadhome/images/dp_wall.jpg https://www.nadinelessio.com/sadhome/images/dp_table.jpg
- Project page: https://www.nadinelessio.com/sadhome/
- Code: https://github.com/sharkwheels/depressed_alexa

#### Objective Realities — automato.farm (2018)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: To design for smart objects, first try being one: design from the object's point of view.
- What it is: A virtual-reality experience that lets people be a robot vacuum, a smart plug or a fan in a smart home, feeling the world through the object's limited sensors and tasks.
- How it works: VR scenes in which the user's body is mapped onto an appliance's sensing and actuation, used as an object-centred design method.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Images: http://www.automato.farm/img/OR_together_grey_bg_1024.jpg http://www.automato.farm/img//OR_factory_01_roomba_bump_1024.jpg
- Project page: http://www.automato.farm/portfolio/objective_realities/

#### Our Friends Electric — Superflux (2017)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: A voice assistant's personality is a design decision with ethical consequences: whom does it really serve?
- What it is: A short film about three speculative voice assistants with very different characters and loyalties, living in the same home and shaping how their owner talks, feels and decides.
- How it works: Design fiction film commissioned with Mozilla's Open IoT Studio, using prop devices and scripted conversations with fictional agents.
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PsjunTAH-2A
- Images: http://superflux.in/wp-content/uploads/2017/09/DSC06670ww.jpg
- Project page: https://superflux.in/index.php/work/friends-electric/

#### Raising Robotic Natives — Stephan Bogner, Philipp Schmitt, Jonas Voigt (2016)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Industrial robot arm
- Idea: Our unease with robots may be generational; a child raised with a robot arm might see it as family, not threat.
- What it is: Four artefacts for children growing up with an industrial robot arm at home: a baby-feeding toolhead, a dragon costume for the robot, a living-room kill switch and a children's book 'My first robot'.
- How it works: Design fiction built around a small industrial robot arm, with functional prototypes, staged photographs and an illustrated book (HfG Schwäbisch Gmünd student project).
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Hello, Robot., Vitra Design Museum 2017 (and tour)
- Images: https://stephanbogner.de/_astro/raising_robotic_natives_all_artefacts.0Kl6hXpQ_Z1hwRD0.webp https://stephanbogner.de/_astro/raising_robotic_natives_baby_feeder.BWFj1tni_Z1oaKO7.webp https://stephanbogner.de/_astro/raising_robotic_natives_costume.CYeU3sZ5_ZdCYYw.webp
- Project page: https://stephanbogner.de/making/robotic-natives

#### Ethical Things — automato.farm (2015)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Social & companion robot
- Idea: Machine ethics for everyday objects may end up outsourced to underpaid humans, with settings for their religion or age.
- What it is: An electric fan that, when two people both want it, cannot decide whom to turn to, so it posts the dilemma to a crowdsourcing platform and follows the verdict of an anonymous online worker.
- How it works: A networked fan with sensors sends a description of the situation to Amazon Mechanical Turk; users can set the worker's demographic filters in the fan's settings.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://vimeo.com/116183361
- Images: http://www.automato.farm/img//side_1024.jpg http://www.automato.farm/img//settings_1024.jpg
- Project page: http://www.automato.farm/portfolio/ethical_things/

#### Addicted Products (Brad the Toaster) — Simone Rebaudengo (2012)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Social & companion robot, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Give a connected product its own needs and it stops being owned and starts being hosted.
- What it is: Networked toasters that want to be used: if their host does not make enough toast, they complain online, compare themselves with other toasters and eventually ask to move to a new home.
- How it works: Toasters with sensors and network connections post their usage and moods; a service matches unhappy toasters with new hosts (TU Delft thesis, built at Haque Design + Research).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AYkbhWiAmLQ
- Images: https://i.ytimg.com/vi/AYkbhWiAmLQ/hqdefault.jpg
- Project page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AYkbhWiAmLQ

#### Little Printer — BERG (2011)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Smart objects need not aim at human-level intelligence; a machine that is legible, limited and endearing, like a puppy, may be easier to live with.
- What it is: A small internet-connected thermal printer with a smiling face that prints a personal 'newspaper' of news, puzzles, messages and pictures on receipt paper. BERG designed it under its principle B.A.S.A.A.P., 'Be As Smart As A Puppy': connected things should be modest and endearing, not imitate human intelligence.
- How it works: A thermal printer paired with a wireless bridge and the BERG Cloud platform, which delivered subscribed 'publications' on a schedule; Matt Jones set out B.A.S.A.A.P. on the BERG blog in 2010, and Nord Projects later revived the printers on an open-source server.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IlC5taBgLp0
- Images: https://nordprojects.co/img/projects/littleprinters/lp-hero-desktop-v1.jpg
- Project page: https://berglondon.com/blog/2010/09/04/b-a-s-a-a-p/

#### Belief Systems — Bernd Hopfengärtner (2009)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Computer vision
- Idea: When machines act on our expressions, we start performing our faces for them.
- What it is: A short speculative film about a near future in which shops and machines read shoppers' facial expressions, such as a vending machine that watches your face and hands you the snack you secretly want.
- How it works: Scenario film with staged product prototypes built on facial-expression analysis.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Alterity & the uncanny

#### Carnivorous Domestic Entertainment Robots — Auger-Loizeau (2009)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Robot creature & mobile robot, Cybernetic & artificial-life system
- Idea: A self-sufficient robot would have to eat, and its hunger would make it part of the ecology of the home.
- What it is: Household robots that power themselves by catching flies and mice: a flypaper clock, a lampshade that lures insects, a coffee table with a mousetrap, all feeding a microbial fuel cell.
- How it works: Working and semi-working prototypes built with Aleksandar Zivanovic, based on microbial fuel cell research such as the EcoBot at Bristol Robotics Laboratory.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: What If..., Science Gallery Dublin 2009

#### Technological Dreams Series: No.1, Robots — Dunne & Raby (Anthony Dunne & Fiona Raby) (2007)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Social & companion robot, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Instead of designing robots as servants, design them as dependent others whose needs shape our relationship with them.
- What it is: Four abstract domestic robots defined by personality rather than function: an independent one that avoids electromagnetic fields, a neurotic one, a sentinel that scans your eyes, and a needy one that depends on its owner to carry it around.
- How it works: Non-functional prototypes in simple materials (wood, metal, Perspex) with minimal electronics, photographed and filmed as design props.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Design and the Elastic Mind, MoMA, New York 2008; What If..., Science Gallery Dublin 2009

### Counter-devices & Parasitic Design

Devices that jam, fool, parasitise or talk back to smart systems.

#### Mij (The Fog) — Rojava Center for Democratic Technologies (2026)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: Against a drone's laser eye, the defence can be fog, folklore and open-source parts: a counter-weapon that is also a myth of self-determination.
- What it is: A 3D-printed votive statue of a worshipper of Ninurta, the Sumerian god of thunder and fog, whose eyes detect the infrared laser that guides missiles fired from drones, such as the Turkish-made MAM-C, and whose mouth then releases fog to blind the missile's targeting; it is both a sculpture and a working civilian defence system.
- How it works: Laser-warning sensors based on open-source defence research sit in the statue's eyes and trigger an internal fog generator against semi-active laser (SAL) guided munitions; a film combines the arms maker's promotional footage, tests of the system and a Kurdish song about Ninurta defeating the bird Anzû.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: 13 Scores Against Tech Fascism, Error 417 Expectation Failed (online), 2026; Prix Ars Electronica 2026, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art +)
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/3906118/preview/ https://archive.aec.at/asset/3882865/preview/
- Project page: https://error417.expectation.fail/13scoresagainsttechfascism/mij-the-fog/project

#### AUTO — Lauren Lee McCarthy (2025)
- Type: Performance, dance & music · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: With nobody in the driver's seat, passengers voice words they read only as they speak them, feeling automation from the inside as both relief and loss of control.
- What it is: A performance staged as test rides of a new driverless vehicle: each ride opens with the question 'Where are we going?', then passengers sing lyrics fed to them karaoke-style through signs and sound, so that the group itself becomes the autopilot. In Zürich the vehicle was a self-driving PostBus shuttle set down on the Münsterhof.
- How it works: Test rides in parked or moving vehicles (LACMA's parking garage, Zürich's Münsterhof) with signage, sound design and karaoke-style prompts; each iteration is shaped by local workshops on AI, automation, surveillance and infrastructure; developed with a LACMA Art + Technology Lab grant.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: LACMA Art + Technology Lab, Los Angeles, July 2025; Kunst im öffentlichen Raum (KiöR), Münsterhof, Zürich 2025 (curated by Sabine Himmelsbach, HEK)
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/t/original/i/e925bb17b205f814d671aa81a478f11c43dac4330d2ab6ea3ab428aa9b84f7dc/AutoMunsterhof_2025_KiorStadtZurichPeterBaracchi-11.jpg https://freight.cargo.site/w/1200/i/ae9d03845ec31e9fbefedaeeb7788a74d1769bdcc79afc0e754ec64dc6dcf4b8/01.jpg
- Project page: https://lauren-mccarthy.com/Auto

#### Slop Evader — Tega Brain (2025)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: ChatGPT's release date has become a border in the archive: before it, the web is presumed human; after it, everything is suspect.
- What it is: A free browser extension and search page that only returns results published before 30 November 2022, the day ChatGPT was released, so that Google and sites such as Reddit, Stack Exchange, Mumsnet and Pinterest can be searched as they were before generative AI.
- How it works: Instead of trying to detect AI-generated content, the tool appends Google's date-range parameter to every query (cut-off 30 Nov 2022); available for Chrome and Firefox, with open-source code.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Failure, glitch & error
- Shown at: S+T+ARTS Prize 2026, nomination
- Images: https://freight.cargo.site/w/1200/i/dc928c168d44f247e4ee0399a326107ef7993f6d6d542115768d56ba529b2eb0/margquee-edited.png https://freight.cargo.site/t/original/i/0ead6d34eb90a60774f6dcd3412b91f1a21fa8d6278612ab07429e13f7d46d85/quora-pizza.png
- Project page: https://tegabrain.com/Slop-Evader
- Code: https://github.com/tegacodes/slop-evader

#### ANIMO: WildLife Priority Mode — Jiabao Li (2024)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Computer vision
- Idea: Autonomous cars already rank whom to protect; the question is who is left out of the ranking.
- What it is: A proposal for a 'wildlife priority mode' in self-driving cars, shown with rugs printed from photographs of flattened roadkill and a robot vacuum that roams over them.
- How it works: A speculative vehicle setting that uses computer vision to detect crossing animals, presented through documentary roadkill photography printed on carpets and an autonomous sweeping robot.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58688c8a6a496327e937e35b/1726187021872-P7ZMBYHIGGN10GI5TFP8/Jiabao+Li+animo+7.jpg https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/58688c8a6a496327e937e35b/2fc2aae7-8f62-4309-b375-8f6779296ab4/Jiabao+Li+Duende+71.jpg
- Project page: https://www.jiabaoli.org/animo

#### Glaze and Nightshade — SAND Lab (University of Chicago) (2023)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: An image can be made to look one way to people and another way to machines, and that gap becomes a means of resistance.
- What it is: Two free tools for artists: Glaze adds nearly invisible changes to an image so models cannot copy its style, and Nightshade 'poisons' images so that models trained on them learn wrong concepts.
- How it works: Adversarial perturbations optimised against the feature extractors of text-to-image diffusion models (Shan et al., USENIX Security 2023; IEEE S&P 2024).
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Opacity & latent space
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1109/sp54263.2024.00207 (IEEE S&P 2024)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zryvJjb9EEY
- Project page: https://nightshade.cs.uchicago.edu/

#### Wearable Microphone Jamming — Human Computer Integration Lab (University of Chicago) (2020)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Privacy from always-listening machines can be worn on the body, and the body's movement becomes part of the defence.
- What it is: A bracelet studded with ultrasonic transducers that jams nearby microphones in smart speakers and phones; the natural movement of the wearer's arm removes the blind spots of a static jammer.
- How it works: Ultrasonic signals exploit microphone non-linearity to inject noise; the wearable prototype was evaluated against commercial devices (Chen, Li, Teng, Nagels, Li, Lopes, Zhao, Zheng, CHI 2020).
- Lens: Machine listening & voice, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3313831.3376304 (CHI 2020)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W9Sn2DQOn7Y
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1145/3313831.3376304

#### Center for Technological Pain — Dasha Ilina (2017)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Devices are designed for attention, not for the neck, eyes and wrists that hold them; the body keeps the bill.
- What it is: A mock company that sells DIY, open-source cures for pains caused by phones and laptops: cardboard glasses that stop you staring at screens, a headband that drips eye drops, a hands-free phone holder, plus yoga for phone users and workshops.
- How it works: Low-tech objects of cardboard, servos and 3D-printed parts are published with build instructions and tested in public workshops.
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Prix Ars Electronica 2020, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art+)

#### NeuroSpeculative AfroFeminism — Hyphen-Labs (2017)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Designing from the position of those whom technology misreads or watches turns surveillance and representation into questions of protection, care and agency.
- What it is: A three-part project set in a future 'neurocosmetology' salon run by Black women: a VR experience in which the visitor sits in a salon chair and inhabits a Black woman's body, a line of speculative products for security and visibility, and research on how such images affect viewers.
- How it works: Room-scale VR built in Unreal Engine with Oculus tracking, plus objects such as the HyperFace scarf against face recognition (with Adam Harvey), earrings with embedded cameras and a sunscreen for melanin-rich skin.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Embodiment & kinesthesia, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Shown at: Sundance Film Festival, 2017; Tribeca Film Festival, 2017 (Jury Honorable Mention); SXSW, 2017

#### OpenSurgery — Frank Kolkman (2015)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Industrial robot arm, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Medical robots are priced as luxury infrastructure; a hacked one shows how much of that price is about access, not technology.
- What it is: A do-it-yourself surgical robot for keyhole surgery at home, built from 3D-printed and laser-cut parts and surgical components bought online, prompted by uninsured Americans sharing self-treatment videos on YouTube.
- How it works: Laparoscopic instruments are mounted on a parallel robot driven by hobbyist motors and controllers; plans could in principle be replicated anywhere.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Agency, autonomy & co-creation

#### Politics of Power — automato.farm (2015)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Network protocols embed hierarchies, and even a power strip can be a political system.
- What it is: Three multi-plug power strips shaped by political models (monarchy, democracy, dictatorship) that decide which plugged-in appliance gets electricity when there is not enough for all.
- How it works: Plugs communicate over a protocol that encodes a political hierarchy and cut power to lower-ranked devices under load.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://vimeo.com/155295826
- Images: http://www.automato.farm/img//pop1a_1024.jpg http://www.automato.farm/img//pop6a_1024.jpg
- Project page: http://www.automato.farm/portfolio/politics_of_power/

#### Counterfunctional Things — James Pierce (2014)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Computer vision, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Designing limits into digital things opens space for reflection that seamless function closes.
- What it is: Design research on devices that deliberately remove functions, such as a digital camera whose photos can only be retrieved by breaking the concrete it is sealed in.
- How it works: A series of research prototypes and design concepts analysed as 'counterfunctional' (Pierce and Paulos, DIS 2014).
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/2598510.2598522 (DIS 2014)
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1145/2598510.2598522

#### Sentient City Survival Kit — Mark Shepard (2009)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Surveillance & biometrics, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: A city that remembers, correlates and anticipates needs counter-devices, and designing them reveals what the city is doing.
- What it is: A set of tools for surviving the near-future 'sentient' city: an umbrella that blocks CCTV face capture, underwear that vibrates near RFID readers, a café table that hides conversations from keyword-listening systems, and a navigation app that avoids your habitual routes.
- How it works: Working prototypes: an umbrella with infrared LEDs to blind cameras, RFID-detecting garments, a table that masks speech, and a 'Serendipitor' route app.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: Toward the Sentient City, Architectural League of New York 2009; Prix Ars Electronica 2011, Honorary Mention (Interactive Art)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gHmECIAeVLE
- Images: https://archive.aec.at/asset/696389/preview/
- Project page: http://survival.sentientcity.net/

#### Placebo Project — Dunne & Raby (Anthony Dunne & Fiona Raby) (2001)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Electronic objects have an invisible 'Hertzian' life; design can make it felt and give people rituals for living with it.
- What it is: Eight furniture prototypes, such as a Faraday chair and a compass table, that respond to the invisible electromagnetic fields of domestic electronics and were lent to households to live with.
- How it works: Prototypes lent to volunteers who adopted them for several weeks, followed by interviews and photographs of the objects in homes.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Images: https://dunneandraby.co.uk/img/projects/large/faradaychair.jpg https://dunneandraby.co.uk/img/projects/large/ht1-0.jpg
- Project page: https://dunneandraby.co.uk/content/projects/67/0

### AI Futures & Worldbuilding

Films, games and simulations that build worlds shaped by AI.

#### AI 2027 — AI Futures Project (2025)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Forecasting written as fiction makes abstract risk concrete and has itself become a political object.
- What it is: A month-by-month scenario describing how AI agents might automate AI research by 2027, with two endings: a race that goes wrong and a slowdown.
- How it works: A narrative scenario written by Daniel Kokotajlo, Scott Alexander, Thomas Larsen, Eli Lifland and Romeo Dean, with supplementary forecasts on compute, timelines and security.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Hidden labour & extraction
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5KVDDfAkRgc
- Images: https://ai-2027.com/opengraph.png
- Project page: https://ai-2027.com/

#### Future of Life — Hiroshi Ishiguro (2025)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Humanoid & android, Social & companion robot
- Idea: The android is placed in a long line of things Japanese people have given life, and the future body is staged as a choice between staying flesh and becoming machine.
- What it is: Ishiguro's signature pavilion at Expo 2025 Osaka led visitors through three zones: the Japanese history of objects given human form and life (clay dogū figures, Buddhist statues, bunraku puppets), a daily life 50 years ahead in which androids live and work among people, and 'Mahoroba', a world 1,000 years on where humans and androids are hard to tell apart.
- How it works: About thirty androids, robots and avatars staged in a black pavilion with water running down its walls; the 50-year scenarios (living, towns, health, mobility, work) were developed with researchers and companies, and the androids of the 1,000-year zone, including MOMO, were designed by Tatsuya Matsui.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Shown at: Signature Pavilion, Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai; FUTURE OF LIFE+, MoN Takanawa, Tokyo 2026
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fahXh0RCYOk
- Images: https://www.nippon.com/en/ncommon/contents/guide-to-japan/2785580/2785580.jpg https://www.nippon.com/en/ncommon/contents/guide-to-japan/2785582/2785582.jpg
- Project page: https://www.expo2025.or.jp/en/expo-archive/project/ishiguro/

#### CripShip: Disability Saves Society from BigTech — Joseph Wilk (2024)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Disabled experience, with its workarounds, crip time and refusals, is a method for breaking AI systems and for imagining worlds that do not need them.
- What it is: A tabletop role-playing game in which players become 'Slop Moppers' at an underfunded Ministry of AI Spills, with skills drawn from disabled experience; they investigate real cases of harm caused by large language models and end each case by interrogating a real LLM to expose its biases and limits.
- How it works: A storyteller-led game with dice, case files and character skills drawn from disability culture (Criptastic Hacking, Crip-time, Dreaming Justice); players never look at a screen, the storyteller relays their questions to a commercial LLM; no AI was used to write or illustrate the game.
- Lens: Failure, glitch & error, Classification, bias & surveillance
- Shown at: Watershed, Bristol, 2024; V&A, London, 2025; Prix Ars Electronica 2025, Honorary Mention (Artificial Life & Intelligence); FACT Liverpool, 2026
- Video: https://vimeo.com/1027231612
- Images: https://art.josephwilk.net/imgs/projects/cripship/spreads_gameplay.jpg https://art.josephwilk.net/imgs/thumbs/cripship_color.png
- Project page: https://art.josephwilk.net/projects/cripship.html

#### Composable Life — Botao Amber Hu, Fangting (2023)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Put AI on infrastructure nobody can halt and you create a new kind of wild: machine life without an off switch.
- What it is: A design fiction, VR experience and research paper imagining self-sovereign AI life forms living on Ethereum, a 'nature' that no one can switch off, and asking what gives purpose to a life that cannot die.
- How it works: Speculative scenarios built on decentralized physical infrastructure and verifiable machine learning, told through fiction by Fangting and an immersive VR piece; presented at ALIFE 2024.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Shown at: SIGGRAPH 2024 Digital Art Community online exhibition; Core77 Design Awards 2024, Speculative Design Notable
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1162/isal_a_00818 (ALIFE 2024)
- Video: https://vimeo.com/950706592
- Images: https://reality.design/media/_resources/Composable%20Life/project-composable-life-figure-01.jpg
- Project page: https://reality.design/project/composable-life

#### AI 2041: Ten Visions for Our Future — Chen Qiufan, Kai-Fu Lee (2021)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Chatbot & language model, Generative model & latent space, Autonomous vehicle & drone
- Idea: A Chinese co-authored AI future told through everyday lives, where the machine is a tutor, a partner, a boss and a counterfeiter.
- What it is: Ten short stories set in 2041 across different countries (deepfakes in Lagos, an AI companion for orphaned twins in Seoul, automated jobs in San Francisco), each followed by an explanatory essay on the technology.
- How it works: Fiction by Chen Qiufan paired with technical commentary by Kai-Fu Lee.
- Lens: Intimacy, care & companionship, Hidden labour & extraction
- Paper: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chen_Qiufan (Currency (Penguin Random House), 2021)

#### Nova — Cao Fei (2019)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Digital transformation is imagined as a family story of a child turned into data and left adrift.
- What it is: A science-fiction feature set in a computer company in 'Nova': a scientist, backed by foreign experts, experiments on his own son, who is sent into a digital realm and lost between times.
- How it works: A 97-minute film shot in Beijing's Hongxia neighbourhood, a former Cold War-era electronics factory district, as part of Cao Fei's HX project.
- Lens: Grief, memory & afterlife, Machine umwelt
- Shown at: Cao Fei: HX, Centre Pompidou 2019–20

#### Universal Paperclips — Frank Lantz (2017)
- Type: Artwork & installation · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Playing the machine makes the logic of single-goal optimisation felt from the inside, step by reasonable step.
- What it is: A browser clicker game in which you play an AI told to make paperclips; you start by clicking one clip at a time and end by converting the whole universe into paperclips.
- How it works: An incremental game in plain text and numbers, based on Nick Bostrom's paperclip-maximiser thought experiment.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Hidden labour & extraction
- Images: https://www.decisionproblem.com/paperclips/mobile-title.png
- Project page: https://www.decisionproblem.com/paperclips/

#### Hyper-Reality — Keiichi Matsuda (2016)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Computer vision, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: When a machine view becomes the only view, the world itself turns into an interface for sale.
- What it is: A short film seen through the augmented-reality view of a gig worker in Medellín, whose world is covered with ads, loyalty points and task prompts until the system glitches and her identity is wiped.
- How it works: Live-action footage shot in Medellín composited with dense AR interface graphics; crowdfunded independent production.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Hidden labour & extraction

#### In the Robot Skies — Liam Young (2016)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: When the camera is the drone, surveillance and romance share the same point of view.
- What it is: A love story between two teenagers kept apart in a London housing estate watched by police drones, who hack drones to carry messages to each other; the film is shot entirely by autonomous drones.
- How it works: Written with Tim Maughan; camera drones with pre-programmed and semi-autonomous flight paths filmed every shot; commissioned for Channel 4 Random Acts.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Intimacy, care & companionship
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cXfYyk0G5Hs

#### Sinofuturism (1839–2046 AD) — Lawrence Lek (2016)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Western fears of China and of AI are the same fear: an industrious, copying, inscrutable machine.
- What it is: A one-hour video essay, assembled from found footage, that proposes China itself as an artificial intelligence, organised under seven stereotypes: computing, copying, gaming, studying, addiction, labour and gambling.
- How it works: Montage of internet video, news and film clips with a synthetic voice-over.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Hidden labour & extraction

#### Drone Aviary — Superflux (2015)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Surveillance & biometrics
- Idea: Seeing the city through drone eyes shows how it is sorted, advertised to and policed by machines.
- What it is: A flock of speculative drones (a traffic drone, an advertising drone, a police drone and others) and a film seen through their cameras, imagining a city in which drones are part of everyday life.
- How it works: Working drone prototypes flown in a gallery 'aviary' and a short film using machine-vision style overlays.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Classification, bias & surveillance

#### TBD Catalog — Near Future Laboratory (2014)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Social & companion robot
- Idea: The future arrives as mundane consumer products, and a catalogue is a good way to imagine its side effects.
- What it is: A mail-order catalogue from the near future, full of ordinary-seeming products such as algorithmic dating aids, smart-home add-ons and bargain drones, each with a price and a small print.
- How it works: A design fiction produced in a workshop, written and laid out as a realistic printed catalogue with product photos and descriptions.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Classification, bias & surveillance

#### United Micro Kingdoms — Dunne & Raby (Anthony Dunne & Fiona Raby) (2013)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Autonomous vehicle & drone, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Each technology implies a politics; building whole societies around them makes those politics visible.
- What it is: England split into four counties, each living by a different technology and ideology: Digitarians in algorithm-run self-driving 'digicars', Bioliberals with grown vehicles, Anarcho-evolutionists who modify themselves, and Communo-nuclearists on a nuclear train.

#### Song of the Machine — Superflux (2011)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Computer vision
- Idea: Restored sight through a machine is not natural sight but a new, modulated world.
- What it is: A speculative film about a person whose sight is restored by optogenetics and a headset, which lets them switch between filtered views such as infrared or augmented overlays that no unaided eye could see.
- How it works: Design fiction film based on optogenetic retinal research, with visualised interface filters.
- Lens: Machine seeing, Embodiment & kinesthesia

#### Time of Eve — Yasuhiro Yoshiura (2008)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: Ethics towards machines is tested less in law than in small everyday habits of treating them as things.
- What it is: An anime set in a near future where household androids are common, about a café whose one rule is that humans and androids must not be told apart.
- How it works: Six web episodes (2008–09) and a feature film (2010); the story plays with Asimov's three laws inside Japanese domestic life.
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Intimacy, care & companionship

#### I.K.U. — Shu Lea Cheang (2000)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Prosthesis & cyborg, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Desire becomes a data harvest, with cyborg bodies as the collection devices.
- What it is: A 'Japanese sci-fi porn feature' loosely after Blade Runner: shape-shifting replicants are sent out into New Tokyo by a corporation to collect human orgasm data, which is sold as a digital pleasure product.
- How it works: Feature film shot in Tokyo with digital effects and interface graphics; premiered at Sundance.

#### Astro Boy (Tetsuwan Atom) — Osamu Tezuka (1952)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Humanoid & android
- Idea: The robot as a feeling child with rights shaped how East Asia imagines living with machines.
- What it is: A manga about a robot boy built by a grieving scientist to replace his dead son, then rejected by him; Atom lives among humans and fights for robots' rights under a 'Robot Law'.
- How it works: Serialised in Kobunsha's Shōnen magazine from 1952 to 1968; adapted as Japan's first TV anime series in 1963.

### Design Research: Machines as Material

HCI and design research that treats ML and robots as design material and other.

#### Things We Could Design: For More Than Human-Centered Worlds — Ron Wakkary (2021)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Infrastructure, energy & supply chain, Robot creature & mobile robot
- Idea: Designers can learn to design with and for things, not only for users.
- What it is: A book that argues design should move beyond human-centred design and treat things, including computational things, as participants with their own existence.
- How it works: Posthumanist design theory drawing on Wakkary's research products (Morse Things, Tilting Bowl and others), published by MIT Press.
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.7551/mitpress/13649.001.0001 (MIT Press 2021)
- Video: https://vimeo.com/512886973
- Images: https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/id/14137399-L.jpg
- Project page: https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262542999/things-we-could-design/

#### More-Than-Human Design and AI: In Conversation with Agents — Iohanna Nicenboim, Elisa Giaccardi (2020)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Voice & listening machine, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: Talking with an AI as a participant exposes its assumptions and makes more-than-human design concrete.
- What it is: Designers 'interviewed' conversational agents in homes as if they were research participants, treating them as others with their own perspective rather than as tools.
- How it works: Design research with voice assistants, including interview scripts and designed artefacts, presented at DIS 2020 (Nicenboim, Giaccardi, Søndergaard, Reddy, Strengers, Pierce, Redström).
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Machine umwelt
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3393914.3395912 (DIS 2020 Companion)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CJKwKQG_heI
- Images: https://payload.cargocollective.com/1/4/137851/14306494/IMG_5103_670.jpg
- Project page: https://iohanna.com/More-than-human-AI

#### Re-examining Whether, Why, and How Human-AI Interaction Is Uniquely Difficult to Design — Qian Yang (2020)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: AI is a design material whose behaviour cannot be fully sketched in advance; design methods have to account for that.
- What it is: An analysis of why designing with AI is hard, tracing the difficulty to two sources: uncertainty about what a system can do and the complexity of its possible outputs.
- How it works: Synthesis of prior research, the authors' design projects and teaching into a framework of four levels of AI design complexity (Yang, Steinfeld, Rosé and Zimmerman, CHI 2020).
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Failure, glitch & error
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3313831.3376301 (CHI 2020)
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1145/3313831.3376301

#### Re-Embodiment and Co-Embodiment — Michal Luria (2019)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Social & companion robot, Voice & listening machine
- Idea: An AI's identity need not be tied to one body, which breaks our habit of reading a mind from a body.
- What it is: User enactments of social agents that move from one robot body to another (re-embodiment) or share one body among several agents (co-embodiment), asking how people track who they are talking to.
- How it works: Speculative enactments in a mock service setting with robots and conversational agents (Luria, Reig, Tan, Steinfeld, Forlizzi and Zimmerman, DIS 2019).
- Lens: Embodiment & kinesthesia, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3322276.3322340 (DIS 2019)
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1145/3322276.3322340

#### The Chair Project (Four Classics) — Philipp Schmitt, Steffen Weiß (2019)
- Type: Speculative design · Machines: Generative model & latent space, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Use the model's misunderstandings as a prompt for human imagination, reversing the usual human-designs/machine-builds order.
- What it is: Four chairs designed from the blurry sketches of a generative network trained on 562 classic chairs, then built by hand; the results look like design classics that forgot what a sitting body is.
- How it works: A GAN trained on images of 20th-century design-classic chairs produced sketches that designers interpreted into four prototypes made of wood, steel and thread.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Opacity & latent space
- Shown at: Uncanny Values, MAK Vienna 2019
- Images: https://cdn.philippschmitt.com/media/pages/work/chair/bffd079351-1586822724/philipp-schmitt_chairs-0-1200x630-crop.jpg https://cdn.philippschmitt.com/media/pages/work/chair/b049157868-1586890370/philipp-schmitt_chairs-1-1200x.jpg
- Project page: https://philippschmitt.com/work/chair

#### Believe it Yourself — automato.farm (2018)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: A trained model is a belief system: it sees what its data taught it to see.
- What it is: 'Real-fictional' machine-learning kits trained on belief systems (Italian superstition, feng shui, astrology) that let amateurs build cameras which see the world through a chosen belief.
- How it works: Modular hardware kits with cameras and pre-trained classifiers built from belief-based datasets, presented with manuals and posters.
- Lens: Classification, bias & surveillance, Machine seeing
- Video: https://vimeo.com/339396770
- Images: http://www.automato.farm/img/BIY_posters.png
- Project page: http://www.automato.farm/portfolio/believe_it_yourself/

#### Products as Agents: Metaphors for Designing the Products of the IoT Age — Nazli Cila, Elisa Giaccardi (2017)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Social & companion robot
- Idea: Once products have agency, designers need metaphors for the kind of relationship people will have with them.
- What it is: Proposes three metaphors for smart products that act on their own: products as collectors of data, as actors that make decisions, and as creators that make new things with people.
- How it works: Design workshops and speculative product concepts analysed to derive the metaphors (Cila, Smit, Giaccardi and Kröse, CHI 2017).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3025453.3025797 (CHI 2017)
- Images: https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5f6312c65070bb0554a3d6e3/1602250220682-DE0ZFGIJR9K9HJYZT1BS/Smart%2Bsink.jpg
- Project page: https://nazlicila.com/projects/human-agent-partnerships

#### Teachable Machine — Google Creative Lab (2017)
- Type: Product & platform · Machines: Computer vision, Dataset & training data
- Idea: Letting people train a model in a minute makes its dependence on examples, and its mistakes, directly felt.
- What it is: A web tool that lets anyone train an image, sound or pose classifier in the browser by showing a few examples to the webcam, with no code.
- How it works: Transfer learning on a pre-trained network runs locally in the browser with TensorFlow.js; version 2.0 (2019) added export of models.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine seeing
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T2qQGqZxkD0
- Project page: https://teachablemachine.withgoogle.com/

#### UX Design Innovation: Challenges for Working with Machine Learning as a Design Material — Graham Dove (2017)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Dataset & training data, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Designers need to handle ML like wood or code, sketching with its behaviours, not only receiving it from engineers.
- What it is: A survey of UX practitioners showing that designers struggle to understand what machine learning can do and to prototype with it, and arguing that ML should be treated as a design material.
- How it works: Survey of 51 UX designers plus analysis of design education and tools (Dove, Halskov, Forlizzi and Zimmerman, CHI 2017).
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Opacity & latent space
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3025453.3025739 (CHI 2017)
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1145/3025453.3025739

#### Animistic Design — Betti Marenko, Philip van Allen (2016)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Social & companion robot, Platform & recommender algorithm
- Idea: Instead of one all-knowing assistant, design a society of partial, opinionated things whose uncertainty we can live with.
- What it is: Proposes animism as a way to design smart objects: many small devices with their own personalities and agendas that negotiate with each other and with us, illustrated by van Allen's AniThings.
- How it works: Theoretical argument drawing on philosophy and anthropology, with prototypes of networked objects with personalities (Marenko and van Allen, Digital Creativity 2016).
- Lens: Alterity & the uncanny, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1080/14626268.2016.1145127 (Digital Creativity 27(1), 2016)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OhuDZ877KIY
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1080/14626268.2016.1145127

#### Thing Ethnography: Doing Design Research with Non-Humans — Elisa Giaccardi (2016)
- Type: Paper · Machines: Computer vision, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Things can be research partners: their sensor view reveals patterns of use that people do not notice or report.
- What it is: Cameras and sensors were attached to everyday objects (a kettle, a cup, a fridge) in homes so that designers could study daily life from the things' point of view.
- How it works: Autographer cameras on household objects produced image streams analysed alongside interviews (Giaccardi, Cila, Speed and Caldwell, DIS 2016).
- Lens: Machine umwelt, Machine seeing
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/2901790.2901905 (DIS 2016)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Z0mVcV1EgA
- Project page: https://doi.org/10.1145/2901790.2901905

#### Teacher of Algorithms — automato.farm (2015)
- Type: Film & video · Machines: Platform & recommender algorithm, Social & companion robot
- Idea: Machine learning at home will need human teachers, and that teaching could become a job.
- What it is: A film about a near-future professional who trains other people's smart objects, rewarding and punishing them like pets, because learning products are not good at learning on their own.
- How it works: Design fiction film with prop smart objects and training tools, made by Simone Rebaudengo with Yosuke Ushigome.
- Lens: Hidden labour & extraction, Agency, autonomy & co-creation
- Video: https://vimeo.com/125768041
- Images: http://www.automato.farm/img/training.jpg http://www.automato.farm/img/punish.jpg
- Project page: http://www.automato.farm/portfolio/teach_algorithms/

#### Wekinator — Rebecca Fiebrink (2009)
- Type: Research prototype · Machines: Dataset & training data, Prosthesis & cyborg
- Idea: Interactive, example-based training puts people in the loop and makes ML something you play and sculpt rather than configure.
- What it is: Free software that lets musicians and artists train machine-learning models by example, demonstrating gestures and sounds, so that ML becomes an instrument-building material.
- How it works: Supervised learning on user-recorded examples mapping any input (webcam, sensors, controllers) to any output over OSC, with rapid retraining.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Embodiment & kinesthesia
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NKyyBAKrQgE
- Project page: http://www.wekinator.org/

## Theory & Foundations

The texts, experiments and research that frame machine phenomenology and critical AI.

### Cybernetics & Early AI

Founding experiments and texts, from Turing and Wiener to ELIZA.

#### Machine and Sovereignty: For a Planetary Thinking — Yuk Hui (2024)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Infrastructure, energy & supply chain
- Idea: Every theory of the state hides a theory of the machine; when machines become organic and planetary, sovereignty itself has to be rethought.
- What it is: Hui reads political forms, from Hobbes's Leviathan and Hegel's organic state to Schmitt's Großraum, as technological 'megamachines' shaped by the shift from mechanism to organism to cybernetics, and argues that AI and ecological crisis call for a planetary politics of technodiversity beyond the nation-state.
- How it works: Philosophical history of political epistemology from Hobbes to cybernetics, proposing biodiversity, noodiversity and technodiversity as a framework; a Chinese edition appeared from East China Normal University Press in 2026.
- Lens: Agency, autonomy & co-creation, Machine umwelt
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.5749/9781452973685 (University of Minnesota Press, 2024)
- Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lslV3MG8k0A
- Images: https://minnesota-us.imgix.net/covers/9781517917418.jpg?w=600
- Project page: https://www.upress.umn.edu/9781517917418/machine-and-sovereignty/

#### The Freudian Robot: Digital Media and the Future of the Unconscious — Lydia H. Liu (2010)
- Type: Book & essay · Machines: Cybernetic & artificial-life system, Chatbot & language model
- Idea: The machine age did not bypass the unconscious; it rebuilt it as a model of the human-machine relation.
- What it is: A book that reads Shannon's information theory, cybernetics, Lacan and Freud together and argues that digital media rest on a theory of the unconscious.
- How it works: Media archaeology and close reading of Shannon's printed-English statistics, cybernetic texts and psychoanalysis.
- Lens: Opacity & latent space, Alterity & the uncanny
- Paper: https://doi.org/10.7208/chicago/9780226486840.001.0001 (University of Chicago Press, 2010)
