Known for: AI Now Institute (co-founded 2017); The Steep Cost of Capture (2021). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meredith_Whittaker
- **Milagros Miceli** (Berlin, DE) — Argentine sociologist at the Weizenbaum Institute who studies the data annotators and content moderators of the Global South, and co-leads the Data Workers' Inquiry written by the workers themselves. Known for: Studying Up Machine Learning Data (2022); Data Workers' Inquiry (2024). https://www.weizenbaum-institut.de/en/portrait/p/milagros-miceli/
- **N. Katherine Hayles / 凯瑟琳·海勒** (Los Angeles, US, 1943–) — American literary theorist of the posthuman who insists on embodiment against disembodied information, and describes machines as 'nonconscious cognizers'. Known for: How We Became Posthuman (1999); Unthought: The Power of the Cognitive Nonconscious (2017); Bacteria to AI (2025). http://nkhayles.com/
- **Norbert Wiener / 诺伯特·维纳** (Cambridge, US, 1894–1964) — American mathematician who founded cybernetics, the science of control and communication in animals and machines, and warned early about automation and labour. Known for: Cybernetics (1948); The Human Use of Human Beings (1950); God & Golem, Inc. (1964). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norbert_Wiener
- **Oliver Grau** (Krems, AT, 1965–) — German art historian who founded the Archive of Digital Art (formerly Database of Virtual Art), a key record of media and machine art. Known for: Virtual Art: From Illusion to Immersion (2003); Archive of Digital Art (ADA, founded 1999). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Grau
- **Orit Halpern** (Dresden, DE, 1972–) — Historian of cybernetics and design whose Beautiful Data traces how postwar cybernetics reshaped vision and reason into data, and whose The Smartness Mandate critiques 'smart' everything. Known for: Beautiful Data (2014); The Smartness Mandate (2022, with Robert Mitchell). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orit_Halpern
- **Paul Virilio / 保罗·维利里奥** (Paris, FR, 1932–2018) — French theorist whose The Vision Machine imagined 'sightless vision', cameras and computers that see and interpret without any human looking. Known for: War and Cinema (1984); The Vision Machine (1988). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Virilio
- **Peter-Paul Verbeek** (Amsterdam, NL, 1970–) — Dutch philosopher of technology who extends postphenomenology to show how artefacts mediate perception and moral action; his 'composite intentionality' opens space for machine perception. Known for: What Things Do (2005); Moralizing Technology (2011). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter-Paul_Verbeek
- **Phil Agre** (Los Angeles, US) — American AI researcher who proposed 'critical technical practice', building AI while reflecting on its assumptions, an approach later adopted by artists and designers. Known for: Pengi (1987, with David Chapman); Computation and Human Experience (1997); Surveillance and Capture (1994). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_Agre
- **Phoebe Sengers** (Ithaca, US) — American HCI researcher who built 'schizophrenic' agents to expose how AI design splits behaviour, and founded reflective design as critical technical practice. Known for: Anti-Boxology: Agent Design in Cultural Context (1998); Reflective Design (2005). http://www.cs.cornell.edu/people/sengers/
- **Robert Sparrow** (Melbourne, AU) — Australian philosopher who argued early that robot pets for older people depend on deception, and that autonomous weapons create a gap in responsibility. Known for: The March of the Robot Dogs (2002); Killer Robots (2007); In the Hands of Machines? The Future of Aged Care (2006, with Linda Sparrow). https://research.monash.edu/en/persons/robert-sparrow
- **Ron Wakkary** (Vancouver, CA) — Canadian design researcher whose Morse Things, ceramic bowls that talk to each other in Morse code over the network, were lived with in homes to study a world of things with their own lives. Known for: Morse Things (DIS 2017); Things We Could Design: For More Than Human-Centered Worlds (2021). http://eds.siat.sfu.ca/
- **Roy Ascott / 罗伊·阿斯科特** (London, UK / Shanghai, CN, 1934–) — British artist and theorist of cybernetic and telematic art whose teaching and writings made feedback, interaction and networks central to art, including later in China. Known for: Behaviourist Art and the Cybernetic Vision (1966–67); La Plissure du Texte (1983); Telematic Embrace (2003). https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/staff/rascott
- **Ruha Benjamin** (Princeton, US, 1978–) — American sociologist whose Race After Technology names the 'New Jim Code', the way seemingly neutral systems reproduce racial hierarchies. Known for: Race After Technology (2019); Viral Justice (2022); Imagination: A Manifesto (2024). https://www.ruhabenjamin.com/
- **Safiya Umoja Noble** (Los Angeles, US, 1970–) — American scholar whose Algorithms of Oppression showed how search engines represent Black women through racist and sexist results. Known for: Algorithms of Oppression (2018). https://safiyaunoble.com/
- **Selma Šabanović** (Bloomington, US) — Bosnian-American researcher of social robotics who studies how robots such as PARO are designed and lived with across cultures, especially in Japan and the US. Known for: Robots in Society, Society in Robots (2010). https://r-house.luddy.indiana.edu/
- **Sherry Turkle / 雪莉·特克尔** (Cambridge, US, 1948–) — American psychologist at MIT whose studies of children and elders with Furby, AIBO and PARO describe 'the robotic moment', when we accept machine companionship as enough. Known for: The Second Self (1984); Alone Together (2011); Reclaiming Conversation (2015). https://sherryturkle.mit.edu/
- **Shoshana Zuboff / 肖莎娜·祖博夫** (Maine, US, 1951–) — American scholar who described 'surveillance capitalism', the extraction of human experience as behavioural data for prediction products. Known for: In the Age of the Smart Machine (1988); The Age of Surveillance Capitalism (2019). https://shoshanazuboff.com/
- **Simone Browne** (Austin, US, 1973–) — American scholar whose Dark Matters traces surveillance technologies, including biometrics, back to the policing of Black life under slavery. Known for: Dark Matters: On the Surveillance of Blackness (2015). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simone_Browne
- **Stanisław Lem / 斯坦尼斯瓦夫·莱姆** (Kraków, PL, 1921–2006) — Polish writer and philosopher whose Golem XIV, a superintelligent computer lecturing humans on their limits, remains one of the sharpest imaginings of truly alien machine minds. Known for: Summa Technologiae (1964); The Cyberiad (1965); Golem XIV (1981). https://lem.pl
- **Ted Chiang / 姜峯楠** (Seattle, US, 1967–) — American science-fiction writer whose The Lifecycle of Software Objects follows digital pets raised for years like children, and whose essays sharply describe what language models are. Known for: The Lifecycle of Software Objects (2010); ChatGPT Is a Blurry JPEG of the Web (2023). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Chiang
- **Timnit Gebru / 蒂姆尼特·格布鲁** (San Francisco, US, 1983–) — Ethiopian-born Eritrean-American computer scientist whose work on face-analysis bias and large language models, and her dismissal from Google in 2020, reshaped debates on AI ethics; founder of DAIR. Known for: Gender Shades (2018, with Joy Buolamwini); Datasheets for Datasets (2018); On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots (2021); DAIR Institute (founded 2021). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timnit_Gebru
- **Tomasz Hollanek** (Cambridge, UK) — Researcher at the Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence whose speculative scenarios of 'deadbots' propose design rules for the AI afterlife industry. Known for: Griefbots, Deadbots, Postmortem Avatars (2024, with Katarzyna Nowaczyk-Basińska). https://www.lcfi.ac.uk/people/tomasz-hollanek
- **Valentino Braitenberg** (Tübingen, DE, 1926–2011) — Italian-Austrian neuroscientist whose thought experiment Vehicles shows how tiny wired machines appear to feel fear, love or curiosity, a founding text of synthetic psychology. Known for: Vehicles: Experiments in Synthetic Psychology (1984). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentino_Braitenberg
- **Vilém Flusser / 威廉·弗卢塞尔** (São Paulo, BR / Robion, FR, 1920–1991) — Czech-Brazilian philosopher who described the camera as an 'apparatus' whose program the photographer plays within, a theory that anticipates image-making machines. Known for: Towards a Philosophy of Photography (1983); Into the Universe of Technical Images (1985). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vil%C3%A9m_Flusser
- **Virginia Eubanks** (Troy, US, 1972–) — American political scientist whose Automating Inequality shows how algorithmic systems profile, police and punish the poor. Known for: Automating Inequality (2018). https://virginia-eubanks.com/
- **Wendy Hui Kyong Chun** (Vancouver, CA, 1969–) — American-Canadian media theorist whose Discriminating Data shows how machine learning's logic of homophily ('like likes like') builds segregation into networks. Known for: Programmed Visions (2011); Updating to Remain the Same (2016); Discriminating Data (2021). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Hui_Kyong_Chun
- **Yuk Hui / 许煜** (Rotterdam, NL / Hong Kong, 1985–) — Hong Kong philosopher whose idea of 'cosmotechnics' argues that there is no single universal technology, opening non-Western ways to think about machines and AI. Known for: On the Existence of Digital Objects (2016); The Question Concerning Technology in China (2016); Recursivity and Contingency (2019); Machine and Sovereignty (2024). https://digitalmilieu.net/yuk/

### Curators & critics

- **Amelie Klein** (Weil am Rhein, DE) — Curator at the Vitra Design Museum whose touring exhibition Hello, Robot. Design between Human and Machine surveyed robots from science fiction to smart homes. Known for: Hello, Robot. Design between Human and Machine (Vitra Design Museum, 2017). https://www.design-museum.de/en/exhibitions/detailpages/hello-robot.html
- **Antonio Somaini** (Paris, FR, 1968–) — Italian film and media theorist at Sorbonne Nouvelle who curated The World Through AI at the Jeu de Paume (2025), an exhibition on how AI sees, classifies and generates images. Known for: The World Through AI (Le monde selon l'IA) (Jeu de Paume, 2025); Algorithmic Images: Artificial Intelligence and Visual Culture (2023). https://jeudepaume.org/en/evenement/the-world-through-ai/
- **Christiane Paul** (New York, US) — German-American curator of digital art at the Whitney Museum and author of the standard survey Digital Art; she curated the 2024 Whitney show of Harold Cohen's AARON. Known for: Digital Art (1st ed. 2003); Programmed: Rules, Codes, and Choreographies in Art (Whitney, 2018); Harold Cohen: AARON (Whitney, 2024). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christiane_Paul_(curator)
- **Claudia Schmuckli** (San Francisco, US) — Curator of contemporary art at the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco whose Uncanny Valley: Being Human in the Age of AI brought critical AI art to a major US museum. Known for: Uncanny Valley: Being Human in the Age of AI (de Young, 2020). https://www.famsf.org/exhibitions/uncanny-valley
- **Eva Jäger** (London, UK) — Curator at Serpentine Arts Technologies and co-founder of the Creative AI Lab with King's College London, which studies how artists work with AI as a medium and an institution. Known for: Creative AI Lab (co-founded with Mercedes Bunz, 2019); Future Art Ecosystems (Serpentine, 2020–). https://creative-ai.org/
- **Franziska Nori** (Frankfurt, DE, 1968–) — Director of the Frankfurter Kunstverein who co-curated I Am Here to Learn (2018), one of the first exhibitions devoted to how machines interpret the world. Known for: I Am Here to Learn: On Machinic Interpretations of the World (Frankfurter Kunstverein, 2018, with Mattis Kuhn). https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franziska_Nori
- **Gerfried Stocker** (Linz, AT, 1964–) — Austrian media artist and artistic director of Ars Electronica since 1995, where the festival and Prix have been a main stage for robot and AI art. Known for: Artistic director of Ars Electronica (1995–); Ars Electronica Futurelab (founded 1996). https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerfried_Stocker
- **Ine Gevers** (Eindhoven, NL, 1960–) — Dutch curator whose large exhibition Robot Love (2018) asked whether robots can love and whether people can learn love from robots. Known for: Robot Love (Eindhoven, 2018); Niet Normaal: Difference on Display (2009). https://robotlove.nl/
- **Irini Papadimitriou** (Manchester, UK) — Greek-British curator and creative director of FutureEverything, previously head of digital programmes at the V&A, whose programmes examine AI, data and the ethics of technology. Known for: FutureEverything (creative director); V&A Digital Design Weekend (2010s). https://futureeverything.org/
- **Jasia Reichardt** (London, UK, 1933–) — Polish-British curator and writer whose Cybernetic Serendipity at the ICA (1968) was the first major exhibition of computer and cybernetic art, with robots, drawing machines and Pask's Colloquy of Mobiles. Known for: Cybernetic Serendipity (ICA London, 1968); Robots: Fact, Fiction and Prediction (1978). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasia_Reichardt
- **Joasia Krysa** (Liverpool, UK) — Polish-British curator and scholar of 'exhibitionary AI' whose project The Next Biennial Should Be Curated by a Machine tests what happens when AI curates. Known for: The Next Biennial Should Be Curated by a Machine (2021, with Leonardo Impett); Liverpool Biennial (co-curator, 2016). https://www.ljmu.ac.uk/Research/Centres%20and%20institutes/Institute-of-Art-and-Technology/Expertise/Exhibition-Research-Lab
- **Kathy Rae Huffman** (US / UK, 1943–) — American curator and pioneer of video and net art, and of early cyberfeminist networks, whose work since the 1970s has tracked the arrival of new media machines in art. Known for: Video art curator, Long Beach Museum of Art (1978–84); Face Settings (1997–2000, with Eva Wohlgemuth). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Rae_Huffman
- **Laurence Bertrand Dorléac** (Paris, FR, 1957–) — French art historian who co-curated Artists & Robots at the Grand Palais (2018), a survey of robot and algorithmic art from Schöffer to today. Known for: Artists & Robots (Grand Palais, 2018, with Jérôme Neutres). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Bertrand_Dorl%C3%A9ac
- **Legacy Russell** (New York, US, 1986–) — American curator and writer whose Glitch Feminism treats the glitch, the machine error, as a site of refusal for queer and Black bodies online; executive director of The Kitchen. Known for: Glitch Feminism: A Manifesto (2020); Black Meme (2024). https://www.legacyrussell.com
- **Maholo Uchida / 内田真帆罗** (Tokyo, JP) — Japanese curator at Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation, Tokyo), where she worked on android exhibitions with Hiroshi Ishiguro, and co-curator of AI: More than Human. Known for: AI: More than Human (Barbican, 2019, with Suzanne Livingston); Android exhibits at Miraikan (2014–). https://www.barbican.org.uk/whats-on/2019/event/ai-more-than-human
- **Nora N. Khan** (Los Angeles, US, 1983–) — American writer and curator whose Seeing, Naming, Knowing examines how machine vision names and judges, and whose criticism shaped how the art world writes about AI. Known for: Seeing, Naming, Knowing (2019); Refiguring the Future (2019, co-curator with Lola Kramer). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nora_Khan
- **Peter Weibel / 彼得·魏贝尔** (Karlsruhe, DE, 1944–2023) — Austrian artist, theorist and long-time director of ZKM Karlsruhe, whose exhibitions such as Open Codes placed algorithms, AI and machine agency at the centre of art. Known for: Open Codes (ZKM, 2017–19); Artistic director of ZKM Karlsruhe (1999–2023); Net_Condition (ZKM, 1999). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Weibel
- **Pontus Hultén** (Stockholm, SE / Paris, FR, 1924–2006) — Swedish curator and founding director of the Centre Pompidou's museum whose MoMA exhibition The Machine as Seen at the End of the Mechanical Age surveyed art's relation to machines at the dawn of computing. Known for: The Machine as Seen at the End of the Mechanical Age (MoMA, 1968); Bewogen Beweging (Stedelijk, 1961). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontus_Hult%C3%A9n
- **Sabine Himmelsbach** (Basel, CH, 1966–) — German curator and director of HEK (House of Electronic Arts) in Basel, whose exhibitions such as Entangled Realities look at how we live with AI and machines. Known for: Entangled Realities: Living with Artificial Intelligence (HEK, 2019); Director of HEK Basel (2012–). https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabine_Himmelsbach
- **Suzanne Livingston** (London, UK) — British curator and writer who co-curated AI: More than Human at the Barbican (2019), a large survey that toured internationally and mixed art, science and the history of AI. Known for: AI: More than Human (Barbican, 2019, with Maholo Uchida). https://www.drsuzannelivingston.com/
- **Zhang Ga / 张尕** (Shanghai / Beijing, CN) — Chinese curator and artistic director of Chronus Art Center in Shanghai whose triennials of media art at the National Art Museum of China brought robot, AI and bio art to Chinese audiences. Known for: Synthetic Times (NAMOC, 2008); Translife (NAMOC, 2011); Thingworld (NAMOC, 2014); Artistic director of Chronus Art Center. https://chronusartcenter.org/

### Engineers & roboticists

- **Billy Klüver** (New York, US, 1927–2004) — Swedish Bell Labs engineer who built machines with Tinguely, Rauschenberg and Warhol and co-founded Experiments in Art and Technology, the model for artist–engineer collaboration. Known for: Homage to New York (1960, with Jean Tinguely); 9 Evenings: Theatre and Engineering (1966); Experiments in Art and Technology (E.A.T., founded 1967). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Kl%C3%BCver
- **Blake Lemoine** (San Francisco, US) — American engineer who was dismissed by Google in 2022 after publicly claiming that its LaMDA chatbot was sentient, a flashpoint for debates on machine interiority. Known for: Is LaMDA Sentient? – an Interview (2022). https://cajundiscordian.medium.com/is-lamda-sentient-an-interview-ea64d916d917
- **Christoph Bartneck** (Christchurch, NZ, 1973–) — German HRI researcher who studied whether people hesitate to switch off a pleading robot, robot abuse, and whether robots are racialised by their colour. Known for: Daisy, Daisy, Give Me Your Answer Do! (2007); Godspeed questionnaires (2009); Robots and Racism (2018). https://www.bartneck.de/
- **Claude Shannon / 克劳德·香农** (Cambridge, US, 1916–2001) — American mathematician who founded information theory and built Theseus, a mechanical mouse that learned a maze, as well as the 'useless machine' that only switches itself off. Known for: A Mathematical Theory of Communication (1948); Theseus maze-solving mouse (1950); Ultimate Machine (1952, after Marvin Minsky). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Shannon
- **Cynthia Breazeal / 辛西娅·布雷齐尔** (Cambridge, US, 1967–) — American roboticist who founded social robotics with Kismet, an expressive robot head that responded to people's emotions, and later Jibo, one of the first social robots for the home. Known for: Kismet (1998–2000); Designing Sociable Robots (2002); Leonardo (2003, with Stan Winston Studio); Jibo (2014–). https://www.media.mit.edu/people/cynthiab/
- **David Hanson** (Hong Kong, 1969–) — American robot designer and founder of Hanson Robotics, maker of lifelike humanoid heads such as Bina48 and Sophia, a robot granted Saudi citizenship in 2017. Known for: Philip K. Dick android (2005); Bina48 (2010, for Terasem); Sophia (2016). https://www.hansonrobotics.com/
- **Eugenia Kuyda** (San Francisco, US) — Russian-born founder of Replika, which began as a chatbot built from the messages of her late friend Roman Mazurenko and became a companion app used by millions. Known for: Roman (memorial bot of Roman Mazurenko) (2016); Replika (2017). https://replika.com/
- **Gil Weinberg** (Atlanta, US, 1967–) — Israeli-American music technologist at Georgia Tech whose robotic musicians Haile and Shimon listen and improvise with human players. Known for: Haile (2006); Shimon (2009–); Robotic prosthetic drumming arm (2014). https://www.gilweinberg.com/
- **Guy Hoffman** (Ithaca, US) — Israeli roboticist who draws on acting and animation to design non-humanoid social robots, from a robotic desk lamp to the soft, handcrafted Blossom. Known for: AUR robotic desk lamp (2007); Shimon (2009, with Gil Weinberg); Travis / Shimi (2010s); Blossom (2017). https://hrc2.io/
- **Hans Moravec / 汉斯·莫拉维克** (Pittsburgh, US, 1948–) — Austrian-Canadian roboticist behind Moravec's paradox, the observation that what is easy for humans, like walking and seeing, is hardest for machines. Known for: Stanford Cart (1979); Mind Children (1988); Moravec's paradox (1988). https://frc.ri.cmu.edu/~hpm/
- **Heather Knight** (Corvallis, US) — American roboticist who studies charisma and social intelligence through robot performance, including a NAO robot doing stand-up comedy that adapts to audience laughter. Known for: Data, a stand-up comedy robot (2010); Marilyn Monrobot (company, 2010s); Robot Film Festival (2012–). https://www.charismarobotics.com/
- **Hiroshi Ishiguro / 石黑浩** (Osaka, JP, 1963–) — Japanese roboticist who builds lifelike androids, including a copy of himself, to study what 'human presence' is; his androids act in theatre, museums and films. Known for: Geminoid HI-1 (2006); Telenoid (2010); Erica (2015); Alter (2016, with Takashi Ikegami). https://eng.irl.sys.es.osaka-u.ac.jp/
- **Hod Lipson** (New York, US, 1967–) — Israeli-American roboticist at Columbia whose robots build models of their own bodies, an experimental approach to machine self-awareness. Known for: Resilient Machines Through Continuous Self-Modeling (2006, with Josh Bongard and Victor Zykov); Self-replicating robots (2005); Robot self-image from vision (2022). https://www.hodlipson.com/
- **Hugh Herr** (Cambridge, US, 1964–) — American engineer and climber, a double amputee, who leads MIT's Biomechatronics group and builds bionic limbs that the body feels as its own. Known for: BiOM bionic ankle (2010s); Agonist-antagonist myoneural interface (2018). https://www.media.mit.edu/people/hherr/overview/
- **Ichiro Kato / 加藤一郎** (Tokyo, JP, 1925–1994) — Japanese engineer at Waseda University who built WABOT-1, the first full-scale humanoid robot, and WABOT-2, which read sheet music and played the organ. Known for: WABOT-1 (1973); WABOT-2 (1984). https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/加藤一郎_(ロボット研究者)
- **Jacques de Vaucanson / 雅克·德·沃康松** (Paris, FR, 1709–1782) — French inventor (1709–1782) whose automata, a flute player that really blew into its flute and a duck that appeared to eat and digest, made the body itself a machine question. Known for: The Flute Player (1737); The Digesting Duck (1739). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_de_Vaucanson
- **Joseph Engelberger** (Danbury, US, 1925–2015) — American engineer called the 'father of robotics', whose Unimate arm began work at General Motors in 1961, the industrial robot that later became a material of art. Known for: Unimate (1961, General Motors); Robotics in Practice (1980); HelpMate (1980s). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Engelberger
- **Josh Bongard** (Burlington, US, 1974–) — Canadian roboticist at the University of Vermont who, with Michael Levin, designed xenobots, living machines assembled from frog cells by an evolutionary algorithm. Known for: Resilient Machines Through Continuous Self-Modeling (2006); Xenobots (2020, with Michael Levin); How the Body Shapes the Way We Think (2006, with Rolf Pfeifer). https://jbongard.github.io
- **Kaname Hayashi / 林要** (Tokyo, JP) — Japanese engineer who led Pepper's development at SoftBank and then founded GROOVE X to make LOVOT, a warm, useless robot designed only to be loved. Known for: Pepper (development lead, 2014); LOVOT (GROOVE X, 2019). https://lovot.life/
- **Kenneth Colby** (Stanford, US, 1920–2001) — American psychiatrist who wrote PARRY, a chatbot simulating a paranoid patient, which in 1972 'met' ELIZA for a machine-to-machine therapy session. Known for: PARRY (1972); Artificial Paranoia (1975). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Colby
- **Kerstin Dautenhahn** (Waterloo, CA, 1964–) — German roboticist whose child-sized, minimally expressive robot KASPAR is used with autistic children, showing that simplified robot faces can support social interaction. Known for: KASPAR (2005–); Socially Intelligent Agents (2002, ed.). https://researchprofiles.herts.ac.uk/portal/en/persons/kerstin-dautenhahn(0d00e4af-1f2d-433e-8d0e-ac8690288e4c).html
- **Kevin Warwick** (Coventry, UK, 1954–) — British engineer who implanted an RFID chip (1998) and then a 100-electrode array in his arm (2002), linking his nervous system to a robot hand and to his wife's implant. Known for: Project Cyborg 1.0 (1998); Project Cyborg 2.0 (2002); I, Cyborg (2002). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Warwick
- **Maja Matarić** (Los Angeles, US, 1965–) — Serbian-American roboticist at USC who defined socially assistive robotics, robots that help people through social rather than physical interaction, in stroke rehabilitation, autism and elder care. Known for: Socially assistive robotics (2005, with David Feil-Seifer); The Robotics Primer (2007). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maja_Matari%C4%87
- **Marc Raibert** (Waltham, US, 1949–) — American roboticist who founded Boston Dynamics, whose legged robots and viral videos of them being kicked and dancing shaped public feelings about robot bodies. Known for: Boston Dynamics (founded 1992); BigDog (2005); Spot (2016–); Atlas (2013–). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Raibert
- **Masahiro Mori / 森政弘** (Tokyo, JP, 1927–2025) — Japanese roboticist whose 1970 essay on the 'uncanny valley' described the unease caused by almost-human machines, and whose The Buddha in the Robot finds Buddha-nature in machines. Known for: The Uncanny Valley (Bukimi no Tani, 1970); The Buddha in the Robot (1974); Robocon (1988–). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masahiro_Mori_(roboticist)
- **Michael Levin** (Medford, US, 1969–) — American developmental biologist whose xenobots and anthrobots blur the line between organism and machine and who proposes a framework for recognising minds in unconventional bodies. Known for: Xenobots (2020, with Josh Bongard and Sam Kriegman); Anthrobots (2023); Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere (2022). https://drmichaellevin.org/
- **Michio Okada / 冈田美智男** (Toyohashi, JP, 1960–) — Japanese researcher of 'weak robots', machines that cannot finish their tasks alone, such as a trash-can robot that needs passers-by to pick up litter, making dependence the basis of care. Known for: Weak Robots (Yowai Robotto, 2012); Muu (2000s); Gomi-bako robot (2010s); NICOBO (2021, with Panasonic). https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/岡田美智男
- **Pierre Jaquet-Droz** (La Chaux-de-Fonds, CH, 1721–1790) — Swiss watchmaker (1721–1790) whose android automata, including The Writer, which can be programmed to write any text of 40 characters, are ancestors of programmable robots. Known for: The Writer (1768–74); The Draughtsman (1768–74); The Musician (1768–74). https://www.jaquet-droz.com/fr/the-extraordinary-history-jaquet-droz
- **Radhika Nagpal** (Princeton, US) — Indian-American roboticist whose thousand-robot Kilobot swarm and termite-like builders show collective behaviour emerging from simple machines. Known for: Kilobot swarm of 1,024 robots (2014); TERMES termite-inspired builders (2014); Blueswarm (2021). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radhika_Nagpal
- **Raffaello D'Andrea** (Zurich, CH, 1967–) — Canadian-Italian-Swiss engineer who co-created The Table, a robot table that chooses a visitor to follow, co-founded Kiva Systems (now Amazon Robotics) and choreographed drones. Known for: The Table (2001, with Max Dean); Kiva Systems warehouse robots (2003); Flying Machine Arena (2008); Sparked (Cirque du Soleil, 2014). http://raffaello.name/
- **Rebecca Fiebrink** (London, UK) — American researcher at UAL Creative Computing Institute whose Wekinator lets artists train machine-learning models by demonstration, treating ML as a creative, embodied instrument. Known for: Wekinator (2009); Machine Learning for Musicians and Artists (Kadenze, 2016). https://www.doc.gold.ac.uk/~mas01rf/
- **Rodney Brooks / 罗德尼·布鲁克斯** (Boston, US, 1954–) — Australian roboticist whose behaviour-based robotics replaced central planning with layered, embodied reflexes, from the six-legged Genghis to the Roomba vacuum cleaner. Known for: Elephants Don't Play Chess (1990); Genghis (1989); Cog (1993–); Roomba (iRobot, 2002). https://rodneybrooks.com/
- **Rolf Pfeifer** (Zurich, CH, 1947–) — Swiss AI researcher who championed embodied intelligence, showing that a robot's body and materials do part of its thinking ('morphological computation'). Known for: Understanding Intelligence (1999, with Christian Scheier); How the Body Shapes the Way We Think (2006, with Josh Bongard); ECCE / Roboy (2010s). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolf_Pfeifer
- **Steve Mann** (Toronto, CA, 1962–) — Canadian engineer who has lived with wearable computers and head-mounted cameras since the late 1970s and coined 'sousveillance', watching the watchers from below. Known for: WearComp / EyeTap (late 1970s–); Sousveillance (2002). http://wearcam.org/
- **Susumu Tachi / 馆暲** (Tokyo, JP, 1946–) — Japanese engineer who proposed 'telexistence' in 1980 and built the TELESAR robots that let a person see, hear and feel through a remote robot body. Known for: Telexistence (1980); TELESAR series (1980s–); Optical camouflage (2003). https://tachilab.org/en/
- **Takanori Shibata / 柴田崇德** (Tsukuba, JP, 1967–) — Japanese engineer at AIST who created PARO, a baby harp seal robot used in dementia care worldwide, and a central case in debates on machine care. Known for: PARO therapeutic seal robot (research from 1993; released 2004). https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/柴田崇徳
- **Takashi Ikegami / 池上高志** (Tokyo, JP, 1961–) — Japanese artificial-life scientist at the University of Tokyo who gives machines spontaneous, self-organising behaviour; his android Alter moves by a neural network and central pattern generators. Known for: Mind Time Machine (YCAM, 2010); Alter (2016, with Hiroshi Ishiguro); Alter 3 in Scary Beauty (2018). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takashi_Ikegami
- **Tomotaka Takahashi / 高桥智隆** (Kyoto, JP, 1975–) — Japanese robot creator whose small humanoids include Kirobo, the first talking robot companion in space, and RoBoHoN, a robot that is also a phone. Known for: Kirobo (2013, on the ISS); Robi (2013); RoBoHoN (2016). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomotaka_Takahashi
- **W. Grey Walter** (Bristol, UK, 1910–1977) — American-born British neurophysiologist whose light-seeking robot tortoises Elmer and Elsie showed lifelike, unpredictable behaviour from two 'neurons', the first autonomous robots. Known for: Machina speculatrix tortoises Elmer and Elsie (1948–49); The Living Brain (1953). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Grey_Walter
- **Wang Xingxing / 王兴兴** (Hangzhou, CN, 1990–) — Chinese engineer and founder of Unitree Robotics, whose quadruped and humanoid robots danced yangge with handkerchiefs on the 2025 Spring Festival Gala, a landmark for public images of robots in China. Known for: Unitree Robotics (founded 2016); Unitree H1 humanoids at the CCTV Spring Festival Gala (2025). https://www.unitree.com/
- **Wendy Ju** (New York, US) — American interaction researcher at Cornell Tech whose Ghost Driver hid a driver inside a car seat costume to study how pedestrians react to 'driverless' cars. Known for: Ghost Driver (2015); The Design of Implicit Interactions (2015). http://www.wendyju.com/

### Museums & art centres

- **Aksioma – Institute for Contemporary Art** (Ljubljana, Slovenia) — Ljubljana nonprofit that produces and publishes critical art on networks, algorithms and power, including the PostScriptUM publication series. https://aksioma.org/
- **Ars Electronica Center / 林茨电子艺术中心** (Linz, Austria) — The 'museum of the future' of Ars Electronica. Its permanent exhibition Understanding AI (since 2019) shows how machines perceive and classify, with works such as Anatomy of an AI System and Gender Shades. https://ars.electronica.art/center/en/
- **Art Center Nabi / Nabi 艺术中心** (Seoul, South Korea) — Korea's first art centre dedicated to digital art, founded by SK Group. It has run robot art, AI and creative-technology programmes and hackathons for more than two decades. http://www.nabi.or.kr/
- **Barbican Centre / 巴比肯艺术中心** (London, UK) — London arts centre whose exhibition AI: More than Human (2019) became a template for AI surveys, running from the dream of artificial beings through mind machines and data worlds. https://www.barbican.org.uk/
- **Carnegie Museum of Art (Hillman Photography Initiative) / 卡内基艺术博物馆** (Pittsburgh, US) — Pittsburgh museum whose Hillman Photography Initiative ran Mirror with a Memory (2020–21), a programme on AI, photography, surveillance and bias, including Trevor Paglen's Opposing Geometries. https://carnegieart.org/
- **Centre Pompidou / 蓬皮杜艺术中心** (Paris, France) — Paris's national modern art centre. Its Mutations/Créations series staged Neurones, les intelligences simulées (2020), a history of neural and simulated intelligence across art, design and science. https://www.centrepompidou.fr/en/
- **Chronus Art Center / 新时线媒体艺术中心** (Shanghai, China) — Shanghai's first nonprofit art centre dedicated to media art, with exhibitions, research and a lab. A main venue in China for machine, algorithmic and kinetic work, including the Chinese tour of ZKM's Open Codes. https://www.chronusartcenter.org/
- **Computer History Museum / 计算机历史博物馆** (Mountain View, US) — Silicon Valley museum and archive of computing. Its collection and exhibition Revolution include AI and robotics milestones such as Shakey the robot, with oral histories of the engineers. https://computerhistory.org/
- **de Young Museum (FAMSF) / 笛洋美术馆** (San Francisco, US) — San Francisco fine arts museum that staged Uncanny Valley: Being Human in the Age of AI (2020), which read the uncanny valley politically as the gap between AI's promises and its effects on data, labour and bias. https://www.famsf.org/visit/de-young
- **FACT Liverpool / 利物浦艺术与创意技术基金会** (Liverpool, UK) — The UK's leading centre for art and creative technology (Foundation for Art and Creative Technology). It commissions and shows work on data, surveillance and AI, often with community co-production. https://www.fact.co.uk/
- **Fondazione Prada / 普拉达基金会** (Milan, Italy) — Milan art foundation whose Osservatorio hosted Training Humans (2019), conceived by Kate Crawford and Trevor Paglen: the first major exhibition of the training images that teach machines to see people. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fondazione_Prada
- **Furtherfield** (London, UK) — London's longest-running art-and-technology organisation, with a gallery and lab in Finsbury Park. It stages critical exhibitions and games on AI, data, blockchain and more-than-human futures. https://www.furtherfield.org/
- **Haus der Kulturen der Welt (HKW) / 世界文化之家** (Berlin, Germany) — Berlin centre for contemporary arts and discourse. Long-term projects such as Technosphere (2015–19) examined computation, infrastructure and planetary technology. https://www.hkw.de/en
- **HEK (House of Electronic Arts) Basel / 巴塞尔电子艺术之家** (Basel, Switzerland) — Swiss centre for digital culture and new art forms. Its 2019 show Entangled Realities: Living with Artificial Intelligence brought together LAUREN, Tay's resurrection and Autonomous Trap 001. https://www.hek.ch/en/
- **iMAL** (Brussels, Belgium) — Brussels centre for digital cultures and technology with an exhibition space and fablab. It shows and produces work on algorithms, sensing and automation. https://www.imal.org/en
- **Jeu de Paume / 网球场国家美术馆** (Paris, France) — Paris centre for photography and the image. The World Through AI (2025) split AI into analytical and generative systems and set artworks beside historical 'time capsules' of machine vision. https://jeudepaume.org/en/
- **KADIST** (Paris, France / San Francisco, US) — Nonprofit contemporary art organisation that collects and commissions globally. Its exhibition Apophenia, Interruptions: Artists and Artificial Intelligence at Work (2024) looked at pattern-finding and misrecognition. https://kadist.org/
- **Kapelica Gallery / Kersnikova Institute** (Ljubljana, Slovenia) — Ljubljana gallery for 'investigative' art, including robotics, bio art and body-machine performance (Stelarc, Špela Petrič). The Kersnikova Institute also runs the RAMPA and BioTehna labs. https://kersnikova.org/
- **LABoral Centro de Arte y Creación Industrial / LABoral 艺术与工业创造中心** (Gijón, Spain) — Spanish art centre for art, science, technology and industrial creation, set in a former labour university. Its exhibitions and production labs address automation, labour and machines. https://www.laboralcentrodearte.org/
- **LAS Art Foundation** (Berlin, Germany) — Berlin foundation that commissions large works at the edge of art, science and technology, such as Lawrence Lek's NOX (2023), a rehab centre for sentient self-driving cars. https://www.las-art.foundation/
- **MAK – Museum of Applied Arts, Vienna / 维也纳应用艺术博物馆** (Vienna, Austria) — Design museum that hosts the Vienna Biennale for Change. It co-produced Hello, Robot (2017) and staged Uncanny Values: Artificial Intelligence & You (2019), linking design and critical AI. https://www.mak.at/en
- **Miraikan – National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation / 日本科学未来馆** (Tokyo, Japan) — Tokyo science museum where the public meets humanoid and android robots, from ASIMO demonstrations to Hiroshi Ishiguro's androids Otonaroid and Kodomoroid (2014). https://www.miraikan.jst.go.jp/en/
- **Mori Art Museum / 森美术馆** (Tokyo, Japan) — Contemporary art museum in Roppongi Hills. Its survey Future and the Arts: AI, Robotics, Cities, Life (2019–20) presented over 100 projects on how humans will live with machines. https://www.mori.art.museum/en/
- **Nam June Paik Art Center / 白南准艺术中心** (Yongin, South Korea) — Museum and archive of Nam June Paik, whose Robot K-456 (1964) was an early robot performer. It shows and researches media art that continues Paik's play with machines, broadcast and the body. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nam_June_Paik_Art_Center
- **NTT InterCommunication Center [ICC] / NTT 互动交流中心** (Tokyo, Japan) — Tokyo's media art centre, run by NTT East, devoted to communication technology and art. Its exhibitions and archive are a key reference for Japanese machine, sensor and interactive art. https://www.ntticc.or.jp/en/
- **Onassis Stegi / 奥纳西斯文化中心** (Athens, Greece) — Athens cultural centre of the Onassis Foundation with a strong digital culture programme. Its exhibition You and AI: Through the Algorithmic Lens (2021) examined how AI sees and sorts people. https://www.onassis.org/
- **Science Gallery / 科学画廊** (Dublin / London / Bengaluru / Melbourne) — University-based network of galleries where art meets science for young audiences. Its AI shows, from Science Gallery Dublin's early exhibitions to London's AI: Who's Looking After Me? (2023), moved from automation to bias to care. https://sciencegallery.org/
- **Science Museum, London / 伦敦科学博物馆** (London, UK) — UK national science museum. Its exhibition Robots (2017) showed more than 100 robots across 500 years, from mechanical automata to humanoids, and still anchors the popular history of the robot. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_Museum,_London
- **Serpentine Arts Technologies / 蛇形画廊艺术与技术部** (London, UK) — Serpentine's programme for art made with AI, blockchain and game engines, with commissions such as Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst's The Call (2024). It co-runs the Creative AI Lab and publishes the Future Art Ecosystems reports. https://www.serpentinegalleries.org/arts-technologies/
- **Society for Arts and Technology (SAT) / 蒙特利尔艺术与技术协会** (Montréal, Canada) — Montréal centre for immersive and digital art with a dome, research lab and residencies, developing telepresence and immersive tools used by artists. https://sat.qc.ca/en/
- **Taikang Art Museum / 泰康美术馆** (Beijing, China) — Beijing museum of the Taikang collection. Its exhibition Creative Machine (2024–25) traced sixty years of machine creativity, from early computer art to drawing robots such as Patrick Tresset's Human Study #1. https://tam.taikang.com/
- **Taiwan Contemporary Culture Lab (C-LAB) / 台湾当代文化实验场** (Taipei, Taiwan) — Taipei cultural lab in a former air force base, with a Technology Art Center, a sound lab and the Future Media Arts festival. A key venue for Taiwanese art on AI and machines. https://clab.org.tw/en/
- **Tate Modern / 泰特现代美术馆** (London, UK) — London's national modern art museum. Electric Dreams: Art and Technology Before the Internet (2024–25) traced the pre-internet lineage of machine art, and Anicka Yi's Hyundai Commission (2021) filled the Turbine Hall with floating machine organisms. https://www.tate.org.uk/visit/tate-modern
- **UCCA Center for Contemporary Art / UCCA 尤伦斯当代艺术中心** (Beijing, China) — China's leading contemporary art institution, with venues in Beijing, Beidaihe and Shanghai. It has staged major surveys of artists working with digital bodies and automation, such as Cao Fei: Staging the Era (2021). https://ucca.org.cn/en/
- **V&A – Victoria and Albert Museum (Digital Art) / 维多利亚与阿尔伯特博物馆** (London, UK) — London design museum that holds the UK's national collection of computer and digital art, from 1960s plotter drawings to Anatomy of an AI System, which it acquired. https://www.vam.ac.uk/
- **V2_ Lab for the Unstable Media / V2_ 不稳定媒体实验室** (Rotterdam, Netherlands) — Interdisciplinary centre for art and media technology that ran the Dutch Electronic Art Festival (DEAF). Its lab, publications and online archive document decades of work on the body, sensors and machines. https://v2.nl/
- **Vancouver Art Gallery / 温哥华美术馆** (Vancouver, Canada) — Canadian art museum whose exhibition The Imitation Game: Visual Culture in the Age of Artificial Intelligence (2022) traced AI in visual culture from automata to machine vision. https://www.vanartgallery.bc.ca/
- **Vitra Design Museum / 维特拉设计博物馆** (Weil am Rhein, Germany) — Design museum whose touring exhibition Hello, Robot. Design between Human and Machine (2017) sorted robots by culture, work, home and body, and became a reference for how design meets machines. https://www.design-museum.de/en/
- **Whitney Museum of American Art (artport) / 惠特尼美国艺术博物馆** (New York, US) — New York museum whose online portal artport (since 2001) commissions net and software art. Its 2024 exhibition Harold Cohen: AARON showed the drawing program drawing live in a gallery for the first time. https://whitney.org/
- **Yamaguchi Center for Arts and Media [YCAM] / 山口情报艺术中心** (Yamaguchi, Japan) — Japanese media arts centre whose in-house R&D team, YCAM InterLab, co-develops works on dance, sensing and machines with artists, releasing tools and research as open source. https://www.ycam.jp/en/
- **ZKM | Center for Art and Media Karlsruhe / ZKM 卡尔斯鲁厄艺术与媒体中心** (Karlsruhe, Germany) — Europe's largest media art museum, with a collection spanning computer art to AI. Exhibitions such as Open Codes (2017) and BioMedia (2021) framed machine learning, algorithmic governance and life-like media systems. https://zkm.de/en

### Festivals & exhibition series

- **ACM Creativity & Cognition / ACM 创造力与认知会议** (Itinerant) — ACM conference on human creativity and computation, founded by Ernest Edmonds in 1993, with papers, pictorials and an art exhibition on co-creation with machines. https://cc.acm.org/
- **ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) / 人机交互国际会议（HRI）** (Itinerant) — The main research conference on human-robot interaction. Its studies of trust, anthropomorphism and robot bullying are core evidence for how people read machine bodies. https://humanrobotinteraction.org/
- **Ars Electronica Festival / 林茨电子艺术节** (Linz, Austria) — The world's longest-running festival for art, technology and society. Editions such as Artificial Intelligence – The Other I (2017), with its Artificial Intimacy section, set the agenda for machine art. https://ars.electronica.art/festival/en/
- **Art & Science International Exhibition and Symposium (Tsinghua) / 艺术与科学国际作品展暨学术研讨会** (Beijing, China) — Recurring exhibition and symposium initiated in 2001 at Tsinghua University by physicist T.D. Lee and painter Wu Guanzhong, now held at the Tsinghua University Art Museum. China's main art-and-science series. https://www.artmuseum.tsinghua.edu.cn/
- **Beijing Media Art Biennale / 北京媒体艺术双年展** (Beijing, China) — Biennale at the CAFA Art Museum, Central Academy of Fine Arts. Its first edition Ethics of Technology (2016) and Post-Life (2018) are key Chinese-language frames for art about machines. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAFA_Art_Museum
- **CVPR AI Art Gallery / CVPR AI 艺术画廊** (Itinerant) — Online and on-site gallery of the CVPR computer vision conference, showing artworks that use or question computer vision; its archive documents each year's selection. https://thecvf-art.com/
- **Elektra / International Digital Art Biennial (BIAN)** (Montréal, Canada) — Montréal festival and biennial for digital art, which often features robotic and machine installations; BIAN editions include the robotics-themed Automata (2016). https://elektramontreal.ca/
- **EVA London – Electronic Visualisation and the Arts** (London, UK) — Annual London conference on electronic visualisation and the arts, run with the BCS Computer Arts Society, spanning early computer art history to AI. https://www.eva-london.org/
- **FILE – Electronic Language International Festival** (São Paulo, Brazil) — Latin America's largest electronic art festival, held in São Paulo, with robotic, interactive and AI art and an extensive online archive. https://file.org.br/
- **Impakt** (Utrecht, Netherlands) — Utrecht organisation for critical media culture, with a yearly festival, residencies and a centre for media culture. Its themes often address algorithms, surveillance and machine perception. https://impakt.nl/
- **International Conference on Computational Creativity (ICCC) / 国际计算创造力会议** (Itinerant) — Annual conference of the Association for Computational Creativity on whether and how machines can be creative, from art-making systems to evaluation. https://computationalcreativity.net/
- **ISEA International (International Symposium on Electronic Art) / 国际电子艺术研讨会** (Itinerant) — The main academic symposium and exhibition for electronic art, held in a different city each year since 1988. Its online archive holds decades of papers on robot art, A-life and AI. https://isea-international.org/
- **Japan Media Arts Festival / 日本文化厅媒体艺术节** (Tokyo, Japan) — Festival and awards of Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs (1997–2022) across art, entertainment, animation and manga. Sony's aibo and the robotic opera Pendulum Choir were among its prize-winners. https://j-mediaarts.jp/en/
- **KIKK Festival** (Namur, Belgium) — International festival of digital and creative cultures in Namur, with talks and installations by designers and artists working on AI, robots and speculative futures. https://www.kikk.be/
- **Microwave International New Media Arts Festival / 微波国际新媒体艺术节** (Hong Kong) — Hong Kong's long-running new media arts festival, with themed exhibitions and forums that have included machine and AI art from Asia. https://www.microwavefest.net/
- **NeurIPS Creative AI Track / NeurIPS 创意 AI 单元** (Itinerant) — Juried track of the NeurIPS machine learning conference for art and design work with and about AI, following the Machine Learning for Creativity and Design workshops (2017–22). It puts artists in the room with ML researchers. https://neurips.cc/
- **NIME – New Interfaces for Musical Expression** (Itinerant) — International conference on new musical instruments and interfaces, including robotic instruments, AI co-performers and machine listening. https://www.nime.org/
- **SIGGRAPH Art Gallery & Art Papers / SIGGRAPH 艺术画廊** (Itinerant (North America / Asia)) — The art programme of ACM SIGGRAPH, the computer graphics conference, and SIGGRAPH Asia. For decades it has shown computational, robotic and AI art beside the research that makes it possible. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIGGRAPH
- **STRP Festival** (Eindhoven, Netherlands) — Eindhoven festival for creative technology, set in a former Philips industrial complex, whose editions explore living with robots, AI and sensing environments. https://strp.nl/
- **Sónar+D** (Barcelona, Spain) — Creativity and technology congress of the Sónar music festival, with talks and showcases on AI in music, synthetic voices and human-machine performance. https://sonar.es/en
- **transmediale / 柏林跨媒体艺术节** (Berlin, Germany) — Berlin festival for art and digital culture, known for critical rather than celebratory themes (Capture All 2015, face value 2018, for refusal 2021–22). It co-publishes the APRJA journal. https://transmediale.de/
- **WRO Media Art Biennale / WRO 媒体艺术双年展** (Wrocław, Poland) — Central Europe's longest-running media art biennale, run by the WRO Art Center in Wrocław, with exhibitions on sound, machines and networked media. https://wrocenter.pl/en/
- **xCoAx – Computation, Communication, Aesthetics & X** (Itinerant (Europe)) — Conference and exhibition on computation, communication and aesthetics, with papers and artworks on algorithms, generative systems and the nature of computing. https://xcoax.org/

### Awards & prizes

- **Human AI Art Award / 人类 AI 艺术奖** (Bonn, Germany) — Annual award by the Art Collection Deutsche Telekom and Kunstmuseum Bonn for art that reflects on AI: Lauren Lee McCarthy's LAUREN (2024) and Nicolas Gourault's Unknown Label (2025). https://www.art-collection-telekom.com/en/
- **LG Guggenheim Award / LG 古根海姆奖** (New York, US) — US$100,000 award for technology-based art from the LG Guggenheim Art & Technology Initiative. Winners: Stephanie Dinkins (2023), Shu Lea Cheang (2024), Ayoung Kim (2025) and Trevor Paglen (2026). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LG_Guggenheim_Award
- **Lumen Prize / Lumen 数字艺术奖** (London, UK) — International prize for art made with technology, with an AI award since 2018 (e.g. Lichtsuchende, a light-seeking robot society). Much of it is generative, so its winners need case-by-case selection. https://www.lumenprize.com/
- **Mozilla Creative Media Awards / Mozilla 创意媒体奖** (Global) — Mozilla Foundation grants for art, games and media that make the harms of AI tangible to the public, especially bias, surveillance and platform power. https://foundation.mozilla.org/en/what-we-fund/awards/creative-media-awards/
- **Prix Ars Electronica / 电子艺术大奖** (Linz, Austria) — The leading prize for media art. Its Artificial Life & Intelligence category honours work on what AI and life science mean for being human, with Golden Nicas for Paul Vanouse's Labor (2019) and Forensic Architecture's Cloud Studies (2021). https://ars.electronica.art/prix/en/
- **RobotArt Competition / 机器人艺术竞赛** (US / Online) — Annual competition (2016–18) for robots that paint with physical brushes, which gathered university and artist teams and made robot painting visible as a craft. https://robotart.org/
- **S+T+ARTS Prize / S+T+ARTS 奖** (Linz, Austria / EU) — European Commission prize for innovation at the nexus of science, technology and the arts, run by Ars Electronica. Winners include Project Alias (2019), Holly+ (2022), Calculating Empires (2024) and the AI War Cloud Database (2025). https://ars.electronica.art/starts-prize/en/
- **VIDA – Art & Artificial Life International Awards / VIDA 艺术与人工生命国际奖** (Madrid, Spain) — Fundación Telefónica's prize (1999–c.2015), the only award devoted to art and artificial life: robots that sweat, walking tables, autonomous protest agents and virtual ecologies. https://www.fundaciontelefonica.com/

### Labs & research centres

- **Abundant Intelligences** (Montréal, Canada / Global) — Indigenous-led research programme based at Concordia University that conceptualises, designs and builds AI from Indigenous knowledge systems. https://abundant-intelligences.net/
- **Ada Lovelace Institute / 艾达·洛芙莱斯研究所** (London, UK) — Independent research institute of the Nuffield Foundation ensuring data and AI work for people and society, with public-attitude studies on biometrics and facial recognition. https://www.adalovelaceinstitute.org/
- **AI Now Institute / AI Now 研究所** (New York, US) — Policy research institute co-founded by Kate Crawford and Meredith Whittaker on the social consequences of AI. Its reports on bias, labour and concentrated industry power shaped critical AI discourse. https://ainowinstitute.org/
- **Antikythera** (Los Angeles, US / Global) — Think tank for the speculative philosophy of computation, directed by Benjamin Bratton and incubated at the Berggruen Institute. It studies planetary computation and synthetic intelligence through studios, publications and film. https://antikythera.org/
- **ANU School of Cybernetics / 澳大利亚国立大学控制论学院** (Canberra, Australia) — School founded by anthropologist Genevieve Bell, from the 3A Institute, to revive cybernetics as a way of building, steering and critiquing AI-enabled systems. https://cybernetics.anu.edu.au/
- **Ars Electronica Futurelab / 电子艺术未来实验室** (Linz, Austria) — The R&D studio of Ars Electronica, working with industry and universities on drone swarms, robots and human-AI collaboration, and presenting the results as art. https://ars.electronica.art/futurelab/en/
- **Artists + Machine Intelligence (Google AMI) / 谷歌艺术家与机器智能计划** (Mountain View / Global) — Google programme that pairs artists with machine intelligence researchers; it supported early DeepDream-era art and projects such as K Allado-McDowell's Pharmako-AI. https://ami.withgoogle.com/
- **Creative AI Lab / 创意 AI 实验室** (London, UK) — Collaboration between Serpentine Arts Technologies and King's College London's Department of Digital Humanities. It studies AI as an artistic medium and keeps a database of tools and resources for artists. https://creative-ai.org/
- **Creative Machines Lab (Columbia University) / 哥伦比亚大学创意机器实验室** (New York, US) — Hod Lipson's robotics lab, known for self-modelling robots that learn their own body image, robots that paint and machines that design machines. https://www.creativemachineslab.com/
- **Data & Society / 数据与社会研究所** (New York, US) — Independent research institute founded by danah boyd that studies the social implications of data-centric and automated technologies, from platform labour to algorithmic accountability. https://datasociety.net/
- **Distributed AI Research Institute (DAIR) / 分布式 AI 研究所** (Distributed) — Independent, community-rooted AI research institute founded by Timnit Gebru after her dismissal from Google. It centres the people harmed by AI, including data workers. https://www.dair-institute.org/
- **Forensic Architecture / 法证建筑** (London, UK) — Research agency at Goldsmiths that investigates state and corporate violence with spatial, media and machine-vision analysis. It trains classifiers on synthetic data and won the 2021 Golden Nica for Cloud Studies. https://forensic-architecture.org/
- **Gramazio Kohler Research (ETH Zurich)** (Zurich, Switzerland) — ETH Zurich chair for architecture and digital fabrication, which put industrial robots to work building walls and structures and made robotic construction a design subject. https://gramaziokohler.arch.ethz.ch/
- **Hiroshi Ishiguro Laboratories (ATR / Osaka University) / 石黑浩实验室** (Kyoto / Osaka, Japan) — Hiroshi Ishiguro's android labs, which built the Geminoid copies, Erica and, with Kōdai-ji temple, the android Kannon Mindar. They are the main testbed for questions of presence and the uncanny valley. http://www.geminoid.jp/en/
- **Humanoid Robotics Institute (Waseda University) / 早稻田大学人形机器人研究所** (Tokyo, Japan) — Successor to Ichiro Kato's lab, which built WABOT-1 (1973), the first full-scale humanoid robot, and later emotional and musical humanoids such as the flute-playing WF series. https://www.humanoid.waseda.ac.jp/
- **Ikegami Lab (University of Tokyo) / 池上高志实验室** (Tokyo, Japan) — Takashi Ikegami's artificial life lab, which built the android Alter with Ishiguro's team to test whether spontaneous, life-like movement can emerge from neural networks. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takashi_Ikegami
- **Institute of Network Cultures / 网络文化研究所** (Amsterdam, Netherlands) — Research centre at the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences founded by Geert Lovink, publishing open-access books and readers on platforms, internet critique and AI. https://networkcultures.org/
- **Intelligent Instruments Lab / 智能乐器实验室** (Reykjavík, Iceland) — ERC-funded lab at the University of Iceland studying musical instruments that embed AI as creative partners and what such instruments mean for musicianship. Distinction in the Prix Ars Electronica AI in ART Award. https://iil.is/
- **IRCAM / 法国声学与音乐研究协调所** (Paris, France) — Paris institute for music and acoustic research founded by Pierre Boulez at the Centre Pompidou. Its research on machine listening, voice synthesis and AI co-improvisation (OMax, Somax) shapes human-machine music. https://www.ircam.fr/
- **KIM – AI and Media Philosophy (HfG Karlsruhe) / 卡尔斯鲁厄设计学院 AI 与媒体哲学研究组** (Karlsruhe, Germany) — Research group on artificial intelligence and media philosophy at the Karlsruhe University of Arts and Design, known for its work on the social history of AI and the Nooscope diagram. https://kim.hfg-karlsruhe.de/
- **Knowing Machines** (Global) — Research project tracing the histories, practices and politics of how machine learning systems are trained to interpret the world, including Models All the Way Down, a visual investigation of the LAION-5B dataset. https://knowingmachines.org/
- **LACMA Art + Technology Lab / 洛杉矶郡艺术博物馆艺术与技术实验室** (Los Angeles, US) — Grant and residency programme that revives LACMA's 1967–71 Art and Technology programme, pairing artists with tech companies on projects about AI, robotics and sensing. https://www.lacma.org/lab
- **Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence / 剑桥大学利弗休姆未来智能中心** (Cambridge, UK) — Cambridge research centre on the long-term impact of AI. Its AI Narratives and Global AI Narratives projects study how stories shape what we expect of machines, and it has researched griefbots and 'digital afterlife' ethics. https://www.lcfi.ac.uk/
- **metaLAB (at) Harvard / 哈佛 metaLAB** (Cambridge, MA, US) — Creative research group at Harvard's Berkman Klein Center, whose projects include the AI Pedagogy Project and artworks on machine classification and moral decisions. https://metalab.harvard.edu/
- **MIT Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS) / MIT 高级视觉研究中心** (Cambridge, MA, US) — Fellowship centre founded by György Kepes at MIT (1967–2009) where artists worked with engineers on light, kinetic and cybernetic art; a model for later art-and-technology labs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Advanced_Visual_Studies
- **MIT Media Lab – Affective Computing Group / MIT 媒体实验室情感计算组** (Cambridge, MA, US) — Rosalind Picard's group, which founded affective computing: machines that sense and respond to emotion. Its work underlies both care technologies and the emotion recognition that artists critique. https://www.media.mit.edu/groups/affective-computing/overview/
- **MIT Media Lab – Personal Robots Group / MIT 媒体实验室个人机器人组** (Cambridge, MA, US) — Cynthia Breazeal's group, which grew out of her sociable robot Kismet (1990s) and went on to build Leonardo and the social robot Jibo. It is the reference lab for robots designed as companions, tutors and carers. https://www.media.mit.edu/groups/personal-robots/overview/
- **Mixed Reality Laboratory (University of Nottingham) / 诺丁汉大学混合现实实验室** (Nottingham, UK) — HCI lab with a long collaboration with Blast Theory. Its Cat Royale (2023) let a robot arm play with three cats for twelve days to test the ethics of robots caring for animals. https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/research/groups/mixedrealitylab/
- **Ory Laboratory / Ory 研究所** (Tokyo, Japan) — Kentaro Yoshifuji's company behind the avatar robot OriHime and the Avatar Robot Café DAWN, where people with ALS and other disabilities work as waiters through robots. https://orylab.com/en/
- **Reality Design Lab / 现实设计实验室** — Design research lab led by Botao Amber Hu that makes mixed-reality and speculative works on other minds and machines, such as EchoVision (what is it like to be a bat?), City of Sparkles (how might an AI perceive our city?) and AI Mom™. It also builds the open HoloKit toolkit and runs the Machinic Reality Inspire gallery. https://reality.design/
- **Robotic Musicianship Group (Georgia Tech) / 佐治亚理工机器人音乐组** (Atlanta, US) — Gil Weinberg's group at the Georgia Tech Center for Music Technology, which built the improvising marimba robot Shimon, a machine that listens and plays with humans. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gil_Weinberg
- **SHARE Lab / SHARE Foundation** (Novi Sad, Serbia) — Research and data investigation lab of the SHARE Foundation, led by Vladan Joler, which maps the invisible infrastructures of networks and AI. It is the home of the maps behind Anatomy of an AI System. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHARE_Foundation
- **STUDIO for Creative Inquiry (CMU) / 卡内基梅隆大学创意探究工作室** (Pittsburgh, US) — Carnegie Mellon's lab for atypical, anti-disciplinary art research, directed by Golan Levin. It hosts residencies and projects on computer vision, robotics and creative coding. https://studioforcreativeinquiry.org/
- **UAL Creative Computing Institute / 伦敦艺术大学创意计算研究所** (London, UK) — University of the Arts London institute for creative computing research and teaching, including interactive machine learning for artists (Wekinator) and critical AI practice. https://www.arts.ac.uk/creative-computing-institute
- **UCLA Art|Sci Center / UCLA 艺术|科学中心** (Los Angeles, US) — Victoria Vesna's centre at UCLA for collaborations between artists and scientists, a hub of the art-science network behind many machine and bio-art projects. https://artsci.ucla.edu/
- **Waag Futurelab / Waag 未来实验室** (Amsterdam, Netherlands) — Amsterdam research institute for technology and society that runs public labs, including critical work on AI, biometrics and the 'public stack'. https://waag.org/en/

### Residencies & programmes

- **Akademie Schloss Solitude (Web Residencies) / 孤独城堡学院** (Stuttgart, Germany) — Stuttgart residency academy whose online Web Residencies, published on Schlosspost, fund artists responding to curated calls, many on AI, bots and algorithmic culture. https://www.akademie-solitude.de/en/
- **China Academy of Art – School of Inter-Media Art / 中国美术学院跨媒体艺术学院** (Hangzhou, China) — China's leading school for new media, installation and network art at the China Academy of Art, a training ground for Chinese artists working with machines and AI. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_Academy_of_Art
- **Eyebeam** (New York, US) — Nonprofit that supports artists working with technology through residencies and fellowships, with a strong line of alumni projects on surveillance, bias and algorithmic justice. https://www.eyebeam.org/
- **Goldsmiths Computational Arts / 伦敦大学金史密斯学院计算艺术** (London, UK) — Goldsmiths' computational art programmes and embodied interaction research (EAVI), which trained many artists who work with machine learning, bodies and sound. https://www.gold.ac.uk/pg/ma-computational-arts/
- **Gray Area** (San Francisco, US) — San Francisco nonprofit arts centre for creative technology, with an incubator, education programmes and the Gray Area Festival on art, AI and society. https://grayarea.org/
- **IAMAS – Institute of Advanced Media Arts and Sciences / 情报科学艺术大学院大学** (Ogaki, Japan) — Japanese graduate school for media arts and sciences in Gifu, whose alumni include many Japanese device, sensor and machine artists. https://www.iamas.ac.jp/en/
- **NEW INC** (New York, US) — The New Museum's cultural incubator for art, design and technology, whose members have developed many projects on AI and its social effects. https://www.newmuseum.org/new-inc/
- **NYU ITP / IMA / 纽约大学互动电信项目** (New York, US) — NYU Tisch's Interactive Telecommunications Program and Interactive Media Arts, a hub for physical computing, creative machine learning (ml5.js) and artists building with technology. https://tisch.nyu.edu/itp
- **S+T+ARTS Residencies / S+T+ARTS 驻留计划** (EU) — European Commission initiative that funds artist residencies inside technology and research projects, many on AI, robotics and sustainability. https://starts.eu/
- **SAIC Art and Technology Studies / 芝加哥艺术学院艺术与技术系** (Chicago, US) — School of the Art Institute of Chicago department, rooted in Sonia Sheridan's Generative Systems programme (1970), that teaches robotics, kinetics and electronics as art. https://www.saic.edu/atsp
- **School for Poetic Computation (SFPC) / 诗意计算学校** (New York, US) — Artist-run school in New York for art, code, hardware and critical theory, with classes on the poetics and politics of machines. https://sfpc.study/
- **School of Creative Media, City University of Hong Kong / 香港城市大学创意媒体学院** (Hong Kong) — Hong Kong media art school that hosts the Art Machines symposium on computational media art, and a centre for robotic and AI art in Asia. https://www.scm.cityu.edu.hk/
- **Somerset House Studios / 萨默塞特宫工作室** (London, UK) — Experimental workspace for artists and makers inside Somerset House, home to studios working on AI, sound and speculative design, and producer of exhibitions such as 24/7 (2019). https://www.somersethouse.org.uk/somerset-house-studios
- **UCLA Design Media Arts / UCLA 设计媒体艺术系** (Los Angeles, US) — UCLA department for media art and design whose faculty include Casey Reas (Processing) and Lauren Lee McCarthy (LAUREN). https://dma.ucla.edu/

### Archives & databases

- **ACM SIGGRAPH History Archive (Digital Art Archive) / ACM SIGGRAPH 数字艺术档案** (Online) — Online archive of SIGGRAPH art galleries, artworks and art papers since the 1980s, a record of computational and robotic art beside graphics research. https://history.siggraph.org/
- **AI Art Gallery (aiartonline.com) / AI 艺术在线画廊** (Online) — Online gallery of the NeurIPS Workshop on Machine Learning for Creativity and Design, curated by Luba Elliott, archiving the art selected by the ML community 2017–2021. https://www.aiartonline.com/
- **AI Incident Database / AI 事故数据库** (Online) — Open archive of real-world harms and near-harms caused by AI systems, started at the Partnership on AI, which catalogues machine failures from misidentification to autonomous vehicle crashes. https://incidentdatabase.ai/
- **AI Myths / AI 迷思** (Online) — Resource by Daniel Leufer debunking common misconceptions about AI, such as 'AI has agency' or 'AI can be objective', with references to research. https://www.aimyths.org/
- **AIAAIC Repository / AIAAIC 事件库** (Online) — Independent, public-interest repository of AI, algorithmic and automation incidents and controversies, classified by sector, technology and harm. https://www.aiaaic.org/
- **AIArtists.org** (Online) — Directory of artists working with AI, organised by critical questions such as bias, dataset ethics and robotic production. It leans generative, so it is best used as a lead list. https://aiartists.org/
- **Anatomy of an AI System / AI 系统解剖图** (Online) — Kate Crawford and Vladan Joler's map and essay of the human labour, data and planetary resources behind one Amazon Echo request; in the MoMA and V&A collections. https://anatomyof.ai/
- **Archive of Digital Art (ADA) / 数字艺术档案** (Krems, Austria) — Scholarly database of digital art founded by Oliver Grau, documenting hundreds of artists and thousands of works and texts, with strong coverage of robotic and A-life art. https://www.digitalartarchive.at/
- **Ars Electronica Archive / 电子艺术节档案** (Linz, Austria) — Archive of Prix Ars Electronica entries since 1987, festival catalogues and documentation: the largest record of how media art engaged robots, A-life and AI. https://ars.electronica.art/archive/en/
- **Atlas of Surveillance / 监控地图集** (US / Online) — EFF and University of Nevada, Reno database of surveillance technologies used by US police, from face recognition to drones and automated licence plate readers. https://atlasofsurveillance.org/
- **Better Images of AI / 更好的 AI 图像** (Online) — Nonprofit collaboration offering a free library of images that represent AI more accurately than glowing brains and humanoid robots, commissioned from artists. https://betterimagesofai.org/
- **Calculating Empires / 计算帝国** (Online) — Large-scale research visualisation by Crawford and Joler, A Genealogy of Technology and Power 1500–2025, tracing how communication and computation systems grew with control; S+T+ARTS Grand Prize 2024. https://calculatingempires.net/
- **Critical Algorithm Studies: a Reading List / 批判算法研究书单** (Online) — Reading list by Tarleton Gillespie and Nick Seaver of the Microsoft Research Social Media Collective on algorithms as social concern, a standard entry point for critical algorithm studies. https://socialmediacollective.org/reading-lists/critical-algorithm-studies/
- **Cybernetic Serendipity archive / 控制论的意外发现档案** (Online) — Online archive of Jasia Reichardt's 1968 ICA exhibition Cybernetic Serendipity, the founding show of computer and cybernetic art, with Gordon Pask's Colloquy of Mobiles and Edward Ihnatowicz's SAM. https://www.cyberneticserendipity.net/
- **cyberneticzoo.com** (Online) — Illustrated history of cybernetic animals and early robots, from Grey Walter's tortoises to forgotten walking machines, compiled from period sources. https://cyberneticzoo.com/
- **Daniel Langlois Foundation for Art, Science and Technology / 丹尼尔·朗格卢瓦艺术、科学与技术基金会** (Montréal, Canada) — Foundation whose online archive documents Experiments in Art and Technology (E.A.T.) and early media art, including essays on artists who worked with machines and cybernetics. https://www.fondation-langlois.org/
- **Data Workers' Inquiry / 数据劳工调查** (Berlin / Global) — Community research project of DAIR and the Weizenbaum Institute in which data workers who label and moderate for AI document their own conditions in reports, films and zines. https://data-workers.org/
- **Database of Digital Art (compArt daDA) / 数字艺术数据库** (Bremen, Germany) — Database from the compArt centre at the University of Bremen on the pioneers of computer art and their exhibitions, including Cybernetic Serendipity (1968). http://dada.compart-bremen.de/
- **Excavating AI / 发掘 AI** (Online) — Essay by Kate Crawford and Trevor Paglen on the politics of images in machine learning training sets, which examined ImageNet's 'person' categories and fed into ImageNet Roulette. https://excavating.ai/
- **Exposing.ai** (Berlin, Germany) — Adam Harvey and Jules LaPlace's research project (successor to MegaPixels) that traces how face and biometric datasets were built from scraped photos and lets people search whether theirs were used. https://exposing.ai/
- **Machine Vision in Art, Games and Narratives (database) / 艺术、游戏与叙事中的机器视觉数据库** (Bergen, Norway) — ERC project at the University of Bergen whose open database codes about 500 artworks, games and stories as 'situations' of who does what to whom with which machine-vision technology. https://machinevisionuib.github.io/
- **Media Art Net / 媒体艺术网** (Karlsruhe, Germany) — Bilingual (German/English) online platform by ZKM and the Goethe-Institut with works, artists and essays on media art history, including robotics and cybernetic art. http://www.medienkunstnetz.de/
- **Media Arts Database (Japan) / 日本媒体艺术数据库** (Tokyo, Japan) — National database of Japanese media arts, including records of media art exhibitions, festivals and works, useful for tracing Japanese machine and device art. https://mediaarts-db.artmuseums.go.jp/
- **Monoskop** (Online) — Wiki and digital library for art, media and the humanities founded by Dušan Barok, with rich pages and scans on cybernetic art, media art festivals and machine theory. https://monoskop.org/
- **ROBOTS Guide (IEEE Spectrum) / IEEE 机器人指南** (Online) — IEEE's illustrated catalogue of real robots, with photos, videos and specifications for hundreds of humanoids, companion robots and industrial arms. https://robotsguide.com/
- **The Glass Room / 玻璃房间** (Berlin, Germany / Online) — Tactical Tech's exhibition about data and surveillance, styled as a tech store, with more than 40 exhibits under themes such as We Know You and Big Mother; now toured in community and online editions. https://theglassroom.org/

### Journals, books & podcasts

- **AI & Society (Springer) / 《AI 与社会》期刊** (Global) — Journal of knowledge, culture and communication on the societal implications of AI, including art, labour and ethics. https://link.springer.com/journal/146
- **AI Weirdness** (Online) — Janelle Shane's blog and newsletter on the strange ways AI fails, from neural-net paint colours to hallucinated giraffes: a long-running record of machine error as a window into machine 'minds'. https://www.aiweirdness.com/
- **APRJA – A Peer-Reviewed Journal About** (Aarhus, Denmark / Berlin) — Open-access journal produced with transmediale and Aarhus University, each issue built from a research workshop on topics such as machine research and machine feeling. https://aprja.net/
- **Blood in the Machine / 机器中的血** (Online) — Brian Merchant's newsletter and book on the Luddites and today's fight against automation, reporting how AI reshapes work. https://www.bloodinthemachine.com/
- **Computational Culture / 《计算文化》期刊** (Online) — Open-access journal of software studies, publishing research on algorithms, machine learning and the cultural life of code. https://computationalculture.net/
- **Critical AI (Duke University Press) / 《批判性 AI》期刊** (US) — Interdisciplinary journal and Rutgers-based initiative that brings humanities methods to AI, from large language models to data labour. https://criticalai.org/
- **Cybernetic Forests / 控制论森林** (Online) — Eryk Salvaggio's newsletter on AI, art and cybernetics, reading generated images as infographics of their datasets and arguing against AI hype. https://www.cyberneticforests.com/
- **e-flux journal / e-flux 期刊** (New York, US) — Online art journal that published key texts on machine vision and AI, such as Hito Steyerl's 'A Sea of Data: Apophenia and Pattern (Mis-)Recognition' (2016). https://www.e-flux.com/journal/
- **Leonardo (MIT Press) / Leonardo ISAST / 《莱昂纳多》期刊** (Cambridge, MA, US / San Francisco, US) — Journal of arts, sciences and technology founded by kinetic artist Frank Malina, where artists such as Eduardo Kac and Simon Penny published foundational texts on robotic art. Leonardo also runs a book series and the LASER talks. https://leonardo.info/
- **Logic(s)** (US) — Magazine about technology and its politics, relaunched as Logic(s) with a focus on Black, Asian and Indigenous perspectives; issues on intelligence, bodies and supply chains. https://logicmag.io/
- **meson press** (Lüneburg, Germany) — Open-access publisher of media theory, with titles on machine learning, pattern discrimination and the history of computing. https://meson.press/
- **Mute** (London, UK) — London magazine on culture and politics after the net, with long-running critical writing on automation, labour and digital capitalism. https://www.metamute.org/
- **Mystery AI Hype Theater 3000** (Online) — DAIR podcast and stream in which linguist Emily M. Bender and sociologist Alex Hanna take apart claims of machine intelligence and AI hype. https://www.dair-institute.org/maiht3k/
- **nettime** (Online) — Mailing list for net criticism founded in 1995, where the net.art and tactical media generations debated networks, software and machines. https://www.nettime.org/
- **Neural** (Bari, Italy) — Bilingual (Italian/English) magazine on new media art, electronic music and hacktivism, founded by Alessandro Ludovico and long a chronicle of critical machine art. https://neural.it/
- **Noema Magazine** (Los Angeles, US) — Magazine of the Berggruen Institute that publishes long essays on AI, minds and planetary computation by writers such as Benjamin Bratton, Blaise Agüera y Arcas and Tobias Rees. https://www.noemamag.com/
- **Open Humanities Press / 开放人文出版社** (Online) — Open-access academic publisher whose books include Joanna Zylinska's AI Art: Machine Visions and Warped Dreams (2020). https://www.openhumanitiespress.org/
- **Philosophy & Technology (Springer) / 《哲学与技术》期刊** (Global) — Philosophy journal on technology, including postphenomenology, machine agency and AI ethics. https://link.springer.com/journal/13347
- **Posthumanities (University of Minnesota Press) / 《后人类》丛书** (Minneapolis, US) — Book series edited by Cary Wolfe, including Ian Bogost's Alien Phenomenology (2012), a core shelf for thinking about nonhuman and machine experience. https://www.upress.umn.edu/search-grid/?series=posthumanities
- **Real Life** (Online) — Online magazine (2016–2022) about living with technology, whose essays on smart speakers, algorithms and machine intimacy remain an archive of everyday machine phenomenology. https://reallifemag.com/
- **Tech Won't Save Us (podcast)** (Online) — Weekly podcast by Paris Marx with critical perspectives on tech, AI hype and the labour and infrastructure behind it. https://techwontsave.us/
- **Technophany** (Online) — Journal of the Research Network for Philosophy and Technology (Yuk Hui and others), publishing philosophy of technology, cosmotechnics and machine thought. https://technophany.philosophyandtechnology.network/
- **The Good Robot (podcast) / 好机器人播客** (Cambridge, UK) — Podcast by Eleanor Drage and Kerry McInerney asking feminist thinkers and technologists what good technology is. https://www.thegoodrobot.co.uk/

### Networks & nonprofits

- **AIxDesign** (Amsterdam, Netherlands / Global) — Community and studio of designers, artists and researchers working critically with AI, running programmes, publications and a slow-AI research line. https://aixdesign.co/
- **Algorithmic Justice League / 算法正义联盟** (Cambridge, MA, US) — Organisation founded by Joy Buolamwini that combines art and research to expose bias in AI, starting from the 'coded gaze' of face recognition shown in Gender Shades. https://www.ajl.org/
- **AlgorithmWatch / 算法观察** (Berlin, Germany) — Nonprofit research and advocacy organisation that investigates automated decision-making systems and their impact on society in Europe. https://algorithmwatch.org/en/
- **Black in AI** (Global) — Network co-founded by Timnit Gebru and Rediet Abebe to increase the presence and inclusion of Black people in AI. https://blackinai.github.io/
- **Coding Rights** (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil) — Brazilian feminist organisation on technology and human rights, whose Not My A.I. project maps AI deployed against marginalised people in Latin America. https://codingrights.org/
- **Computer Arts Society (CAS) / 计算机艺术学会** (London, UK) — British society founded in 1968, the year of Cybernetic Serendipity, to support computer use in the arts; publisher of the bulletin PAGE and a specialist group of the BCS. https://computer-arts-society.com/
- **Constant** (Brussels, Belgium) — Brussels artist-run association for art, media and technology, home to Algolit, which explores machine learning through literature and code. https://constantvzw.org/
- **Critical Engineering Working Group / 批判工程工作组** (Berlin, Germany) — Group behind The Critical Engineering Manifesto (2011), which asks engineers and artists to expose the inner workings of the technologies we depend on. https://criticalengineering.org/
- **Data for Black Lives** (US) — Movement of activists and scientists using data to improve Black lives and fighting algorithmic discrimination. https://d4bl.org/
